attorneys.name: Anthony T. Adolf
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Fort Wayne, IN
attorneys.bio:
A Trusted Ally For Troubling Times

Whether you are struggling with debt or facing a serious family law problem, it may be hard to find light at the end of the tunnel. Rest assured, there are solutions to the legal problems you face. Adolf Law Office in Fort Wayne is here to help you find them.

Attorney Anthony T. Adolf has extensive experience helping people get out of debt by guiding them through the bankruptcy process. He has also helped numerous individuals and families achieve their legal goals in divorce, child custody disputes and other family law matters.

A better future lies ahead. We are here to help you get there.

Proven Debt Relief Services

Debt can make life miserable, but there is a way out. By filing for bankruptcy, you can get creditors off your back while reducing and in some cases completely eliminating your debt burden.

It may seem like your creditors hold all the cards, but you have powerful legal protections at your disposal. Anthony T. Adolf is a trusted and respected bankruptcy lawyer who can make the law work for you.

Knowledgeable Family Law Guidance

When a legal matter affects your family, the stakes are enormous. We understand this and handle divorce, child custody and other family law issues with the utmost care and attention to detail.

We strive to resolve family law dispute amicably whenever possible, but we are always prepared for strong legal action when our clients’ personal and financial future is at stake.

Discuss Your Legal Matters With An Experienced Lawyer

You don’t have to face debt problems or family law issues alone. Our law firm is here to provide you with the skilled advocacy and attentive service you deserve. To reach our Fort Wayne law office, contact us online or by telephone at 260-530-5549.

We are a debt relief agency. We help people file for bankruptcy relief under the Bankruptcy Code.

attorneys.name: Jacob Ahler
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Law Lawyers in Rensselaer, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jacob Ahler is an Attorney in Rensselaer, Indiana who works in a general practice setting. Jacob primarily focuses his practice on Commercial Law, Estate Planning, Civil Litigation, and Criminal Defense. Jacob also serves as a public defender in Jasper and Tippecanoe County.

Jacob also serves a number of municipal clients in Northwestern Indiana, including serving as the County Attorney for Benton and Pulaski County Indiana.

Before practicing law as an Attorney, Jacob worked as a Certified Legal Intern for Michael Riley Esq and as an Associate Justice on the Staton Moot Court Board where he was appointed to the Order of the Barristers. Jacob received his J.D. at Indiana University and his A.B. from Wabash College. While at Wabash, Jacob was a member of the Beta Theta Pi fraternity.

Jacob is admitted to practice law in the State of Indiana, as well as the Northern Federal District in Indiana. Jacob is a member of the Indiana State Bar Association and the Jasper County Bar Association.

Prior to returning to Rensselaer, Jacob worked for the Office of the Indiana Attorney General where he investigated licensed professionals for misconduct. Jacob also worked as an assistant to U.S. Senator Richard Lugar in Washington D.C. and as a law clerk at the law firm of Spagnolo & Hoeksema LLC in Chicago, Illinois.

Jacob is a proud native of Rensselaer who decided to move back to his hometown and get involved in community improvement. Jacob serves is involved in the Knights of Columbus, Rensselaer Rotary Club, and volunteers his time with the Boy Scout Troop 152 where he earned the rank of Eagle Scout. In his free time, Jacob enjoys skiing, exercising, traveling and spending time with his family.

attorneys.name: Scott B. Ainsworth
attorneys.firm_name: DeVoss, Baker, Ainsworth & Razo, A Professional Corporation
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate / Title Insurance Lawyers in Decatur, IN
attorneys.bio:
Scott B. Ainsworth has practiced law in Decatur, Indiana, his hometown, for over 30 years, and has worked hard to gain the respect of his clients and fellow attorneys by providing quality and efficiency in his practice. His personal areas of practice are in business representation (large and small), corporate/entity formation, real estate/title insurance, wills/trusts/probate/estate planning, contracts, school law, and general legal matters. Please review the practice areas section for more details.

Scott is a 1981 graduate of Bellmont High School, graduated, with High Distinction from Indiana University, Bloomington, in December 1984, with a B.A. in Economics, and received his J.D. from Indiana University School of Law, Bloomington (now the Maurer School of Law) in May 1988, graduating in the top ten in his class, Magna Cum Laude, and Order of the Coif. He is a member of the Adams County and Indiana Bar Associations. He has been with this firm for his entire legal career. Throughout his career, Scott has had varied experiences, representing nationally active RV manufacturing /transportation entities, multi-state heavy construction companies, regional real estate developers, builders and construction companies, local businesses, a public school system, or just people/families down the street. He has always tried to focus on one thing; getting the job done for his client in the most effective and efficient manner possible. He is also a former member on the Board of law examiners, the entity which prepares and administers the Indiana Bar exam and character and fitness determinations for new attorneys in Indiana. Scott also is on the Board of Directors for the local chapter of Junior Achievement.

Returning to his hometown was always a priority for Scott, and he has been being active in the community. He is a member of St. Paul Lutheran Church, has been on the Board of Directors for the Decatur Public Library, the Adams County United Way, the Cross Creek Men's Golf Association and the Decatur Men's Golf Hall of Fame, and has been involved in coaching youth/school basketball teams, among his many local activities. He is married and the father of 3 boys, and at this time 1 perfect grand-daughter.

Honors

National Merit Scholar

attorneys.name: Ms. Jennifer R. Aldridge J.D.
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer R. (Mann) Aldridge is an Indianapolis area attorney whose practice primarily includes estate planning, probate and estate administration, business formation, civil and probate mediation, and real estate. Jen has practiced in these areas for over 16 years. Jen has received additional training as a Guardian Ad Litem for both adults and children, as well as training as a Collaborative Practitioner. She strives to provide clients with honest and practical legal advice while also empathizing with them as they navigate difficult and emotional times in their lives.

Jen graduated from Indiana University (Bloomington) with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Psychology, with minors in Biology and Business, in 2003. She was also a 4-year scholarship athlete for the Indiana University Women's Soccer Team. In addition to playing soccer at IU, Jen was a four-year member of the Alpha Beta Honorary, a three-time recipient of Academic All-Big Ten honors, and was honored with the Big Ten Sportsmanship Award during her senior season. She received her Doctorate of Jurisprudence from the Indiana University McKinney School of Law in 2008.

Jen’s volunteer activities include serving as a Guardian ad Litem through Kids’ Voice of Indiana and the Marion Superior Court 8 Pro Bono Project for both minors and incapacitated adults. She has also volunteered her time providing legal advice and assistance to underprivileged members of the community through the Indy Bar’s Free Wills Clinic and Kids’ Voice of Indiana’s Community Mobile Law Program. In addition to her pro bono work, Jen serves on the Indianapolis Bar Association’s Estate Planning & Administration Executive Committee and the Indiana State Bar Association’s Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity Committee. She is a proud graduate of the Indianapolis Bar Association’s Bar Leadership Program - Class XIII. She has also been honored as a Super Lawyer Rising Star for 2017, 2019, 2020, and 2021, and more recently as a Super Lawyer for 2022-2025. Jen enjoys spending time with her family and friends, traveling, scuba diving, and staying active. She resides near downtown Indianapolis with her family.

attorneys.name: David Allen
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Fishers, IN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney David Allen has been practicing law for over 25 years, focusing his practice primarily on helping injured clients. As an Indianapolis medical malpractice attorney, David has prosecuted nursing home negligence, medical devices/pharmaceutical negligence, surgical errors, failure/delay in diagnosis, fetal demise and mass tort claims So entrenched in these areas, for a period of time he was a member of the plaintiffs' steering committee in the multidistrict litigation (MDL) of vaginal mesh cases. In addition to medical malpractice, David also has deep experience as an Indiana personal injury lawyer.

David's practice also includes a wide range of personal injury matters from dog bites and auto accident claims to catastrophic injury cases. He is empathetic toward the plight of clients and the difficulties associated with suffering from an injury caused by another's negligence, be it a fender bender or slip and fall or a major medical mistake from a defective medical device or medication.

Regardless of the type of case, David represents his clients zealously, working to achieve the best result possible as quickly as possible, whether that is through mediation, arbitration, or a trial on the merits.

Attorney David Allen Is Deeply Rooted in Indiana

David grew up just south of Indianapolis in Martinsville. He joined the United States Navy after high school and served four years with multiple deployments around the world.

Following his service in the Navy, David attended Indiana University Bloomington campus for two years and then transferred to Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis (IUPUI) to complete his bachelor's degree. After graduating, he attended law school at Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law.

Before committing his career to personal injury and medical malpractice clients, David worked several years in Marion County Municipal Court and Superior Courts while he completed his undergraduate and law school studies.

The Personal Side of Attorney David Allen

David Allen is more than an Indiana medical malpractice and injury lawyer. In his free time, he loves to spend time with his adult daughter, who lives in Colorado. Closer to home, he enjoys relaxing with his golden retriever, Chance, and can be found spending time outdoors hiking and exercising.

Contact Attorney David Allen for Your Medical Malpractice Representation Needs

If you have fallen victim to medical malpractice, have been injured by a medical device or medication, or have suffered injuries as the result of an accident or event of any kind, you need an experienced and passionate Indiana medical malpractice and injury lawyer like David Allen at Camden & Meridew, P.C. With support from the firm's wider litigation team, David is ideally suited to help you fight for your right to be compensated for your injuries and hold the responsible party accountable.

attorneys.name: Eric N. Allen
attorneys.firm_name: Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Greenfield, IN
attorneys.bio:
Eric N. Allen grew up in Munster, Indiana and graduated from Munster High School in 1970. After graduating from Purdue University in 1974, he attended Indiana University School of Law -- Indianapolis, and graduated in January 1978. Having taken and passed the Indiana Bar in October 1977; he was admitted on January 18, 1978. He immediately joined the Greenfield firm of Ging Free Brand Tosick & VanWinkle as an associate attorney, and he has practiced in the same location since that date. In 1980, Mr. Allen was asked to join the firm as a named partner and the firm became known as Free Brand Tosick & Allen. At that time the firm was primarily litigation oriented concentrating in Divorce, Personal injury and Criminal cases. Mr. Allen was instrumental in expanding the scope of the firm's offerings into a variety of other areas including Real Estate, Commercial Litigation and Bankruptcy, as well as expanding the geographical scope to the practice to numerous other communities throughout Central and Eastern Indiana. In 1988, following the retirement of Stephen Free, the firm was renamed Brand & Allen. Following the death of James L. Brand, the firm was renamed Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP

Mr. Allen is a member of the Indiana State Bar Association, the Indianapolis Bar Association, and the Hancock County Bar Association, where he served as Vice President in 1984 and President in 1985. He currently carries an AV Peer Review Rating with Martindale-Hubbell Law Digest and is listed in the Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers.

attorneys.name: Lisa A. Anderson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Lisa Anderson is a partner in the firm's private client division, concentrating her practice in family law matters.

Lisa has been practicing law since 2000 and the majority of her time in practice has been devoted to handling family law cases. Lisa began her legal practice in Columbus, Indiana, with Sharpnack Bigley LLP. There she initially handled many different types of cases, including family law, insurance defense, and general litigation cases. However, Lisa quickly realized that her true passion was in family law cases. As one of only a few female attorneys in Columbus, Lisa was approached often to handle family law cases by both men and women. In 2005, Lisa became a partner at Sharpnack Bigley LLP.

In July, 2006, Lisa began representing the State of Indiana and advocating on behalf of abused and neglected children. She was staff attorney for the Bartholomew County Department of Child Services from July, 2006 until March, 2008. While that work was rewarding, it did not allow Lisa the client contact that she enjoyed. In March, 2008, Lisa returned to the practice of family law with Andy Mallor and Kendra Gjerdingen.

Lisa is a Certified Family Law Specialist, as certified by the Family Law Certification Board, and a Registered Domestic Relations Mediator. She is able to assist with any family law matter, including divorce, child custody matters, adoption, guardianship, and children in need of services proceedings. Lisa has completed Parent Coordinator training and collaborative law training, and is a member of the Bloomington Association of Collaborative Professionals.

Lisa, her husband and their two children reside in Monroe County. Lisa is also active in the community, lending her services to several child-related organizations. She has served on the Board of Directors for the Boys & Girls Club of Bloomington, and previously served as President of the Board of Directors for Children, Incorporated. She also volunteers as a basketball and softball coach for the Richland Bean Blossom Youth Sports organization.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Recognized by Best Lawyers®, Family Law, 2023-2026; Family Law Mediation, 2024-2026; 2026 “Lawyer of the Year” Award – Family Law (Columbus, Indiana region)

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Munster, IN
attorneys.bio:
Doug has been a Fellow of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers since 1990, making him one of 1600 attorneys in the United States to be recognized by both judges and other attorneys as a preeminent family law practitioner for his high level of knowledge, skill and integrity. He has been repeatedly selected by his peers for inclusion in The Best Lawyers in America and in Indiana Super Lawyers since 2007 in the field of Family Law and is a Family Law Mediator in the state of Indiana.

Doug has been and continues to be a presenter and chairman of numerous continuing legal education seminars in the area of family law, and is recognized by both judges and other lawyers for his leadership in improving the quality of legal services which are provided to families in Northwest Indiana.

Range of Experience:

Trial experience includes:

Serving as lead counsel for initial intake to judgement in numerous jury and bench trials, including predominantly contested family law cases;

Expert testimony on substantive areas of family law;

Retained by other attorneys to prepare qualified domestic relations orders and on family law related issues in bankruptcy court;

Consultation with other attorneys in family law cases at both state and federal trial and appellate levels;

Prosecution and defense of appellate proceedings, including oral argument before the Indiana Supreme Court;

Former Court Coordinator and Temporary Judge Lake Circuit Court conducting pre-trial conferences, developing and implementing case-flow management and docket control systems, developing and implementing modifications to local practices to satisfy requirements of federally and state mandated operational guidelines and record keeping systems;

Former public defender Gary City and Lake County Courts' and, former Assistant Lake County Attorney.

attorneys.name: Albert Anzini III
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Fort Wayne, IN
attorneys.bio:
Albert Anzini III has practiced law for more than twenty years. He is admitted to practice law in the State of Indiana and the Commonwealth of Virginia. He is also admitted to practice before the Federal District Courts for the Northern District of Indiana and the Eastern District of Virginia. His practice is concentrated in the area of criminal defense with a focus on DUI/OWI defense, drug dealing and possession cases, domestic battery allegations, and plaintiff injury cases.

Al Anzini is a graduate of the Marshall-Wythe School of Law at the College of William & Mary. He is a member of the Indiana and Allen County Bar Associations, the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, a former barrister in the Benjamin Harrison Chapter of the American Inns of Court and a former member of the National College for DUI Defense. Al Anzini also serves on the Board of Directors for the Stop Addiction Foundation.

Al Anzini is qualified in Standardized Field Sobriety Testing and is a graduate of the National Advocacy Center.

Al Anzini is a decorated Veteran whose military awards include the Meritorious Service Medal and the Army Commendation Medal with three Oak Leaf Clusters. He served eight years in the U.S. Army JAG Corps and zealously defended soldiers facing court martial, non-judicial punishment and administrative sanctions throughout Europe, Asia and the United States. Al Anzini is a graduate of the Army's Combined Arms Services Staff School and the 32nd AADCOM Noncommissioned Officer's Academy.

Before entering private practice in 2003, Al Anzini practiced law as a Senior Military Defense Counsel, Military Trial Counsel, Special Assistant U.S. Attorney and an Allen County Deputy Prosecuting Attorney holding the position of Chief of the Narcotics and Asset Forfeiture Unit.

He is a member of the Indiana and Allen County Bar Associations, the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, a former barrister in the Benjamin Harrison Chapter of the American Inns of Court and a former member of the National College for DUI Defense. Al Anzini also serves on the Board of Directors for the Stop Addiction Foundation.

Al Anzini is qualified in Standardized Field Sobriety Testing and is a graduate of the National Advocacy Center.

Al Anzini is a decorated Veteran whose military awards include the Meritorious Service Medal and the Army Commendation Medal with three Oak Leaf Clusters. He served eight years in the U.S. Army JAG Corps and zealously defended soldiers facing court martial, non-judicial punishment and administrative sanctions throughout Europe, Asia and the United States. Al Anzini is a graduate of the Army's Combined Arms Services Staff School and the 32nd AADCOM Noncommissioned Officer's Academy.

Before entering private practice in 2003, Al Anzini practiced law as a Senior Military Defense Counsel, Military Trial Counsel, Special Assistant U.S. Attorney and an Allen County Deputy Prosecuting Attorney holding the position of Chief of the Narcotics and Asset Forfeiture Unit.

attorneys.name: Robert Douglas Aplin
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Fort Wayne, IN
attorneys.bio:
Robert Douglas Aplin is a partner at Scott & Aplin LLC. He was born in Auburn, Indiana in December, 1973 where he lived until the closing of the Fort Wayne International Harvester Plant caused his family to relocate to Ohio in 1986. He spent the balance of his childhood in Springfield, Ohio and Toledo, Ohio. After graduating from law school, he practiced law in Defiance, Ohio until he returned to Indiana in 2005. Mr. Aplin is a 1992 graduate of Sylvania Southview High School in Sylvania, Ohio. He received his Bachelor of Arts Degree from Kent State University in 1996 and received his Juris Doctor Degree from The Ohio Northern University Claude W. Pettit College of Law in 1999.

In 2025, Mr. Aplin celebrated twenty (25) years practicing law. He is licensed to practice before all state courts in the states of Ohio and Indiana. He is also licensed to practice before the Federal District Court for the Northern District of Ohio.

Mr. Aplin has been a Mortgage Foreclosure Workout Facilitator as appointed by various Courts throughout Northeast Indiana. Since 2010, Mr. Aplin has assisted numerous homeowners in Adams, Allen, Dekalb, Wells and Whitley Counties save their homes from foreclosure. In the past, he has served as the Village Solicitor for the Village of Hicksville in Defiance County, Ohio and the Village of Melrose in Paulding County, Ohio.

Mr. Aplin concentrates his practice in the areas of construction litigation, real estate and general civil litigation. He currently represents the legal interests of over 30 homeowner's associations in and around the greater Fort Wayne area, numerous small businesses and various contractors in the building trades.

Mr. Aplin and his wife, Catherine, reside in rural Huntington County, Indiana. In his free time, Mr. Aplin enjoys spending time with his children and grandchild. He is the proud parent of United States Marine currently stationed abroad.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Fort Wayne, IN
attorneys.bio:
Bart L. Arnold was born in Anderson, Indiana in 1970. Mr. Arnold was admitted to practice law in Indiana in 1997. Mr. Arnold attended college at Indiana University and earned a Bachelor’s degree in Telecommunications and English in 1992. He attended the Valparaiso University School of Law and earned his Juris Doctor degree in 1997. attorneys.name: Jenna M. Bailey
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jenna concentrates her practice in criminal defense, family law, and civil litigation. She enjoys being in the courtroom and is determined to advocate for her clients. Jenna is a former Marion County deputy prosecuting attorney, specifically from the Special Victims Division. Jenna has significant experience in the courtroom handling both major and minor felonies, as well as misdemeanors. Jenna defends felony and misdemeanor cases, such as drunken driving and drug possession. She also defends higher-class felonies, such as drug dealing and burglary. Jenna advises clients regarding the new Indiana Second Chance Expungement Law, and when appropriate, guides clients through the process to expunge past arrests or convictions.

Jenna represents clients in all areas of family law, including divorce, legal separation, custody, parenting time, child support, paternity, emancipation, post-decree modifications and enforcement (including contempt actions), relocation, education orders, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, protective orders, and restraining orders. Jenna also serves as a Guardian Ad Litem.

attorneys.name: Timothy E Baker
attorneys.firm_name: DeVoss, Baker, Ainsworth & Razo, A Professional Corporation
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning, Estate Administration Lawyers in Decatur, IN
attorneys.bio:
Timothy E. Baker is a 1978 graduate of the Indiana University School of Law, Indianapolis, IN, and was admitted to practice law in the State of Indiana in June of the same year. Upon obtaining his Doctorate of Jurisprudence, he returned to his home town of Decatur, Indiana, to practice law. He joined the DeVoss law firm and has been a member of this prominent firm ever since. Mr. Baker is a 1971 graduate of Bellmont High School and graduated from Purdue University in 1975 where he earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science.

While attending law school, Mr. Baker worked in the Indiana Secretary of State's Office, Corporations Division, Legal Department where he was responsible for reviewing and approving documentation filed for the creation or merger of business entities. In addition, while in law school, Mr. Baker clerked for the DeVoss law firm where he assisted in estate planning and administration, real estate and commercial transactions. Mr., Baker's practice has been concentrated in these areas, in addition to personal injury law and municipal law.

Over the years, Mr. Baker has acquired extensive experience in municipal law. He served as County Attorney for Adams County from 1989 through 1996. He has served as attorney for the Adams County Economic Development Corporation since 1989 and has served as the attorney for the Adams County Solid Waste Management District since 1991. Having served in three mayoral administrations, 2021 marks the fourteenth year he has served as City Attorney for the City of Decatur, Indiana.

Tim firmly believes that as an attorney he has an obligation to give back to his community and help make it a better place in which to live, work and raise a family. He has been actively involved in St, Mary's Parish and St. Joseph School by serving multiple terms on the Parish Pastoral Council and on the St. Joseph School Board. In addition, over the years he has volunteered for numerous Parish projects and has donated legal services to the Parish and School. He supports the United Way and is a past Board member of the Adams County Cancer Society. Likewise, he truly values the deep friendships with everyone at DeVoss, Baker, Ainsworth & Razo who are a second family. The importance of relationships carries over to clients as well.

Mr. Baker enjoys the practice of law because he enjoys the challenge of finding or creating a solution to a problem, resolving a dispute, helping a client through a difficult time or making a client's dream become a reality. He enjoys the practice of law and looks forward to being of service to those who are in need of legal assistance.

Mr. Balczo was born in Northwest Indiana and graduated from Highland High School in 2012. In high school, he was active in Key Club, a community service organization that provided volunteers for beach cleanups and monthly dances for children with disabilities.

Outside of work, Mr. Balczo is an avid reader and enjoys visiting museums. He is the Scholarship Director and Board member of the Highland chapter of Kiwanis International, a community service organization aimed at assisting young people and others in need.

attorneys.name: Christian Baldwin Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fort Wayne, IN
attorneys.bio:
Facing a divorce or family law matter in Fort Wayne, Indiana can be emotionally challenging for everyone involved. The results of these cases can have a significant impact on you and your family. The attorneys at Stange Law Firm know this and work hard to develop a plan to diligently guide you throughout your case. Based in our Fort Wayne, IN office, Christian Baldwin is a Junior Associate Attorney. Licensed to practice law in Indiana, Christian looks forward to helping you get through this difficult time.

Christian attended law school at the Indiana University Maurer School of Law in Bloomington, IN, graduating with his Juris Doctorate in May 2023. While in law school, Christian served as an Associate and then the Managing Editor for the Indiana Journal of Global Legal Studies while earning the Hunt Fellowship academic scholarship. Before law school, he attended Indiana University Kelly School of Business where he graduated with his Bachelor of Science in Business, majoring in Marketing with a minor in Political Science and Human Resource Management.

Before joining the Fort Wayne, Indiana divorce and family lawyers at Stange Law Firm, Christian most recently served as a Certified Legal Intern at the Indiana Attorney General’s Office, drafting legal documents, representing the State in licensing hearings under supervision, and preparing enforcement actions like cease-and-desist letters. Concurrently, during academic breaks and summers, he worked as a Sales Intern at Kirby Risk, where an Excel quote tracking tool was developed, significantly improving sales efficiency. Before this, he interned with Judge Mary DeBoer, conducting legal research on Indiana Trial Rules and adoption petitions while analyzing complex legal documents to support judicial decisions. Christian also previously worked as a Data Processing Associate at The Center for Survey Research, ensuring quality standards for large-scale survey data.

Note: The choice of a lawyer is an important decision and should not be based solely upon advertisements.

attorneys.name: Brad Banks
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Brad has significant experience in the Criminal/DUI legal area. Brad served as a major felony prosecutor in Hamilton County where he tried numerous cases including DUI, burglaries, batteries, drug offenses and many other cases. Brad next served as a major felony prosecutor in Marion County, Indiana. During this time, Brad tried robberies, rape, aggravated batteries, burglaries, and financial crimes.

During his time in Marion County, Brad also spent two years in the Homicide Unit of the Prosecutor’s office. During this time Brad tried 10 homicide juries, achieving successful verdicts on all 10 trials. Next, Brad was promoted to Division Chief. Brad was responsible for supervising 36 attorneys serving in Marion County’s misdemeanor and D Felony courts. Included in this position, Brad supervised the DUI Unit of the Marion County Prosecutor’s Office. Throughout his nearly 10 years as a Prosecutor, Brad maintained a 95% success rate at jury trial.

Prior to serving as a Deputy Prosecutor, Brad worked for a prestigious civil law firm in Valparaiso, Indiana. It was during this time where Brad learned how to effectively, compassionately, and aggressively represent individuals in family law. Brad has handled divorce trials, child custody matters, child support, and property settlements. Brad has a reputation for representing his clients in a manner that is attentive to their needs and goals while assuring their rights are protected.

Brad was born and raised in Marion, Indiana. Brad and his family reside in Fishers, Indiana. Brad is a very active member of the Fishers community and is a dedicated volunteer serving as the Rec. Director for the Fishers Soccer Club.

attorneys.name: Beth A. Barnes
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Beth A. Barnes focuses her practice exclusively in the area of family law. She made the transition to family law in May 2016 after spending six years in civil litigation that comprised of family law, insurance defense, personal injury, collections, and bankruptcy. Beth represents clients with all types of family law issues including: divorce and legal separation; custody; parenting time (visitation); child support; paternity; prenuptial and postnuptial agreements; post-decree modification and enforcement; contempt actions; guardianships; emancipation; relocations; adoptions; protective orders; and Guardian Ad Litem work. Beth represents clients at both the trial and appellate level. Beth has been named a "Rising Star" by Indianapolis Monthly Super Lawyers magazine for 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, and 2022, and was selected to Super Lawyers in 2025.

Beth received her Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice and Criminology in 2003 from Ball State University. She earned her Juris Doctorate from Indiana University School of Law-Indianapolis in December 2009 where she was a member of the Appellate Clinic, Indiana Health Law Review, Order of the Barristers in the Stanton Intramural Moot Court Competition, and served as the Secretary and member of the Indianapolis Bar Association Law Student Division Board.

Beth joined Cross Glazier Reed Burroughs, P.C. in May 2016. She was admitted to practice in the State of Indiana on May 17, 2010, as well as, both the Northern and Southern District Federal Courts of Indiana. Beth is a member of the American Bar Association, Indiana State Bar Association, and Indianapolis Bar Association.

When not working, Beth spends her time raising her three children, being an active member of her church, traveling with friends and family, returning to the family farm, attending sporting events, cooking, baking and spending time with her family and pets.

attorneys.name: Christian Bartholomew
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Hammond, IN
attorneys.bio:
Christian is a recent transplant to Northwestern Indiana and the newest associate at Efron, Efron & Yahne. He grew up in central Indiana, near Marion, and is thus quite familiar with soybeans and cornfields. A 1999 graduate of Oak Hill High School, he went on to study at Ball State University, where he triple-majored in English, German and Philosophy. After graduating from Ball State in 2003, Christian went on to study at Indiana University's Maurer School of Law and at IU's School of Public and Environmental Affairs in Bloomington. While there, he was an active participant in the Sherman Minton Moot Court Competition, finishing as a Quarterfinalist and serving on the moot court board. He was also an Articles Editor for the Indiana Journal of Global Legal Studies. Never one to shy from adventure, Christian completed his first legal internship with a small law firm in western Africa, where he learned that traditional lawyers' white wigs and black robes might easily mix with dusty courtyards filled with errant chickens and goats. A continuing interest in German culture and European issues led Christian to serve as IU Law's first exchange student to the Friedrich-Schiller University in Jena, Germany, where he spent a semester. Before graduating from Indiana University, he also spent three months as an intern with the Monroe County Prosecutor's Office, gaining experience in both the juvenile and traffic courts and building his familiarity with criminal law.

After graduating law school in 2008, Christian completed both the Indiana and Illinois bar examinations, and immediately prior to joining Efron, Efron & Yahne, he served as an intern at the Indiana Department of Homeland Security, researching privacy issues, legal issues in emergency management, and sensitive-but-unclassified information. He was also afforded the opportunity to shadow one of Grant County's Superior Court Judges, gaining behind-the-bench insights into small-claims and criminal law matters.

In his free time, Christian enjoys reading, learning languages, and travel. He has also been known to make attempts at playing the guitar and piano.

attorneys.name: Todd C. Barsumian
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Newburgh, IN
attorneys.bio:
Todd is a member of Barsumian Armiger Injury Lawyers. He started his legal career at a large corporate and insurance firm in Evansville, Indiana where he was a litigation partner often hired to defend claims brought by the injured, including several cases that made it to the Indiana Supreme Court. However, Todd now only represents persons who have been seriously injured or the families of those who have suffered a wrongful death. Since 2000, Todd has also been licensed in Kentucky, where he has handled cases from trial courts up to the Kentucky Supreme Court. Todd has tried multiple jury trials to verdict in state and federal court in Indiana and Kentucky.

In addition to being selected as a Top 100 Attorney in Indiana by the National Trial Lawyers Association, Todd has been AV-Preeminent rated by his peers as recognized by Martindale- Hubbell, which is considered the highest rating of professional excellence. Todd has also been selected by Super Lawyers as an Indiana Super Lawyer in the field of Personal Injury Law since 2018. Super Lawyers had previously named him a Rising Star in the areas of Personal Injury and Business Litigation. Todd was selected to The National Trial Lawyers Association: Top 40 under 40 and a "Top 100 Civil Plaintiff's Attorney" in the State of Indiana. Todd has also received a 10 out of 10 rating from Avvo.

attorneys.name: Andrew Barton
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
An Indianapolis native and graduate of the Indiana University McKinney School of Law, Andrew brings a refined and highly specialized skillset to Doyle Family Law. Before transitioning to family law, he spent nearly a decade in personal injury litigation at a Fortune 500 insurance company, where he mastered issue spotting, evidence analysis, negotiating with difficult parties, and developing strategic case resolutions. His exceptional performance earned him multiple internal awards recognizing his attention to detail, professionalism, and consistent results.

At Doyle Family Law, Andrew leverages this experience to handle some of the firm’s most complex matters, including high-asset divorces, business valuations, and cases involving extensive financial records or complicated data. His meticulous approach ensures every case is organized, strategically developed, and presented with precision, whether in negotiations or the courtroom.

During law school, Andrew distinguished himself as a Barrister in Moot Court and laid the foundation for his strong advocacy skills. He remains committed to the legal profession as an active member of the Indianapolis Bar Association, staying current with developments in family law and consistently refining his practice.

Outside of work, Andrew enjoys the finer things in life—whether that’s exploring great restaurants, appreciating good craftsmanship, or spending quality time with friends and family. His thoughtful nature, sharp legal mind, and commitment to excellence make him a trusted advocate for clients facing life’s most complex and personal legal challenges.

attorneys.name: Carrie L. Batalon
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Carrie is a partner at Mallor Grodner Plummer Attorneys. Her primary area of practice is family law, including divorce, post-divorce modification, child custody and support issues, premarital and post-marital agreements, adoptions, guardianships, jurisdictional/interstate issues, and paternity matters. Carrie has been a Certified Family Law Specialist, by the Family Law Certification Board, since 2011.

Carrie offers her clients the full range of legal process options. She appreciates that legal process, particularly related to the family, is frightening and stressful for the participants and believes that a good understanding of the process, the applicable law and what to expect diminishes the stress factor. As such, Carrie provides her clients with understanding of their options based on realistic expectations and compassionately addresses the sensitive aspects of each case.

As a seasoned trial attorney, Carrie provides strong advocacy for her clients in traditional divorce and post-divorce conflicts, including high asset and high conflict cases, when amicable resolution cannot be achieved. She is also a skilled and resourceful negotiator, guiding her clients through alternative dispute resolution processes including mediation and Collaborative Divorce. In addition to Carrie's comprehensive practice of family law, she continues to represent clients in civil litigation and landlord/tenant law.

A graduate of Bloomington High School South, Carrie is a long-term and active member of the community. She has previously served on the Board of Directors for the Monroe County Chapter of the American Red Cross and as a volunteer with the Girl Scouts of Central Indiana. Carrie presently serves on the Family Law Certification Board and the Family Law Council for the Family Law Section of the Indiana State Bar Association. She is also a volunteer attorney for Counsel in the Court and the Maurer School of Law Protective Order Project.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Rob Beatson was born and raised near Boston, Massachusetts. After earning a bachelor’s degree from Fordham University in New York City, he officially became a Hoosier while attending Indiana University Maurer School of Law, where he graduated with honors in 2013.

For 12 years, Rob served as a Deputy Prosecutor in Marion County, where he conducted over 50 major felony jury trials for crimes including murder, robbery, and narcotics and firearms offenses. He also worked on complex legal issues such as death penalty cases, insanity defenses, and electronic searches and seizures and provided training to law enforcement agencies, community organizations, and schools. Rob lives on the northeast side of Indianapolis with his wife and three children. While he’s now a proud Hoosier, he remains a die-hard Red Sox and Patriots fan.

attorneys.name: Robert H. Bellinger II
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fort Wayne, IN
attorneys.bio:
My mission statement is a basic one -- provide the best customer service anytime, anyplace.

Let me introduce myself:

I grew up in eastern Whitley County, graduated from Columbia City High School and went on to graduate from IPFW and Thomas M. Cooley Law School. I always liked school because I enjoyed learning new things.

Unlike many attorneys I have actually "seen the inside of a courtroom" and I have much jury trial experience.

I am also the chairman and co-founder of the American Unity Party. The AUP is an independent, and therefore non-partisan, party designed to cater to the interests of the shrinking middle-class.

Lastly, I believe that religious training and participation in volunteer activities are important to the communities in which we live. I have participated in volunteer programs that are too numerous to list and I am active with the First Church of God in Columbia City.

When my office was founded I decided to base it upon principles that you wouldn't expect from other law firms. I believe in providing the best customer service through "bread-basket advocacy" -- period! To me customer service means being accessible, meeting with a real lawyer -- not a paralegal, listening more than talking, being knowledgeable, showing empathy, and possessing a friendly and outgoing personality. By bread-basket advocacy I mean finding a voice for the common middle class of citizens like you and I who make up the pulse of our communities.

It is vitally important that the bread-basket have a voice and that it be heard. The legal system is not designed for the very wealthy or the very poor. My office caters to the grassroots of the community by providing legal services that address and solve everyday concerns that are important to the individual, rather than "wining and dining" high profile clients.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Hammond, IN
attorneys.bio:
Nicole A. Bennett is a partner and owner of Westland & Bennett P.C., with her husband, Dave. "I am honored to work every day alongside the smartest person I've ever known - even though he doesn't believe me"

Nicole grew up on the west side of Lansing, Michigan, in the small town of Potterville, aka "Gizzard City." Nicole knew she wanted to be an attorney when she was 13. This goal led Nicole to Alma College in Alma, Michigan where she graduated cum laude in 1994, having earned her bachelor's degree in 3 years.

Nicole then moved to NWI to attend Valparaiso University School of Law, only to be seriously injured in a head-on automobile collision and forced to withdraw from law school during her second semester. Nicole fought to return to law school the next year and she graduated in 1997, just 4 months behind her law school class. Nicole is straight-forward and committed and she gives this same dedication to her clients.

Nicole spent the first 6 years of her career as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney at the Office of the Lake County Prosecuting Attorney in Crown Point, Indiana. In 2004, she went into private practice where she furthers her desire to help people.

attorneys.bio:
Brooke Bernhardt is a founding partner of Bernhardt Phillips, LLP, and an experienced family law attorney. Prior to starting the firm, Brooke worked for a prominent family law firm in Indianapolis where she developed and refined her skills as a family law litigator and negotiator.

Known for her ability to efficiently and effectively resolve a wide array of family law issues, Brooke competently handles matters in Indianapolis and all over the State of Indiana. Regardless of where your case is in Indiana, Brooke will be able to represent you. Clients often turn to Brooke for adoptions, child support issues, child custody matters, contempt actions, divorces, guardianships, grandparent visitation cases, modifications, name changes, paternity cases, parenting time issues, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, relocations, spousal maintenance, third-party custody, step-parent adoptions, step-parent visitation matters, and other matters involving family members or children.

Brooke is both a highly skilled negotiator and litigator, who uses her innate creativity to develop unique solutions to achieve her clients’ desired results. Brooke always strives to reduce conflict and amicably resolve a matter whenever possible. As an accomplished negotiator Brooke develops smart and creative strategies to resolve matters without the cost and expense of litigation. However, if an agreement cannot be reached, then Brooke is prepared to advocate zealously for her clients’ interests in the courtroom. Brooke’s talent and skill in the courtroom were developed by litigating countless family law matters throughout the State of Indiana. Her knowledge and experience will help ease your concerns and ensure your interests are protected.

attorneys.name: Kevin W. Betz
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Kevin W. Betz has tried more than 20 jury trials, bench trials or arbitrations in his more than 25 years of trial work. Kevin has won jury verdicts in individual rights cases of more than $300,000 in Marion County and $600,000 in Shelby County as well as a $3.1 million verdict in the federal district court for the Southern District of Indiana. These were each considered ground-breaking verdicts in unique cases with novel claims. Besides other successful federal court trials, Kevin has also tried cases to juries in Delaware, Hamilton, Hendricks and Johnson counties in Indiana.

In 2010 Kevin earned certification from the National Board of Trial Advocacy and is now recognized as a Board Certified Trial Attorney based on his skills and experience. In addition, in May of 2012 he also earned certification from the National Board of Trial Advocacy in Civil Pretrial Practice. He has been a master lawyer in the Sagamore American Inns of Court since 1998 (now emeritus); member of the National Employment Lawyers Association; and a founding board member of the Indiana Hemophilia & Thrombosis Center, one of the largest such centers in the country providing more than $1.5 million in free medical services to Hoosiers every year; and is an appointed member of the Indiana Supreme Court's Committee on Character and Fitness to practice law in Indiana since 1998. As well, the International Network of Boutique Law Firms (INBLF) selected his firm as its Indiana individual rights representative.

To begin his career, Kevin served for two years as a law clerk for the Chief Justice of the Indiana Supreme Court, Randall T. Shepard, and then practiced for five years in the litigation department at Krieg DeVault. As an appointment by the governor, he next served as the Chief Counsel for the Indiana Department of Environmental Management during the Evan Bayh and the Frank O'Bannon administrations, overseeing more than 20 attorneys and the litigation and enforcement divisions for an entire state agency. Betz + Blevins now has five attorneys and two paralegals and since 1997 has had a successful trial and litigation practice primarily on behalf of individuals and small businesses. He has also been selected on multiple occasions as a Super Lawyer in Indiana.

In 1993, Kevin created and was President of The Lawyers Bar Review, a biannual six-week preparatory course for bar candidates seeking to pass the Indiana Bar Exam. A national bar review purchased The Lawyers Bar Review in 1998. Besides serving as editor of the materials covering 26 areas of Indiana and federal law, Kevin lectured in the areas of contracts and techniques and tactics for bar exam testing. He is also regularly selected as a lecturer for Indiana and national continuing legal education programs, including a conference regarding discrimination and bullying at Yale University in 2012.

Mr. Betz was also the creator and lead author from 1990-2002 of a law review article that analyzes the Indiana Supreme Court's docket, dispositions, and voting. It is published annually in the Indiana Law Review, see, e.g., An Examination of the Indiana Supreme Court Docket, Dispositions, and Voting, 35 Indiana Law Review 1117 (2002).

Mr. Betz's undergraduate degrees are from Indiana University in journalism and political science in 1982. He also earned a master's degree from Northwestern University in 1984. During law school, he was a law clerk from 1986 to 1988 for The Honorable Marc R. Kellams, a state trial court judge in Monroe County, Indiana.

attorneys.name: P. Lynn Bibbs
attorneys.firm_name: P. Lynn Bibbs, Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
In 1985 P. Lynn Bibbs was commissioned in the Judge Advocate General's Corps (JAG) as a Captain in the United States Army where she served as both a Prosecutor at Schofield Barracks, Hawaii and a Senior Defense Counsel at Fort Jackson, South Carolina. While serving as Senior Defense Counsel and during Desert Storm, Ms. Bibbs was awarded the Meritorious Service Medal for her performance as a JAG Officer and for her professionalism.

In February 1992, Ms. Bibbs came to Indianapolis to serve as a Marion County Deputy Prosecutor for the Marion County Prosecutor's Office. She worked in two special divisions. First, the Metro Gang Task Force, and in 1993 she moved to the Sex Crimes Division. In 1994, she was assigned special victims cases which included the Central State Closing and the Condom Rapist case (a serial rapist with between 8 -12 suspected victims).

Ms. Bibbs left the Marion County Prosecutor's Office in 1995 and has practiced in Criminal Defense since that time. In the summer of 1995, she traveled to South Bend, Indiana, to work on the Capital case of State v. Ajabu. While there Ms. Bibbs presented the defense of Post Traumatic Stress Syndrome for Kofi Ajabu with an expert witness. Kofi did not receive the Death Penalty in that triple murder case.

In the past 25 years, Ms. Bibbs has litigated just about every type of criminal case from the violent murder case to the white collar crime. She has received acquittals (verdicts of not guilty) in front of juries and judges.

As recently as October 21, 2009, in a 13 charge white collar crime case, Ms. Bibbs' client was charged with conspiracy to defraud financial institutions, mortgage fraud, and the Indianapolis Housing Agency. Ms. Bibbs together with her co-counsel Rick Kammen, who represented a co-defendant, won a Suppression hearing, where they showed that the Police received an unconstitutional search warrant. The State had to dismiss all 13 charges against their clients.

Ms. Bibbs remains thorough and professional since the days of her JAG officer training. She is the type of attorney that will leave no stone unturned and no plausible theory undeveloped. She is the type of attorney you want on your side.

attorneys.bio:
Matt was the second of five children in the house and learned from a young age to independent and that he would have to work for anything he wanted. While at McKinney, Matt interned with the Indiana State Senate minority counsel's office and with the Marion County Prosecutor's office where he was assigned to the Sex Crimes Division.

After being admitted to the Bar in 2010, Matt began his career as a deputy prosecutor in Warrick County, Indiana where he prosecuted various misdemeanor and felony offenses. He stayed in Warrick Co. for eight months until he was able to return to Indianapolis and take a position with the Marion Co. Prosecutor's Office. Over his five years with the Marion County Prosecutor's Office, Matt spent the majority of his time prosecuting OVWI cases. His final two years as a deputy prosecutor were as the Fatal Alcohol Crash Team prosecutor. As the FACT prosecutor, Matt was the sole deputy prosecutor responsible for prosecuting all fatal traffic crashes in Indianapolis. Matt was involved in cases from their investigation at the scene of the crash all the way to sentencing In addition to dozens of jury trials before he was the FACT prosecutor, Matt was able to take ten FACT cases to jury trial and see that the victims of these crimes received justice. Five years in a very specific and specialized area of law has also given Matt a strong background in the pharmacology and toxicology of alcohol and controlled substances, crash reconstruction, and the fundamentals of how law enforcement agencies investigate these cases. Matt was able to see firsthand the devastating effects of motor vehicle accidents and how the families of the victims struggle for it all to make sense. When deciding to leave the prosecutor's office, Matt wanted to apply what he had learned and continue to help those harmed by another's poor decisions or negligence.

Matt lives in Indianapolis with his wife, Sarah, and his two children, Eloise and Archie. He enjoys doing projects around his house and spending time with his family. He is licensed to practice before the Indiana Supreme Court as well as the Northern and Southern Districts of the United States District Courts of Indiana.

attorneys.bio:
Named as an Indiana Super Lawyer in the area of litigation since 2004, Michael concentrates his practice in the areas of mediation, arbitration, probate and trust litigation, and civil litigation. He is recognized by Best Lawyers in America in Alternate Dispute Resolution and Arbitration and Trust and Estate Litigation since 2006. In 2008 he was selected as a Member of the American Arbitration Association National Roster of Neutrals and serves on its Large Complex Case Panel. Michael has an AV Peer Rating from Martindale-Hubbell.

Michael received his Juris Doctorate from Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in 1980. Following graduation he served as Law Clerk to the Honorable James E. Noland, United States District Court, Southern District of Indiana. Michael is a Fellow>of the International Academy of Mediators, a Fellow of the American College of Civil Trial Mediators, Fellow of the National Academy of Distinguished Neutrals, Master Fellow of the Indiana Bar Foundation, and a Distinguished Fellow of the Indianapolis Bar Association.

Mr. Bishop is the Author of "Civil Mediation" Indiana Alternative Dispute Resolution Practice Guide, a member of the faculty of the Indiana Trial Advocacy College and is ICLEF's Primary Trainer for Continuing Mediation Training for Civil Trial Mediators in Indiana. Michael is past Chair of the Litigation Section of the Indianapolis Bar Association and a founding member of the IBA Settlement Week. He served as Secretary to the Board of Governors for the Indiana State Bar Association, was Chair of the ISBA ADR Section, was a District Representative on the ISBA Board of Governors, a member of the Board of Directors for Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum, and is Past President to the Board of Directors for the Indiana Bar Foundation. Michael is also past President of the Sagamore American Inn of Court, where he continues to serve as one of the founding Benchers of the Inn. He is a member of the Board of Visitors for the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law.

attorneys.name: Leo T. Blackwell
attorneys.firm_name: Ruckelshaus Kautzman Blackwell Bemis & Duncan, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Police & Fire Representation Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Leo T. Blackwell is a lifelong resident of Indianapolis and attended Bishop Chatard High School. While working as an Indianapolis police officer, Leo completed his Bachelor of Science degree at Indiana University-Purdue University at Indianapolis, graduating in 1976. He was awarded his Doctor of Jurisprudence from Indiana University McKinney School of Law in 1984 and was admitted to the Bar in 1985.

While a member of the Indianapolis Police Department, Leo was assigned to the Operations Task Force and the Traffic and Investigative Divisions. He also served as a motorcycle officer and a member of the prestigious IPD Motorcycle Drill Team.

In 1986, Leo was elected president of the Indianapolis Fraternal Order of Police Lodge #86. He represented the 1,200 member union until his retirement from the Indianapolis Police Department in 1991. Following his retirement from the IPD, Leo joined the Ruckelshaus Kautzman Blackwell Bemis Duncan & Merchant, LLP becoming a partner in 1994. He has dedicated his legal career to the representation and protection of public safety officers in personal and professional matters including legal defense, legislative, and collective bargaining agreements.

In August, 2021 Leo was awarded the first ever National Fraternal Order of Police Attorney Lifetime Achievement Award. This prestigious award was presented at the 2021 National FOP Conference in Indianapolis, Indiana which is attended by FOP leaders from across the United States. Leo was joined by his family and members of his law firm on stage in the surprise presentation. Leo's dedication to the men and women of public safety has spanned decades. He has positively impacted the lives of law enforcement around the state of Indiana and the country through his zealous advocacy.

attorneys.name: Gregory Karyl Blanford
attorneys.practice_type: Family Lawyers in South Bend, IN
attorneys.bio:
I have many responsibilities to my clients, but there are two I place right at the top.

My first responsibility is to make sure you have the information and resources you need in order to make knowledgeable, well-reasoned, and well-informed decisions.

This is more than simply telling you what the law is. And it's certainly more than saying "that's just the way it's done." It's an obligation to explain things to you: the process; the alternatives; consequences, benefits and costs. It's a promise to discuss with you the practical effects of our decisions or the positions we want to maintain.

My second responsibility to you is candor. A commitment to be straightforward; to have frank and honest conversation with you about your legal matter. I will always tell you what you need to know - whether it's what you want to hear or not - because anything short of that does you no favors.

The reason I consider the above responsibilities to be my most important to you is because they are critical to your meaningful participation in the resolution of your own legal matter. While I may have the legal experience and knowledge to assist you in your matter, I cannot, and will not presume to know what's best for you or your family. You're the only person that can make that decision. And making the best one requires that you have as complete an understanding of your legal circumstances and options as is reasonably possible.

Erin Borcherding Bauer grew up in Posey County where she attended North Posey High School. She attended the University of Southern Indiana and majored in History with a minor in Anthropology. Upon graduation from law school, Erin returned to Evansville and became an associate attorney at Barber & Shoulders, LLP. In 2011, she became partner of Barber & Bauer, LLP. She has a general practice and regularly handles cases in the areas of employment law, Social Security Disability, short-term and long-term disability, family law, personal injury, estate planning, general litigation, and appeals. She has successfully tried jury trials and argued in the Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit. She has published opinions from both the Indiana Court of Appeals and the Seventh Circuit. She has been named as an Indiana Super Lawyer Rising Star and Indiana Super Lawyer. She has served on the Evansville Bar Association (“EBA”) Board of Directors for six years and as President of the EBA.

attorneys.name: Erin C. Borissov
attorneys.firm_name: Parr Richey Frandsen Patterson Kruse LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Regulatory law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Borissov focuses on infrastructure in Indiana. She represents energy, communications, and infrastructure companies in a variety of practice areas including regulatory law, cooperative law, carbon capture and sequestration and CO2 pipeline law, labor and employment matters, real estate, right-of-way acquisition, commercial transactions, and corporate compliance. In addition, Ms. Borissov works extensively with corporate boards to cultivate sound governance practices, improve decision-making methods, navigate evolving industry trends, prioritize corporate compliance, and identify and manage risk. Areas of concentration include:

Understanding Indiana’s laws on carbon capture and sequestration (CCS) and carbon dioxide pipelines and advising clients on how to navigate those untested laws.

Assisting energy clients as they develop renewable and clean energy projects and providing solutions when third party projects intersect with existing infrastructure.

Supporting electric cooperatives and broadband companies as they expand fiber infrastructure and broadband service to unserved rural areas in Indiana.

Navigating grant and loan programs funded under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), Broadband Equity Access and Deployment Program (BEAD), and other federal and state funding programs.

Recognizing the interplay of Section 45 investment and production tax credits with project finance and construction and helping clients comply with prevailing wage, apprenticeship, community benefits plan, and domestic content requirements to ensure maximum loan and grant funding eligibility and Section 45 tax credit realization.

Collaborating with new large energy consumers (“Megaloads”) to craft customized solutions to meet unprecedented energy and infrastructure needs.

Ms. Borissov began her professional career as a consultant, working with utilities on rate design, cost of service studies, and rate case filings. In addition, before attending law school, she gained valuable regulatory experience as a public utility analyst with the Arizona Corporation Commission.

As an attorney, Ms. Borissov has served in the role of outside counsel with Parr Richey and in-house counsel with NiSource, Inc., a large investor-owned utility company. While in-house, she concentrated on regulatory and business matters including rate cases, financing cases, regulatory compliance, infrastructure investment decisions, and customer complaints.

Through her experience as a consultant and as an attorney, Ms. Borissov honed a deep understanding of corporate business functions, industry trends, and a client’s position in its industry. Ms. Borissov leverages her substantial technical and business experience to understand complex governance, economic, financial, and accounting issues that affect her clients. Ms. Borissov serves as a trusted business advisor by creating valued business partnerships with clients and external stakeholders, proactively identifying opportunities for the client, and maintaining a firm understanding of her clients’ business and political drivers.

attorneys.name: Kevin M. Bowen
attorneys.practice_type: Transportation Accidents Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Kevin M. Bowen is the founding attorney of KMB Legal, a litigation-driven personal injury law firm based in Indiana. With over a decade of courtroom experience, Kevin is known for his relentless advocacy on behalf of clients who have suffered life-changing injuries due to the negligence of others. He prepares every case as though it will go to trial, a reputation that not only earns the respect of his clients—but also the attention of defense firms and insurance carriers across the state.

Kevin’s approach is hands-on and client-focused. He guides injured individuals and their families through every stage of the legal process with clarity, compassion, and constant communication. Whether by text, call, or in-person meeting, Kevin ensures clients never feel left in the dark.

He is especially skilled in high-stakes cases involving catastrophic injury, wrongful death, transportation accidents, and complex premises liability claims. With a foundation built on thorough case preparation and courtroom excellence, Kevin has secured numerous life- changing settlements and verdicts throughout Indiana.

Kevin earned his Bachelor’s degree from Indiana University Bloomington in 2009 and his Juris Doctor from the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis in 2013. He is admitted to practice in all Indiana state courts, as well as the U.S. District Courts for both the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana.

He is a certified civil mediator and has completed advanced litigation training through the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association’s Trial Advocacy College. Kevin has been recognized as a Super Lawyers Rising Star for over a decade and was named a Super Lawyer in 2025. He currently serves as Secretary of the Indiana State Bar Association’s General Practice Section and has held past leadership roles in the Boone County Bar Association (President, 2019 and 2020) and the Solo & Small Firm Section of the ISBA.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney Blake Bower has accumulated an impressive list of credentials as an Indiana Civil Litigator focusing on the legal areas of business, utility, construction, family, contract law and more. Serving clients throughout the state of Indiana, Blake brings enthusiasm and knowledge to his clients’ cases and works to find creative legal solutions to their problems.

Meet Attorney Blake Bower

Blake is licensed to practice law in the states of Indiana and Michigan. While attending Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law and after graduating law school, Blake has had very diverse legal experience. He has worked as a legal intern in Marion County Office of Corporation Counsel, a law clerk in a national firm that focuses on employment law, and a law clerk in a small medical malpractice firm and served as a judicial intern for Honorable Judge Mark Stoner of Marion Superior Court, Major Felony Division. After passing the Indiana bar exam, Blake served as a law clerk for the Honorable Judge David Dreyer of Marion Superior Court, Civil Division.

In 2024 and 2025, Blake was named to the Indiana Super Lawyers® Rising Stars® list. This recognition is based on peer evaluation and fewer than 2.5 percent of lawyers in a state are named to the list each year.

An Experienced Indianapolis Civil Litigator

Blake Bower is a skilled litigator. Prior to joining Camden & Meridew, P.C., he worked as lead staff attorney for the Indiana Department of Child Services (DCS) in Marion County for more than three years. In that position, Blake was specially chosen to serve as a member on DCS’ Litigation Advisory Council as a representative of the Marion County DCS Regional Division. While at DCS, Blake successfully tried more than a dozen child in need of services and termination of parental rights cases to adjudication or judgment.

Indiana Utility Law, Business Law, and More

attorneys.name: Kaelyn Bowman
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Kaelyn was born and raised outside of Peoria, Illinois. She attended Indiana State University in Terre Haute and earned a Bachelor of Science Degree in Criminology and Criminal Justice and minored in Psychology and International Studies. Kaelyn has always dreamt of becoming a lawyer since she toured a courthouse at the young age of 13. In 2020, after being a paralegal for a divorce law firm for 1.5 years, Kaelyn decided to pursue her dream of becoming a lawyer. She moved back to Indiana and attended Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law, where she published an article in Volume XXI of the Indiana Health Law Review and received the Civil and Human Rights Law Graduate Certificate upon graduation in December 2023.

After graduating, Kaelyn continued her legal career by becoming a Deputy Prosecutor in Marion County where she helped establish, enforce, and modify child support cases. Her experience assisting unrepresented individuals who faced emotional and difficult situations has helped her understand the importance of empathy, patience, and communication. Today, Kaelyn is passionate about fiercely advocating for those who have been wrongly injured and serving her community.

Kaelyn is an active member and in good standing with the Indianapolis Bar Association and Indiana State Bar Association. She resides in Greenwood, Indiana and enjoys being a mother, making memories with her family and friends, traveling, trying new things, and spending time outdoors.

attorneys.bio:
Tom Bowman joined Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP, in June 2017, as an associate and became a partner in 2023. Previously, he worked in an insurance defense practice in northwest Indiana and then for three years at a general practice law firm in Logan, Utah, representing both individuals and businesses in various matters. Originally from Shelbyville, Indiana, he graduated cum laude from Wabash College in 2009 with a major in history. While at Wabash, Tom was a member of the Phi Gamma Delta (FIJI) fraternity and studied abroad for a semester in Perugia, Italy. He also worked as a research assistant and served as a pro bono extern for Magistrate Judge Calabrese of the Starke County Circuit Court.

Tom resides in Greenfield with his wife, Michelle, son, Logan, and their dog, Reggie. In his spare time, Tom enjoys watching sports (Go Dawgs!), traveling, and attempting to make meals he sees on cooking shows.

He is a current board member of the Hancock County Chamber of Commerce and a member of the Rotary Club of Greenfield.

attorneys.name: Seamus P. Boyce
attorneys.practice_type: Education Lawyers in Noblesville, IN
attorneys.bio:
Séamus (pronounced shay-mus) P. Boyce has a general law practice with the firm of Church, Church, Hittle & Antrim and often represents clients in matters involving education, schools, or intellectual property.

He has been admitted to practice law in Indiana and has served as a member on the Board of Governors for the Indiana State Bar Association. His professional association memberships include the Education Law Association ("ELA"), Hamilton County Bar Association, Indiana School Boards Association, Indiana State Bar Association, Indianapolis Bar Association, and National School Boards Association ("NSBA"). He is a frequent speaker and contributor for organizations including the American Association of School Administrators ("AASA"), ELA, Indiana School Boards Association, Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum ("ICLEF"), Lorman Education Services, National Business Institute, and NSBA. Séamus drafted the briefs on behalf of the NSBA and AASA in the matter of Safford v. Redding before the Supreme Court of the United States.

Séamus graduated from Wabash College and currently serves on the Board of the Indianapolis Association of Wabash Men. During his time at Wabash, he was a member of the Sphinx Club, Sigma Chi Fraternity and Rugby Club. He also participated in an off-campus study program at the National University of Ireland, Maynooth. After Wabash, Séamus attended the University of New Hampshire School of Law where he earned both a law degree and a masters in education law. During his time at New Hampshire, Séamus received an Albert Schweitzer Fellowship which he used to create a mentoring program for special education students. In addition, he competed in moot court at the College of William & Mary. Before graduating from New Hampshire, he received the American Bar Association and American Law Institute Award for the graduating student who best demonstrates both scholarship and leadership.

Séamus was born and raised in Indiana and currently resides in Fishers with his wife, Erin, who is a school teacher for special needs students. He enjoys spending time with his eight siblings and being actively involved in his community including assisting with the Indiana Bar Foundation sponsored We The People competition and the Indiana State Bar Association's Clients Financial Assistance Fund.

His inspirational life and powerful example of faith through service to others has left an indelible mark on all of us as well as our firm and helps define our mission.

attorneys.name: Kamryn Bridges
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Kamryn Bridges is an attorney whose primary area of practice is family law. She understands that family law isn’t just about legal issues – it’s about people, relationships, and finding stability during times of change. Kamryn’s goal is to help clients navigate transitions with dignity while providing steady, strategic advocacy every step of the way.

Kamryn began working with Mallor Grodner Plummer as a law clerk in 2024, where she developed a deep appreciation for the impact family law can have on clients’ lives. As an attorney, she continues to learn from and collaborate with some of the most respected family law attorneys in the field – colleagues at Mallor Grodner Plummer whose insight and mentorship shape her practice today.

She earned her J.D. from the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in 2025. She is also a proud Purdue Boilermaker, graduating in 2022 with degrees of Highest Distinction in Psychology and Political Science. Her background in psychology gives her a unique understanding of the emotional and behavioral dynamics that often arise during divorce and custody matters. She recognizes the profound impact these experiences can have on both parents and children, and she approaches every case with compassion, balance, and a focus on long-term family well-being.

Kamryn enjoys giving back to her community through her volunteer work with 4-H, where she helps support programs that inspire responsibility and growth. In her downtime, she loves being outdoors, spending time with family and friends, and never turns down the chance to see live music.

attorneys.name: BJ Brinkerhoff
attorneys.practice_type: Business Disputes Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
BJ offers clients a wealth of experience on a wide variety of business advice and litigation matters, representing individuals, closely-held companies and multi-national corporations with many of their legal and entrepreneurial needs.

He focuses his practice on business disputes, including employment matters such as restrictive covenants and trade secrets, as well as shareholder claims, director and officer liability and day-to-day business disputes. BJ also manages product liability matters, wrongful death and catastrophic injury defense, restaurant and retail liability, civil rights matters, contract disputes, insurance matters, personal injury and appeals.

Indiana has a vibrant startup community and BJ has been at the forefront, alongside his clients, working with entrepreneurs to address their unique concerns and challenges. BJ counsels small business owners and entrepreneurs to guide them through their legal issues including: negotiation of real estate disputes; franchising and intellectual property matters; issues between partners and founders and counseling business owners on how to avoid legal risks.

BJ also represents clients at all phases of litigation, such as initial post-loss investigation (including immediate response examinations and inspections), alternative dispute resolution, bench and jury trials and appeals. BJ brings a unique perspective to client’s disputes — he understands business, he understands litigation and most of all, he brings calm, thoughtful guidance to achieve outcomes that satisfy his clients’ goals.

Often times, the risks and costs of litigation can be intimidating, especially considering the uncertainty of how lawsuits will proceed. Applying the benefits of his litigation experience, BJ seeks to collaborate with clients and their in-house counsel, employees, insurers and others to minimize those risks and maximize his clients’ potential outcomes at each step along the way. Most importantly, BJ strives to work with those same clients to evaluate and develop methods to reduce the risk of future litigation.
