attorneys.name: Katie Ellen Brinkmeyer
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Income Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
My drive to assist persons with disabilities began with my close personal experiences with both friends and family members suffering from debilitating impairments. Seeing their issues upfront helped me better understand their numerous obstacles and internalize their struggles getting the care they deserved.

Upon graduating from law school, I began working for a small personal injury firm in Carmel, Indiana, and I grew their Social Security Disability and Workers Compensation departments. After a few years of representing Social Security claimants, I left the private sector to serve as an attorney advisor for the Social Security Administration's Office of Hearing Operations. As an attorney advisory, I worked closely with the Administrative Law Judges ("ALJs") to write timely and legally defensible draft decisions pursuant ALJ instructions covering a wide range of issues, procedural and substantive, in the determination of disability for Title II and Title XVI claims, including cases remanded by the Seventh Circuit and Federal District Courts. This tremendous experience bestowed me with immense knowledge of the Social Security Disability Regulations and Rulings, as well as an in-depth understanding of the clockwork behind each step in the disability evaluation process.

One of the major issues I observed in Social Security was that many disabled claimants with complex issues are not able to find the specialized level of representation that their case necessitated and knew that I could help.

I joined the Law Office of Annette Rutkowski LLC in July 2021, so that I could pursue my passion on a more personal level and work directly with disabled individuals in need of Social Security Disability Benefits. attorneys.name: Anne
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce & Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Anne-Marie Briscoe is an attorney at Hollingsworth Law Group, LLC. Since 2008, Anne-Marie has been working alongside founding partner, Kena Hollingsworth, in her mission to find a healthier way to divorce. Anne-Marie’s practice is 100% focused on divorce and family law. Anne-Marie was one of the earliest inspirations for the firm’s commitment to Divorce Done Differently. Her practice areas include divorce, legal separation, custody, parenting time/visitation, child support, paternity, step-parent adoptions, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, post-decree modifications and enforcements, spousal maintenance/alimony, guardianships, emancipations, relocations, protective orders, grandparent rights, and military divorces, to name a few.

What Makes Her Uniquely Qualified?

When it comes to shielding her clients from the stress and nerve-wracking effects of family law cases, such as divorce, Anne-Marie Briscoe is determined and steadfast. Named to the Super Lawyers® Rising Stars ℠ list by Indianapolis Monthly and Law & Politics Magazine for ten consecutive years, she has a reputation for being a tough, yet passionate advocate, both inside and outside the courtroom. As a Carmel divorce lawyer at Hollingsworth Law Group, LLC, and a dedicated mother of three amazing boys, she brings a wealth of knowledge, insights and empathy to the table to offer her clients compassion legal counsel, focused on the long-term wellbeing of families and children.

Because each case that reaches her desk is different, she creates and implements effective negotiation strategies that are unique to each client’s needs. She truly cares about the men and women she represents, and it shows in everything that she does. Her relentless and hands-on approach has resulted in countless positive outcomes throughout Central Indiana.

Lou began his legal career in Indianapolis in 2008 at a regional civil litigation firm, eventually becoming a partner there. He is admitted to practice in the State of Indiana, the United States District Court for the Northern District of Indiana, the United States District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit.

Outside of the office, Lou enjoys spending time with his family, coaching softball and basketball, and traveling.

attorneys.name: Peter A. Britton
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in South Bend, IN
attorneys.bio:
Since 2005, Peter has concentrated his legal career almost exclusively on criminal law. He began as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney in Elkhart County, Indiana, where he tried more than 70 cases to verdict. His prosecutorial work focused on drug offenses—investigating and prosecuting possession, distribution, and manufacturing cases—in collaboration with local and federal law enforcement. He also assisted the Elkhart County Interdiction and Covert Enforcement (ICE) Unit on long-term investigations and managed the county’s complex civil forfeiture program. Later in his career, Peter handled child-victim prosecutions, including cases of child battery, molestation, and sexual misconduct.

In 2016, Peter co-founded Francisco Britton LLP and shifted to private practice, focusing on criminal defense. After his former partner’s 2024 judicial appointment, Peter formed Britton Law LLC. As a defense attorney, Peter has tried numerous cases to verdict, from simple misdemeanors to complex murder cases. Since 2016, Peter has been dedicated to defending the rights of individuals throughout Northern Indiana.

attorneys.name: Adam Brower
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal/DUI Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Adam Brower is an experienced litigator having worked as a deputy prosecutor for nearly three years in Marion County, Indiana. He has tried over 150 criminal cases to completion ranging from simple misdemeanors to complex felonies. He spent over a year prosecuting misdemeanors, nearly a year concentrating in a specialized litigation unit focused on OVWI/DUI prosecution, and over a year prosecuting felonies. Adam also has experience at the major felony level.

Before joining the prosecutor’s office, Adam was Corporate Counsel for a large, multi-million dollar construction management firm, Envoy, Inc. As corporate counsel, he personally drafted and reviewed all different types of corporate and construction documents. He was personally involved in creating/drafting an entire new set of corporate documents, including buy-sell agreements, bylaws, and shareholders agreements. He also facilitated litigation on various construction accident claims as well.

Adam lives in Brownsburg, IN, and has a beautiful wife and two children. He spends numerous hours a week volunteering in the community and coaching different sporting events.

Andrew enjoys spending time with family and friends, coaching baseball, and going for walks with his wife and dog.

attorneys.name: Josh Brown
attorneys.practice_type: Franchising Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Josh Brown is a franchise attorney with a national practice helping business owners make smart franchise decisions. Josh works with new and emerging franchisors to help them work through their legal challenges and grow through the franchise model. This includes assisting with business set up, trademarking, licensing issues, employment matters, HR issues and all other legal-related matters pertaining to a franchise or licensing structure. Additionally, he helps entrepreneurs identify and pursue good franchise opportunities. Finally, when a franchise relationship breaks down, Josh helps his clients with litigation and workout arrangements.

Josh is a recognized Indiana Super Lawyer, Franchise Legal Eagle, and Immediate Past Chairman of the Board for a national non-profit organization (College Mentors For Kids) that provides weekly mentoring for at risk youth.

Before becoming an attorney, Josh worked in business management, sales, marketing, and operations for several businesses, including two franchise systems. He combines his business background, entrepreneurial skills, and legal experience to help entrepreneurs in all aspects of their business growth, with a focus on franchising.

Josh is the creator and host of Franchise Euphoria, a top-rated podcast that sheds light on the evolving world of business franchising. In addition to all things franchising, Josh enjoys spending time with his family, traveling, and playing golf. To learn more or tune in to the Franchise Euphoria podcast, click here: https://indyfranchiselaw.com/franchise-euphoria-podcast/

attorneys.practice_type: Adoption Lawyers in Muncie, IN
attorneys.bio:
Rebecca is an experienced adoption attorney who can help you navigate your adoption journey.

I am blessed by adoption in so many ways. My husband (and law partner) and I have adopted 4 children (and fostered others). I have the privilege of having a law practice that is all about adoption. Over the years, I have helped many families adopt children, and have helped birth parents find loving homes for precious children. I have been doing this for enough years now that I sometimes find myself approached by a young adult when I'm out in the community who recognizes me from his or her "adoption day" photos. It is humbling, really, to be a part of something so wondrous.

Rachel is an advocate for her clients while also recognizing the delicate nature of these sensitive issues. attorneys.name: Shan L. Bryant
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Shan Bryant-Haase brings her unique experiences and background as both a Registered Nurse and attorney to her practice at Garau Germano, P.C.

Shan is a Hoosier native. Shan attended Indiana University and graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Nursing. Shan began working in the health care industry while in Nursing School and continued for several years after graduating. Shan has experience caring for a variety of patients including orthopedic patients, post-surgical patients, and patients with multiple complex medical problems. Shan later became a medical device consultant with a focus in medical surgical, pediatrics, neonatal intensive care, and obstetrics.

Shan attended Law School at the Indiana University School of Law at Indianapolis and earned a J.D. degree with a concentration in Health Law. Shan joined the firm of Garau Germano, P.C. in 2006. Shan focuses her areas of practice on medical malpractice, personal injury, and wrongful death.

Shan's care and compassion for the patient and their families as a bedside nurse has carried over to her practice of law and the approach she takes with helping injured patients and their families. Shan strongly advocates for the patient and their loved ones who have been injured by the negligent acts of another. Shan empathizes with those individuals who are wrongly injured, and she strives to obtain the remedy and compensation they deserve.

Shan is a member of the Indianapolis and Indiana State Bar Associations as well as a member of the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association, The American Association of Nurse Attorneys, and the American Association for Justice.

attorneys.name: James A. L. Buddenbaum
attorneys.firm_name: Parr Richey Frandsen Patterson Kruse LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jim Buddenbaum is a partner with the Indianapolis office of Parr Richey Frandsen Patterson Kruse LLP where he concentrates his practice representing businesses in all respects including in utility, real estate/zoning and employment law. He chairs the firm’s utility law section.

Mr. Buddenbaum is experienced in representing all types of utilities, including electric generation and transmission utilities, rural distribution cooperatives, sewer, water and gas utilities. Mr. Buddenbaum has also represented telecommunication clients before the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission and federal courts on issues related to the Telecommunications Act of 1996 and state specific matters. He regularly negotiates large energy sale and purchase agreements, real estate transactions, and has successfully presented more than fifty zoning and land use petitions in dozens of counties and cities throughout the state of Indiana for public utilities. He also represents the firm’s clients in matters of employment and labor law.

Mr. Buddenbaum has distinguished himself by having litigated large-document, complex commercial utility, bankruptcy and anti-trust matters. He has tried a case to a verdict in excess of $1 million and practices before state and federal courts and administrative agencies including the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

Mr. Buddenbaum’s industry and community responsibility is reflected in his representation of unique and innovative utilities including his participation on the legal committee which established ACES Power LLC, an energy and power trader, his work with public utilities utilizing self-sustaining wetland technology, and landfills which sell their methane byproduct to direct users.

attorneys.name: Kathryn Hillebrands Burroughs
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Kathryn Hillebrands Burroughs concentrates her practice in matrimonial and family law including premarital agreements; cohabitation agreements; dissolution of marriage; child custody, parenting time and support; and interstate disputes and modifications.

Ms. Burroughs became a Certified Family Law Specialist - Family Law Certification Board in 2002, the first year it was available in Indiana. Kathryn is the immediate past chair of the Indiana State Bar Association, Family and Juvenile Law Section. She also serves as a board member of the State of Indiana Independent Certification Organization, which certifies family law specialists.

Kathryn presently serves as a member of the Indiana Board of Law Examiners by appointment of the Indiana Supreme Court. She also serves on the Indiana Child Custody and Support Advisory Committee, a committee created by statute to make recommendations to the Indiana Supreme Court on the Child Support Guidelines and other terms relating to the welfare of children of families no longer intact.

attorneys.name: Mark Busby
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
An accomplished trial attorney with 25 years litigation experience, Mark uses his extensive trial experience to fight for the clients at Banks and Brower. In addition to well over 200 criminal jury and bench trials, Mark has over seven years of litigation experience in civil and family law matters, including training in collaborative divorce practice, service as a guardian ad litem and four years as the Executive Director of the State’s largest Child Advocacy Center. Mark’s blend of civil and criminal practice – in addition to four years working closely with the department of child services – gives him unique experience that few other family law attorneys can boast. This ranges from a familiarity with the department of child services, experience in tracking down financial assets and streams of income, to presenting complex cases in court.

Mark’s previous experience includes years of family and child-focused litigation – Adoption, Child Custody, Child Support, Parental and Grandparent Rights, Guardianship, Paternity, Prenuptial & Marital Agreements, and Restraining Orders. Mark’s time as a prosecutor focused on trial work dedicated to prosecuting sex crimes, child abuse and homicide cases for nearly two decades.

What sets Mark apart from most former Deputy Prosecuting Attorneys is his work as the Executive Director of the Marion County Child Advocacy Center. The Child Advocacy Center served as the hub of a multi-disciplinary team that included the Department of Child Services. Daily interaction with the Department of Child Services provided valuable insight that allowed him to quickly transition into private practice in 2014, when he first began working on family law cases. Sound investigation, strong advocacy skills and hard work provide the backbone of his legal practice.

Mark has represented clients in a variety of other civil matters including employment matters, whistleblowing protection, Olympic law, sexual harassment, homicide charges, insurance claims against national carriers and complex internal investigations. Mark has also participated in discovery compliance with Senatorial and Congressional inquiries and has reviewed of hundreds of tortious claims of sexual abuse.

Born in Canada and raised in Saudi Arabia, Mark received his law degree from the University of Notre Dame in 2000, and became a naturalized Citizen of the United States in 2007.

attorneys.name: Melanie Cain Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Fort Wayne, IN
attorneys.bio:
Navigating a difficult family law matter can be an overwhelming and emotional experience. Having a knowledgeable and compassionate attorney on our side is so important. Melanie Cain, a Junior Associate Attorney at Stange Law Firm, PC, is dedicated to guiding clients through these challenging situations with care and clarity. From the firm’s Fort Wayne, Indiana office, she proudly serves individuals and families throughout Allen County and the surrounding areas, offering steady support and legal representation every step of the way.

Melanie Earned her Juris Doctor from Ohio Northern University Pettit College of Law in Ada, Ohio, in May of 2024. Before pursuing her legal education, Melanie attended Bowling Green State University in Bowling Green, Ohio, where she earned her Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy, Politics, Economics, and Pre-Law, graduating with University Honors in December 2020. Melanie’s academic background also includes published research, her honors project, “Trust, Political Participation, and Poverty: The Effects of Poverty on Political Behavior” (2020), offers insight into the intersection of socioeconomic factors and civic engagement.

Before becoming a Junior Associate Attorney with the Fort Wayne divorce and family lawyers at Stange Law Firm, Melanie most recently served as a Law Clerk with the firm. Before that, she served as an Intern at the Ohio Northern Legal Clinic. In that time, she gained hands-on experience performing research and drafting legal documents for Transactional Clinic clients and assisting interns and supervisors with of the Litigation Clinic with intake interviews. Her professional experience, combined with her academic foundation, equips her to advocate effectively for her clients with dedication and empathy.

Note: The choice of a lawyer is an important decision and should not be based solely upon advertisements.

He has argued appeals before the Indiana Court of Appeals, Indiana's Supreme Court and before the Federal Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals. In addition to being an experienced trial attorney in the areas of personal injury, contract disputes, real estate disputes, business disputes, insurance disputes and criminal law, Mr. Campiti maintains a large practice in the area of family law. attorneys.name: John S. Capper IV
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury - Accidents Lawyers in Crawfordsville, IN
attorneys.bio:
John S. Capper IV (Indiana University, J.D.) has been practicing law for over 40 years concentrating in the area of family law relating to complex financial divorce litigation, paternity litigation, contested child custody, parenting time and adult and child guardianships. Mr. Capper’s divorce, paternity and guardianship practice is individually tailored to the needs of each of his clients.

Mr. Capper also has extensive experience in representing seriously injured individuals and their families who are victims of auto accidents, truck collisions, wrongful death, premises liability and other plaintiff personal injury matters.

Mr. Capper has over 40 years experience in the areas of estate, trusts, wills and has litigated numerous will contests and contested trust matters resulting in successful settlements for numerous clients. Mr. Capper has used his farm experience to organize and manage the sale of multiple tracts of farm real estate in estates and trusts working with the client to coordinate successful strategies to obtain optimum results in the sale of farm real estate.

Mr. Capper litigated one of the first compensation cases in the State of Indiana under the National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act that was appealed to the United States Supreme Court. Mr. Capper was selected as local counsel in the largest toxic tort case filed in the State of Indiana (75 defendants) wherein he selected the jury prior to settlement. Mr. Capper was involved in the longest jury trial in Montgomery County on record involving the Town of Whitestown and their sewer contractor resulting in a verdict in favor of the town. Mr. Capper has tried numerous criminal and civil jury trials throughout his career.

Mr. Capper is Senior Partner of the law firm Capper, Tulley and Reimondo an AV-rated law firm Martindale-Hubbell that has been in existence since 1907.

Mr. Capper is admitted to practice before the U.S. Supreme Court; U.S. Court of Appeals, Seventh Circuit; U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit; and Southern Districts of Indiana and all Courts in the State of Indiana.

Mr. Capper has been President of the Montgomery County Bar Association, Montgomery County Pro-Bono of the year attorney, 17 year member of the Crawfordsville Parks and Recreation Board and a 16 year member of the City of Crawfordsville Board of Public Works. He has been married to his wife Jill for over 40 years and has 3 children. Mr. Capper is a member of St. Luke’s United Methodist Church, Indianapolis, Indiana.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey Richard Cardella
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Jeff Cardella Criminal Defense Attorney & Expungement Lawyer
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jeff Cardella is a criminal defense attorney and expungement lawyer serving clients throughout Indianapolis and the entire State of Indiana. He has personally handled thousands of criminal cases and has extensive experience in every stage of the criminal justice process, including jury trials, court trials, suppression hearings, post-conviction relief, forfeiture litigation, civil rights lawsuits, federal and state appeals, oral argument, probation violations, expungements, specialized driving privileges, and plea negotiations. Jeff began his legal career as a criminal defense lawyer in Indianapolis, focused on protecting the Constitutional rights of individuals accused of crimes. Over the years, he has built a reputation as one of the best criminal attorneys in Indianapolis, known for his deep knowledge of criminal law, strategic defense work, and the ability to identify flaws in the State’s case that other attorneys might miss. Many clients specifically seek him out when they want an Indianapolis criminal defense attorney who combines trial experience with detailed legal analysis. He also taught Criminal Law at the Indiana University School of Law and has served as a Judge pro tem. His experience teaching criminal law has helped him stay current on developments in Indiana criminal procedure, constitutional law, and evidentiary issues that affect everyday cases. Jeff’s work has shaped Indiana law. He filed the federal class action Washington v. Marion County Prosecutor, in which Indiana’s vehicle forfeiture statute was held unconstitutional under the Due Process Clause of the United States Constitution. He also co-authored the amicus brief in Timbs v. State of Indiana, a landmark United States Supreme Court case holding that Indiana’s forfeiture practices violated the Excessive Fines Clause of the U.S. Constitution. In addition, Jeff has filed more than a dozen successful federal lawsuits against the Indiana Department of Correction challenging solitary-confinement procedures, and he has prevailed in multiple civil rights lawsuits against the Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department for unconstitutional arrests violating the First Amendment. Jeff has been selected as one of the Top 100 Attorneys by The National Trial Lawyers, recognized as a Top Ten Attorney in Indiana by the American Institute of Criminal Law Attorneys, and honored as a Top 10 Under 40 Criminal Defense Attorney by the National Academy of Criminal Defense Attorneys. These recognitions, along with the results he has achieved for clients, have led many to regard him as one of the top criminal defense attorneys in the State of Indiana. His appellate work, expungement practice, and criminal trial experience have further strengthened this reputation statewide. His clients have included a fellow criminal defense attorney, an Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Officer, and two former Marion County Sheriff’s deputies accused of criminal misconduct—individuals who placed their professional reputations in his hands. This trust reflects the level of confidence placed in Jeff by people who understand the criminal justice system. In law school, Jeff worked for the Hendricks County Prosecutor’s Office, giving him key insight into how prosecutors build cases and where procedural weaknesses can be found. This dual perspective allows him to spot errors, leverage technical defects, and identify opportunities to protect his clients’ rights. Jeff is known for providing high-quality representation at reasonable prices compared to other top criminal defense attorneys in Indiana. He treats every client as a real person—not just a case number—and he believes that even good people can find themselves facing criminal charges. His goal is simple: provide excellent legal representation, explain the law clearly, listen to each client’s goals, and fight for the best possible result. Jeff serves clients across all 92 Indiana counties, including Indianapolis/Marion County; Carmel, Fishers, and Noblesville in Hamilton County; Greenwood and Franklin in Johnson County; Danville and Plainfield in Hendricks County; Bloomington, Muncie, Anderson, Lebanon, Martinsville, Greenfield, and many more communities throughout Indiana. His work throughout these regions has led many longtime clients to refer to him—quietly and without fanfare—as one of the top criminal defense attorneys in the State of Indiana, a reflection of both results and reputation. If you have been charged with a crime, are seeking an expungement, or need help with forfeiture, civil rights violations, DUI, drug cases, domestic violence allegations, theft charges, federal criminal matters, or any other criminal issue, you may contact Jeff directly at 317-695-7700 for a free consultation. Phone calls are answered seven days a week.

Top Ten Attorney in the State of Indiana by the American Institute of Criminal Law Attorneys, 2019

Top 10 Under 40 Criminal Defense Attorney by The National Academy of Criminal Defense Attorneys, 2019

His pastimes include cycling, golf, going to the movies and coaching his kids' various sports teams. An avid fan of the Colts, Notre Dame football and IU basketball, he clings to the hope every year that his beloved Cubs will finally win another World Series.

attorneys.name: Julie Chambers
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Julie Chambers graduated with honors from The University of Toledo College of Law in 2007, and she received her Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science from the University of Michigan - Ann Arbor in 2003.

Julie focuses her practice on criminal defense and traffic law, representing individuals throughout central Indiana. She has significant trial experienace and has worked in a variety of areas of law, including working in immigration law, serving as a law clerk in family court during law school, and spending a summer as an Extern with the United States Attorney's Office - District of Hawaii in Honolulu, Hawaii, where she assisted in the preparation of federal criminal cases for trial.

In 2008, Julie accepted a position with the Marion County Prosecutor's Office in Indianapolis, IN as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney, handling misdemeanor and felony prosecutions. During her time as a Deputy Prosecutor, Julie served as lead counsel and secondary counsel on several jury trials and bench trials and has appeared in court on hundreds of occasions. She not only prosecuted misdemeanor and felony cases, she also worked as a deputy prosecutor in the mental health court and served as the Marion County Traffic Court Deputy Prosecutor.

After almost five years as a deputy prosecutor, Julie founded Chambers Law Office, LLC. Drawing on her years of experience as a trial lawyer at the prosecutor's office and her experience in other areas of the law, Julie is dedicated to providing exceptional, personal legal representation to every client.

Julie is admitted to practice law in the State of Indiana, before the United States District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana, and the State of Michigan. She is a member of the Indianapolis Bar Association and the State Bar of Michigan. Additionally, in 2018, she was elected to the Hamilton Southeastern Schools Board of School Trustees and was proud to serve in that role until 2022.

attorneys.name: Jessica Cicchini
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jessica Cicchini was born and raised in rural Ohio. She grew up racing motocross and working at her family’s business – a motocross track in southern Michigan.

Jessica went on to study political science at Eastern Michigan University, where she captained the mock trial team and learned that her future would be forged in the courtroom. After leaving Ypsilanti, MI, she became a proud Gopher at the University of Minnesota Law School and introduced a new generation to trial advocacy as a coach of the local undergraduate mock trial team. In her last year of law school, Jessica discovered her passion for social and criminal justice as a visiting student at Indiana University McKinney School of Law.

A career litigator with over sixteen years of trial experience, Jessica has built a practice defined by effective, high-stakes work on both sides of the courtroom. She handled hundreds of cases as a public defender for 12 years, including the most serious crimes, and she was always ready to go to trial when needed. Her goal was simple in name but required countless hours of research and dedication: put her clients in a better position than when they met her. During her tenure, she developed a special interest in children charged as adults, individuals with mental illness, and the unique challenges they each faced in the criminal justice system.

In 2021, Jessica joined the Marion County Prosecutor’s Office as co-director of Indiana’s first Conviction Integrity Unit (CIU) – a division dedicated to identifying and remedying wrongful convictions. Under her leadership, the CIU exonerated two men who were wrongfully convicted of murder, securing their release from prison after decades of unjust incarceration.

Jessica’s other major projects at the CIU included a review of excessive sentencing in non-violent drug cases, which resulted in the release of approximately 30 people from unjust prison sentences, along with audits of police misconduct that led to the dismissal or reversal of dozens of criminal convictions affected by inappropriate behavior. She also regularly joined the office’s trial teams to prosecute critical cases in court.

Yet no matter where she has practiced law, Jessica has remained a stalwart advocate who is committed to ensuring that justice is sought and miscarriages of justice are rectified whenever they occur. Her approach to litigation is consistently client-centered, striving to serve their best interests with integrity and provide efficient, compassionate, and results-driven representation. Her extensive trial background puts her in an ideal position to advocate for her current clients at Hensley Legal Group, where she has been making a difference on behalf of injured victims since 2025.

Jessica lives with her husband in the Broad Ripple area. She enjoys bicycling on the Monon, cooking, DIY projects, and lots of crafting.

Jessica’s other major projects at the CIU included a review of excessive sentencing in non-violent drug cases, which resulted in the release of approximately 30 people from unjust prison sentences, along with audits of police misconduct that led to the dismissal or reversal of dozens of criminal convictions affected by inappropriate behavior. She also regularly joined the office’s trial teams to prosecute critical cases in court.

Yet no matter where she has practiced law, Jessica has remained a stalwart advocate who is committed to ensuring that justice is sought and miscarriages of justice are rectified whenever they occur. Her approach to litigation is consistently client-centered, striving to serve their best interests with integrity and provide efficient, compassionate, and results-driven representation. Her extensive trial background puts her in an ideal position to advocate for her current clients at Hensley Legal Group, where she has been making a difference on behalf of injured victims since 2025.

Jessica lives with her husband in the Broad Ripple area. She enjoys bicycling on the Monon, cooking, DIY projects, and lots of crafting.

Kelly was born and raised in Will County, Illinois but moved to Northwest Indiana for law school in 2003 and has been a proud Hoosier for the last 20 years. Kelly attended Valparaiso University School of Law where she participated in Moot Court (Appellate Advocacy) and was editor-in-chief of the school’s student run publication. Kelly has dedicated the last 16 years of her career to representing individuals who have been injured as a result of the carelessness of others. Kelly joined Hensley Legal Group in 2023 and is looking forward to continuing to passionately represent people who have been severely injured.

Kelly has experience in handling many kinds of personal injury cases including:

automobile accidents, trucking accidents, premises liability, dog bites, slip & fall, trip & fall, invasion of privacy, voyeurism, asbestos exposure, defective products, swimming pool accidents, dram shop liability and wrongful death.

Outside the office, Kelly and her husband have a blended household of four children who all play sports. Kelly can usually be found at a baseball field, football field or in the gym at a local sports event. Kelly resides in Porter County and is active in her community previously serving in Christian ministries and as a board member at the YMCA. Kelly enjoys the outdoors including camping, concerts, and sporting events.

attorneys.name: Kathryn M. Cimera
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Kathryn Cimera represents employers and individuals in a wide range of employment matters, including employment discrimination actions, non-competition matters, wage and hour issues, as well as issues related to employer's retirement plans. Kathryn has significant experience representing clients in both State and Federal Courts, in mediation and arbitration, and matters pending before administrative agencies, including the Department of Labor, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, and the Indiana Civil Rights Commission.

Kathryn's practice includes providing advice to employers on various employment issues, including workplace investigations, disciplinary matters, leaves of absences, reductions in force, and policy and procedure review. Kathryn assists business leaders with negotiating contracts and managing outside vender agreements. She conducts trainings for managers and employees on work-place issues, including harassment. Kathryn also has experience with ERISA compliance and has advised board members and plan administrators on fiduciary obligations and board governance best practices.

Kathryn serves as an adjunct faculty member at Indiana University's O'Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs, teaching Employment Law for Human Resources Majors, and is a frequent speaker on employment law related topics.

Kathryn earned a Juris Doctorate from Pepperdine University School of Law. While in law school, she was a member of the Pepperdine Law Review, the Appellate Advocacy Team, and a recipient of the State Bar Foundation Exceptional Merit Scholarship. She earned a Bachelor of Arts in English and Political Science from Indiana University. Prior to attending law school, she served as a volunteer in Thailand with the United States Peace Corps.

attorneys.name: Andrea L. Ciobanu
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Matters Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Andrea focuses her practice in Civil Litigation, Family Law and Domestic Relations, Civil Rights and ADA Compliance, as well as Appellate Law. Andrea also has experience in complex fraud and white collar crime litigation. Andrea has argued before the Indiana Northern and Southern District Federal Courts, as well as the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals. Andrea has Indiana Appellate Court experience, including engaging in oral argument before the Indiana Appellate and Supreme Courts. Further, Andrea is a registered civil and domestic mediator as well as a foreclosure facilitator. Andrea is also an adjunct professor of law at Indiana University Purdue Indianapolis. She is a graduate of the inaugural Indiana State Bar Association Leadership Development Academy, FBI Citizens Academy, Stanley K. Lacy Leadership Series, as well as the inaugural Columbia Club Impact Community Program. She has been ranked as a Rising Star SuperLawyer every year since 2012. She is AV rated from Martindale-Hubbell. She is a frequent speaker and writer on such topics as mediation, domestic relations, including adoption, civil rights, including ADA Compliance.

Andrea is committed to public interest and serving the community. She has served on various boards throughout the community, including, but not limited to: Indianapolis Bar Association Steering Committee; Indianapolis Law School Repayment Program Host and Standing Committees, Indiana University Alumni Board; Indiana University Purdue Indianapolis Paralegal Advisory Board, and has served as Past-President of the Indianapolis Equal Justice Works Division. Andrea is also very active within her local, city, state, and national bar association, serving in a wide array of leadership positions within those bar associations.

In addition to providing the highest degree of representation to the firm's clients, Andrea is dedicated to public interest law and serving the underprivileged. Andrea has volunteered at various organizations throughout the community which serve the underprivileged and pursue equal access to justice, including, but not limited to: Disability Legal Services of Indiana; Indiana Coalition Against Domestic Violence; Indiana Protective Order Pro Bono Project; Ask A Lawyer; Indiana Pro Bono Commission; Center for Victim and Human Rights; and other such organizations.

Andrea is fluent in American Sign Language and utilizes this skill to pursue her passion of meeting the legal needs and challenges of the Deaf Community throughout Indiana.

In addition to Andrea's unique skill set and community-oriented approach to the practice of law, Andrea has helped form Ciobanu Law, PC to provide the firm's clients with the highest quality of legal representation while maintaining cost effective representation and unparalleled client communication.

attorneys.name: Bryan L. Ciyou
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Bryan L. Ciyou, an Eagle Scout, lives each day on the bedrock principle of the Boy Scout Motto, "Be Prepared." This way of life - his mantra - was then forged on the anvil of hardships endured during his significant humanitarian aid work in places like Haiti and Central America. In these countries, making a plan and executing it, and always being prepared, was not a choice but a necessity in order to survive daily life. A few years later, Mr. Ciyou attended Indiana University, Indianapolis, completing the honors program and graduating with a bachelor of arts, with distinction, in 1991; and from its law school with a doctor of jurisprudence, cum laude, in 1994. Mr. Ciyou then entered the private practice of law in 1994.

With his diverse life experiences and academic successes, Mr. Ciyou brings to the table, in every legal matter he handles, deft organizational and leadership skills. And he has a strong moral compass, personal values and integrity, along with relentless drive - the keys to his success as a lawyer.

Professionally, Mr. Ciyou has extensive civil trial and appellate practice experience, having briefed and orally argued cases before the Indiana Court of Appeals and Indiana Supreme Court. Further, Mr. Ciyou has researched, drafted, and filed Certiorari Petitions with the United States Supreme Court. Other professional interests include complex domestic relations, litigation, and business law.

Mr. Ciyou is also a prolific writer, publishing a number of professional articles each year; and he is sought after as a frequent presenter and lecturer for continuing education for other lawyers and other professionals. Mr. Ciyou's written works and speaking topics range from the legal aspects of safety and security in the workplace, alternative dispute resolution, and complex domestic relations.

A few years later, Mr. Ciyou attended Indiana University, Indianapolis, completing the honors program and graduating with a bachelor of arts, with distinction, in 1991; and from its law school with a doctor of jurisprudence, cum laude, in 1994. Mr. Ciyou then entered the private practice of law in 1994.

With his diverse life experiences and academic successes, Mr. Ciyou brings to the table, in every legal matter he handles, deft organizational and leadership skills. And he has a strong moral compass, personal values and integrity, along with relentless drive - the keys to his success as a lawyer.

Professionally, Mr. Ciyou has extensive civil trial and appellate practice experience, having briefed and orally argued cases before the Indiana Court of Appeals and Indiana Supreme Court. Further, Mr. Ciyou has researched, drafted, and filed Certiorari Petitions with the United States Supreme Court. Other professional interests include complex domestic relations, litigation, and business law.

Mr. Ciyou is also a prolific writer, publishing a number of professional articles each year; and he is sought after as a frequent presenter and lecturer for continuing education for other lawyers and other professionals. Mr. Ciyou's written works and speaking topics range from the legal aspects of safety and security in the workplace, alternative dispute resolution, and complex domestic relations.

attorneys.name: Jason P. Cleveland
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
A seasoned employment law and civil litigation attorney in the Indianapolis area, Jason has practiced law since 2003. He's handled multiple federal injury trials in the Northern and Southern District of Indiana Courts and represented clients at the EEOC, MSPB, SEAC and ICRC, as well as Indiana State Courts, local government bodies and boards.

He's a DePauw University graduate, with a degree in Philosophy, who grew up in New Castle, Indiana. A third generation small business owner, he follows in his father and grandfather's footsteps. Jason lives in Indianapolis with his wife, Jill, and his three children.

After earning his law degree at Indiana University Maurer School of Law in Bloomington, Jason spent the first seven years of his career as an attorney at Hostetter & O'Hara in Brownsburg, practicing general civil litigation before federal and state courts. At John H. Haskin & Associates (formerly Haskin & LaRue), Jason focused his practice exclusively on employment and discrimination law.

You will not meet a bigger Indianapolis Colts fanatic, with his love for Hoosier basketball ticking in at a close second. Jason also enjoys running, regularly participating in local marathons and half marathons, and joins his family in the Drumstick Dash every year. Aside from his devotion to the Horse (and his wife and kids, of course) Jason enjoys jamming out to live music and watching Quentin Tarantino movies.

attorneys.name: Lance D. Cline
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Lance Cline knew at a young age that when he grew up, he would be a personal injury attorney representing people who have been injured, and families who had had a member killed, as a result of the negligent conduct of others. His father was a successful and well-regarded personal injury attorney in Columbus, Indiana. Lance grew up listening to stories about how his father's clients had been injured, how the law allowed such individuals to seek redress for their harms and losses, and the hard work and excitement associated with jury trials. In high school, he worked in his father's office as a file clerk and attended several jury trials with his father. Lance knew at an early age that his calling in life was to be a lawyer for injury victims.

Lance attended the McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis, Indiana from 1977 to 1980. In addition to being a full-time student, Lance worked full-time as a law clerk in one of the busiest and most respected personal injury law firms in Indiana. He graduated from law school in 1980 and began his practice as a plaintiff personal injury attorney right away in the same law firm in which he had served as a law clerk. He has continued his exclusive practice of personal injury law for forty-five years. Lance worked in his original law firm for thirteen years before leaving that firm with three other attorneys to open a new personal injury law practice. He continued to practice with those three attorneys for the next twenty-seven years. In 2020, Lance chose to continue his practice of law in a smaller law firm near his home. He created The Cline Law Firm where he presently practices with Lindsay Popejoy and Spencer Hatfield.

Lance has dedicated his forty-five year legal career to representing victims of health care malpractice, motor vehicle collisions, consumer product defects, and other injury-producing events. Lance's long legal practice has made him a knowledgeable litigator representing injured people and their loved ones against health care providers, motor vehicle operators, large corporations, and other formidable opponents. He is a tireless and fearless advocate for his clients.

Lance's dedication to his clients and his level of skill in trial advocacy have earned him membership in the prestigious Inner Circle of Advocates, a national organization limited to one hundred of the best plaintiff attorneys in the United States. Members of the Inner Circle are invited to apply for membership and undergo a rigorous selection process. Information is obtained regarding each nominee from peers, opposing counsel, and trial judges. Few attorneys are invited to apply for membership and even fewer are selected. Lance is one of only three Indiana attorneys elected into to the Inner Circle during its 53 year history. The Inner Circle provides Lance with daily contact and consultation with many of the best plaintiff personal injury attorneys in the United States. Lance is also a member of the American College of Trial Lawyers, an organization comprised of only 1% of trial attorneys nationwide. Selection to that group is through peer nomination and voting.

There is no greater honor for a trial attorney than peer recognition from other attorneys. Lance has been honored by his peers many times. In addition to his admission to the Inner Circle of Advocates and the American College of Trial Lawyers, Lance has been selected by his peers as an Indiana Super Lawyer every year since the inception of the award in 2004. He was selected as one of the Top 10 lawyers in Indiana in 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, and 2022. He has also been selected as a Top 50 lawyer in Indiana eighteen times. Lance has also been recognized by an organization known as the Best Lawyers in America in both personal injury law and medical malpractice law every year since 1997. He has been voted the Indianapolis Medical Malpractice Lawyer of the Year in 2011-2012, 2013-2014, and 2014-2015 and the Indianapolis Personal Injury Lawyer of the Year in 2019 and 2025. The Indiana Trial Lawyers' Association honored Lance as its Trial Lawyer of the Year in 2018.

Lance has obtained multiple seven figure jury verdicts for clients and has settled over one hundred cases for clients for seven figure amounts.

As a personal injury and wrongful death attorney, Lance runs his law practice by the golden rule. He treats and represents each of his clients as he would want to be treated and represented if he was the client of an attorney. He devotes the majority of his time and energy during his waking hours championing the legal claims of his clients.

attorneys.name: Charles A. Cohen
attorneys.practice_type: Business and Tax Planning Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Chuck Cohen concentrates in the areas of business and tax planning, estate planning healthcare, and employee benefits. Mr. Cohen has an AV Preeminent Peer Review rating from Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory. Born in Greenville, Kentucky, Mr. Cohen graduated from Greenville High School as the salutatorian, then attended Indiana University. There, he was a member of Sigma Alpha Mu, graduating in 1963 with a B.S. in Accounting, being elected to Beta Gamma Sigma, business scholastic honorary, and being commissioned as a 2nd Lieutenant in the U.S. Army (ROTC). He graduated from Indiana University-Bloomington law school in 1966 with a J.D. degree, having served on the Law Review (senior symposium editor), and being elected to the Order of the Coif (scholastic honorary). While in law school, Mr. Cohen successfully completed the CPA exam. Following graduation, Mr. Cohen entered the U.S. Army in the Medical Service Corps serving in Ft. Myer, Virginia (1966-67) and at the 3rd Surgical Hospital, Dong Tam, Vietnam (1967-68) where he was awarded the Bronze Star for meritorious service in a combat zone. He completed his military service as a Captain in 1968. Mr. Cohen is serving or has served the local Jewish Community as: President of the Jewish Federation of Greater Indianapolis President of the Jewish Community Center of Indianapolis President of Broadmoor Country Club Chair of the Federation Endowment Committee Co-Chair Federation Annual Campaign (1995,2000 and 2013) Co-Chair Operation Exodus II Co-Chair Israel Emergency Campaign (2006) President Indianapolis Hebrew Congregation Foundation Board Member Indianapolis Hebrew Congregation Mr. Cohen is serving or has served the national Jewish Community as: Jewish Federations of North America Board of Trustees, Chair of Intermediate Cities Trustees Co-Chair and Chair of Jewish Federations of North America Planned Giving and Endowment Committee Jewish Federations of North America Israel and Overseas Committee Sigma Alpha Mu Certificate of Merit 2012 Board of Directors of America's Voices in Israel In October, 2004, Mr. Cohen received the Jerusalem Medal from the Israel Bond organization for service to Israel and was appointed a Sagamore of the Wabash by the Governor of Indiana, the highest honor the State of Indiana can bestow on a citizen.

attorneys.name: Cassie Ann Coleman
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Cassie graduated from high school in 2018 and attended college at Ohio University in Athens, Ohio. While obtaining her Bachelors degree in Psychology, Cassie found a passion for the criminal justice system through the Ohio Innocence Project. Through the Ohio Innocence Project, Cassie learned of the many shortfalls of the criminal justice system. Especially, the need for every individual to receive proper representation through all criminal proceedings. Cassie quickly picked up a double major pairing her Psychology degree with a Sociology Pre-Law Degree.

After graduating college, Cassie chose to pursue her passion for Criminal Law by attending the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in Downtown Indianapolis. During her second year of law school, Cassie became a criminal legal intern with Eskew Law in 2024. While interning at Eskew Law, Cassie drafted motions to address evidentiary issues, drafted expungement petitions, and conducted supervised court hearings for level 6 Felony and Misdemeanor cases. Cassie graduated Cum Laura from Law School in May of 2025. In October of 2025, Cassie passed the Bar Exam and was admitted into practice.

After becoming a Criminal Attorney, Cassie handles level 6 Felony and Misdemeanor cases, violations of probations, expungement cases, and registry related cases. Cassie is committed to utilizing her passion for the criminal justice system to ensure each client receives proper advocacy, fairness, and justice.

attorneys.name: Michael C. Cooley
attorneys.firm_name: Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy and Bankruptcy Litigation Lawyers in Greenfield, IN
attorneys.bio:
Michael has been an attorney with Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP in Greenfield, Indiana, since 2006 and currently serves as the firm’s managing partner. He concentrates his practice in the areas of business and commercial law, and complex litigation in state and federal court. Michael regularly advises clients in the areas of business planning, contracts, employment law, prelitigation planning, dispute resolution and workouts. He also advises farmers in business and succession planning, and government regulation including disputes arising under the Food and Security Act of 1985. While Michael’s practice is focused in central Indiana, he regularly represents clients throughout the state and regionally.

Michael has significant appellate practice experience, and regularly represents clients in appellate matters in both administrative and judicial reviews over a wide range of legal areas. He has briefed and argued cases as lead and sole counsel before the Indiana Court of Appeals and the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit and served as lead counsel on Petitions to Transfer to the Indiana Supreme Court. Michael successfully obtained reversal of a United States Department of Agriculture wetland determination before the Seventh Circuit in Boucher v. USDA, 934 F.3d 530 (7th Cir. 2019), an important decision addressing the requirements of a wetland under the Swampbuster provisions of the Food and Security Act.

Michael also oversees the firm’s bankruptcy and insolvency work, representing debtors and creditors in cases and litigation arising under Chapter 7, Chapter 12, Chapter 13, and Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code. Michael also represents debtors, financial institutions, and receivers in foreclosure and receivership cases arising under state law.

Michael grew up in Rush County, Indiana, and obtained his undergraduate degree from Franklin College in Franklin, Indiana, and his law degree from the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law. He resides in the Meridian Kessler neighborhood of Indianapolis with his wife Michele, and their sons, Evan and Ryan.

attorneys.name: Daniel E. Coots
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate Transactions and Business Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Daniel E. Coots concentrates his law practice to representing individuals and entities in the areas of corporate/business law, telecommunications/utility law, real estate transactions, and estate planning/probate administration.

Dan’s corporate/business law practice includes assisting his clients in transactions involving mergers and acquisitions, corporate restructuring, covenants not to compete, shareholder buyouts and disputes, employment contracts and wage claims, and other general contract needs. In addition, Dan assists his clients with the formation, organizational, and management needs of his clients’ businesses, as well as business succession planning for closely held business entities.

In Dan’s telecommunications/utility law practice, he represents entities ranging from a major wireless communications carrier to large and small tower companies in all facets of wireless communications infrastructure transactions and implementation. He performs extensive contract negotiations and drafting, and provides land use/planning/zoning representation in various jurisdictions throughout the State of Indiana.

Dan assists individuals and businesses with residential and commercial real estate transactions. He advises his clients in all stages of a real estate transaction through the closing, including document preparation. In addition, Dan helps his clients with land planning and zoning needs with local governmental/zoning authorities to allow for each client’s contemplated development/use of real estate.

As life and financial needs change, Dan advises and guides his clients through the estate planning cycle, from the newly married couple with small children to those clients with more advanced estate tax planning needs. His estate and trust administration practice covers all administration areas, including the preparation of income and transfer tax returns.

Tim represents clients from Indiana and other states, advocating on their behalf in disputed claims and threatened or pending litigation. Mr. Coriden has successfully served as counsel in dozens of jury trials and administrative hearings throughout Indiana. Tim routinely advises both clients and attorneys alike on the rights and remedies bestowed upon injured workers within the Indiana Worker’s Compensation Act. Mr. Coriden also provides counsel to his clients on the complex interplay between the Indiana Worker’s Compensation Act and Federal programs such as the Center for Medicare & Medicaid Services and Social Security Disability.

Drawing upon his extensive municipal law experience, Mr. Coriden also counsels the firm’s private clients on local and state government regulations and laws. Appointed as City Attorney, by then Mayor Fred L. Armstrong, Tim oversaw the Department of Law for the City of Columbus between 2004-2010. On December 7, 2010, Tim was awarded a “Key to the City” and a Proclamation was issued on his behalf for his service to the City of Columbus. Mr. Coriden also served as the City Attorney for Greensburg, Indiana, from 2008-2011, appointed by current Mayor Gary Herbert. Tim utilizes these experiences to help his clients navigate their way through local laws and regulatory schemes throughout Indiana.

Prior to joining Coriden & Coriden, LLC, in 2001, (formerly Coriden Coriden Andrews & Glover & Coriden Law Office), Tim graduated from Xavier University in 1997 and he received his law degree from Toledo University in 2001. Tim is married to Ann Coriden, formerly a fellow attorney with Coriden & Coriden, LLC, and they have two children, Peter and Danny. Tim is the son to late firm founder G. Terrence Coriden and the Hon. Kathleen “Kitty” Coriden, Judge of Superior Court II in Bartholomew County. He is continuously active on boards for local and state not-for-profit organizations, as well as professional organizations. Tim spends his leisure time coaching, serving as Athletic Director for St. Bartholomew Catholic School and attempting to play golf.

attorneys.name: G Terrence Coriden
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Columbus, IN
attorneys.bio:
Terry Coriden practices worker’s compensation law as a Partner at Coriden & Coriden, LLC. His entire professional career as an attorney has been committed to worker’s compensation law and making a difference in his community. He is also highly experienced in mediation.

“As a worker’s compensation attorney, I appreciate the opportunity to help a client solve their legal problem. I also value mediation because it presents the best course to both expeditiously and fairly bring a case to a final resolution. It avoids the strain of years of litigation. I have the unique position of bringing 32 years as a Judge to the mediation table. This is one reason why my mediations result in a successful conclusion 95% of the time.”

Terry is a member and past president of the Bartholomew County Bar Association, a member of the Indiana State Bar Association, and a former board member of the Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum (ICLEF). Terry is a former board member of numerous local civic organizations including the Columbus Human Rights Commission, Family Services of Bartholomew County, and St. Bartholomew Parish Council. He is a Pro Bono Attorney for Bartholomew Area Legal Aid and Attorney for the Bartholomew County Fair Board. Terry also serves as a board member of Kid’s Chance of Indiana, Inc., an organization dedicated to providing educational opportunities to children of people seriously injured in work-related accidents. In recognition of his civic work, Governors Orr, Bayh, O’Bannon, and Kernan have each bestowed upon Terry the state’s highest distinction, the Sagamore of the Wabash.

In 1974, Indiana Governor Bowen appointed Terry to the position of a Hearing Judge of the Workers’ Compensation Board of Indiana. Since then, Terry served under Indiana Governors Orr, Bayh, O’Bannon, Kernan, and Daniels and was Chairman of the Workers’ Compensation Board from 1992 until 2004. Terry has served as a worker’s compensation judge for more than 30 years. He also served as City Attorney for Columbus, Indiana, from 1996 through 2004, and served as the City Utility Attorney in Columbus, Indiana, from 1996 through 2008.

Terry made Columbus, Indiana, his home in 1971, after graduating from the University of Toledo College of Law. Over the past forty years, Terry has served the people of Indiana in a number of different capacities at both the state and local levels. In 1971, Terry started Legal Services of Bartholomew, Brown, and Jackson Counties, a program that has provided legal aid to low-income families.

“The personality of your community often dictates what the needs of the individuals are. Therefore, a good understanding of the community will help understand the needs of the worker in bringing a case to conclusion.”

Terry was born in Hammond, Indiana, and graduated from Xavier University in Cincinnati, Ohio, in 1968, with a Bachelor of Science Degree. Terry then attended law school at the University of Toledo, where he met his wife, Kitty. Terry and Kitty are the parents of Tim Coriden and Erin Kendall and the grandparents of three grandsons, who all live in Columbus, Indiana.

In Memoriam of G. Terrence Coriden

attorneys.name: Stacy J. Crider
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Stacy J. Crider is a Partner at the Hankey Marks & Crider, which she joined in 2010. Her primary practice areas are Social Security Disability, Worker's Compensation, and Personal Injury.

She graduated from law school in 2009, and earned her J.D. from the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law. While in law school, she served as a student attorney for the Criminal Defense and Wrongful Conviction Clinic where she represented clients pro bono in the Marion County D Felony Court, as well as worked on wrongful conviction appeals. She was a member of Phi Delta Phi legal fraternity and was selected as a pupil for the Indianapolis branch of the American Inns of Court. She received her Bachelor's Degree in Criminal Justice with minors in Psychology and Political Science from Indiana University. While at Indiana University, she was chosen to work for the Innocence Project as a research assistant, a cause which remains very important to her.

Stacy always wanted to be in a profession where she could help others which is what led her to practice law. As a Social Security Disability attorney, she prides herself on advocating hard for her clients while also being compassionate, straightforward, and honest with them. Prior to joining the Hankey Marks & Crider, Stacy worked as a criminal defense attorney in Bloomington, Indiana.

In June 2019, she traveled to Washington, DC, and was sworn into the Supreme Court of the United States Bar, which gives an attorney the ability to file a case with the High Court. She was honored to be sworn in by all members of the SCOTUS, including one of her personal heroes, Ruth Bader Ginsburg.

Mrs. Crider was born and raised in Columbus, Indiana. After getting married and having children, she and her husband, Bobby, moved back to the area. They built a home on a quiet piece of land, where they now reside with their three children, Sam, Max, and Millie. Stacy enjoys traveling with her family and providing fun and meaningful experiences for her children. In her spare time, Stacy loves to run, attend concerts, sing, kayak, and spend time relaxing with family and friends at any lake or beach.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Cross is a senior partner of the firm, a Certified Family Law Specialist-Family Law Certification Board, a Registered Family Law Mediator, and has been a fellow of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers since 1993. In 2011 she was appointed by the Supreme Court as a Commissioner on the State of Indiana Disciplinary Commission, is currently serving on the Legislative Committee of the Indiana State Bar Association, has served on the Board of Governors, and is a former Chairperson of the Family Law Section of the Indianapolis Bar Association. Ms. Cross has written numerous articles and lectured at family law seminars throughout her career. Ms. Cross is listed in The Best Lawyers in America (Woodward/White) and has been featured in Indianapolis Monthly magazine as one of the top ten divorce attorneys in Indianapolis. Beginning in 2005 and continuing to date, she has been recognized by Indianapolis Monthly as one of the 25 foremost female attorneys in Indiana and has consistently been named one of the state's Super Lawyers by Indianapolis Monthly since 2004. Ms. Cross has restricted her practice to family law, including divorce litigation, mediation and appellate work for more than 30 years. She is a 1979 graduate of the University of Nebraska College of Law and resides with her two sons in Zionsville, Indiana.

attorneys.name: Jay Curts
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law - Mergers and Acquisitions Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jay Curts joined Coots, Henke & Wheeler in 1988 and concentrates his practice in estate planning and administration, as well as business organizations and transactions. Jay's estate planning practice includes clients at every level of the estate planning spectrum, from newly married couples requiring an estate planning foundation for themselves and their children to those with more complex family/business inheritance, asset transfer, and estate tax issues. Jay listens to his client's objectives and works with them to develop documents representing a practical plan that clients understand.

His estate and trust administration practice emphasizes comprehensive attention to administration issues, including preparation of all necessary income and transfer tax returns to maximize economic benefit for heirs. Jay acts as counsel to either personal representatives/trustees in charge of the administration process, or beneficiiary/heirs seeking to understand their rights. Additoinally, Jay represents client in both the assertion and defense of estate/trust administration disputes and Will or Trust contests. He approaches litigation and negotiation strategies with a practical focus on his clients' desire for timely resolution and the best possible economic outcome.

Jay's business organizations and transactions practice includes counsel to clients during both the formation and management of their business with attention to issues concerning business succession planning for single owner and closely held business entities, business organization documentation and contract needs.

Jay is the Managing Partner at the CHW firm.

attorneys.name: Robert T. Dassow
attorneys.practice_type: Wrongful Death Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Robert T. Dassow was born in Sheboygan Wisconsin on January 4, 1965. He was admitted to the Indiana Bar in 1990. He is a graduate of Beloit College (BA Economics; Concentration Biochemistry, 1987). While there he was a Volrath Scholar and played three sports: basketball (captain), baseball, and tennis (captain). He lives in Indianapolis, Indiana with his wife Kathy (J.D. Indiana University, 1993 Summa Cum Laude) who also assists Rob on special projects, and their three children Reid (30), Jack (27) (J.D. Loyola University, 2023), and Ellie (26) (J.D. Harvard University, 2024).

Robert graduated from Valparaiso University School of Law (J.D. 1990) where he was an Articles Editor for the Law Review. He was also an Adjunct Professor of Business Law at Valparaiso University. He was also a Summer Intern for Chief Judge Loren A. Smith, U.S. Court of Federal Claims (formerly U.S. Claims Court). Rob not only is admitted to practice before all of the Federal and State Courts in Indiana but has also actively practiced in numerous State and Federal Courts across the country including the United States Court of Federal Claims.

Rob is one of the four partners of Hovde Dassow + Deets, an Indianapolis based law firm with over 50 years of experience in litigating complex defective product, personal injury cases, and wrongful death cases. Previously, he was a partner of the law firm of Siegel Carter & Dassow, and prior to that an associate at the law firm of Locke Reynolds. He received a Bachelor of Arts degree in Economics with a concentration in Biochemistry from Beloit College in Beloit, Wisconsin, and a Juris Doctor degree from Valparaiso University in 1990, where he was Editor of the Valparaiso Law Review and a Professor of Business Law at Valparaiso University. He is currently a Member of the American Bar Association, Federal Bar Association, Indiana Bar Foundation, American Association for Justice, Litigation Counsel of America, and a Board Member of the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association.

Mr. Dassow is admitted to practice before the bar in Indiana and admitted in the Northern and Southern District Courts of Indiana. He is also admitted to the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit. Rob is also admitted pro hac vice to practice in California, New Jersey, Tennessee, New York, Alabama, Louisiana, and New Mexico. He has represented thousands of clients in various mass torts, class actions, and other multidistrict litigation including third party payor litigation. While not a complete list, he has represented clients in the following mass tort cases:

In Re: Diet Drug Litigation, In Re: Vioxx Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Bextra Products Litigation, In Re: Avandia Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Trasylol Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Chantix Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Fosamax Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Kugel Mesh Hernia Patch Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Depuy Orthopaedics, Inc. Hip Implant Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Premarin/Prempro Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Yaz, Yasmin, Ocella Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Zoloft Products Liability Litigation, In Re Zyprexa Products Liability Litigation, In Re Transvaginal Mesh Products Liability Litigation, In Re Zimmer NexGen Knee Replacement Products Liability Litigation, In re Testosterones Replacement Therapy Products Liability Litigation, In re Johnson & Johnson Talcum Powder Products, In Re: Xarelto (Rivaroxaban) Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Depuy Orthopaedics, Inc., Marketing, Sales Practices, Johnson & Johnson Talcum Powder Litigation, Juul Litigation, Elmiron Litigation, Intuitive Surgical Da Vinci Robot and Products Liability Litigation, and RCA class action litigation.

For multiple years, Mr. Dassow has been selected Best Lawyers in America, Top 100 Plaintiff's Lawyer, Top 25 Mass Tort Lawyers, and a Super Lawyer in Mass Torts and Class Actions.

In 2013, Mr. Dassow was selected as National Liaison counsel for the Biomet Hip Implant Litigation where more than 2,000 cases were settled for an amount in excess of $160,000,000.00.

Mr. Dassow has also been co-lead in In Re Raptiva Litigation in Alameda County, California; a mass tort case involving a biologic agent used to treat psoriasis in 2015. He has served as Plaintiffs' Liaison Counsel in the Indiana State Court for the MDL 2545- Testosterone Replacement Therapy Production Liability Litigation in Illinois. Rob was also designated as co-trial counsel for Third Party Payor Claims in the Vioxx litigation.

In July 2018, Mr. Dassow was a member of the trial team with the Lanier Law Firm helped secure a $4.69 billion verdict on behalf of 22 women who alleged that decades of daily use of Johnson & Johnson's Baby Powder and Shower to Shower products have been laced with asbestos for decades, despite denials the company made to the federal Food and Drug Administration and others. Most proudly, as a result of the litigation, Johnson and Johnson removed Johnson’s baby powder from the market.

In May of 2019, Rob received a verdict of $11,600,000.00 in Gulf Shores, Alabama on behalf of a 24-year-old client who was rendered a quadriplegic after diving into shallow water. At trial, we successfully argued the Defendant's sales and marketing created the impression that the property was safe for diving and other water activities. Further, the existing warning was inadequate to advise renters of the dangerously shallow nature of the Little Lagoon.

In January 2020, Rob and his team obtained a $42,000,000.00 settlement with a national trucking company for the families of two people killed in a trucking crash in New Mexico.

In February 2023, Rob and his team obtained a $77,000,000.00 judgment and $6,500,000 punitive damage award against Edkar Pilot Car Services in a semi-tractor truck wrongful death of a driver and a young passenger.

Mr. Dassow is currently serving on the Plaintiff's Steering Committee for the National Collegiate Athletic Association Student-Athlete Concussion Injury Litigation-Single Sport/Single School (Football), MDL 2492, in the United States District Court Northern District of Illinois Eastern Division.
