Robert T. Dassow was born in Sheboygan Wisconsin on January 4, 1965. He was admitted to the Indiana Bar in 1990. He is a graduate of Beloit College (BA Economics; Concentration Biochemistry, 1987). While there he was a Volrath Scholar and played three sports: basketball (captain), baseball, and tennis (captain). He lives in Indianapolis, Indiana with his wife Kathy (J.D. Indiana University, 1993 Summa Cum Laude) who also assists Rob on special projects, and their three children Reid (30), Jack (27) (J.D. Loyola University, 2023), and Ellie (26) (J.D. Harvard University, 2024).

Robert graduated from Valparaiso University School of Law (J.D. 1990) where he was an Articles Editor for the Law Review. He was also an Adjunct Professor of Business Law at Valparaiso University. He was also a Summer Intern for Chief Judge Loren A. Smith, U.S. Court of Federal Claims (formerly U.S. Claims Court). Rob not only is admitted to practice before all of the Federal and State Courts in Indiana but has also actively practiced in numerous State and Federal Courts across the country including the United States Court of Federal Claims.

Rob is one of the four partners of Hovde Dassow + Deets, an Indianapolis based law firm with over 50 years of experience in litigating complex defective product, personal injury cases, and wrongful death cases. Previously, he was a partner of the law firm of Siegel Carter & Dassow, and prior to that an associate at the law firm of Locke Reynolds. He received a Bachelor of Arts degree in Economics with a concentration in Biochemistry from Beloit College in Beloit, Wisconsin, and a Juris Doctor degree from Valparaiso University in 1990, where he was Editor of the Valparaiso Law Review and a Professor of Business Law at Valparaiso University. He is currently a Member of the American Bar Association, Federal Bar Association, Indiana Bar Foundation, American Association for Justice, Litigation Counsel of America, and a Board Member of the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association.

Mr. Dassow is admitted to practice before the bar in Indiana and admitted in the Northern and Southern District Courts of Indiana. He is also admitted to the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit. Rob is also admitted pro hac vice to practice in California, New Jersey, Tennessee, New York, Alabama, Louisiana, and New Mexico. He has represented thousands of clients in various mass torts, class actions, and other multidistrict litigation including third party payor litigation. While not a complete list, he has represented clients in the following mass tort cases:

In Re: Diet Drug Litigation, In Re: Vioxx Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Bextra Products Litigation, In Re: Avandia Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Trasylol Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Chantix Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Fosamax Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Kugel Mesh Hernia Patch Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Depuy Orthopaedics, Inc. Hip Implant Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Premarin/Prempro Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Yaz, Yasmin, Ocella Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Zoloft Products Liability Litigation, In Re Zyprexa Products Liability Litigation, In Re Transvaginal Mesh Products Liability Litigation, In Re Zimmer NexGen Knee Replacement Products Liability Litigation, In re Testosterones Replacement Therapy Products Liability Litigation, In re Johnson & Johnson Talcum Powder Products, In Re: Xarelto (Rivaroxaban) Products Liability Litigation, In Re: Depuy Orthopaedics, Inc., Marketing, Sales Practices, Johnson & Johnson Talcum Powder Litigation, Juul Litigation, Elmiron Litigation, Intuitive Surgical Da Vinci Robot and Products Liability Litigation, and RCA class action litigation.

For multiple years, Mr. Dassow has been selected Best Lawyers in America, Top 100 Plaintiff's Lawyer, Top 25 Mass Tort Lawyers, and a Super Lawyer in Mass Torts and Class Actions.

In 2013, Mr. Dassow was selected as National Liaison counsel for the Biomet Hip Implant Litigation where more than 2,000 cases were settled for an amount in excess of $160,000,000.00.

Mr. Dassow has also been co-lead in In Re Raptiva Litigation in Alameda County, California; a mass tort case involving a biologic agent used to treat psoriasis in 2015. He has served as Plaintiffs' Liaison Counsel in the Indiana State Court for the MDL 2545- Testosterone Replacement Therapy Production Liability Litigation in Illinois. Rob was also designated as co-trial counsel for Third Party Payor Claims in the Vioxx litigation.

In July 2018, Mr. Dassow was a member of the trial team with the Lanier Law Firm helped secure a $4.69 billion verdict on behalf of 22 women who alleged that decades of daily use of Johnson & Johnson's Baby Powder and Shower to Shower products have been laced with asbestos for decades, despite denials the company made to the federal Food and Drug Administration and others. Most proudly, as a result of the litigation, Johnson and Johnson removed Johnson’s baby powder from the market.

In May of 2019, Rob received a verdict of $11,600,000.00 in Gulf Shores, Alabama on behalf of a 24-year-old client who was rendered a quadriplegic after diving into shallow water. At trial, we successfully argued the Defendant's sales and marketing created the impression that the property was safe for diving and other water activities. Further, the existing warning was inadequate to advise renters of the dangerously shallow nature of the Little Lagoon.

In January 2020, Rob and his team obtained a $42,000,000.00 settlement with a national trucking company for the families of two people killed in a trucking crash in New Mexico.

In February 2023, Rob and his team obtained a $77,000,000.00 judgment and $6,500,000 punitive damage award against Edkar Pilot Car Services in a semi-tractor truck wrongful death of a driver and a young passenger.

Mr. Dassow is currently serving on the Plaintiff's Steering Committee for the National Collegiate Athletic Association Student-Athlete Concussion Injury Litigation-Single Sport/Single School (Football), MDL 2492, in the United States District Court Northern District of Illinois Eastern Division.

attorneys.bio:
Melissa A. Davidson is an attorney at the Hankey Marks & Crider. She's been with our office since 2000, and handles cases in the areas of Social Security disability, long term disability, personal injury, ERISA and life insurance litigation. She also works with veterans by helping them with their VA disability claims.

She earned her law degree from Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law. She was a member of the Indiana International and Comparative Law Review and completed her studies in the evening while working for the office full time during the day. She earned her Bachelor's Degree in psychology from Ball State University.

Before becoming an attorney, she worked as an investigator for Child Protective Services in the Indiana Department of Family and Children. She also managed a group home for mentally challenged adults and worked at a treatment facility for mentally ill youth.

In her free time, she enjoys spending time with her family.

attorneys.name: Ashley N. Dayhuff
attorneys.practice_type: General Litigation Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Ashley was born and raised in Indianapolis, Indiana. She and her husband, Michael, are blessed with two beautiful children, Beau and Madelyn. Ashley started out her legal career in 2003 with an internship, which quickly turned into a job as a personal injury legal assistant from 2004-2008 during her undergraduate years at Indiana University Purdue University Indianapolis (IUPUI). Ashley obtained a bachelor's degree in psychology from IUPUI with a minor in criminal justice.

While an undergrad, Ashley received the Psychology Neel Award for graduating as the psychology major with the highest academic achievement. She then worked as a personal injury paralegal from 2008 to 2015. Ashley was admitted to the Bar in Indiana in September 2015 after obtaining her law degree from Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in May 2015. While a law student, Ashley excelled in her writing and oral classes. She was a Moot Court barrister in 2012, and she served as a Deans Tutorial Society (DTS) tutor from 2012-2014.

Ashley cares for her clients, and she is dedicated to maintaining open, prompt, and thorough communication at all times. Because Ashley worked her way up from internship to legal assistant to paralegal to attorney, she knows the ins and outs of litigation from start to finish, and she promises to work diligently, professionally, and passionately for each and every client. When not working, Ashley spends the majority of her time with her family. She is passionate about her Lord and Savior, her family, and her career, and she also enjoys reading and scrapbooking.

Jonathan R. Deenik is a Certified Family Law Specialist - Family Law Certification Board. He is also a trained collaborative lawyer, as trained by the Central Indiana Association of Collaborative Professionals. Jonathan is a registered Domestic Relations Mediator, and a Parenting Coordinator.

Jonathan served on the Executive Committee of the Family Law Section of the Indianapolis Bar Association for 11 years, including as Chair. Jonathan has been sought after to be a presenter a number of seminars for the National Business Institute and the Indianapolis Bar Association and the Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum.

Jonathan has represented medical, legal, accounting, financial, closely held business owners, family farms, executives and other professionals and spouses. Jonathan practices in both family law and estate planning.

Jonathan understands and appreciates that the best way to be successful in any family law or estate planning matter is to work as a team with his client. Jonathan knows the only way to work as a team is to maintain an open line of communication with his clients to best serve their evolving needs .

Jonathan resides with his Wife and three daughters in Center Grove. He is an avid golfer, though he swears he is much better at the practice of law.

attorneys.name: Nicholas C. Deets
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Nicholas C. Deets is a nationally recognized trial attorney and Partner at Hovde Dassow & Deets, focusing his distinguished legal career exclusively on representing plaintiffs in personal injury, medical malpractice, wrongful death, and product liability litigation. With over 80 jury trials taken to verdict, Nick is regarded as one of Indiana’s most experienced and respected trial lawyers.

He has successfully litigated and argued numerous high-profile and precedent-setting cases before both state and federal courts, including the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit and the United States Supreme Court. Notably, Nick played a key role in landmark decisions such as Cosme v. Erie Insurance (2024), which modified Indiana’s standard on directed verdicts, and Kosarko v. Padula (2012), further shaping the state’s tort law.

Nick's bar and professional affiliations are extensive. He is a past President of the American Board of Trial Advocates, Indiana Chapter, and an active member of the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association, Indiana State Bar, and the Indiana Bar Foundation. His fellowships in prestigious organizations such as the American College of Trial Lawyers, International Academy of Trial Lawyers, Indiana College of Trial Lawyers, and Litigation Counsel of America reflect his exceptional standing in the legal profession.

Nick's excellence has been widely recognized:

Best Lawyers® “Lawyer of the Year” in: Medical Malpractice Law – Plaintiffs (2020 and 2026)

Best Lawyers® “Lawyer of the Year” in: Personal Injury Litigation – Plaintiffs (2022)

Super Lawyers, Plaintiff's Personal Injury 2006-present, Top 10 Lawyer in Indiana (2024-present), Top 50 Lawyer in Indiana (2020-present)

Best Lawyers® “Lawyer of the Year” in: Mass Tort Litigation / Class Actions – Plaintiffs (2017)

Indiana Trial Lawyers Association’s Trial Lawyer of the Year (2010)

Recognized in The Best Lawyers in America® since 2010 in multiple categories including Personal Injury, Medical Malpractice, and Mass Tort Litigation

In addition to his trial accomplishments, Nick maintains a strong commitment to legal education and scholarship. He has authored and delivered impactful lectures and publications, including:

“Plaintiff’s Personal Injury Law: Practice Tips and Application”, National Business Institute

“Effective Closing Arguments on behalf of the Plaintiff”, presented to both the Indianapolis and Allen County Bar Associations

Scholarly articles in Verdict, covering state court venue under Indiana Trial Rule 75 and vicarious liability settlements

His commitment to justice extends beyond the courtroom. Nick has engaged in meaningful pro bono service, including representation of the families of Netherlands special forces members tragically killed in Indianapolis. He also served as President of Crooked Stick Golf Club (2013–2016), reflecting his engagement in community leadership.

Nick holds a Bachelor of Science in Industrial Management (B.S.I.M.) with honors from Purdue University (1989) and was admitted to the Indiana Bar in 1993.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Nicholas C. Deets is a nationally recognized trial attorney and Partner at Hovde Dassow & Deets, focusing his distinguished legal career exclusively on representing plaintiffs in personal injury, medical malpractice, wrongful death, and product liability litigation. With over 80 jury trials taken to verdict, Nick is regarded as one of Indiana’s most experienced and respected trial lawyers.

He has successfully litigated and argued numerous high-profile and precedent-setting cases before both state and federal courts, including the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit and the United States Supreme Court. Notably, Nick played a key role in landmark decisions such as Cosme v. Erie Insurance (2024), which modified Indiana’s standard on directed verdicts, and Kosarko v. Padula (2012), further shaping the state’s tort law.

Nick's bar and professional affiliations are extensive. He is a past President of the American Board of Trial Advocates, Indiana Chapter, and an active member of the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association, Indiana State Bar, and the Indiana Bar Foundation. His fellowships in prestigious organizations such as the American College of Trial Lawyers, International Academy of Trial Lawyers, Indiana College of Trial Lawyers, and Litigation Counsel of America reflect his exceptional standing in the legal profession.

Nick's excellence has been widely recognized:

Best Lawyers® “Lawyer of the Year” in: Medical Malpractice Law – Plaintiffs (2020 and 2026)

Best Lawyers® “Lawyer of the Year” in: Personal Injury Litigation – Plaintiffs (2022)

Super Lawyers, Plaintiff's Personal Injury 2006-present, Top 10 Lawyer in Indiana (2024-present), Top 50 Lawyer in Indiana (2020-present)

Best Lawyers® “Lawyer of the Year” in: Mass Tort Litigation / Class Actions – Plaintiffs (2017)

Indiana Trial Lawyers Association’s Trial Lawyer of the Year (2010)

Recognized in The Best Lawyers in America® since 2010 in multiple categories including Personal Injury, Medical Malpractice, and Mass Tort Litigation

In addition to his trial accomplishments, Nick maintains a strong commitment to legal education and scholarship. He has authored and delivered impactful lectures and publications, including:

“Plaintiff’s Personal Injury Law: Practice Tips and Application”, National Business Institute

“Effective Closing Arguments on behalf of the Plaintiff”, presented to both the Indianapolis and Allen County Bar Associations

Scholarly articles in Verdict, covering state court venue under Indiana Trial Rule 75 and vicarious liability settlements

His commitment to justice extends beyond the courtroom. Nick has engaged in meaningful pro bono service, including representation of the families of Netherlands special forces members tragically killed in Indianapolis. He also served as President of Crooked Stick Golf Club (2013–2016), reflecting his engagement in community leadership.

Nick holds a Bachelor of Science in Industrial Management (B.S.I.M.) with honors from Purdue University (1989) and was admitted to the Indiana Bar in 1993.

attorneys.practice_type: General Litigation Lawyers in Highland, IN
attorneys.bio:
History and Achievements

Mr. Dobosz was born in East Chicago, Indiana on September 24th 1963, graduating from Griffith High School in 1982, before moving on to study at East Tennessee State University, where he majored in psychology, and minored in political science and criminal justice. He started his academic career as a high-flyer, graduating summa cum laude in 1986, with the highest GPA in his graduating class, while acting as a member of Phi Kappa Phi.

His legal career began in 1989 when he was awarded his Juris Doctor from Indiana University School of Law, and he joined the Indiana Bar in the same year. He is now admitted to practice in the United States Federal District Court and the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana.

Areas of Law

Mr. Dobosz is dedicated to representing and counseling clients. He focuses primarily on personal injury cases, including those involving wrongful death, medical malpractice, automobile accidents, construction accidents, premises liability, and injuries arising from defective products.

He also has extensive experience in handling cases arising from worksite accidents, covering negligence of site managers and employers, as well as OSHA compliance issues, construction contracts, foreclosures, professional negligence, collections, and non-competition agreements.

In addition to personal injury cases, Mr. Dobosz is also highly skilled in all areas of estate planning, including issues with probate and elder law, real estate law, and corporate law. He has worked with countless clients to advise on managing trusts and wills, dividing assets, naming executors and beneficiaries, avoiding probate, and post-mortem estate planning. Litigation is also a strength, and Mr. Dobosz has represented clients in will and deed contests, will constructions, executor replacement, and decedent claims.

Previous Cases

In the past, Mr. Dobosz has represented plaintiffs against state and county governments, as well as doctors, nurses, hospitals and medical institutions, and insurance companies in both state and federal courts.

attorneys.name: Eric K. Doyle
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
As a former prosecutor for the Special Victims Unit in Marion County, I bring an exceptional combination of courtroom experience and a deep, empathetic commitment to individuals and families facing some of life’s most challenging situations. My years as a prosecutor provided invaluable insights and skills for navigating even the most complex and emotionally intense cases. Now, in family law, I draw upon that experience to support clients through difficult transitions, such as divorce, child custody, and other family-related disputes. My approach to legal advocacy is rooted in a dedication to achieving fair, just, and practical outcomes for each client, always balancing strong representation with compassionate guidance.

Throughout my career, I have encountered cases of varying complexity, and I understand how emotionally charged family law matters can be. Divorce and custody disputes, in particular, often bring heightened levels of stress and conflict. I am here to help alleviate that burden by being a steady advocate, providing knowledgeable counsel, and fostering a supportive environment where clients feel safe, heard, and understood. I strive to ensure that my clients' voices are always at the forefront of every decision and strategy we pursue together. My goal is to guide clients with clear, cost-effective solutions while remaining sensitive to the unique circumstances and needs of each case.

For me, family law is not simply about the legal process; it’s about creating a path forward for individuals who may be facing life-changing decisions and outcomes. Whether we are negotiating amicable resolutions through mediation or preparing for court in a contested divorce, I am here to provide the expertise and support necessary to protect my clients’ rights and promote the best possible future for them and their loved ones. Each case is unique, and I tailor my approach to meet the specific needs of my clients, working closely with them to understand their objectives and address their concerns every step of the way. Together, we work toward solutions that not only resolve immediate legal issues but also help to build a stronger, more positive foundation for the future.

On a more personal note, I was born and raised in Batesville, Indiana, and my journey in law began with a passion for advocacy rooted in my community. I completed my undergraduate degree at Indiana University, majoring in Political Science, and later attended law school at the Robert H. McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis, where I graduated with the honors of Barrister. Since my admission to the Indiana Bar, I have dedicated my career to serving individuals and families in the greater Indianapolis area. Currently, I live and work in Washington Township, where I continue to be an active member of the community.

Transitioning from criminal prosecution to family law, I was struck by the need for compassionate, client-centered representation in the family law field. Witnessing the profound impact that family legal matters can have on individuals’ lives, I recognized the urgent need for attorneys who not only understand the law but are also attuned to the emotional and personal toll these cases can take. This insight drives my commitment to providing empathetic and diligent representation. I work to empower my clients, helping them navigate difficult situations with clarity, strength, and the assurance that they are not alone in the process.

Every client’s case is unique, and I treat each one with the individualized attention it deserves. I believe that every person’s story matters, and I am here to listen, advocate, and champion the best interests of my clients and their families. My background in law, combined with a deep-rooted commitment to justice and fairness, has shaped my approach as an attorney and my dedication to helping clients find their way forward.

If you are looking for an attorney who will stand by your side and advocate for your rights with tenacity and compassion, I am here to provide the guidance and support you need. Family law can be complex and emotionally challenging, but together, we will work toward resolutions that promote healing, stability, and a positive future. With my support, you can face these challenges confidently, knowing you have an advocate who is dedicated to helping you achieve the best possible outcome.

attorneys.name: Madelyn Eastland Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
With divorce and family law matters can come overwhelming thoughts and feelings. It is important to have a compassionate attorney at your side to guide you through the process and provide the reassurance you deserve. Madelyn Eastland is a dedicated Associate Attorney with Stange Law Firm. Based out of our Indianapolis, Indiana office, she is prepared to represent clients throughout Marion County and surrounding areas.

Madelyn attended law school at Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis. She earned her Juris Doctor in May of 2020. During law school, Madelyn volunteered with the Neighborhood Christian Legal Clinic’s Project GRACE Expungement Help Desk, assisting individuals through the expungement process, conducting legal research, presenting a grant proposal, and providing services at community workshops.

Before joining the Indianapolis divorce and family lawyers at Stange Law Firm, Madelyn most recently served as a Staff Attorney at Indiana Legal Services, where she gained broad civil legal experience in housing, family law, and Medical-Legal Partnership teams, including discovery review, negotiations, and court representation. Her earlier experience includes Associate Attorney roles at two different Indiana-based law firms, where she advised clients across a variety of legal matters, conducted discovery review, negotiated case outcomes, and represented clients in a range of court proceedings. She also served as a Public Defender with the Marion County Public Defender Agency, where she represented indigent clients in criminal matters, advised them on constitutional rights and legal procedures, negotiated plea agreements, and appeared in various court proceedings including trials and motion hearings. With her strong legal background, Madelyn is ready to apply her skills to your family law matter.

Note: The choice of a lawyer is an important decision and should not be based solely on advertisements.

attorneys.name: Brandon C. Elkins
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Brandon C. Elkins-Barkley is a Certified Family Law Specialist, family law litigator, mediator, and parenting coordinator with practice and experience are uniquely tailored to complex asset division, including retirement benefits, and a child-focused approach to custody matters. Brandon provides comprehensive family legal services involving custody disputes, parenting issues, and property division, including high net-worth clients with business interests, complex employment benefits packages, and financial issues. Experienced in state and federal courts, Brandon holds a Masters of Law in Taxation from the University of Denver. While Brandon is a family law attorney with over a 15 years of experience, his practice has allowed him to represent clients in the Indiana Supreme Court, Indiana Court of Appeals, state trial courts, and in federal administrative appeals. Also, Brandon brings his unique experience of having worked in an international family law firm to his client matters involving disputes and issues reaching far beyond Indiana. Brandon regularly presents at continuing legal education seminars about retirement and employee benefits and how those assets are handled in divorce cases, as well as other topics.

A graduate of the Indiana University Maurer School of Law in Bloomington. As the child of parents who divorced in his infancy, Brandon has a direct and personal perspective on how the divorce process effects children , which guides him as a parenting coordinator. Brandon listens, cares, and always gives thoughtful, honest, and practical legal advice.

Your family dynamic is changing, and Brandon is here to provide a complete legal framework for minimizing the impact of those changes.

attorneys.name: James Alex Emerson
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Litigation Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Alex Emerson focuses his practice in civil litigation, public entity/government defense, and real estate.

Litigation:

Alex's civil litigation practice involves insurance defense, prosecuting and defending personal injury claims, pursuing creditors' rights, and representing clients in real estate and business disputes. Alex represents clients at both the trial and appellate level in state and federal court. Alex also has experience handling individual clients in state administrative hearings, including hearings related to a government agency's challenge to the individual's professional license and judicial review of adverse administrative decisions. In addition, Alex assists clients in resolving disputes via mediation, settlement negotiations, and other methods of alternative dispute resolution.

Public Entity/Government:

Alex represents public entities, elected officials, and employees in defending against civil rights, employment, and personal injury claims. Alex has defended police and sheriff departments and individual officers in cases involving excessive force, false arrest allegations, and jail conditions. Alex has also defended towns, cities, counties, and their employees from claims arising from regulatory action, contract disputes, land use, allegations of unlawful employment actions, and premises liability.

Real Estate:

Alex also focuses on representing individuals in disputes involving real estate, including negotiating sales of realty, landlord/tenant disputes, quiet title and adverse possession claims, and issues related to commercial and residential leases.

attorneys.name: Robert D. Esrock
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation and Appeals Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Robert D. Esrock is a senior associate at Clendening Johnson & Bohrer, P.C. admitted to practice in the State of Indiana, Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana, Eastern District of Michigan, and Eastern District of Wisconsin.

Robert’s practice focuses on civil litigation and appeals. His experience includes commercial and business litigation, insurance defense, construction litigation, personal injury litigation, landlord/tenant disputes, housing cooperative law, professional negligence, and land use and easement disputes. Robert has extensive experience handling complex discovery involving confidential and proprietary documentation and expert materials.

Prior to joining CJ&B, Robert worked assisting indigent and low income individuals in cases against landlords, lenders, and debt collectors.

Robert graduated from Indiana University Bloomington's Maurer School of Law in 2020, where he served as Chief Justice of the moot court executive board and was inducted into the Order of the Barristers. Robert also received the CALI Excellence for the Future Award in Trademarks and Unfair Competition and was a member of the Intellectual Property Association. He was the primary author of a moot court brief which qualified his team for oral argument in an international moot court competition, making his team the only U.S. participants to qualify. Robert’s other professional experience includes serving on the board of directors of the Madison Scouts Alumni Association.

Prior to law school, Robert attended the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music, where he studied piano performance and music composition. Robert is an accomplished pianist and has won numerous piano competitions, including winning best in the State of Missouri multiple times. He also has ranked among the top fourteen young pianists in the United States. Robert has experience teaching music and music theory and he has led music ensembles at all levels, including middle school, high school, college, and professional musicians. Robert’s other music experience includes participation in the Madison Scouts drum corps from 2010 through 2014, where he held several leadership roles, and performance with countless other individuals and groups.

attorneys.name: Jeremy L. Fetty
attorneys.firm_name: Parr Richey Frandsen Patterson Kruse LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Utility Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jeremy Fetty joined the firm in 2006. Mr. Fetty is currently on the Management Committee and Chair of the firm’s Utility and Business Section. Mr. Fetty’s practice focuses on utility law including energy, communication services, telecommunications, gas, water and waste management; corporate law; cooperative law; and right-of-way law.

Mr. Fetty advises businesses and utilities (for profit, non-profit and cooperative), on regulatory, day-to-day contract and transactional matters, and compliance issues. Mr. Fetty regularly advises businesses and utilities on matters such as Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission (“IURC”) matters, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC”) matters, Federal Communications Commission (“FCC”) matters, and Independent System Operator (“ISO”) and Regional Transmission Operator (“RTO”) matters. He has represented clients in FERC proceedings related to market based tariffs, formula rate tariffs, transmission, compliance, mergers and acquisitions/dispositions, rates and terms for wholesale electric service, qualifying facilities issues and standards of conduct and affiliate relationships, PURPA issues, electric and capacity market issues and RTO participation, particularly Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc., and PJM Interconnection. Mr. Fetty regularly represents utilities in various IURC proceedings related to energy, telecommunications, sewer, water and gas. He also regularly represents utilities with right-of-way issues, including railroad crossing issues.

Prior to joining the firm, Mr. Fetty worked in Detroit, Michigan, where he spent three years with the Michigan Court of Appeals, first as a research attorney then as a clerk to the Honorable Kathleen Jansen. While in Michigan, he assisted a Special Master in determining individual damages in a 42 U.S.C. § 1983 class action claim against the City of Detroit and assisted a well known arbitrator in the drafting of labor and employment arbitration opinions.

Mr. Fetty is admitted to practice law in Indiana and Michigan, the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit, the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, the Southern District of Indiana, the Northern District of Indiana, the Eastern District of Michigan, and the District of Columbia Court.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Jeremy Fetty joined the firm in 2006. Mr. Fetty is currently on the Management Committee and Chair of the firm’s Utility and Business Section. Mr. Fetty’s practice focuses on utility law including energy, communication services, telecommunications, gas, water and waste management; corporate law; cooperative law; and right-of-way law.

Mr. Fetty advises businesses and utilities (for profit, non-profit and cooperative), on regulatory, day-to-day contract and transactional matters, and compliance issues. Mr. Fetty regularly advises businesses and utilities on matters such as Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission (“IURC”) matters, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC”) matters, Federal Communications Commission (“FCC”) matters, and Independent System Operator (“ISO”) and Regional Transmission Operator (“RTO”) matters. He has represented clients in FERC proceedings related to market based tariffs, formula rate tariffs, transmission, compliance, mergers and acquisitions/dispositions, rates and terms for wholesale electric service, qualifying facilities issues and standards of conduct and affiliate relationships, PURPA issues, electric and capacity market issues and RTO participation, particularly Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc., and PJM Interconnection. Mr. Fetty regularly represents utilities in various IURC proceedings related to energy, telecommunications, sewer, water and gas. He also regularly represents utilities with right-of-way issues, including railroad crossing issues.

Prior to joining the firm, Mr. Fetty worked in Detroit, Michigan, where he spent three years with the Michigan Court of Appeals, first as a research attorney then as a clerk to the Honorable Kathleen Jansen. While in Michigan, he assisted a Special Master in determining individual damages in a 42 U.S.C. § 1983 class action claim against the City of Detroit and assisted a well known arbitrator in the drafting of labor and employment arbitration opinions.

Mr. Fetty is admitted to practice law in Indiana and Michigan, the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit, the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, the Southern District of Indiana, the Northern District of Indiana, the Eastern District of Michigan, and the District of Columbia Court.

attorneys.name: Sam Fife
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Sam Fife is a former prosecutor turned criminal defense attorney who brings a unique perspective to every case. He’s dedicated to defending clients and helping them move forward through expungements and experienced legal advocacy.

Sam’s law career started in 2018 after graduating from Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law. After graduating, he worked for the Marion County Prosecutor’s Office for a few years, prosecuting misdemeanors, felonies, homicides, and juvenile delinquencies. Sam desired a change in his life and felt the best way to do that would be to try and help make a change in others. In 2021, he joined a criminal defense firm where he vigorously defended clients charged with numerous different crimes all over the state of Indiana. Through the ups and downs Sam takes pride in being there for his clients every step of the way and feels confident that he dedicates an effort that others may not. Sam has also assisted hundreds of clients in getting their records expunged and takes great joy in helping people enter a new chapter of their lives, unburdened by their past mistakes. After a brief stint gaining some experience in civil litigation, he joined the Banks & Brower team as a Criminal Defense Attorney, satisfied that he joined a practice that shares his ethos in helping clients through their struggles.

With Sam having experience as both a prosecutor and a defense attorney, he can get a bird’s eye view of a case that other people may not have. He knows what the prosecution will be looking for and the angles they capitalize on. This allows him to assess the relative strengths and weaknesses of a case from both perspectives. This has benefitted his clients’ countless times, and he’s ready for it to benefit you, too. He has experience in almost every county in the state and vast experience litigating many types of crimes, giving him solid relationships with prosecutors.

Sam was born and raised in Fort Wayne, Indiana. He attended Northrop High School where he swam for his high school’s swim team. After high school he attended Indiana University and graduated in three years with a Bachelor’s of Arts in History. Sam then came to Indianapolis for law school, as he felt there was a greater need for his talents here. In his free time, Sam loves playing golf, exercising, watching his favorite sports teams, and being with family.

attorneys.name: Eleanor Finnell
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
With more than 15 years of experience as a litigator, Magistrate, and Senior Judge, Eleanor brings deep insight and empathy to every family law case. As a skilled mediator and dedicated advocate, she’s focused on achieving the best outcome while always seeing and supporting the person behind the case.

Eleanor was born and raised in Indianapolis, Indiana. She earned her undergraduate degree from Purdue University and obtained her law degree from Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis.

An innovative and experienced attorney, Eleanor brings a wealth of knowledge and experience to the family law practice, with extensive experience as a Magistrate Judge presiding over matters in all areas of family and juvenile matters. This experience has given her considerable empathy and understanding, allowing her to care about more than just the case, but the person behind it, too.

After serving as a Magistrate, Eleanor became, and still is, a Senior Judge presiding over matters throughout the State of Indiana. She is also a Registered Domestic Relations Mediator. She is a skilled negotiator and has proven time and time again that her expertise gives her an advantage over the situation, allowing her to bring the other party into agreement.

Eleanor has more than 15 years of experience in litigation, judicial proceedings, client management, and as a lead attorney in both State and Federal jury trials. Adept at presiding over complex cases, she has conducted depositions, issued legal rulings, and managed a caseload of 100+ active cases. Eleanor has a proven ability to develop mitigation strategies, pragmatic policies, and align legal strategy to drive positive outcomes. Never one to shy away from a trial, Eleanor is willing to do whatever it takes to get the outcome you deserve.

In addition to her extensive legal experience and capabilities, Eleanor excels at connecting with people, embracing diverse perspectives, and being a fearless advocate for her clients.

She is admitted to practice law in the State of Indiana and the U.S. District Court, Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana.

Eleanor resides in Marion County and is a proud mom of three children. She finds tremendous joy in supporting them in their academic and athletic pursuits. Eleanor has a long-standing commitment to community engagement. She has contributed to various civic leadership projects, including service as Board Member for a residential housing complex and former President of a Federal Credit Union for a faith-based community.

attorneys.name: Randy Fisher
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Randy Fisher has built a thriving practice at Hollingsworth Roberts Means, LLC and serves a diverse range of clients throughout Indiana. Mr. Fisher has extensive jury trial experience and has earned an exceptional reputation within the legal community for his trial skills. Mr. Fisher's clients benefit from the combination of his resilient work ethic, vast knowledge of legal issues, and an unsurpassed competitive drive for obtaining favorable results.

Based upon talent, reputation, and most importantly, proven results, Mr. Fisher is consistently retained on high-profile matters. Many of his criminal cases have attracted significant media attention. These matters typically include major felony charges, complex and challenging fact patterns, and matters of local and even national intrigue. In fact, Mr. Fisher has represented several professional athletes and celebrities on various legal issues.

Additionally, Mr. Fisher has established himself as a fierce litigator and trusted advocate on civil matters, including family law and business matters. Clients benefit from Mr. Fisher's professional and systematic approach to case preparation, his remarkable abilities to construct and negotiate comprehensive resolutions, and a willingness to take matters to trial, if necessary.

Mr. Fisher's talents extend beyond the courtroom into his appellate practice. Mr. Fisher has successfully briefed and argued cases to the Indiana Court of Appeals and the Indiana Supreme Court.

Past Experience

Mr. Fisher previously practiced as an Associate Attorney with the Indianapolis firm of Riley Bennett & Egloff, LLP, from 2005-2006. While at Riley, Bennett & Egloff he practiced in the areas of Civil and Commercial Litigation, Business and Employment Law, Insurance Defense, Intellectual Property, Contract Disputes, Mergers and Acquisitions.

Mr. Fisher began his legal career as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney in Allen County, Indiana, 38th Judicial Circuit, serving the community from 2003 to 2005. While with the Allen County Prosecutor's Office he litigated State handgun crimes as the "Gun Prosecutor" under a Federal Firearms grant funded by the United States Department of Justice and Project Safe Neighborhoods.

attorneys.name: Adrienne Flannery
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law, Probate, Medicaid Lawyers in Lawrenceburg, IN
attorneys.bio:
Adrienne M. Flannery was born and raised in Lawrenceburg, Indiana. Adrienne began her legal practice in 2010 as an associate attorney. She left her prior firm in 2016 to start Miller Flannery Law LLC where she is managing partner.

Adrienne represents individuals in planning their estates, long-term care and family law. She has a comprehensive knowledge base of Social Security law, Medicare and Medicaid.

Adrienne graduated from Indiana University in 2007 and the University of Dayton School of Law in 2010. Adrienne represents individuals in planning their estates, probate, long-term care, and family law. She also represents non-profit organizations. Adrienne served as a court-appointed GAL for children and adults in domestic relations matters and guardianships for several years. She is qualified to serve both as a parenting coordinator and a domestic relations mediator. This combination of experience provides Adrienne with a unique background to assist clients with difficult family law matters involving chiildren. Adrienne works with individuals experiencing divorce or custodial issues.

Adrienne also works in the area of divorces with no children. She represents both men and women and is skilled in navigating areas of dispute to attempt to reach a resolution in the most efficient way possible. Adrienne works to gather the appropriate information in a timely manner to work to make sure that family law cases progress as smoothly as possible.

In 2019, Adrienne became legal counsel for the Dearborn Community Foundation, a charitable non-profit community foundation that advances charitable giving in Dearborn County, Indiana.

Adrienne has served in several leadership positions locally. She was a member of the Board of Directors for Youth Encouragement Services, (YES) Home. She was the President of Dearborn/Ohio County Bar Association. She served on the Southeast Indiana Chamber Foundation Board as Secretary/Treasurer. She is a past President of the Dearborn County Clearing House for Emergency Aid Board of Directors and she previously served on the Board of Directors for the Hoosier Hills Literacy League. She volunteered with the Greater Cincinnati Big Brothers Big Sisters was named Site-Based Big Sister of the Year in 2016. She also served as a board member with the North Dearborn Food Pantry. Currently, Adrienne volunteers legal services with several local non-profits by providing free and reduced legal services when needed.

Adrienne is passionate about representing charitable entities, working with the disabled, as well as estate planning for minor children. She enjoys advocating for families in difficult situations. She lives in Dover with her husband, Nick, their children and dogs. She loves spending time with her family attending soccer games and enjoying the outdoors.

attorneys.name: Katherine Elizabeth Flood
attorneys.practice_type: divorce Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Indianapolis divorce attorney Katherine E. ("Kate") Flood is a distinguished G. Kent Frandsen scholar and a cum laude graduate of the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law. As a family law lawyer, Ms. Flood has concentrated her practice on dissolution, legal separation, relocation, child custody, paternity, parenting time/visitation, spousal maintenance/alimony, and guardianships.

In dissolution actions, Kate concentrates on child-related matters, taking a very active and engaged role when it comes to her clients and their children. She also places great emphasis on the financial matters that accompany divorce: analyzing, valuing, dividing, restructuing and protecting marital assets. Her experience extends to the application and drafting of prenuptial and post-nuptial agreements, protective orders, restraining orders, post-secondary education issues, and all post-dissolution matters. Kate is certified in Collaborative Law.

Ms. Flood has a breadth of litigation experience, including representing clients at evidentiary hearings and trials before paternity courts, IV-D Support Enforcement courts, and family law courts in counties throughout central Indiana. She also has experience with alternative dispute resolution both as counsel representing clients involved in the mediation process, and as a civil mediator. In addition, Kate has co-authored appellate legal briefs submitted before the Indiana Court of Appeals.

As a student of the IU McKinney School of Law, Kate was active within the Dean's Tutorial Society, being selected as the Director of the One-on-One Tutoring Program during her third year. Kate was also a faculty research assistant, and served as the Spanish language translator/interpreter for the law school's Civil Practice and Health & Human Rights Clinics. Ms. Flood holds the distinction of being named a G. Kent Frandsen scholar, and was prominently featured in the premier issue of "The McKinney Lawyer," the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney Alumni Magazine. Read the article featuring Kate on page eight, here.

During law school, Ms. Flood also worked as law clerk to the Honorable Judge William Hughes of the Hamilton Superior Court, performed transactional work for the Indiana Economic Development Corporation, and she participated in a medical-legal partnership initiative with Wishard Health Services, wherein healthcare providers and legal professionals worked together to provide comprehensive patient care to low-income individuals in Indianapolis.

Kate is a Butler University alumna, earning a degree in English Literature cum laude as well as a degree in Spanish with high honors. While attending Butler, Kate earned the Elaine Blaine Rudolph Scholarship Award, was named to Butler University's Top 100 Students in 2006, and was inducted into a number of academic honor societies.

Kate is admitted to all Indiana Courts, as well as the Northern and Southern District Courts of Indiana.

attorneys.name: Andrew Flores
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Hammond, IN
attorneys.bio:
Andrew Flores is an Associate Attorney at Westland & Bennet P.C. Born and raised in Northwest Indiana, he earned his undergraduate degree from Indiana University Northwest and his law degree from Valparaiso University School of Law.

After graduating from law school, Andrew began his legal career as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney in Tippecanoe County. In that role, he prosecuted criminal traffic cases and enforced child support obligations, gaining practical courtroom experience and insight into Indiana’s criminal and family law processes.

Andrew later transitioned to private practice with a general practice firm in Lake County. His work focused on criminal defense, estate planning, expungements, and assisting clients with the restoration of driving privileges. He now brings that combined public service and private practice backrgound to Westland & Bennett P.C., where he is committed to offering clear, dependable, and solutions-focused representation.

Outside the office, Andrew enjoys playing guitar and spending time with his family and friends.

attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Matt is an attorney with Mallor Grodner Plummer practicing estate planning, business selection, formation, governance, and succession planning.

Matt earned his Bachelor’s degree from Indiana State University and his J.D. from Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in 2015, both with honors.

A native of Indiana, Matt was a partner with a law firm in Peru, Indiana where he provided clients, many that were family-owned businesses, with representation related to estate planning and farming operations, including taxation, succession, and retirement.

Matt’s passion is ensuring that each client’s wishes are carried out, and that family-owned businesses prosper now, and well into the future. Accomplishing those goals takes a willingness to understand each family’s particular dynamics, a high attention to detail, a commitment to working with each family’s other advisors, and a thorough knowledge of the tax code. Each plan is different. He enjoys meeting new families and their advisors, to help them structure the best plans possible.

Outside of his work at the firm, Matt enjoys spending time with his wife and three daughters, coaching/attending his daughters’ events, watching the Green Bay Packers, and working around the house.

attorneys.firm_name: Parr Richey Frandsen Patterson Kruse LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Lebanon, IN
attorneys.bio:
Kent Frandsen has practiced with the firm since 1977 concentrating in civil litigation, zoning and land use, electric utility, and education law. Following graduation from law school, Mr. Frandsen served as a law clerk to The Honorable James E. Noland, Judge of the United States District Court for the Southern District of Indiana.

Mr. Frandsen has tried nearly 100 civil jury trials in state and federal courts, representing both plaintiffs and defendants. He has presented briefs in more than 30 appeals in state and federal courts. He has also served as the panel chair in over 200 medical malpractice panel proceedings administered by the Indiana Department of Insurance. Mr. Frandsen is a certified civil mediator and has conducted nearly 100 civil mediations over the past several years. He has also served as an arbitrator for the American Arbitration Association in both construction and tort disputes. He currently serves as general counsel for two central Indiana school districts as well as the Indiana CPA Society, Inc.

attorneys.name: Dustin F. Fregiato
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Dustin Fregiato was born and raised in a small town in Eastern Ohio. Growing up in "Coal Country", as it is commonly known to those who live there, not only taught him the value of a hard day's work but also taught him his core values of: faith, family and friendship and how they should be applied to every aspect of one's life, including one's career. Dustin left that small town to attend undergraduate studies at The Ohio State University. After graduating cum laude with a BA in political science at OSU, he moved to Indianapolis to attend law school at the Indiana University McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis. While there, Dustin focused his legal education on litigation and trial practice, clerked for the Marion County Prosecutor's Office and later for Marion County Judge Carol Orbison.

Dustin began working with Ladendorf Law as a law clerk in 2010. At Ladendorf Law he quickly learned to appreciate the practice of representing injured clients and the relationship a trial attorney's practice has to those core values he learned in his hometown. After graduating from the Indiana University McKinney School of Law, Dustin continued working at Ladendorf Law as an Associate Attorney where he has remained to the present. Throughout his time as an attorney, Dustin has represented and been successful in obtaining the needed compensation for clients impacted by wrongful death, medical malpractice and injuries of all kinds. He understands the frustration and anguish an injury can cause to a family that extends well beyond the superficial bruise or broken bone and uses his knowledge about this intricate area of law to fight for his clients.

Dustin is licensed to practice before the Indiana Supreme Court as well as the Northern and Southern Districts of the United States District Courts of Indiana and is a Certified Civil Mediator under Indiana A.D.R. Rule 2.5. Dustin has authored "The Indiana Medical Malpractice Act's Statute of Limitations" which appeared in the Indiana Trial Lawyer's Associations': Verdict and was a speaker in the spring of 2015 at the Indiana Trial Lawyer Association's Lifetime Achievement Awards' Ceremony. Dustin's practice areas include personal injury, premises liability, medical malpractice and wrongful death.

attorneys.name: Craig Fugate
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Craig Fugate is the managing partner and co-founder of the firm. Craig is a business, franchise and real estate attorney licensed to practice law in Indiana. His practice focuses primarily on assisting franchisees and other entrepreneurs in transactional law including franchisee representation, business structuring, entity organization, financing transactions, acquisitions and sales of businesses, drafting and reviewing contracts, and real estate lease and purchase transactions.

Craig was admitted to the bar in 2008. Since 2008, Craig has worked in and with small and medium sized companies as well as Fortune 500 companies. In 2012 Craig formed Fugate Legal which became Fugate Gangstad in 2019.

Craig provides general counsel services to several small businesses, represents new and existing franchisees in franchise purchases and renewals, advises his clients in real estate lease and purchase transactions, and helps entrepreneurs form their business entities and draft the necessary documents to protect their assets.

Additionally, Craig uses his MBA in finance and his business experience to advise clients on general business issues enabling them to have expert business advice without having to hire a consultant or another employee. Craig enjoys becoming an integral part of his clients' businesses.

Craig is a member of the American Bar Association's Forum on Franchising and Business Law Division.

attorneys.name: Jerry A. Garau
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jerry Garau represents individuals in medical malpractice and serious personal injury claims. He was named Indiana Trial Lawyer of the Year by the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association in 2019 after securing a $15 million verdict in a medical malpractice action and having that verdict affirmed by the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit. Webster v. CDI Ind., LLC, 917 F3d 574 (7th Cir. 2019). He is a fellow of the American College of Trial Lawyers, an invitation-only fellowship of exemplary trial lawyers from the U.S. and Canada. Membership in ACTL is limited to 1% of the total lawyer population in the U.S. and Canada. He is also a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates, is listed in the Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers, and has been named an Indiana Super Lawyer every year since 2012.

Jerry began his career in 1986 after graduating with honors from the Indiana University School of Law at Indianapolis. He has secured verdicts for individuals throughout the state of Indiana, and has argued before the Indiana Court of Appeals, the Indiana Supreme Court, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit. He has served on the executive committee of the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association and is currently secretary of the organization.

In 1997, Jerry and four other attorneys started a firm focused on representing victims of medical malpractice. That firm, now known as Garau Germano, P.C., has its offices in Indianapolis and represents individuals throughout the state. In addition to the firm's work in medical malpractice, the firm also represents individuals in claims involving serious personal injury, sexual abuse, and nursing home negligence.

Gard is an attorney at the firm who represents individuals, families, and organizations in a wide array of business law matters, including business formation, transactions, employment law, and real estate transactions. He provides strategic counsel to closely-held business owners and fiduciaries in the areas of business and estate planning, probate and trust administration, and taxation.

Drawing on his background in business management, Gavin brings a practical, business-oriented approach to his work, particularly when advising clients on complex issues such as business planning, mergers and acquisitions, and succession strategies. As a dedicated, client-centered attorney, Gavin is committed to fostering long-term relationships with his clients, helping them resolve legal issues and find practical solutions to their legal challenges. Outside of the office, he enjoys spending time with family and friends, golfing, and studying leadership and management practice through books and podcasts.

attorneys.practice_type: Business Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Named one of Indiana's Super Lawyers by the Indianapolis Monthly Magazine, Bob Garelick concentrates in the areas of business, personal injury, and domestic relations litigation.

Mr. Garelick graduated cum laude from Indiana University in 1963, and its law school in 1966, where he served as a writer for the Indiana Law Journal. He is qualified to mediate civil and domestic relations disputes under Rule 2.5 (A) (2) of the Rules of the Supreme Court of Indiana. He has presented lectures and papers on Alternate Dispute Resolution and Trial Practice to the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association, Indianapolis Bar Association, Continuing Legal Education Forum, and for the National Business Institute, Inc. Bob is a member of the Academy of Family Mediators, and has served as Secretary of the Alternate Dispute Resolution section of the Indianapolis Bar Association.

Mr. Garelick completed a two-year term in 1994 as President of the Indianapolis Law Club, which consists of 150 experienced trial lawyers whose membership is by invitation only. He also has been Vice President of the Indianapolis Bar Association, President of the Indiana University Law Alumni Association, and Chairman of the Indiana State Bar Association, Federal Judiciary Committee.

attorneys.name: Carla Vittoria Garino
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Westfield, IN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Carla V. Garino has served clients for nearly two decades. She has significant experience in negotiation, litigation, and in handling complex jury trials. As an attorney with Webster Legal, LLC, Carla focuses her practice on divorce and family law, business law and litigation, estate planning and administration, and special needs planning and guardianships.

Previously an owner of a fitness franchise, Carla offers a unique perspective to business owners to help them avoid and address potential legal issues. She also enjoys assisting individuals in following their dreams to establish new businesses and in helping clients take steps to avoid the associated legal pitfalls.

Carla graduated summa cum laude and with Honor’s from Butler University in Indianapolis, Indiana, with majors in both English and Latin. She then obtained her Law Degree from the Indiana University Maurer School of Law, graduating magna cum laude. During law school, Carla served as an Articles Editor and Associate Member with the Indiana Law Journal and was a member of the Women’s Law Caucus, Public Interest Law Foundation, and Children’s Law Discussion Group. Carla began her legal career with the United States District Court for the Southern District of Indiana as a Law Clerk for the Honorable David F. Hamilton, now a Judge with the Seventh Circuit.

Carla is admitted to the Indiana State Bar and has been admitted to practice before the United States District Court for the Southern District of Indiana and the United States District Court for the Northern District of Indiana. She is a member of the Westfield Chamber of Commerce.

In her free time, Carla enjoys all topics related to health and wellness, including cooking, nutrition, and running, as well as spending time with family and friends.

attorneys.name: Douglas A. Garner
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Lawrenceburg, IN
attorneys.bio:
Douglas graduated from the University of Cincinnati College of Law in 1991 after earning his B.A. in History from the same university in 1988. He began his legal career as a contract Public Defender in Hamilton County, Ohio, and later worked as an associate at Beirne & Wirthlin.

In 1994, Douglas returned closer to home and opened his private practice in Dearborn County, Indiana, where he also served as a Public Defender in the Dearborn County Superior Court until 2001. Since then, he has focused his practice on Social Security Disability and Criminal Defense, while also representing local non-profit organizations, small businesses, and the Dearborn County Solid Waste Management District.

Douglas’s dedication to the legal profession extends beyond his practice. He served on the Indiana Public Defender Council Board of Directors from 1996 to 2008, including two years as Chairman, and taught trial skills at the Indiana Public Defender Trial Practice Institute for five years. He is also a member of the National Organization of Social Security Claimants’ Representatives.

Equally committed to his community, Doug serves on the Board of Directors of Heart House, Inc. and LifeTime Resources, and has been recognized with awards for his volunteer legal services and advocacy for older clients.

When he’s not working, Doug enjoys cooking, boating, and reading, and most of all, spending time with his wife and daughter. With decades of legal experience and a passion for helping others, Doug looks forward to guiding his clients through life’s challenges with knowledge, dedication, and care.

attorneys.name: Thomas J. Gaunt
attorneys.firm_name: Thomas J. Gaunt Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Litigation Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Gaunt is a long-term resident of the Indianapolis area. He earned his J.D. from the University of Toledo, distinguishing himself as a recipient of an American Jurisprudence Award for excellence in a specific subject matter. Since admission to the bar in 1996, Gaunt has been a civil and criminal litigator in both State and Federal Courts and has extensive bench and jury trial experience as lead counsel.

He approaches every case as if it is the most important matter in a client's life, because most of the time, it is.

As counsel for a class action suit, he successfully negotiated a Federal Court class settlement on behalf of well over one hundred class members.

He has served as lead trial counsel on many hundreds of cases, across nearly half the counties in Indiana. Many of these cases ended without a trial through successfully negotiated compromises. Those which did go to trial include a number of successes, including verdicts in city, state, and the United States District Court (Southern District).

He has received favorable trial pronouncements against a leading bank and against one of the larger national car rental companies.

Deeply satisfying for Mr. Gaunt, he has enjoyed a pattern of helping clients win to gain or contest custody of their children in a number of cases across many court jurisdictions in both paternity and divorce litigation.

Attorney Gaunt has won favorable verdicts and outcomes, including dismissals with prejudice, in many county prosecutions across the state.

attorneys.name: Rebecca W. Geyer
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Rebecca W. Geyer is the founder of Geyer Legal Group, PC where her practice concentrates in estate planning, estate and trust administration, elder law, tax planning, and business services. A board certified Indiana trust and estate specialist* and a Fellow of the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel, Rebecca is also an adjunct professor of elder law at the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law.

Rebecca completed her undergraduate degree at Indiana University, majoring in Political Science. She went on to earn her Juris Doctor in 1998 at the Indiana University Maurer School of Law. An avid volunteer in both the legal community and the Indianapolis community at large, Rebecca often speaks and writes on estate planning and elder law topics, and annually provides pro bono legal services to individuals through her work with the Indianapolis Bar Association, the Albert and Sara Reuben Senior Resource and Community Center, and the Shepherd’s Center of Hamilton County.

As a frequent lecturer and seminar presenter, Rebecca has authored numerous seminars with ICLEF, ALI-CLE, ISBA, and IBA. Her recent presentations include “Estate Planning for Medicaid Benefits,” “Tips for Unwinding Irrevocable Trusts,” “Trust Decanting,” “Maximizing Social Security Benefits,” “Estate Planning with Retirement Plans,” “Alternatives to Guardianship,” and “Estate Planning for Same-Sex Couples in Light of Obergefell and Dobbs.”

Rebecca is Chair of the Indiana Chapter of the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel, served as 2023 President of the Indianapolis Bar Association, is Past President of the Indianapolis Bar Foundation, former Chair of the Estate Planning and Administration Section of the Indianapolis Bar Association, former Chair of the Elder Law Section of the Indiana State Bar Association, and a Past President of the Indiana Section of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys (NAELA). She served on the Board of Governors of the Indiana State Bar Association from 2016-2018. In 2023, Rebecca was recognized as one of the 250 most influential business leaders in Indiana by the Indianapolis Business Journal. Since 2014, Rebecca has been named to the prestigious list of Super Lawyers® for estate planning, and has been designated as one of the top 50 attorneys in Indiana and one of the top 25 women lawyers in Indiana since 2016 by Law & Politics Magazine and Indianapolis Monthly. Since 2022, Super Lawyers® has recognized Rebecca as a top 10 attorney in Indiana. In 2018, Rebecca was recognized by the Indianapolis Bar Association for service to the profession, and was awarded the Indianapolis Bar Association’s Dr. John Morton Finney Award for Excellence in Legal Education in 2013. Rebecca also volunteers in the community where she serves as President of the Congregation Beth-El Zedeck Foundation, Treasurer of the Indianapolis Section of the National Council of Jewish Women, and a member of the Public Policy Committee for CICOA.

Rebecca’s professional memberships also include the Estate Planning and Administration Section of the Indianapolis Bar Association, the Probate, Trust and Real Property Section and the Elder Law Section of the Indiana State Bar Association, the Indiana Probate Review Committee, Estate Planning Council of Indiana, and the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys. Rebecca was recognized as a distinguished fellow by the Indianapolis Bar Foundation in 2010.

*Certified by the Indiana Trust and Estate Specialty Board

attorneys.name: Brandi A. Gibson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Brandi A. Gibson concentrates her practice in family law. Brandi has a wide range of courtroom and trial experience, which she utilizes as a Registered Civil Mediator and Family Law Mediator.

Brandi represents clients in all areas of family law, including divorce, legal separation, custody, parenting time, child support, paternity, emancipation, post-decree modifications and enforcement (including contempt actions), relocation, education orders, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, contested adoptions, protective orders and restraining orders. Brandi frequently serves as a Family Law Mediator. Brandi is also a Guardian Ad Litem and a Parenting Coordinator.

Brandi also has litigation experience involving diverse areas of law including insurance defense, premises liability, motor vehicles accidents, civil rights, school liability, construction litigation, real estate disputes, and employment disputes and discrimination. Brandi has represented cities, towns, townships and counties throughout the State of Indiana and works closely with local municipal and governmental officials to defend their interests. She has defended numerous governmental entities, police departments and police officers in cases involving false arrest and excessive force claims, police action shootings, police pursuits, jail conditions, and premises liability claims.

attorneys.name: Heather Gilbert
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Valparaiso, IN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Heather Gilbert joined Langer & Langer as a highly skilled defense attorney with a deep commitment to helping those who have been hurt or wronged find justice. She has gained valuable experience during in nearly two decades of private practice and public service. In addition to providing her clients with skilled counsel on medical malpractice and negligence matters, her matters include wrongful death cases in Indiana and Illinois at various stages from pre-suit investigation through trial. Heather regularly engages in alternative dispute resolution, including mediations and settlement conferences, and presents arguments before the trial court and appellate court. Kindness, enthusiasm, and determination are the core values that she brings to her life and her work.

Previously, Heather handled complex matters for Illinois law firms focused on general civil litigation and medical malpractice. She represented clients in a wide range of civil actions including general negligence, transportation, catastrophic injury, premises liability, product liability, breach of contract, wrongful death, medical/professional negligence, and civil rights. Of note, she represented professionals before administrative agencies, including the Indiana Department of Insurance, Indiana Attorney General/Licensing Boards, Illinois Department of Professional Regulation, and EEOC.

attorneys.bio:
Kendra G. Gjerdingen chairs the firm's Appellate Law Group and handles the legal needs of private and business clients in civil litigation and family law. Her concentration includes family law and jurisdiction, interstate and international custody disputes, appeals, and civil litigation.

Kendra is a leading family law and appellate lawyer in Indiana. She also has extensive experience in jurisdictional disputes. She has represented many clients in Hague Convention cases, as well as those involving interstate custody disputes, in addition to assisting fellow practitioners and members of the judiciary in understanding the complexities involved when parents live in different states or countries.

Kendra utilizes the Family Law Group's team approach to assure that a client's needs are addressed quickly and efficiently. Kendra is a successful litigator with extensive courtroom experience. She also brings her compassion and knowledge to each case, as well as her attention to detail and dedication to civility in the practice of law. Kendra is an advocate of alternative dispute resolution, especially in family law, understanding the importance of reducing conflict in order to reach desired results.

Kendra is a Registered Family Law Mediator and a Certified Family Law Specialist, by the Family Law Certification Board. She is a past-chair of the Indiana State Bar Association Appellate Practice Section. She is a past member of the council of the Family and Juvenile Law Section of the ISBA. Kendra is married to a law professor at the Indiana University Maurer School of Law, and they have two children and three granddaughters.

attorneys.name: Erick T Gjerdingen
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Erick T. Gjerdingen is the Managing Partner of Mallor Grodner Plummer Attorneys and represents individuals and organizations in a wide range of business law matters. Erick regularly represents clients in the purchase and sale of businesses and their assets, real estate transactions, complex commercial litigation and reorganization, high asset divorce cases, and state and federal appeals. He routinely serves as an outside general counsel to his clients as needs arise and enjoys learning the nuances of his clients' needs and business operations to tailor effective legal strategies and to assemble an effective and efficient team of professionals from across disciplines.

Erick's representative clients include Members of Congress; financial and financial services institutions; software and other technology providers; casinos, hotels, and tourist resorts; construction companies; airlines and related entities; breweries; liquidating trusts and creditors' committees; Ponzi-scheme victims and fraudulent transfer defendants; artists and athletes; high asset individuals and private clients; and non-profit and religious organizations. Also representing auto dealers, he is a member of the National Association of Dealer Counsel (NADC).

Erick is admitted in both Indiana and Nevada. He received his law degree from the University of Arizona's James E. Rogers College of Law and has additional degrees from Harvard University and Carleton College. Prior to becoming a lawyer, he served as a faculty member at a major public university in Thailand.

Erick serves as the President of the Board of Directors of BCT Management, Inc., a private nonprofit organization that manages the historic Buskirk-Chumley Theater, a performing arts center and downtown anchor in Bloomington currently celebrating its centennial.
