attorneys.name: Mark A. Glazier
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
For over 25 years, Mark Glazier has been guiding professionals, business owners, high income earners, individuals with significant net worth, and the spouses of these individuals through complex divorce and family law matters.

Business valuation experience

As a business owner, Mark understands the hard work and risk incurred by owners and entrepreneurs to achieve financial success. He brings his best efforts to each matter to ensure that his client's interests are considered in resolving marital disputes. Mark has extensive experience with complex financial issues incident to divorce such as valuing closely held companies and the tax ramifications associated with divorce.

Executive compensation experience

Mark has worked with many executives, and the spouses of high-profile executives, in complex divorce and child custody proceedings. He understands that discretion is of the utmost importance and works to maintain the integrity and reputation of each client. Mark has experience with many facets of executive compensation involved in family law and divorce cases, including stock options and stock grants, retirement and benefits packages, and other intangible benefits beyond the tax return.

Family farm and landholder experience

A native Hoosier, Mark realizes that landholdings for farm families are part of a legacy of stewardship and must be protected for the prosperity of future generations. He assists multi-generational farm families with negotiating prenuptial agreements, complex estate planning considerations, and if needed, divorce and child custody proceedings. His work for farm families is done with an appreciation of the land and its value to the entire family.

Mark’s approach

Using both a strategic and pragmatic approach, Mark aims to minimize risk while working toward acceptable resolutions. He has conducted over 500 mediations and is trained in collaborative divorce resolution. Having this training and experience furthers his ability to help individuals navigate through the frequently turbulent waters surrounding the dissolution of their marriage and a change in their family dynamic.

For over 25 years, Mark has been a presenter and a panelist at seminars instructing other lawyers on a myriad of diverse issues related to family law such as how to cross examine a psychologist when there is an adverse custodial evaluation to issue spotting when dividing retirement assets.

As the father of four, Mark brings a deep understanding of how different children have different needs and how different parenting styles may have completely different effects on children. He is sensitive to the issues that a stay at home parent will encounter upon having to re-enter the workforce due to an impending divorce. He has extensive experience in custody cases involving the potential relocation of one parent. Understanding these dynamics coupled with the experience of trying scores of contested custody and parenting time disputes enables him to provide seasoned and practical counsel to individuals with families in conflict over children.

Mark is the son of an Eagle Scout, is an Eagle Scout, and is the father of an Eagle Scout. The values learned in Scouting continue to guide his professional and personal life. Mark's clients know that when they are enduring potentially one of their most difficult experiences, he will be there with them every step of the way to counsel them with integrity, sensitivity and with his best efforts and experience.

Jill Goldenberg Schuman concentrates in the areas of family law and alternative dispute resolution.

Jill is certified by the Indiana Certifying Organization of the Indiana Bar Association as an Indiana Certified Family Law Specialist. She is a registered domestic mediator. Since undergoing mediation training in 2002, she has mediated 100’s of cases. She has also served as a family law arbitrator. Ms. Goldenberg Schuman devotes the majority of her practice to family law matters or mediations and arbitrations involving family law matters. She has been a lecturer in various family law and alternative dispute resolution topics for the Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum and has several published family law appellate decisions. She was recognized in 2007 - 2016 as a Best Lawyer in her field of family law and was also recognized in 2008-2016 as a Super Lawyer in her field. From 2011-2016 she was selected as one of Indiana’s Top 50 Super Lawyers and in 2009-2016 as one of Indiana’s Top 25 Women Super Lawyers.

attorneys.name: Alan Goldstein
attorneys.practice_type: Building Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Alan Goldstein practices primarily building and construction law. He counsels clients regarding design professional, general contractor, construction management and subcontract agreements, guaranteed maximum price formulas, design-build contracts, construction joint ventures, fast track and phased delivery methods and green construction. He represents construction industry clients in the negotiation, mediation, litigation and arbitration of construction disputes.

He drafts and negotiates contracts for major construction projects throughout the United States including NFL stadiums, NBA arenas, convention centers, airport facilities, school and university buildings, high-rise office towers, hospitals, extended care facilities, laboratories, clean room facilities, manufacturing plants, apartment complexes and office parks. Among these projects are Lucas Oil Stadium (home of the Indianapolis Colts); the Wier Cook Midfield Terminal and related improvements for the Indianapolis International Airport; Tampa Arena, Tampa, Fla.; Pro-Players Stadium, Miami, Fla.; Thunder Dome, St. Petersburg, Fla.; Cleveland Browns Stadium, Cleveland, Ohio; Bradley Center, Milwaukee, Wis.; Banker's Life Fieldhouse, Indianapolis, Ind.; the Indiana Convention Center, Indianapolis, Ind.; Merrill Lynch Corporate Campus, Plainsboro, N.J.; Procter and Gamble Corporate Headquarters, Cincinnati, Ohio; Chase Tower, Market Tower and One American

Square, Indianapolis, Ind.; Tower Center, East Brunswick, N.J.; One Liberty Place, Philadelphia, Pa.; and Syracuse University Science and Technology Center, Syracuse, N.Y.

As lead counsel in major trials, arbitrations and virtually every form of alternative dispute resolution, he prosecutes and defends delay, acceleration, interference, liquidated damage claims and breach of contract claims. His trial and arbitration experience also includes a broad range of technical design and construction defect disputes including excavation, piling, foundations, concrete, structural systems, curtain walls, masonry, mechanical/electrical systems, roofing and mechanics lien and bond issues.

He also serves as trial and arbitration counsel in business litigation matters including real estate and corporate disputes and breach of contract actions.

Alan is a native of Indianapolis, Indiana. He received his Bachelor of Arts in English literature from Indiana University in 1965 and his juris doctorate, cum laude, from Indiana University H. McKinney School of Law in 1969.

He is admitted to practice law in the state of Indiana and before the 7th Circuit Court of Appeals and United States Supreme Court.

Speaking Engagements

In addition to his practice, Goldstein has written for and lectured at numerous professional seminars on the subjects of civil procedure, evidence and construction law. From 1971 until 1980, he was an adjunct professor of law at the Indiana University School of Law-Indianapolis where he taught courses in civil procedure, evidence and conflicts of law.

attorneys.bio:
Adedoyin Gomih is a principal at the law firm of Adedoyin Gomih, LLC, a law firm in Merrillville, Indiana that handles all kinds of civil law cases. The firm services clients in Lake County, Indiana, as well as clients throughout the state of Indiana.

Her practice areas cover the areas of Business and Commercial Law, Business Formation, Personal Injury, Real Estate transactions as well as plaintiff side employment related issues.

Attorney Gomih is uniquely qualified to handle all kinds of business related issues because of her maturity and her business background. Her business clients include small to medium size businesses, especially family owned businesses.

Our law firm is available and accessible to answer questions regarding your business, or assessing the viability of your claim if your injury is the result of someone else’s wrong doing, or if you are a consumer who has been defrauded by a merchant, or you have been the victim of false misrepresentation by a seller of any consumer good.

We respond to all telephone calls immediately, or within a 24- hour period, for calls received after business hours.

Please call our office for a free consultation on your issue at 219-472-9037.

attorneys.name: Marek Grabowski
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Marek brings a wealth of experience and perspective to his practice, thanks to his background, education, and work for the federal and state government as well as in the private sector. Although he loves solving legal puzzles, Marek understands that for his clients, legal problems fundamentally are expensive and confusing obstacles that can bring normal life to a halt. Marek strives to remove these obstacles in the most efficient way possible, drawing on his extensive experience in both litigation and transactional work. Marek has worked on all sides of taxation disputes, as an administrative law judge for the Indiana Board of Tax Review, as a staff attorney for state tax authority, and as a representative of individual and business clients. He has successfully litigated taxation matters involving oil and gas companies, governmental contractors and Indian tribes, and has negotiated inter-govermental agreements pertaining to confidential taxpayer data. In addition to tax work, Marek has worked as an in-house counsel for a logistics company, where he drafted the company's family and medical leave policies and renegotiated commercial leases. In federal government, Marek has served as an ethics and clearance counsel to the President of the United States, where he was granted top secret security clearance by the government. His work involved evaluating candidates for Senate-confirmed and other government positions, as well as ensuring that existing government officials complied with federal ethics requirements. Having returned to private practice, Marek now focuses on business transactions, taxation and litigation.

Born and raised in Poland, Marek is fluent Polish and has served as a translator in court. After immigrating to the United States, Marek's family settled in the Pacific Northwest. Marek eventually left for Minnesota, where he studied history at Carleton College, taught English as a second language (ESL), and received distinction for his thesis on the post-war experiences of World War II Polish resistance fighters. After a brief but eventful stint working as an independent contractor for a cable TV mapping business, Marek went on to earn his juris doctorate at the Yale Law School, where he worked for the school's small business clinic, assisting local clients with initial business formation and business reorganization. After graduating law school, Marek went on to work and live throughout the United States as his wife completed her medical education, residency and oncology fellowship. Marek and his family are now happily settled in Carmel, Indiana.

Marek has been admitted to the bar in Indiana, New York, New Mexico and Illinois.

attorneys.name: Roy James Graham
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Roy earned his B.A. in Criminal Justice in 1986 and his J.D. from IU School of Law in Bloomington and is licensed to practice law in Indiana since 1991.

Roy services Monroe and surrounding counties, including, but not limited to Bartholomew, Brown, Owen, Lawrence, Morgan, Martin, and will travel further if need be.

Roy always puts his client's interests first.

Roy has over 30 years experience in both criminal matters and some litigation experience as well.

Roy has been a resident of Monroe County for almost 40 years.

He has written several appeals and has tried several cases in front of a jury.

In addition, he serves as Special Public Defender in Owen, Monroe and Brown County.

Roy also has a diverse and interesting personal history.

He came to Bloomington, Indiana, in 1974 to attend the IU School of Music, and studied percussion with world renowned Professor George Gaber.

By 1978, Roy had become involved in the local community managing some rental homes and rehabbing two older homes in rural Monroe County.

Roy owned his own bakery.

In 1981, Roy purchased and operated the long-established Busy Bee Bakery, a scratch bakery, for almost three years.

To top it all off, Roy still plays the piano and composes his own classical pieces!

Secretary Sheriff's Monroe County Merit Board, 1992 - 1996

Preeminent Rating through Martindale

attorneys.bio:
Rob Grant is a graduate of Indiana University (economics) and is a graduate of its law school. His practice areas include Litigation, Subrogation, Creditors Rights, Estate Planning and Probate, and Corporate Business Matters.

He is admitted to practice in Indiana, including all federal courts, the United States Tax Court, United States Court of Military Appeals and the U.S. Supreme Court.

Rob served as an instructor at Indiana University's School of Continuing Studies for 18 years in the area of wills, trusts and estate planning and has served as an instructor in numerous continuing legal education courses in the areas of creditor's rights, subrogation and probate practice for the Indianapolis Bar Association, Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum (ICLEF) and the National Association of Subrogation Professionals (NASP).

Rob is a member of the Indiana State Bar Association, the Indianapolis Bar Association, the National Association of Subrogation Professionals and served on the Board of Directors and Executive Committee of the Greater Indiana Alzheimers Association. He is a veteran of both the Army and Air Force.

attorneys.name: Carolyn (Cari) Small Grant
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
As a former Assistant U.S. Attorney, Cari understands trial work. She has recovered statutory limits for her client in a medical malpractice action before proceeding before the full Indiana Medical Review Panel. Conversely, she has defended doctors in a medical malpractice action for the delivery of a brain damaged baby. On behalf of an insurance company client, she recovered hundreds of thousands of dollars from a third-party tortfeasor for workers compensation benefits paid to an injured employee. Cari recovered EPA cleanup cost assessed against land leased decades earlier to a trucking company. She practices in both state and federal courts.

Cari has served on the executive boards of both the Indianapolis Bar Association and the Indianapolis Bar Foundation. She was the first woman to chair the Litigation Committee of the Indianapolis Bar Association. She has served on the Indiana Supreme Court Disciplinary Commission's investigatory Grievance Committee for more than 25 years. Cari co-chaired the initial Settlement Week program, sponsored by the Indianapolis Bar Association, for several years which introduced mediation to Marion County state courts and was the precursor to the Indiana Supreme Court promulgating the alternative dispute resolution rules. She also served on the Board of Directors for the National Association of Subrogation Professionals (NASP).

Numerous community Boards and committees have benefited from Cari's participation including the Board of Directors for the Horticultural Society of the Indianapolis Museum of Art, Broad Ripple Village Association Board of Directors, the American Lung Association of Central Indiana, and the YWCA Board of Directors.

She has argued before the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit and the Indiana Court of Appeals resulting in numerous published opinions. With this experience, Cari has taught seminars for the Indianapolis Bar Association, Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum, and the NASP conference.

Snyder v. United States, IP 84-1658-C, by the Medical Center Director, V.A. Hospital, North Chicago; U.S. Attorney’s Bulletin, Vol. 34, No. 13, December 15, 1986

attorneys.bio:
“The purpose of human life is to serve, and to show compassion and the will to help others.” — Albert Schweitzer

Sarah Graziano was born and raised in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, but has called Indiana her home since graduating from Valparaiso University School of Law, with honors, in 1999. Sarah began her career focusing on litigation for a well-respected defense firm in Indianapolis, but she quickly realized that her true focus was to help people who have disputes with corporations, insurance companies, and the like. attorneys.name: Betsy K. Greene
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Over her decades in practice, Betsy has earned deep trust from clients and colleagues. She meets every client personally to understand their story, loss and goals. From that first meeting, she focuses on practical solutions that reflect both the legal and human sides of each case.

Betsy believes strong advocacy begins with preparation. She studies every detail, meets with witnesses and builds clear, honest presentations that juries can follow. Her approach combines skill, persistence and respect. Clients describe her as steady during a crisis and tireless in pursuit of fairness.

Each case receives her full attention. Betsy guides her clients through complex legal and insurance issues with patience and transparency. She values communication and keeps clients informed at every stage. Her focus is not only to win cases but also to help people rebuild their lives after tragedy.

Recognition And Leadership

Betsy holds Civil Trial Advocacy certification from the National Board of Trial Advocacy, a credential that recognizes tested skill and ethical standing in the courtroom. She served as past president of both the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association and the Indiana Chapter of the American Board of Trial Advocates.

Her peers have recognized her work in multiple independent listings. Super Lawyers® has selected her for inclusion in the Indiana Super Lawyers list each year since 2005. In 2019, she was listed as Indiana’s #1 Super Lawyer, and she continues to appear among the Top 10 Super Lawyers in the state. She has also been named a Distinguished Barrister by Indiana Lawyer and received national honors such as the Marie Lambert Award from the American Association for Justice Women’s Trial Lawyer Caucus and the Howard Twiggs Commitment to Justice Award from the AAJ.

Outside the courtroom, Betsy invests time in mentoring young lawyers and teaching trial advocacy at continuing education programs nationwide. She supports community projects that promote fairness, education and access to justice.

attorneys.name: Geoffrey M. Grodner
attorneys.practice_type: Business Formation Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Geoffrey M. Grodner oversees the firm's business and professional practice services, including business formation, transactions, employment law and litigation. Geoff has been selected as an Indiana Super Lawyer in the area of business for fifteen years.

As part of his business practice, Geoff represents new and used automobile dealers in Indiana, Ohio, Illinois, Michigan, Kentucky, and Florida. He is recognized for his extensive knowledge of the auto business and is a member of the National Association of Dealer Counsel, an organization of attorneys that devote significant portions of their practice to representing dealers.

Also as part of his business practice, Geoff represents medical and other professionals on business matters including professional practice business planning, succession planning and acquisitions, sales and mergers.

Geoff brings to his practice a unique understanding of the problems and issues regularly faced by businesses and professional practices. He understands clients need aggressive representation, while at the same time seeking creative and cost effective resolutions. Geoff is adamant about the law firm providing quality legal services at every level and maintaining a high standard of client service.

Geoff is the former Counsel to the United States Senate Subcommittee on Constitutional Amendments. He has served on the Boards and as President of numerous not-for-profit organizations, including Indiana's Ivy Tech Community College, several arts organizations, and is frequently asked to provide legal advice to not-for-profits on business matters. Geoff has also frequently served as Chairperson or a member of the faculty for continuing legal education seminars, including master's series seminars for advanced practitioners.

Outside the practice of law, Geoff maintains a strong interest in motor vehicles, golf, and food. Geoff is an accomplished cook and is regularly involved in food activities and programs with professionals in the food world. Geoff has been married to Lorelei Meeker for over 40 years, they have an adult son and a dog.

attorneys.name: Shelley Gupta
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Shelley Gupta was born in Maryland and raised in Fort Wayne, Indiana. She attended Bryn Mawr College, outside of Philadelphia, PA, where she studied philosophy, specifically ethics and ancient political philosophy, graduating in 2009. While at Bryn Mawr, Shelley received the Joy Simonson Internship Grant, which allowed her to intern with the Indiana Pro Bono Commission with the Indiana State Bar Association. She then continued her education at Ohio Northern University, College of Law in Ada, OH, graduating in 2012. While at Ohio Northern, Shelley received the Public Interest in Law Fellowship, which allowed her to intern at the Marion County Prosecutor’s Office. Shelley was admitted to practice in the Indiana State and Federal Courts in October 2012.

Shelley worked in the public sector for 12 years prior to joining Hensley Legal Group, PC. For the first six years of her career, Shelley served as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney in Elkhart and Marion Counties, handling traffic court, misdemeanors, major felony sex crimes, child support matters, and unemployment insurance fraud.

In 2019, Shelley joined Health and Hospital Corporation of Marion County’s Environmental Court Team, where she was Senior Counsel and supervisor. She worked to enforce the health code. Shelley ensured the residents of Marion County were not in conditions that posed a health and safety risk. She loved that she made a visible difference in the community and had a positive impact on the residents of Marion County.

Shelley was appointed to the Judges and Lawyers Assistance Program by the Indiana Supreme Court in July 2025. Additionally, she is an active member with the Indiana State Bar, in which she co-chairs the Diversity Committee. Shelley has also successfully completed the Indianapolis Bar Leadership Series (2018) through the Indianapolis Bar Association and the Leadership Development Academy (2025) through the Indiana State Bar Association.

In her free time, Shelley enjoys crafting, reading/listening to audio books, rock climbing, and binging shows on streaming.

attorneys.name: Jenifer O. Habecker
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Greenwood, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jenny has had the privilege of providing representation for individuals and government entities since 1985. She began her career in general practice as a partner in a small Texas law firm focusing on criminal defense and family law matters. She later transitioned to work as a major felony prosecutor and was the director of a drug task force. While practicing in Texas, Jenny developed one of the first legal aid clinics staffed by volunteer attorneys, which received statewide recognition. Upon moving to Indiana, she returned to assisting diverse clients in family law representation, as well as probate and estate work.

After practicing in Michigan, she served as a Commissioner for the Marion County Circuit Court, where she exclusively worked in the Court’s paternity division. Following her departure from the bench, she now provides assistance to individuals navigating divorces, custody and parenting time matters, child support issues, and guardianships with Deenik Lowe. Jenny’s work is through direct representation in the courtroom, as well as a guardian ad litem, mediator, and collaborative law practitioner. Representing a wide array of people over her many years in practice has taught her that each case is as unique as the people involved and deserves specific attention. Her practice takes her to all of the counties surrounding Marion County, and to some further away.

Jenny and her husband enjoy biking Indiana’s trails and visiting their adult children in Maine and Oregon. A strong proponent of civic engagement and democracy, Jenny can be found every Election Day working at the polls and also as a judge for the Indiana Bar Association’s We The People program. As an avid backyard birder and naturalist, Jenny serves on the Board of the Indiana Audubon Society, and is always happy to help others discover the wonders of Indiana’s natural beauty. When she is not outside, she enjoys trying new recipes, attending all types of theater events, or simply falling into a good book.

attorneys.name: Ashley N. Hadler
attorneys.practice_type: Nursing Home Abuse Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Ashley Hadler focuses her law practice on representing survivors and families affected by nursing home abuse, sexual abuse, and medical malpractice. Ashley handles cases throughout Indiana and Illinois. She grew up in Greensburg, Indiana and attended college and law school in Indiana. After law school, Ashley lived in Chicago where she represented victims of nursing home negligence and medical malpractice against some of the largest hospitals and nursing home chains in the Midwest.

She returned to Indianapolis in 2017 to continue helping people who were injured by abuse, neglect, and malpractice. Ashley's unique background in science, psychology, and health law benefits her clients who have suffered from trauma and have complex medical issues. She understands the issues faced by kids and adults who are injured where they live, are educated, are coached, or receive medical treatment.

Ashley often speaks to group of attorneys, victim advocates, and survivors of abuse about the legal options available to survivors and their families. She knows how to find people and businesses that may be held accountable for abuse and how to find sources of compensation available to survivors.

Ashley's clients range from children to the elderly. She has experience handling sexual abuse and assault cases against churches and religious organizations, residential care facilities, daycares, schools, and sports teams. As a woman and a mother, Ashley brings an important female perspective to litigating civil abuse and neglect cases.

Ashley is a board member of the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association, and a member of the Illinois Trial Lawyers Association and the American Association for Justice. She is a volunteer guardian for the Indianapolis Center for At Risk Elders (CARE). She is a past vice-chair of the Young Lawyer's Council of the National Crime Victims Bar Association and an active member of the Prevent Child Abuse Indiana Advisory Board. Ashley spends her free time with her husband, their son, and Poppy the French Bulldog.

attorneys.name: Stephanie Jane Hahn
attorneys.firm_name: Stephanie Jane Hahn, Attorney at Law PC
attorneys.practice_type: Employment and Labor Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Stephanie Jane Hahn is an employment law attorney practicing in Indiana. Her practice is primarily dedicated to the compassionate representation of employees who are victims of discrimination based on gender, race, disability, age and religious affiliation. Ms. Hahn represents employees in respect to other legal matters impacting their employment as well, including sexual harassment, pregnancy discrimination, hostile work environment, violations of the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), wrongful termination, retaliation, claims under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA), in addition to wage and hour violations under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA).

Ms. Hahn received her Juris Doctor from Valparaiso University. While attending law school, she was part of the school's moot court team and competed nationally on behalf of the law school and the moot court team in the Civil Rights Moot Court Competition in 1995. She was admitted to practice law in the state of Indiana and before the Northern and Southern District Courts of Indiana in 1995. The following year, she was admitted to appear before the 7th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. Ms. Hahn is a member of the Indiana State Bar Association and currently serves as a member of the Executive Board of the Employment and Labor Law Council. Widely respected by her peers, she is a frequent lecturer on a wide array of employment law topics at seminars and workshops for attorneys and other professionals.

With nearly 20 years of employment law experience and an established record of dedication to her clients in the state of Indiana, Ms. Hahn has represented clients in federal and state courts as well as before administrative bodies and commissions, including the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC). Her experience includes the negotiation and drafting of employment contracts, severance agreements, and nondisclosure and noncompete covenants and agreements. In addition, she has trained unionized employees, including employees of an international Fortune 500 company, on matters relating to employment discrimination, retaliation and their rights under various state and federal employment laws. Her wide-ranging experience makes her a compelling figure both in and out of the courtroom and is a testament of her dedication to her clients

attorneys.name: Joshua Hains
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce & Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Joshua Hains is a seasoned family law attorney who has spent nearly two decades guiding clients through life’s most personal and pivotal transitions. Before joining Hollingsworth Law Group, Josh built and ran his own successful practice, where he earned a reputation for his steady presence, practical wisdom, and genuine care for the people he serves. His work reflects the very heart of “Divorce Done Differently” — combining skillful advocacy with compassion, clarity, and respect.

Josh’s practice includes the full range of family law matters: divorce, child custody and support, parenting time, adoptions, guardianships, spousal maintenance, protective orders, and pre- and post-nuptial agreements. He is deeply committed to keeping clients informed, empowered, and supported at every stage of the legal process, helping them find solutions that protect both their present stability and their future peace of mind.

An Indiana native, Josh earned his Bachelor of Arts in Economics with a minor in Psychology from Wittenberg University in Ohio, where he also played soccer and was an active member of Beta Theta Pi. He went on to earn his Juris Doctor from Valparaiso University School of Law in 2006. Since then, he has represented clients in family law, civil litigation, and even federal criminal defense — experience that gives him a well-rounded perspective and strong advocacy skills.

Outside the courtroom, Josh is passionate about giving back to his community. He has volunteered with the Volunteer Lawyer Network, Kids’ Voice of Indiana, and the Indianapolis Bar Association’s Pro Bono Standing Committee.

Josh, his wife, and their two daughters live in Carmel with their two dogs and two cats. In both his personal and professional life, Josh leads with integrity, kindness, and a deep dedication to family — values that make him a natural and invaluable part of the HLG team.

attorneys.name: Brandon Hall
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accidents Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Brandon received his bachelor's degree in English from UCLA in 2004 and previously worked in the health care industry. His experience there taught him how careful and precise health care professionals have to be to protect their patients and that mistakes in the healthcare field can cost lives.

Brandon went on to earn his Juris Doctor at Indiana University's Maurer School of Law in Bloomington. While attending Maurer, he worked as a legal intern for the city of Indianapolis at the Office of Corporation Counsel's four departments, the City Prosecutor, Counseling, Equal Opportunity, and Litigation.

His abilities in legal research and writing in addition to his professional experience led him to an Associate Instructor position for Legal Discourse and Writing at Maurer.

Brandon graduated law school and started his professional legal career at a small personal injury and work injury firm, Shean Law. There he exclusively represented injury victims and Hoosiers who had been injured on the job.

Brandon has continued to advocate on behalf of all kinds of injury victims throughout Indiana and has worked hard to represent those who are facing giant insurance companies and giant corporations. Brandon is passionate about representing injured workers and knows that it isn't easy to find an attorney who regularly practices in the workers compensation specialty area of the law. He believes that is all the more reason to keep helping injured workers in Indiana because he knows that they are at a disadvantage.

When he's not working, Brandon is a dedicated family man who enjoys spending time with his wife and two daughters.

You can email Brandon at brandon@greeneschultz.com

attorneys.name: Richard M. Hall
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Richard Hall is an attorney in Mallor Grodner Plummer Attorneys’ private client practice group and has been practicing law for more than 40 years. Richard represents individuals, families, closely-held business owners, and fiduciaries in the areas of business law and transactions, estate planning, probate and trust administration, farm and business succession planning, and taxation. During his career, he has been involved in more than 250 transactions involving sales, reorganizations, and acquisitions of business and investment properties. His background in accounting and business management has proven to be invaluable when counseling clients and businesses regarding transactions and tax matters.

Richard received his JD from the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law, in 1981, and his undergraduate degree in business, with a major in accounting, from Indiana University, Bloomington. He is a certified public accountant (inactive status).

Richard has spoken at professional seminars and advisor meetings on topics ranging from estate planning, trust administration, fiduciary taxation, and farm and business succession planning. He is a member of the Indianapolis Bar Association and previously served as Chair of the Estate Planning and Solo/Small Firm Sections of the Indy Bar. Richard has been listed in the Martindale-Hubbell registry of preeminent lawyers and named to the Indiana Super Lawyers list for Estate Planning and Probate 18 times.

Richard and his wife, Lisa, live in Brown County, Indiana, and share three adult children.

attorneys.name: Joel D. Hand
attorneys.practice_type: Administrative Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Joel Hand has over 25 years of experience as an Indiana attorney and an impressive list of accomplishments.

Criminal Law & Traffic Law

Joel Hand has broad experience not only as a criminal defense attorney but also as a deputy prosecuting attorney in three different Indiana Counties - Marion County, Hamilton County, and Carroll County.

Trials: Mr. Hand has conducted over a hundred jury trials and hundreds of bench trials, from misdemeanors to major felonies to murder. He has prosecuted or defended charges of drug dealing, drug possession, marijuana possession, illegal firearms and handgun possession, domestic violence, battery, neglect of a dependent, theft, shoplifting, conversion, operating while intoxicated (OWI), operating while intoxicated (OWI) causing death, operating while intoxicated (OWI) causing serious bodily injury, driving while intoxicated (DWI) or driving under the influence (DUI), robbery, burglary, and many more.

Other criminal proceedings: In addition to trial work, specialized driving petitions, petitions for rescission of lifetime suspension, probation violations, community corrections violations, and expungements.

Traffic offense experience: As a prosecutor in Marion County, Joel created the concept and obtained federal grant funding for the Fatal Alcohol Crash Team (F.A.C.T.), interviewed and selected all the F.A.C.T. law enforcement officers, and served as the team's first prosecuting attorney and as liaison to the Marion County Traffic Safety Partnership. He also served as the first Hamilton County's F.A.C.T. prosecutor and as liaison to the Hamilton County Traffic Safety Partnership. In 2004, Mr. Hand was named as the first ever Indiana Traffic Safety Resource Prosecutor for the Indiana Prosecuting Attorneys Council where he provided training to police and prosecutors throughout Indiana and across the country. Since going into private practice, Joel has defended numerous moving and non-moving traffic violations including speeding, reckless driving, driving without a license, driving on a suspended license, leaving the scene of an accident, operating as a habitual traffic violator (HTV) and more. He assists clients with license reinstatements and specialized driving privileges (or SDPs, previously called hardship licenses). His clients include those with commercial driving licenses (or CDLs). He understands how vital it is for CDL drivers to keep TSA points off their record and works closely with several trucking companies to assist their drivers.

Education Law

Growing up in a family of educators, Joel has long had a special interest in education issues. In fact, his college education included a minor in secondary education, and he previously held an Indiana teacher's license. He has worked for the Indiana Department of Education as Legal Counsel and as Director of Legislative and Governmental Relations. In private practice he handles 504 hearings and appeals and Special Education Case Conference Committee meetings; Development of Individual Education Plans (IEPs), Student Discipline (suspensions and expulsions) hearings and appeals; and hearings and appeals for suspension or revocation of teacher licenses.

Administrative Law

When Joel was Legal Counsel at the Indiana Department of Education, he served as an administrative law judge and, in addition to the administrative matters discussed above, he handles a variety of matters in state administrative agencies, including hearings and appeals with the Bureau of Motor Vehicles; Indiana State Police (Fire Arms Licensing - Appeals for denials of fire arms permits), Department of Workforce Development hearings and appeals; Indiana Physical Therapy Board (Licenses for Physical Therapists), Department of Education (Teacher Licensing appeals) and unemployment insurance hearings and appeals.

Lobbying

Mr. Hand is a registered legislative lobbyist in Indiana and works on behalf of clients in the Indiana General Assembly. He can work successfully on both sides of the political aisle, draft proposed legislation, and amendments to benefit his clients, or oppose legislation that would hurt his clients.

attorneys.name: Lanae M. Harden
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Litigation Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Lanae Harden is a founding member of HARDEN JACKSON, LLC where she practices family law litigation with more than 15 years of experience in complex family law litigation, including contested custody matters. She chairs the firm's Family Law Practice Group.

Ms. Harden received her Juris Doctor magna cum laude from Indiana University School of Law, finishing in the top 5% of her class. Ms. Harden completed her undergraduate degree at the University of Texas at Austin, where she graduated magna cum laude and was a member of the university's tennis team. She is also a four-time Indiana State Tennis Champion.

Ms. Harden is a skilled litigator and extremely adept at managing heavy caseloads. With extensive trial experience, she has successfully represented a diverse clientele from stay-at-home mothers to professional athletes. Ms. Harden's professional career includes 9 years at one of Indianapolis' larger law firms where she was the only attorney who practiced exclusively in the area of family law. She has also worked in the area of "father's rights".

Ms. Harden's practice philosophy involves developing a specific strategy with each client in order to proceed to final hearing in the best possible position. She thoroughly evaluates her clients' cases in order to determine what is in their and their children's best interests. She frequently utilizes expert witnesses including accountants, bank officers, school officials, mental health professionals and daycare providers to obtain necessary evidence for hearing. As an assertive advocate and trusted advisor, Ms. Harden is able to provide a professional, yet personal level of service for her clients during a difficult and emotionally draining period.

Ms. Harden is a member of the Indianapolis Bar Association, the Indiana State Bar Association, and the Hamilton County Bar Association, for which she serves on the Executive Committee. Ms. Harden has been recognized by her peers for her professionalism and experience, having been named a Super Lawyer by Super Lawyers Magazine in 2010 and 2011.

Ms. Harden resides in the Indianapolis area with her husband and daughters.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Westfield, IN
attorneys.bio:
Kathy is a Certified Family Law Specialist, as certified by the Family Law Certification Board of the Indiana State Bar Association. She was named a Super Lawyers® Rising Star, in 2010, 2011, and 2012.

Kathy has extensive experience representing clients at both the state and appellate court levels in all aspects of family law, including adoptions (child and adult), child support establishment and arrearages, cohabitation agreements, custody proceedings, divorce and legal separation, domestic partnership agreements, grandparent custody and visitation, guardianships, jurisdictional matters involving child support, custody, and parenting time, modification proceedings (custody, parenting time and child support), paternity actions, prenuptial agreements, postnuptial agreements, and protective orders.

Kathy believes the key to her successful representation of her clients is her ability to have the knowledge and preparation necessary to aggressively represent her clients in court while also having the ability to problem-solve and reach creative solutions to avoid the necessity of a hearing if possible.

Kathy is a member of the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association and the Indianapolis Bar Association. She serves as a volunteer guardian ad litem, ensuring children have legal representation in contentious court cases.

attorneys.name: Harold T. Harper
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Valparaiso, IN
attorneys.bio:
Harold Harper has deep roots in the Region. He was born and raised in Valparaiso, Indiana, and graduated from Valparaiso High School and Valparaiso University School of Law. With his wife of over thirty-years, Lisa, he also raised their three children in Valparaiso.

Harold received his Bachelor of Science in Accounting from Indiana University, where he was a member of Beta Gamma Sigma, the Honor Society for Accredited Collegiate Schools of Business. He graduated with High Distinction.

Harold then obtained his Juris Doctor from Valparaiso University School of Law in 1997, where he graduated in the top quartile of his class.

Harold is admitted to practice law before the Indiana Supreme Court as well as the United States District Courts, Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana, and the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals in Chicago, Illinois. He is a member of the American Association for Justice, the Million Dollar Advocates Forum and is a sustaining member of the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association.

Harold is Managing Partner at Harper and Harper, which he co-founded with his father, Robert Harper. His areas of practice include personal injury and wrongful death, including auto accidents, dog bites, premise liability claims and medical malpractice cases.

Mr. Harper has over twenty-five years of first-chair trial and litigation experience. He’s briefed and argued hundreds of contested motions, including motions for summary judgment, protective orders, gag orders, and motions to compel. He’s deposed hundreds of witnesses and parties; and has mediated well over one hundred civil claims.

Harold is an avid fisherman. His favorite fishing experiences have been angling for Halibut, King Salmon, and Ling Cod off Raspberry Island in the Kodiak Island Archipelago.

Harold is also fascinated with computer software. On his 'bucket list' was always to learn how to program. Consequently, he applied and was accepted into a Ruby on Rails web development program and has been developing with Rails and Javascript ever since.

Music is an important part of Harold’s life as well. He is a drummer, having studied at the American Conservatory of Music in Chicago, Illinois and the Berklee College of Music in Boston, Massachusetts.

In addition to practicing law at Harper and Harper, Mr. Harper represents the Porter County Council, where he oversees all legal matters for Porter County Government's fiscal body, which operates with a budget of approximately $43,000,000.00.

Harold also represents the Porter County Council before the Board of Trustees of the Porter County Government Nonprofit Charitable Foundation, a $189,506,000.00 foundation/tax-exempt organization established for the benefit of Porter County residents/taxpayers.

Lastly, Harold spends a significant amount of time representing Porter County indigent youths charged with delinquent acts (for all felony, misdemeanor and status offenses), including in detention proceedings, initial and modification hearings and fact-findings (bench trials).

attorneys.name: Robert P. Harper
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Valparaiso, IN
attorneys.bio:
Robert Harper was born and raised in Northwest Indiana.

He was raised on a small farm in South Lake County, IN. While in school he was active in 4-H and he would show cattle he raised at the Lake County Fair each year.

After graduation from Merrillville High School he went to Ball State University. After four (4) years he graduated and was licensed to teach in Indiana.

He taught elementary school in Portage, IN for two (2) years.

He then enrolled in Valparaiso University School of Law. After one semester he was awarded a full tuition scholarship based on his academic achievements.

In 1968 he graduated from law school and went into private practice in Portage, IN.

In 1970 he was elected Judge of the Portage City Court. Three years later he was elected Porter County Prosecutor.

At the end of his term as county prosecutor he elected not to run again and returned to private practice. He has been in private practice ever since.

Over the years he has practiced mainly in the area of personal injury accidents and criminal defense. He has extensive trial experience in both representing plaintiffs in personal injury cases and defendants in criminal cases.

He also was elected to serve as Porter County Commissioner for 8 years. While there he was instrumental establishing Porter County Animal Shelter as a no kill facility and bringing a new modem hospital to the county. He also led the charge in passing the green space ordinance that provides all new county subdivisions shall have in their plan a substantial amount of land set aside for parks and green space.

After leaving the commissioners office, which was a part-time position he has also worked as a part-time public defender for the past 14 years.

He and his wife, Shirley, live in Valparaiso, IN. He has 6 children. Three of his sons are law school graduates that work in the same office. He has a son that lives in Switzerland and has a management position with World Wildlife Federation. He has two daughters, one lives in Porter County and is a dental hygienist and the other lives in Virginia and teaches online classes to students being homeschooled.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Valparaiso, IN
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in Porter County, Jim graduated with honors from Indiana University and Georgetown University Law Center.

attorneys.name: Austin C. Harris
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Lafayette, IN
attorneys.bio:
Austin Harris was born and raised in Lafayette, Indiana. He attended Indiana University - Bloomington for his undergraduate studies in Accounting at the Kelley School of Business. Following, he was a business development intern for Ice Miller before continuing his education at Indiana University McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis, Indiana.

While at McKinney, Mr. Harris was a Business Law Association member and earned a Graduate Certificate in corporate and commercial law. He also took part in Neighborhood Christian Legal Clinic's Spring4Justice efforts to help raise support towards providing legal assistance and education to low-income individuals. Before joining Luisa White Law, LLC, Mr. Harris also gained valuable experience as a legal intern at the Legal Aid Corporation of Tippecanoe County continuing his efforts towards serving the indigent community. During his time at Legal Aid, he represented clients under attorney supervision in landlord/tenant, family law, and other matters through Legal Intern Certification with the Indiana Supreme Court. His work consisted primarily of drafting, researching, and representing clients in court matters, among other aspects of the attorney-client relationship. Mr. Harris developed a strong understanding and respect for the importance of adequate representation.

Professionally, Mr. Harris's practice areas include civil litigation, criminal defense, bankruptcy and family law. Mr. Harris maintains his commitment towards fighting for client legal rights to achieve successful resolutions amid difficult times.

attorneys.name: Aaron J. Harshman
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Aaron Harshman has over 10 years of experience as an Indiana attorney and an impressive list of accomplishments.

Criminal Law

Aaron Harshman has broad experience not only as a criminal defense attorney but also as a deputy prosecuting attorney in three different Indiana Counties - Hendricks County, Hancock County, and Tippecanoe County.

Mr. Harshman has conducted many jury trials and bench trials, from infractions and misdemeanors to major felonies. He has prosecuted or defended charges of drug dealing, drug possession, marijuana possession, illegal firearms and handgun possession, domestic violence, battery, neglect of a dependent, theft, shoplifting, conversion, operating while intoxicated (OWI), driving while intoxicated (DWI) or driving under the influence (DUI), robbery, burglary, and many more.

Post-Conviction Relief: Mr. Harshman has obtained reversal of charges on multiple cases post-conviction.

Other criminal proceedings: In addition to trial work, Aaron works on sentence modifications, probation violations, community corrections violations, and expungements.

Mr. Harshman has worked as a prosecutor with a focus on domestic violence and crimes against women. He has spoken on complexities of the topic and helped navigate appropriate results, including dismissal for Defendants accused of domestic violence.

Professional Licensing

When Aaron was the Executive Director at the Indiana State Board of Nursing, he served as an expert in the application of criminal law and administrative rules in the determination of what penalty should be applied to accused nurses. He is familiar with the processes and the unique nuances of the board's operation, and can advise you on how to maintain your license.

attorneys.name: Kevin G. Harvey
attorneys.firm_name: Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: General Civil Litigation Lawyers in Greenfield, IN
attorneys.bio:
Kevin G. Harvey joined Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP, in 1997, and has been a partner since 2003. Kevin has created estate plans for hundreds of clients, and he regularly assists families with business and farm ownership transition planning as well as elder law challenges. Kevin does a substantial amount of estate and trust administration work, and he represents many small to medium sized businesses – helping them with business law needs, contract development, and ownership transactions. Kevin also represents clients in civil lawsuits, including estate and trust litigation, business and contract disputes, construction matters, and personal injury.

Kevin grew up in Nebraska (“Go Huskers!”). He graduated from Augustana College in Rock Island, Illinois, in 1991, where he majored in history. While at Augustana, Kevin was inducted into Phi Alpha Theta, National History Honorary Society, and he was the recipient of the O.F. Ander Outstanding History Student Award. Kevin graduated from Indiana University School of Law in 1994, where he was also the Executive Production Editor of the Indiana International & Comparative Law Review.

Kevin was admitted to the Indiana Bar and the United States District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana in 1994. Kevin is a member of the Indiana State Bar Association and the Hancock County Bar Association.

Kevin has served as a member of several boards, including: the Board of School Trustees for the School Corporation of Southern Hancock County (2007 to 2010); the Board of Directors of the Hancock Hope House (2012 to 2017); and the Board of Directors of the Community Foundation of Hancock County (2015-2023). Kevin is currently a member of the Board of Directors of the Hancock Regional Hospital Foundation (since 2020, serving as Board Chair in 2022-23), and Giving Back Hope Together, Inc. (“GBHT”) (since 2022).

Kevin and his wife, Jayme, reside in Greenfield, Indiana, and attend Mercy Road Church Northeast in Fortville. They have two children and are enjoying the experience of spoiling their three grandkids. In his free time, Kevin enjoys bicycling with Jayme, trying to tame the woods in their back yard, woodworking, and making stained glass.

Kevin and Jayme’s daughter and her family are missionaries in Kenya, serving children and families in an informal settlement in Nairobi, through GBHT. Kevin and Jayme’s work with GBHT (website: gbht.org) has taken them to Africa several times, and they are passionate about participating in that ministry.

attorneys.name: Jonathan D. Harwell
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jonathan D. Harwell is the co-founder and managing partner of Harwell Criminal Defense, a premier Indiana law firm known for its aggressive advocacy and strategic litigation in criminal defense and post-conviction relief. A native of Ohio who relocated to Indiana during high school, Harwell has built a legal career defined by excellence, innovation, and a relentless pursuit of justice.

Harwell earned his Bachelor of Science in Legal Studies from Ball State University, graduating cum laude and as a member of the Lambda Epsilon Chi Legal Studies Honor Society. He continued his education at the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law, where he received the CALI Excellence for the Future Award and Gold Level Pro Bono Recognition.

Since founding Harwell Criminal Defense in 2014, Harwell has transformed the firm from a modest practice into a legal powerhouse. His courtroom experience spans murder trials, death penalty cases, federal appeals, and complex post-conviction litigation. Harwell is also a certified mediator, a published legal scholar with LexisNexis, and a graduate of the National Criminal Defense College Trial Practice Institute.

Harwell is deeply committed to community service, legal education, and professional development. He regularly teaches continuing legal education (CLE) courses and participates in leadership programs through the Indiana State Bar Association. His work has earned him recognition not only for legal excellence but also for his strategic business acumen.

attorneys.name: John H. Haskin
attorneys.firm_name: Employment Law Office of John H. Haskin & Associates, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Rights Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Haskin is the founding partner of the Indianapolis law firm of Employment Law Office of John H. Haskin & Associates, LLC, the largest employment law firm representing employees in the state of Indiana. The firm serves clients throughout Indiana from its central location of the former Indianapolis Fire Department Headquarters building in downtown Indianapolis.

A native of Indianapolis, Mr. Haskin graduated from Chatard High School, then Indiana University in 1972. Thereafter, he began working full time for the Indiana Civil Rights Commission as an investigator, conciliator and legal intern while attending the Indiana University School of Law at Indianapolis at night.

Mr. Haskin graduated from law school in 1977 and began practicing law as a solo practitioner. Shortly after opening his own practice, Mr. Haskin began to hire night law school students as law clerks. A majority of the firm's associates served as law clerks for the firm while in law school.

Mr. Haskin has represented numerous clients in employment-related actions both in administrative hearings and federal bench and jury trials. Mr. Haskin has tried, and won, a complicated age discrimination case in which the jury found not only intentional discrimination but also constructive discharge, awarding full back pay and liquidated damages.

In prior years, he has been involved in several important appellate cases, including Carr v. Allison Gas Turbine, General Motors Corporation, where the defense verdict from the bench trial was reversed and judgment entered for the sexual harassment plaintiff by the Court of Appeals. Another case was Lehman v. Yellow Freight, where the plaintiff's reverse race discrimination trial verdict was upheld. Mr. Haskin has also handled an age discrimination jury trial, McKelvey v. American Legion.

Mr. Haskin incorporated the Indiana Veterans Service Officers Association as a non-profit corporation and provides counsel to this organization. He has been appointed to the position of Legal Deputy for over 24 years, by two different Sheriff’s, and has been a presenter at the Masters level continuing legal education for over 10 years. His experience representing employees is unmatched in this geographic area.

attorneys.name: Spencer J. Hatfield
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Spencer Hatfield joined The Cline Law Firm in 2020, bringing a uniquely analytical perspective to the practice of personal injury law. Born and raised in Evansville, Indiana, Spencer grew up witnessing firsthand the profound impact legal advocacy can have on individuals and families facing life-altering circumstances. As the son of a successful personal injury attorney, he developed an early appreciation for how dedicated legal representation could not only secure just compensation but also provide healing and closure for those affected by tragedy.

After graduating from Purdue University in 2011 (Boiler-Up!), Spencer pursued his passion for scientific inquiry, earning a master's degree in Microbiology, Molecular Cell Biology, and Biochemistry from Southern Illinois University, where he graduated magna cum laude. His scientific career included valuable time as a microbiology research scientist working to develop next-generation antibiotics experience that honed his meticulous attention to detail and evidence-based approach to problem-solving.

This scientific background gives Spencer a distinct advantage when handling complex medical negligence cases, as he can navigate intricate medical records and effectively communicate with healthcare professionals and expert witnesses. His transition to law was completed at the University of Illinois College of Law, where he graduated with honors, demonstrating his commitment to academic excellence across disciplines.

Since joining The Cline Law Firm, Spencer has been instrumental in helping clients recover millions of dollars for injuries caused by medical negligence, product defects, and motor vehicle collisions. He approaches each case with the same rigorous methodology he applied in his scientific work-carefully analyzing evidence, identifying causation, and developing compelling arguments that resonate with judges and juries alike.

Spencer's daily focus extends beyond merely securing financial compensation. He is dedicated to understanding each client's unique circumstances and helping them navigate the often overwhelming process of rebuilding their lives after serious injury. His combined scientific and legal expertise allows him to advocate effectively for his clients while providing them with clear, straightforward guidance through every stage of their case.

When not advocating for his clients, Spencer is a devoted father to four young children. He is actively involved in youth sports organizations in Westfield, IN, where he enthusiastically supports his children's development as people through athletics. Spencer believes deeply in the character-building aspects of team sports the lessons of perseverance, sacrifice, teamwork, and resilience that extend far beyond the playing field. His commitment to these formative experiences reflects the same values he brings to his legal practice. Spencer is also a dedicated member of Heart and Soul Church in Fishers, Indiana, where he contributes his time and energy to the community. This balance of professional dedication and family commitment underscores Spencer's holistic approach to both justice and community as foundational elements in building meaningful lives.

attorneys.name: Jenna L. Heavner
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce & Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jenna L. Heavner isn’t just a lawyer — she’s a powerful advocate, a trusted guide, and a deeply compassionate presence during life’s most pivotal transitions. As a partner at Hollingsworth Law Group, Jenna brings not only a wealth of experience and expertise but also a deep well of empathy, creativity, and calm strength. Whether navigating a high-asset divorce, negotiating complex custody matters, or crafting a thoughtful estate plan, Jenna is a steady hand and a fierce protector of what matters most.

Jenna is a Certified Family Law Specialist by the Family Law Certification Board— a distinction that reflects her elite level of knowledge, skill, and commitment to excellence in the field. She is also a top-rated Super Lawyer, a seasoned family law mediator, and a trained collaborative divorce professional. Additionally, Jenna is a dedicated parent coordinator (“PC”) and serves as a court-appointed guardian ad litem (“GAL”). With her vast experience helping families through life’s transitions, she is an incredible asset to our clients. And, although she deeply believes in resolving conflict with dignity, clarity, and heart whenever possible, Jenna is an experienced trial lawyer, ready to fight for her clients in court when necessary.

With over a decade of experience, Jenna’s practice spans the full spectrum of family law — from contested and uncontested divorces, custody, parenting time, and child support issues to guardianships, protective orders, adoptions, military divorces, and prenuptial/postnuptial agreements. She’s also highly skilled and experienced in assisting clients with trusts and estate planning issues. Jenna is available to assist our family law clients by modifying wills and examining estate planning strategies as they begin their new lives after divorce; and she brings all clients peace of mind concerning their legacy and loved ones.

Jenna is the very first attorney to be invited into partnership at Hollingsworth Law Group — a decision rooted not only in her legal excellence but in her extraordinary character. Her integrity, intellect, and deep compassion have been admired by founding partner, Kena Hollingsworth, for years. Jenna’s decision to join the firm as a partner is seen as an incredible gift — to the HLG team, and most importantly, to the clients the firm is honored to serve.

In every case, Jenna’s approach is strategic yet human-centered. She’s earned a reputation for being both exceptionally prepared and deeply present — a rare combination that leaves clients feeling heard, supported, and empowered every step of the way.

Originally from a small farming community in southern Indiana, Jenna has called Indianapolis home since law school. She’s married to a local firefighter, and together they are raising four amazing kids. That blend of real-life perspective, legal brilliance, and unwavering heart is exactly what makes Jenna such a perfect fit at HLG — and such a remarkable advocate for the clients we serve.

attorneys.name: James W. Hehner
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jim Hehner is a partner in the law firm Clendening Johnson & Bohrer, P.C., with offices in Indianapolis and Bloomington, consisting of several litigation attorneys and paralegals. He has over thirty years of experience conducting jury trials and representing clients in both state and federal court, primarily in the areas of first party and third party insurance defense. He obtained his Bachelor of Science degree from the Indiana University Kelley School of Business and his law degree from the Indiana University School of Law-Indianapolis. During law school, he was a member of the Indiana Law Review, where he served as a Note and Development Editor and was also a Moot Court participant. Jim also attended the Indiana Law Enforcement Training Academy, where he obtained a commission as a Police Officer, and worked as a Police Officer for several years while attending college and law school.

He is admitted to practice in Indiana, the United States Supreme Court, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Indiana, and the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals. He is the past president of the Defense Trial Counsel of Indiana (DTCI) and is a member of the Defense Research Institute (DRI). Jim has achieved the Martindale Hubbell Preeminent Peer Review Rating of "AV" (5 out of 5, the highest available) and has been named as an Indiana Super Lawyers ©, for several years. He has also received a lifetime achievement award as one of America's Top 100 Attorneys. Jim is also active in numerous other civic organizations including the Carmel Clay Public Library Board of Trustees and the Carmel Clay Public Library Foundation.

Since obtaining his law degree, Jim has been engaged in the private practice of law, practicing primarily in the area of litigation. He has been lead attorney for many jury trials and tried cases to verdict, including cases involving wrongful death, auto accidents, premises liability. His practice includes cases in both State Court and Federal Court. He has litigated hundreds of cases involving wrongful death, construction law, product liability, auto accidents, premises liability, and all types of personal injury claims. Jim has acted as an arbitrator or mediator on numerous occasions and has extensive experience in both arbitration and mediation proceedings.

In 2016 Jim was asked by Chief Justice Loretta Rush of the Supreme Court of Indiana to serve on the Indiana Civil Justice Initiative Roundtable led by Indiana Justice Geoffrey Slaughter and retired Justice Brent Dickson. The roundtable consists of a small cross section of Indiana lawyers who will make recommendations to the Supreme Court of Indiana regarding ways to improve how our courts handle civil cases.

Jim is a frequent speaker at continuing legal education seminars and has authored or co-authored legal articles including: COVID-19 Best Practices and Procedures. What Have We Learned About How to Practice Law in a New Era, March 4, 2021, Zoom Presentation, The Tri-Parte Relationship: Attorney, Client and Insurer, Downtown Continuing Education, Inc. (2016 and 2020); Litigating and Understanding the Medical Injury, Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum (1995); Litigating Lumbar Spine Injuries, Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum (1995); Stickney 1985 Amendments to the Indiana Medical Malpractice Act 19 Ind L. Rev. 403 (1986); Hehner, Smith The Indiana Insurance Guaranty Association Act: More Problems than Protection 21 Ind. L. Rev. 207 (1988), reprinted in Indiana's Guaranty Fund for the Tort and Insurance Law Seminar, Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum (1988).

Specialties: Insurance Defense (first party and third party),wrongful death, construction law, product liability, agricultural claims including defective feed and other agricultural products, auto accidents, premises liability, all types of personal injury claims, business formation, and business litigation.

attorneys.name: Amanda Hendren
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Brownsburg, IN
attorneys.bio:
Amanda was born in Indianapolis, IN in 1985 and graduated from Avon High School in 2003. Amanda then attended DePauw University in Greencastle, IN and graduated with a B.A. in Communications in 2007. After working in the banking industry following college, Amanda attended the University of Dayton School of Law and graduated from UDSL's two-year accelerated program in the top 25% of her class in 2011.

During law school, Amanda worked for the Honorable Judge Thomas M. Rose of the Federal Southern District of Ohio as a judicial extern and assisted with procedural issues involving ERISA and ECPA. Amanda was cited in two federal opinions due to her substantial contributions in the drafting of those opinions. Since graduating law school, Amanda has gained a majority of her experience in family law. Specific experience includes, but is not limited to, issues of dissolution, custody, support, wage withholding, contempt, and protective orders. Amanda also practices in the areas of criminal law, construction law, premises liability, breach of contract, complex tort, wrongful death, motor vehicle accidents, and governmental liability.

Amanda currently lives on the south side of Indianapolis with her husband and two stepsons. Amanda enjoys attending Colts games with her husband, boating and waterskiing with her family, and watching her stepsons play sports.

attorneys.name: Pamela J. Hensler
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Pamela serves the legal needs of her clients in civil litigation and appellate work. Her concentration includes solving her client disputes both in and of court involving real estate and construction matters, business disputes, and personal injury matters. Pamela understands that being involved in litigation can be daunting, stressful and full of the unknown for many of her clients. Clients love working with Pamela because she's pragmatic, responsive, effective and engaging. Her clients know what to expect, when to expect it, and understand the potential outcomes, risks, costs, and timeframes for each matter.

Pamela received her undergraduate degree from Indiana University and graduated from the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law. In law school, Pamela served as Executive Managing Editor of the Indiana Law Review, competed as a finalist in the school's moot court competition and was selected to be a competitor on the school's appellate advocacy team that competed in ABA National Moot Court Competition.

A southern Indiana native, Pamela practiced with a law firm in Evansville, Indiana before returning to Bloomington. She was an associate attorney working with Geoff Grodner, until 2010, when she became a litigation partner at another Bloomington law firm. She returned to practice at Mallor Grodner Plummer Attorneys, in 2017.

Pamela is an active alumnus of Indiana University and currently serves on the Indiana University Alumni Association Finance Committee and is a former member of the Indiana University Alumni Association Executive Committee and the IU Robert H. McKinney School of Law's Alumni Board of Directors. Pamela volunteers her time assisting underserved clients through the District 10 Pro Bono project and is committed to helping the underserved in her civic, volunteer work.

When she isn't advocating for her clients, she is most often found hanging out with her family, hiking the hills of Southern Indiana with her golden retriever, or curled up with a great piece of literature or even perhaps some questionable sci-fi novels.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
“Since 1998, I’ve been representing you, the people of Indiana. It has been my great pleasure to serve you. Whether you have been involved in an auto accident, or seek Social Security disability benefits, or are the victim of medical malpractice, I have tried to be here for you. I’ve enjoyed all the people I’ve met along the way and the families I have been able to help. If you ever need me, I will do everything I can to help you.”

Born and raised in central Indiana, John Hensley has always possessed an overwhelming desire to protect the rights of his fellow Hoosiers, and therefore, has devoted his practice to assisting those who have been wrongfully injured. John hung his shingle in 1998 by opening his own law office in downtown Indianapolis. There he works daily toward achieving the best results possible for his clients. Known mainly for his compassion for others, John also possesses a common-sense and efficient approach to the practice of law. He will continue to bring experience and integrity to the practice of law and represent his clients vigorously with great success.

attorneys.name: Robert M. Hess
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Crown Point, IN
attorneys.bio:
Robert M. Hess, President and founding member of Miller Sachs & Hess, PC, practices primarily in the areas of Family Law; Personal Injury; and Business Law. He received his B.S. from Indiana University in 1961 and his J.D. from Northwestern University School of Law in 1966. From 1961 to 1963, he served in the United States Army, as a First Lieutenant. Mr. Hess was admitted to the Indiana and Illinois Bars in 1966. He is also admitted to practice before the United States District Court, Northern District of Indiana, and the United States Supreme Court.

Mr. Hess is a member of the Lake County Bar Association and the Indiana Bar Association. During his years of practice, he has been a guest speaker on Family Law for the Lake County Bar Association and the Indiana Bar Association. Mr. Hess has served the community for over four decades, providing quality legal services to the many clients he has represented, including: working families, doctors, lawyers, judges and other professionals as well as businesses and corporations. Mr. Hess has been lead counsel in numerous divorce cases involving multi-million dollar marital estates.

Mr. Hess has represented clients throughout Indiana including: Hammond, Gary, East Chicago, Crown Point, Munster, Highland, Griffith, Dyer, Hobart and Valparaiso and is available to represent clients in Lake County, Porter County, LaPorte County, Jasper County and Newton County, Indiana.

Mr. Hess was given a Martindale-Hubbell ®AV®* rating from his peers in July 1997 and maintained it since that date. The rating means that he was deemed to have very professional ethics and pre-eminent legal ability. Miller Sachs & Hess, PC received notification from LexisNexis Martindale-Hubbell® that Miller Sachs & Hess, PC has received a Martindale-Hubbell Peer Review Rating. Only law firms and lawyers with the highest ethical standards and exceptional qualifications receive a Martindale-Hubbell Peer Review Rating. Mr. Hess has also been selected by his peers for inclusion in the 2011-present editions of "The Best Lawyers in America" in the specialty of Family Law. Robert Hess was named the Best Lawyers ® 2015 Family Law "Lawyer of the Year" in the South Bend Metropolitan Area. The South Bend Metropolitan Area includes (in addition to itself) Crown Point, Elkhart, Goshen, La Porte, Marion, Merrillville, Michigan City, Mishawaka, Munster, Rensselaer, and Valparaiso.

attorneys.name: Judy G. Hester
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Judy G. Hester is a 1986 Cum Laude graduate of Loyola University in Chicago, where she earned her Juris Doctor degree and a Master’s degree in Social Work. She is admitted to practice law in the States of Illinois and Indiana, as well as the U.S. District Courts in the Southern District of Indiana, the Northern District of Illinois, and the Court of Federal Claims. Judy’s diverse experience and training, combined with compassion and understanding, is the foundation for the Brazill Hester law firm and the commitment to promote the legal interests of each of the firm’s clients. Judy concentrates in issues affecting most individuals and families, including divorce, paternity, child custody disputes, parenting time, property valuation/division, and land use issues. She served as a commercial litigator for the prestigious law firm of Seyfarth, Shaw, Fairweather & Geraldson through its Chicago office, subsequently managed the nationwide litigation efforts for Sears Mortgage Corporation (n/k/a PNC Mortgage Corporation), and later continued to counsel Sears Mortgage and its successors following moves to the United Kingdom and later to Indiana. Her litigation and dispute resolution work continued in 1998 in Indiana, representing the Boone County Area Plan Commission, the City of Carmel, and expanding to family companies and individuals. Judy’s clients benefit not only from her skilled representation earned through her comprehensive legal experience, but also from her compassion that has naturally developed as a result of her long-standing commitment to serving others. Judy is a Registered Domestic Relations Mediator and a trained Collaborative Law Professional, Parenting Coordinator, and Guardian ad Litem. She is a member of the Association of Family and Conciliation Courts, Central Indiana Association of Collaborative Professionals, the ISBA, and is the Chairperson for the ISBA Children’s Rights Committee.
