attorneys.name: Richard W. Karcher
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fort Wayne, IN
attorneys.bio:
When faced with a difficult legal situation, Rich wants to make certain that his clients have the best representation in their corner. For over 25 years, Rich has guided his clients by offering the most-sound advice and legal counsel possible. Nothing has been more important to him than upholding his clients’ legal rights and ensuring whatever situation that they face, results in the best possible outcomes.

Rich began his practice by handling multi-discipline cases in the area of family law, criminal law and civil litigation. Rich’s diverse background gives him a strong understanding of the diverse issues presented in domestic relations cases. Rich has now devoted his practice exclusively to family law and related matters.

Rich is a cum laude graduate from Thomas M. Cooley Law School in Lansing, Michigan. Prior to receiving his Juris Doctorate, Rich earned his bachelor’s degree from Indiana University in South Bend, Indiana. He is admitted to practice law in the Indiana Supreme Court and the United States District Court, Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana. He is a former Magistrate for Allen Superior Court, Deputy Prosecuting Attorney with Allen County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office and court-appointed Guardian Ad Litem and Public Defender for Children In Need of Services proceedings. He has extensive career in private practice.

As a former United States Air Force Sergeant, Rich is highly accomplished and meticulously organized, plus his overall professional experience gained from his family, criminal and civil law practice gives him a unique vantage point from which to survey the opportunities and challenges in legal proceedings. He continues to help his clients and their families through the tough times.

During his free time, Rich enjoys spending time with his wife, Rebecca; keeping up to date on the college athletes his son, Justin, coaches; dining out or trying out new recipes in the kitchen, on the grill or smoker and following his favorite Buffalo teams – the Bills and Sabres.

“At his best, man is the noblest of all animals; separated from law and justice he is the worst.” Aristotle

Mike prefers tropical weather and beaches but still calls Indiana home.

Mr. Katzman is the managing partner of the Indianapolis law office of Katzman & Katzman, P.C., where his practice is primarily centered around banking, corporate, contract, real estate, and transactional business law issues. attorneys.name: Mariellen "DeeDee" Katzman
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
I love what I do! Over the past 40 years I have been fortunate to be able to incorporate into my legal career the knowledge and skills I mastered when I attained my Bachelor of Science Degree from the "Indiana University of Medicine" (1973) and experience I gained as a hands-on provider of rehabilitation services to those suffering from acute disabilities (spinal cord injuries, auto accident and burn victims, stroke and other neurological disorders, amputations, surgical complications). I graduated with honors (Cum Laude) from Indiana University School of Law at Indianapolis in May, 1978 and I was able to jump into law almost immediately, having taken and passed the bar exam before I graduated from law school. Although I received top honors (American Jurisprudence Award) in criminal procedure, I have always focused my practice on dealing with people who are seeking legal advice due to their personal struggles - whether it be from the emotional stress and mental anguish connected with divorce and post divorce issues or the physical and emotional pain that results from traumatic injuries.

My husband and other senior partner Alvin Katzman and I are honored to work with six other outstanding lawyers in our firm. Our love of assisting people with their legal issues, is well-reflected by the fact that our daughters both chose to become lawyers. We are blessed to work side-by-side with them in and out of the courtroom.

We have also been privileged and personally gratified to participate alongside with the members of our firm in many philanthropic endeavors that are dear to our hearts. We have assisted in preparing and serving meals to families staying at the Ronald McDonald House, raised money for and walked in fundraisers for the Susan G. Komen Race for the Cure, the Walk to End Alzheimer's, and other worthy causes.

Honors

American Jurisprudence, Criminal Procedure

attorneys.name: Simranjit Kaur Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Facing a divorce or family law matter can be full of emotions and stress. Having compassionate legal representation in your corner can provide you with guidance and reassurance throughout your case. Simranjit Kaur is a dedicated Junior Associate Attorney with Stange Law Firm. Based in our Indianapolis, Indiana office, she is prepared to represent clients throughout Marion County and the surrounding areas.

Simranjit earned her law degree from Wayne State University Law School in Detroit, Michigan, graduating with her Juris Doctor in May 2024. During law school, her extracurricular activities included being a member of the Asian Pacific American Law Students Association, Women’s Law Caucus, and Business Law Society. Prior to law school, Simranjit earned her Master of Arts in Industrial/Organizational Psychology from the University of Detroit Mercy and her Bachelor of Science in Psychology from the University of Michigan.

Before joining the Indianapolis, Indiana divorce and family lawyers at Stange Law Firm, Simranjit worked on a wide range of legal matters with a focus on supporting both institutional and individual clients. Most recently, she represented public school districts and other organizations in civil rights defense, addressing claims under Title VII, the ADA, and Section 1983 through motion practice, agency responses, and discovery planning. She also has experience guiding individuals through immigration matters, including naturalization, J-1 waivers, family-based adjustments, and work permit renewals, ensuring clients understood each step of the process. In addition, she has assisted asylum seekers and other vulnerable populations by preparing detailed memoranda and motions in complex immigration proceedings. Her background also includes courtroom exposure in criminal law, where she managed preliminary examinations, conferences, and plea agreements while supporting trial preparation.

attorneys.name: John F. Kautzman
attorneys.firm_name: Ruckelshaus Kautzman Blackwell Bemis & Duncan, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
John F. Kautzman is a lifelong Indianapolis resident and attended North Central High School. John graduated from Indiana University in 1981 and the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in 1984. He joined the 3522400 in 1985 and also served as a Circuit Court Commissioner for several years.

Mr. Kautzman was elected as the 2005 President of the Indianapolis Bar Association and remains on the IBA Board of Directors. He is a Past President of the Metropolitan Bar Caucus and now serves on the Executive Council of the National Conference of Bar Presidents. He is a Distinguished Fellow of the Indianapolis Bar Foundation. He maintains several professional affiliations, including the Indianapolis Bar Association, the Indiana State Bar Association and the American Bar Association. He is a past President of the Indiana University Foundation Board of Associates and is a Life Member of the Indiana University Alumni Association. Mr. Kautzman is also a past Chair of the McKinney School of Law Board of Visitors.

John is admitted to practice in all Indiana State and Federal Courts. His practice includes both civil and criminal litigation, and he has served as lead counsel on a number of high-profile State and Federal Court jury trials, including the first televised Federal Court jury trial in State history. He has also successfully appeared before both the Indiana Court of Appeals and the Indiana Supreme Court for Oral Argument. Mr. Kautzman is listed in Who's Who, is a frequent seminar speaker, and teaches on the faculty of the ICLEF Trial Advocacy Skills College.

He regularly appears on the Indiana Super Lawyers list for achieving peer recognition as one of the top five percent of attorneys in Indiana. Mr. Kautzman was elected as a Fellow of the American College of Trial Lawyers, a nation-wide invitation only honor limited to one percent of the lawyers in any state. He is also listed in the prestigious "Best Lawyers in America."

John represents individuals and organizations on a broad range of legal matters, and focuses primarily in general litigation, criminal defense, personal injury, and law enforcement discipline and liability defense.

attorneys.name: Jillian C. Keating
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jillian C. Keating was admitted to the Bar in 2007. She is licensed to practice in Indiana and the U.S. District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana. Jillian graduated from Valparaiso University with a Bachelor of Arts degree and was a double major in Political Science and History. She also received her Doctor of Jurisprudence from Valparaiso University.

Jillian concentrates her practice in the areas of criminal defense, family law and general civil litigation. Jillian's experience in criminal defense matters includes defending drunk driving charges, drug possession and dealing, battery, minor consumption/illegal possession of alcohol, violations of probation, traffic offenses and other misdemeanor and felony charges. In regards to her family law practice, Jillian has experience in many areas, including divorce, custody disputes, child support, paternity, post-dissolution matters, guardianships and protective orders.

Jillian is a member of the Indianapolis, Hamilton County, Indiana State and American Bar Associations. Jillian is also a volunteer and advocate with the Hamilton County Guardian Ad Litem Program. The mission of the Hamilton County Guardian Ad Litem (GAL) Program is to advocate for the best interest of children involved in court proceedings. Courts are appointing GALs in a broad variety of cases including guardianship, paternity, divorce, CHINS and juvenile delinquency cases. Jillian also accepts pro bono cases for clients who could not otherwise obtain legal services through the Heartland Pro Bono Council.

attorneys.name: Genevieve Keegan
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce & Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Genevieve Keegan-Bedano is an attorney at Hollingsworth Law Group where she practices exclusively in the area of family law. Genevieve has worked alongside our founder, Kena Hollingsworth, since 2005; and her practice style epitomizes the firm’s commitment to Divorce Done Differently. Genevieve has experience assisting clients with all types of divorce and family law issues including legal separation, custody, parenting time/visitation, child support, paternity, adoptions, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, post-decree modifications and enforcement, guardianships, emancipation, relocations, protective orders, grandparent rights, and military divorces, to name a few.

What Makes Her Uniquely Qualified?

Genevieve is adept with clients who have substantial net marital estates and assets, as well as those who have considerably restricted means. She feels that considerable preparation, patience and empathy, excellent organizational skills, and frequent client communication are key factors in her successful practice. Moreover, she believes in a commitment to education on changing laws and policies.

In addition to her legal practice, Genevieve is involved with the family law community as an active member of local bar associations. She has been a guest speaker on the local radio shows to discuss family law legal. Genevieve has additionally provided pro bono and reduced cost legal representation for clients through Heartland Pro Bono Council, guest lectured at the Robert H. McKinney School of Law on family law issues, and she has been a participate in the Indianapolis Bar Leader Series.

Genevieve selected to practice in the area of family law due to her desire to assist families. She has seen firsthand that legal disputes, regarding division of property and child related issues, can cause emotional trauma. Genevieve seeks to minimize the traumatic effects of these disputes by decreasing conflict through out of court settlements. Where such negotiation is not possible, due to false allegations and/or inability for parties to communicate, she believes in her clients and passionately advocates for their positions in court.

attorneys.name: William A. Keller
attorneys.firm_name: Sweeney Julian Personal Injury Trial Attorneys
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in South Bend, IN
attorneys.bio:
If you have been injured, you need an attorney who understands your concerns, who can guide you through this life changing event and will directly work with you to seek a positive resolution to your claim. Sweeney Julian recruited Bill Keller to join the firm earlier this year and soon after he moved back to South Bend from Seattle. Bill wanted to find a practice where he could focus solely on working with injured people, and Sweeney Julian was the perfect fit.

Prior to joining Sweeney Julian Personal Injury Trial Attorneys was a Partner in the firms Moran & Keller PLLC, and MWW PLLC, where the practice focused on personal injury and high-stakes commercial litigation. Bill started his legal career as an associate at the law firm of LeGros Buchanan & Paul, where he defended the interests of fishing vessels, tug boats, shipping companies and other marine interests. During that time, Bill learned the ins and outs of how insurance companies and defendants evaluate claims and aggressively seek to intimidate injured persons from fully exercising their rights to a reasonable recovery.

Bill received his B.A. as a double major in Political Science and History from Linfield College in McMinnville, Oregon in 1995. Thereafter, Bill graduated with a J.D. from the University of Notre Dame Law School, where he was selected as a member of the Moot Court Appellate board.

Bill has litigated cases at the trial, appellate and Supreme Court level, including most recently having won two cases argued in front of the Washington Supreme Court defending the Constitutional Rights of his clients in Akrie v. T-Mobile et al, and Dillon v. Seattle Deposition Reporters. Bill was named a Rising Star for three straight years by Washington Law & Politics magazine, an honor awarded to less than 2.5 percent of lawyers in the state based upon peer recognition, ethical standards and recognition for achievement in the legal field.

Bill has handled personal injury cases from intake to verdict as counsel for both plaintiffs and defendants, but after many years of seeing a system which focuses on accepting premiums and denying claims Bill is 100 percent dedicated to helping injured people exercise their rights.

attorneys.name: Eric C. Keuling
attorneys.practice_type: Tax Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Eric Keuling is the founding attorney of The Keuling Law Firm, where he practices in the areas of tax law, business law, family law, personal injury law, and immigration law. He is also accredited by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) for the preparation, presentation and prosecution of claims for veterans' benefits.

Mr. Keuling received his law degree from Rutgers University Law School in 2007, where he was a Student Editor of the Rutgers Business Law Review. In 2016, he earned a Master of Laws (LL.M.) degree in Taxation from the University of Florida, the best public law school tax program in the country and among the top three programs in the United States. He is currently admitted to practice before Indiana state courts, New York state courts, New Jersey state courts, the U.S. Tax Court, and the U.S. District Court for the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana.

Mr. Keuling has over ten years of professional experience practicing with law firms and Big 4 accounting firms in the United States and Japan. He previously lived and worked in Tokyo, Japan for more than ten years and speaks fluent Japanese. Eric is currently a member of the Indianapolis Bar (“IndyBar”) Association and the Indiana State Bar Association, Family Law Division, and the Bankruptcy Law and Alternative Dispute Resolution sections. He is also a member of the Japan-America Society of Indiana.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Greenfield, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jon A. Keyes has been an attorney at Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP, since 2005, and has been a partner since 2014. While he handles a wide array of litigation, Jon concentrates his practice in the areas of Criminal Defense, Family Law, and Social Security Disability. Jon’s practice is focused in central Indiana, but he regularly represents clients throughout the state.

Jon earned his law degree from the Indiana University School of Law, graduating in 2005 in the top 15% of his class. During law school, Jon was an Associate Editor of the Indiana Law Review and clerked for the Honorable Judge Reuben Hill in Marion County Criminal Court 18. He is currently admitted to practice law in the State of Indiana and in federal court in both the Southern and Northern U.S. Districts. Jon was named as a Rising Star in Indiana Super Lawyers magazine on multiple occasions.

Jon also represents clients in appellate litigation, where he enjoys the opportunity to clarify Indiana law. He has successfully represented clients in cases before both the Indiana Court of Appeals and the Indiana Supreme Court. Some of Jon's past successful appellate cases have involved juvenile rights, marijuana law, search and seizure, Miranda rights, and traffic law.

Jon is also very involved in the Hancock County problem solving courts. He is the attorney appointed by the courts to represent all participants in both the Hancock County Drug Court and the Hancock County Behavioral Health Court. Through his work with those problem solving courts, Jon has become a strong advocate for those suffering from substance abuse and mental health issues.

Jon resides in Hancock County with his wife, Jill, their two children, Jack and Abby. They attend Cross of Grace Lutheran Church in New Palestine.

attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Noblesville, IN
attorneys.bio:
Steve grew up in Kokomo, Indiana. Steve graduated from Indiana University at Bloomington and earned a B.S. degree (with honors in chemistry). During college, Steve worked in a co-operative study program at General Electric, plastics division, where he worked in a chemical lab. After college, Steve attended law school at Indiana University-Indianapolis, graduating in 1992.

Steve represents individuals seriously hurt by the negligence or intentional wrongful acts of others. His practice focuses in the area of serious personal injury, including injuries resulting from nursing home negligence. His work proudly includes serving as co-counsel to successfully obtaining insurance coverage for a liver transplant wrongfully denied and seeing that client get the transplant.

Steve has been lead counsel in multiple jury and bench trials, representing clients who have been seriously injured in semi truck, car and motorcycle collisions. He has also represented clients injured from dangerous premises, dog bites and from other wrongful acts. Steve also has been actively involved in estate planning and probate administration since 1994. He has drafted hundreds of wills and trusts. He has represented numerous clients through probate and trust administrations. In addition to wills and trusts, Steve has drafted numerous business and health care related powers of attorney and Living Wills.

attorneys.name: Spencer H. King
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
“We make a living by what we get, but we make a life by what we give.” — Winston Churchill

Spencer was born and raised in Florida, but has been a proud Indiana resident since coming to Bloomington to attend law school in 2003. Spencer represented indigent clients in the Community Legal Clinic while attending law school. After graduating from Indiana University School of Law in 2006, Spencer moved to Indianapolis and began his litigation career focusing on defending personal injury actions. Spencer also has experience litigating family law matters. However, Spencer soon realized his true passion was to spend his time fighting for severely injured individuals against insurance companies and large corporations. In 2010, Spencer proudly joined Hensley Legal Group where he exclusively concentrates on representing victims of severe personal injuries. It is his pleasure to work with the good people of Indiana to help them cope with the impact of significant personal injuries.

Spencer is actively involved in the Indianapolis community. He has served as a Big Brother for the past three years in Big Brothers Big Sisters of Central Indiana. Spencer also sits on the board for the Indianapolis Early Learning Center where he strives to create a successful future for all Indianapolis preschool age children, regardless of socio-economic status. Spencer and his wife, Devin, a born and raised Hoosier, live in Carmel with their 3 boys.

Spencer H. King is proud to serve the residents of Indiana.

attorneys.name: Michael Kohlhaas
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Mike joined Cross Glazier Reed Burroughs, P.C., in 2021, after spending two decades as a partner at a large international law firm. Throughout Mike's career, he has seamlessly coordinated and executed a wide array of legal services that cater to the unique needs of high net-worth clients and public figures, including wealth preservation and transition planning, counsel on closely-held business activities, representation in family law matters, and tax counsel.

Mike concentrates his practice in a variety of personal representations, including the areas of matrimonial law and wealth transfer planning. Mike’s practice also includes an emphasis on the drafting of premarital agreements, to preserve and optimize the wealth transfer options of his clients and their families. Mike has represented many of the wealthiest individuals and families in Indiana, and from across the country, in capacities that range from the usual (divorce, wealth transfer, or tax counsel) to the novel (counseling clients in response to attempted blackmail schemes, clients targeted in criminal investigations, etc.). Mike’s clients have included executives, professional athletes, civic leaders, other high-profile and high net worth individuals, and their spouses.

Mike has written extensively on--as well as litigated--various and complex legal subject matters, including business valuation issues, stock option divisions, beneficiary trust interests, asset protection trusts, premarital agreements, legal issues incident to the conclusion of same-sex relationships (before such marriages were legally recognized), and other topics at the fore of the modern matrimonial law practice.

Mike has been interviewed by the Wall Street Journal on trends involving personal legal representation. His writings have been a frequent feature of continuing legal education seminars. Mike is the founder and editor of the Indiana Family Law Update, an electronic publication that provides over 200 attorneys and judges across Indiana, and beyond, with timely updates and analysis regarding developments in the Indiana appellate courts. Mike previously has served as a contributing editor on a handbook for Indiana Appellate Practice, and he gives regular counsel and representation to clients facing or considering an appeal.

Throughout this career, Mike has been repeatedly recognized by the "Super Lawyers" publication.

Licensed to practice law in Florida, as well as Indiana, Mike also assists clients with assorted Florida legal issues, including estate planning, probate, and real estate transactional work for clients that own, or are affiliated with, Florida real estate or business interests.

When not practicing law, Mike enjoys exercise, cooking, travel, music, and spending time with his family. Also a noted photographer, Mike's work has appeared in wildlife and sporting publications, from his work on African safaris, to the hundreds of thousands of images he has taken at lacrosse games up and down the east coast.

attorneys.bio:
“The only true wisdom is knowing you know nothing.” — Socrates

Justin was raised in Martinsville, Indiana, and then went on to obtain a B.S. in biology at IUPUI. While conducting university lab research, Justin realized over time that he did not want to pursue a career that would primarily entail designing and performing scientific experiments. At this time, Justin evaluated his options and decided that law school would provide him with the knowledge and opportunity to find a career tailored to his desires: mainly, a career that would regularly challenge him with new situations, the ability to see more direct results with his work, and the chance to utilize his writing skills. During law school, Justin gained experience by clerking for the Honorable Judge John Paul Godich at the Federal District Court of Southern Indiana. In addition, Justin spent time as law clerk for a creditor-based firm in Indianapolis where he dealt with various legal issues ranging from contract and commercial law to estate and tort law. Justin enjoys practicing with Hensley Legal Group, PC due to its emphasis on client-focused work. He is licensed to practice in the state and federal courts of Indiana.

Certified Mediator Justin J. Kosiba is proud to serve the residents of Indiana.

attorneys.name: Eric Krupp
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Eric Krupp completed his undergraduate education at Butler University with a B.A. in Telecommunications and a minor in Business Administration. He was awarded his Juris Doctorate from Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis, Indiana. Upon successful completion of the bar exam in 2003, he began his legal career as a criminal defense attorney with the Marion County Public Defender Agency.

For 15 years he was a zealous advocate for individuals in Marion County who were deemed to be indigent by the Courts. He represented clients accused of misdemeanor, low level and major felony crimes. For more than a decade he concentrated his practice at the agency in the defense of those accused of major felony drug crimes. During the last 2 years of his employment at the agency he was the supervising attorney in the major felony drug and gun court. He tried numerous cases to both the Court and jury during his employment at the agency.

Beginning in 2005, Eric also began engaging in the private practice of law, focusing on criminal defense. He has handled hundreds of matters over the years for individuals accused of traffic infractions, misdemeanors, felonies and murder. He has traveled across the state of Indiana on behalf of individuals who need representation in matters that can affect their livelihood and freedom.

attorneys.name: Paul S. Kruse
attorneys.firm_name: Parr Richey Frandsen Patterson Kruse LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lebanon, IN
attorneys.bio:
Paul S. Kruse joined the law firm after graduation from law school in 1981 and has been a partner since 1984. He is a past member of the management committee and has been member of the firm’s litigation section for over 20 years. Concentrating his practice in personal injury litigation, he has extensive experience in handling catastrophic damage and wrongful death claims involving all types of personal injury liability cases.

Mr. Kruse has handled thousands of injury claims and has tried over 90 civil jury trials in state and federal courts his past 24 years with the firm. These trials have involved a full range of personal injury matters, including product liability, premises liability, motor vehicle collisions, and medical malpractice claims.

He takes pride that the civil jury trials he has tried have been throughout Indiana. A lifetime Hoosier, he has personal injury experience with appearances in over 40 Indiana counties and Federal Court for both the Northern and Southern districts of Indiana. Mr. Kruse also represents injury victims outside the state of Indiana as well, including Illinois and Ohio.

In representing injured persons for the past two decades, Mr. Kruse has obtained numerous settlements each year from defendants and their insurance companies. His experience in representing victims who have suffered traumatic and catastrophic damages has established his reputation in the state as an effective and experienced personal injury attorney.

attorneys.name: Daniel A. Ladendorf Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Daniel A. Ladendorf is an Indiana Personal Injury Lawyer who gained significant investigative and courtroom trial experience early in his career as legal counsel to the Marion County Grand Jury and as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney during the terms of Marion County Prosecutors Steve Goldsmith, Jeff Modisett and Scott Newman. After leaving local government in 2000, Dan has pursued his passion in civil practice through Ladendorf Law, where he seeks fair and reasonable results for his injured clients and their families through insurance claims, litigation, trial and appeals when necessary.

Dan also recognizes the importance of advancing justice through other forums. For several years, he has volunteered as Legislative Co-Chairman for the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association (ITLA), where he also is one of sixty members on the Board of Directors and one of eleven members of its governing Executive Committee. The ITLA Board of Directors recognized Dan's tireless efforts in promoting legislative changes to Indiana's Hospital Lien Statute for the benefit of future clients by awarding him the 2013 "Trial Lawyer of the Year" award, one of ITLA's highest annual honors. Through his legislative work, Dan tries to put into practice the observation of Don Keenan, the noted trial lawyer from Atlanta, Georgia, who wrote that a true trial lawyer does one-third of his good in the courtroom, one-third of his good educating the public about safety issues, and one-third of his time actually bringing about change before the legislature.

As a multiple-term mayoral appointee to the five-member Indianapolis-Marion County Board of Ethics, Dan continues his service to Indianapolis and Marion County government. The Board of Ethics oversees the implementation and enforcement of the ethics ordinance enacted by the City-County Council for all local government employees and officers.

Dan has extensive administrative experience in the trial court system having served as Chief Deputy Clerk for the Marion County Circuit and Superior Courts, as well as Court Administrator to the then-Presiding Municipal Court Judge Harold Kohlmeyer.

Dan served as General Counsel to the Marion County Election Board from 2001 through 2006. The county election board is responsible for the administration of all federal, state and local elections in Indianapolis and Marion County, including local school board elections.

Dan is member of the Indiana State Bar Association and the Indianapolis Bar Association, where he has been inducted as a Distinguished Fellow of the Indianapolis Bar Foundation. Dan has lectured as a member of the faculty for a number of continuing legal education seminars, including programs sponsored through the Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum (ICLEF) and Indiana Trial Lawyers Association.

Dan holds the distinguished Martindale-Hubbell "AV" peer-review rating and has been recognized multiple years since 2006 as one of Indiana's Super Lawyers by Law & Politics. In addition to being a graduate of the Indiana University (Kelley) School of Business (B.S., 1983) and (McKinney) Law School (J.D., 1986), Dan also received a Certificate in Public Affairs (1983) during his undergraduate studies through the Indiana University School of Public and Environmental Affairs.

Dan is an attorney at Ladendorf Law focusing his practice in the representation of clients who have suffered injury through the negligence of another party, including the damages that result from such injuries because of motor vehicle and motorcycle collisions; premises liability cases; medical malpractice; product liability; and wrongful death.

attorneys.bio:
Mark C. Ladendorf is an Indiana Injury Lawyer. He has devoted his over thirty-five (35) years of legal practice exclusively to representing injured victims of automobile and motorcycle accidents, product defects, premises liability, construction/work-related accidents, medical malpractice, wrongful death, or other types of accidents causing injury to people and their families.

Mark has been selected to "The Best Lawyers in America" as well as the "National Trial Lawyers Top 100 Trial Lawyers". Mr. Ladendorf is featured in Martindale-Hubbell's Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers under three distinct categories of practice, which include personal injury, medical malpractice, and wrongful death litigation. Mark holds an "AV" rating as an attorney, the highest ranking an attorney can attain.

Mark served as President of the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association during the May, 2013 to May, 2014 term, and holds an emeritus position on its Board of Directors, having served since 1990. Mark is also a Life Member of the National Registry of Who's Who, as well as being selected as one of Indiana's Super Lawyers in Indianapolis Monthly magazine and Indiana Super Lawyers magazine, every year of its publication. He has authored and lectured extensively in the field of tort law and trial litigation, as demonstrated in his Resume.

Mark has represented clients throughout the State of Indiana and the United States. He has personally argued cases before the Indiana Supreme Court, the Indiana Court of Appeals, the U.S. Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals in Chicago, and the Northern and Southern districts of the United States District Courts of Indiana.

attorneys.name: Steven Lammers
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Steven Lammers grew up in South Bend, Indiana. He attended Miami University (Ohio) where he graduated cum laude with a degree in Finance. Lammers went on to Valparaiso University School of Law and obtained his law degree in 2006. Lammers is admitted to practice law in Indiana and Illinois and the federal courts in these two states.

Out of law school, Lammers practiced in northwest Indiana for a large law firm for over 9 years before coming to the Indianapolis area to practice. Lammers is a litigator and trial lawyer. Lammers’ practice is devoted to representing clients in court in various personal injury, wrongful death, civil rights, medical malpractice, legal malpractice, professional liability, construction, business disputes and other liability and litigation claims. Lammers handles matters throughout the State of Indiana for individuals and businesses and has a range of experience. His unique health care, construction, business and financial background makes him a valuable resource in any case or matter. He has significant jury trial experience. In early 2020, Lammers obtained an almost $1 million verdict for his client following a business dispute jury trial involving assisted living facilities. In 2023, Lammers was one of the main attorneys in a civil rights wrongful death case, procuring a settlement for $625,000 against a well-known jail medical provider. Lammers has settled numerous other cases for clients, obtaining favorable results.

Lammers is a member of the Indiana State Bar Association (“ISBA”) and participated in the Leadership Development Academy with the ISBA. Lammers was recognized in the “20 under 40” by the Northwest Indiana Times in 2014. He was selected to the Indiana Super Lawyers “Rising Stars” in 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019 & 2020.

Lammers was selected to Indiana Super Lawyers in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024. He was also named to the 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 U.S. News Best Lawyers® in America.

Outside the office, Lammers enjoys the time he spends with his children and the many activities in which they are involved.

attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Valparaiso, IN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Sara Langer brings to Langer & Langer an insatiable desire to succeed, as well as an insurmountable sense of advocacy on behalf of those who have been victimized by others.

Following in her father Steven’s footsteps, the law has always been part of Sara’s life. Admiring his work ethic, she saw how he has been able to help people during very difficult times, and strives to bring that passion to her own practice.

Sara earned her undergraduate degree in criminal justice and sociology, also at IU, where she graduated with honors. attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Valparaiso, IN
attorneys.bio:
Why Robert Langer Became An Attorney:

From a tender age, I understood that there are moments in life where we are unable to shield ourselves, needing an advocate to step forward and not just offer aid, but to steer situations towards justice. My personal acquaintance with adversity began in elementary school, where I grappled with the challenges posed by dyslexia, a learning disability that impeded my ability to read, write, and spell.

My path could have been one of endless struggle, had it not been for the formidable advocacy of an attorney very close to my heart – my father, Steve Langer. Amidst predictions of a future devoid of an education, it was his unwavering belief and persistent advocacy that altered my trajectory, helping to find alternate solutions that accommodated my unique learning style. This journey not only saw me defy the odds to graduate high school but fueled a passionate resolve within me.

Inspired by my personal journey and the unyielding support I received, I resolved to help others in situations where they often feel helpless. My aspiration blossomed into a steadfast commitment to championing the rights and voices of those unable to do so themselves.

Today, as an attorney, I represent patients and their loved ones who have endured harm due to medical malpractice. My practice extends to fighting tirelessly for individuals who have been victims of road accidents, involving cars and trucks, ensuring that justice isn’t just served but seen to be served, echoing the empathy, determination, and spirit of advocacy instilled in me by my father.

Not Only Winning For My Clients:

In my quest for justice, I draw parallels from my ardent involvement in the fiercely competitive and highly disciplined world of triathlon racing. This multi-discipline sport, comprising relentless segments of swimming, cycling, and running, demands more than just physical stamina; it seeks a harmonious symphony of perseverance, agility, and a mind that can see beyond the pain to the finish line.

Competing rigorously in triathlons doesn’t just satisfy a personal ambition to constantly outdo my previous benchmarks; it forms an integral canvas of my life, providing a vital outlet to rejuvenate my mind and body. Each day, as I plunge into the water, pedal tirelessly, or pound the pavement, I am not just training for a race; I am honing a mindset that cherishes resilience, embraces the joy in endurance, and fosters a camaraderie that goes beyond just encouraging fellow racers.

The philosophies nurtured in racing have seamlessly woven themselves into my professional ethos. My journey in the triathlon world, graced with the honors of representing Team USA in the Triathlon Age Group World Championships and consistently ranking in the top of my age group nationally, mirrors my commitment to my clients: a promise of relentless pursuit, an embrace of the journey with all its hardships, and a pledge to cross the finish line with grace, dignity, and unmatched determination to succeed.

attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Matthew D. LaTulip, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accidents Lawyers in Merrillville, IN
attorneys.bio:
General Background:

Attorney LaTulip was born in East Chicago, Lake County, Indiana in 1974, and grew up in Northwest Indiana. His parents, and generally, entire family are working class, blue collar people affiliated with the trades (Operator Engineers Union Local 150; Laborer's Union Local 81) Attorney LaTulip is a vested member of the Laborer's Union Local 81, out of Valparaiso, Porter County, Indiana.

Education, Experience, Distinguishment and Awards:

Attorney LaTulip attended Elementary and Secondary Schooling in Lowell and Hanover Central, in Cedar Lake, Lake County, Indiana. After High School, Attorney LaTulip maintained his home roots and attended college at Indiana University, Northwest Campus in Gary, Lake County, Indiana. Coming from his background, Attorney LaTulip was able to support himself while attending college by working construction as a Union Laborer. Attorney LaTulip, as his always remembers where he has come from, and where he has been when representing clients.

While attending Law School, Matt served as Production Editor for the Indiana International & Comparative Law Review. Additionally, Matt served as the President of the Criminal Law Association. Matt also worked with the Lake County Prosecutor's Office, the United States Department of Justice, U.S. Attorney's Office; and Lake County Community Corrections Work Release/Alternative Placement Kimbrough Center as an Intern.

In 1996, Matt received his Bachelors of Science Degree majoring in Criminal Justice, and minoring in Sociology, with a core grade point average of 3.7 out of a 4.0. While in attendance at Indiana University Northwest, he became a member of Alpha Phi Sigma (a National Criminal Justice Honor Society) and Phi Alpha (a National Honor Society for Public Affairs & Administration). Further, while in college Matt gained experience and worked as an Intern with the Lake County Indiana Prosecutor's Office, and, The Lake County Sheriff's Work Release Center.

After graduating from undergraduate college, Matt attended Law School at Indiana University School of Law in Indianapolis, Marion County, Indiana. While attending Law School, he accrued many honors and accomplishments. For example, in 1999 Matt became the recipient of the Glenn D. Peters Scholarship for Academic Excellence. Further, he was President of the Criminal Law Association (99-2000), Member of the Moot Court Society, and Executive Board Production Editor for the Indiana International and Comparative Law Review, a journal of scholarly writings subscribed and referred to by many local and national jurisprudence. During Law School Matt gained additional experience by interning with the United States Attorney General's Office, Department of Justice, and clerking with the law firm of Baldwin and Dakich, in Indianapolis, Marion County Indiana.

Matt graduated from Indiana University-School of Law within the top twenty (20%) percent of his class, and received his Doctor of Jurisprudence in May of 2000. Thereafter, he continued his legal career with the law firm of Spangler, Jennings, and Dougherty, where he remained employed until forming his own law offices in Merrillville, Lake County, Indiana.

Since then, Matt has had the experience and pleasure of representing individuals, businesses, and municipalities both in prosecution and defense of claims involving personal injury, motor vehicle/ automobile accidents, defense of those accused of crimes, discrimination, harassment, civil rights violations, premises liability/ premises injury, traffic offenses, and many other areas requiring legal counsel and help. He has handled cases and represented clients from the inception of cases, all the way to The Indiana Court of Appeals, the Indiana Supreme Court, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit. Matt has been appointed and served as Judge pro tempore in the Lake County Superior Courts, and as well as, the Lake County Superior Courts, During his service as Judge Pro tem, Matt has heard and ruled upon numerous legal issues. As an attorney helping clients resolve legal problems in Northwest/ Indiana, and the Chicago land area, Matt has been admitted to practice in all of the Superior and Circuit Courts within the State of Indiana; the Federal District Courts for the Southern and Northern District of Indiana, and the Federal Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit which encompasses Indiana, Illinois, and Wisconsin. Nonetheless, given his roots to the Northern Indiana area (Lake, Porter, LaPorte, Newton, Jasper, St. Joseph and Starke Counties) a larger percentage of his case load is focused in these areas.

Memberships and Personal Activities:

On a professional note, Matt is a member of the American College of Inns of Court, and The Indiana Public Defenders Council. On a personal note, Matt is an avid outdoorsman, conservationist, dedicated family man, and devoted Christian. As such, Matt is a member and presiding officer (Secretary) of the Cedar Lake Gun and Conservation Club, as well as a sustaining sponsoring member of Ducks Unlimited. Further, Matt, his Wife and three children all attend and substantially contribute to the Church of Christ that meets in Lowell, Lake County, Indiana.

attorneys.name: Meghan U. Lehner
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Meghan grew up on Long Island, NY. Following her graduation from Hofstra University, she moved to Indiana to attend law school at Indiana University McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis. After experiencing Hoosier Hospitality first hand, Meghan decided to make Indiana her home and has been practicing law here since 2005.

With a focus on employment law and civil rights. Meghan represents employees in cases concerning Title VII, ADA, ADEA, FMLA, FLSA, wage claims, and Due Process and First Amendment violations. She’s a frequent contributing author and has presented continuing legal education seminars and presentations in employment law and discrimination.

Meghan has over 19 years of experience representing employees in Federal Court, as well as federal administrative agencies like the EEOC and MSPB, and state agencies like SEAC. In addition to the federal courts in the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana, Meghan is also admitted to the Seventh Court of Appeals. She’s successfully briefed and presented oral arguments on behalf of clients in the Indiana Court of Appeals, Indiana Supreme Court and the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals.

Meghan is active in the Indianapolis Bar Association where she serves on the Executive Committees for the Solo/Small Firm Division (current Chair) and the Labor and Employment Section (past Chair). She is also a member of the Indianapolis Bar Foundation who recently awarded her the recognition of Distingished Fellow, as well as, NELA – the National Employment Lawyers Association. Since 2023, Meghan has held the distinction of Super Lawyer.

When she is not working, Meghan is dedicated to giving back to her community and regularly volunteers at Gleanors Food Bank and recently had an opportunity to help out during the Indy 500 Kids Day. She lives in Fishers with her husband and 2 sons who keep her busy shuttling them around to baseball and drum practice. Some of Meghan’s favorite things to do are vacation with her family, especially cruising, watch the Yankees, volunteer at her kids’ schools, and attend local sporting events.

attorneys.name: Claire E. Lewis
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Claire E. Lewis
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Claire E. Lewis has more than forty years of experience in the field of elder law. A founding member and first Chair of the Indiana State Bar Association's Elder Law Section, she currently serves as Chair of its Public Policy Committee. An active member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys (NAELA), Lewis was a founding member and first President of the Indiana chapter of NAELA and was re-elected as President of the organization for 2016 and is a current board member. She recently completed her term on the Executive Committee of the Estate Planning Section of the Indianapolis Bar Association. Lewis completed six years of service on the Board of Directors of CICOA Aging and In-Home Solutions (formerly the Central Indiana Council on Aging), serving as Secretary of the Board during her last two year term. She also completed a term of six years on the Board of Directors of the Alzheimer's Association of Indiana for which she chaired its Mission and Outreach Committee.

Lewis was called upon by the State of Indiana to provide the initial review of the exams to be given to attorneys seeking the CELA (Certified Elder Law Attorney) certification. As a member of the Advisory Panel on Attorney Specialization for the Indiana Commission for Continuing Legal Education, she was involved in the initial approval of the elder law certification in the state of Indiana.

As former Director of the Senior Law Project of the Legal Services Organization of Indiana, Lewis headed the Indiana sub-state Ombudsman Program for Central Indiana, promoting quality of care and nursing home residents' rights for Indiana's most vulnerable citizens.

Editor of the Indiana State Bar Association's popular book, the Laws of Aging (formerly the Legal Reference for Older Hoosiers), Lewis has authored or co-authored numerous papers and booklets on elder law issues including Medicaid in Indiana, Advance Directives, Medicaid for the Aging and Disabled in Indiana, Guardianship and Alternatives, The Legal Rights of Indiana Nursing Home Residents, and Housing Alternatives for the Older Person.

Lewis is a regular faculty member and program chair for the Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum (ICLEF). For the past couple of decades, she has chaired ICLEF'S Elder Law Institute, Advanced Medicaid Forum, and Advanced Elder Law Forum. Lewis is also a regular faculty member for educational seminars presented by the Indianapolis Bar Association (IBA). She has chaired seminars for the IBA covering such topics as Medicaid Estate Recovery, the effect of the Deficit Reduction Act on Medicaid eligibility issues, and Special Needs Trusts. She has been a guest professor at the McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis, focusing primarily on topics that relate to elder law. Lewis has served in an advisory capacity to Medicaid workers throughout the state and trained caseworkers, attorneys, and elder care professionals on Medicaid rules and regulations and other issues impacting older adults. She also volunteers for the IBA's Hospice Program, assisting those with terminal illnesses on estate planning and planning for incapacity.

Lewis was named a Super Attorney in Elder Law by her peers as published by Indianapolis Monthly magazine for 2005 through 2024. She is the only elder law attorney who has received this recognition for twenty consecutive years. Lewis has also twice been named one of the Top 25 Women Lawyers in Indiana by her peers in Indianapolis Monthly and was named a Five Star Wealth Manager by Indianapolis Monthly as well. She was selected by her peers as one of the "Best Lawyers in America" in the area of elder law for more than fifteen years as announced by "Best Lawyers" and U.S. News Media Group, the publisher of U.S. News and World Reports and the nation's leading source of rankings and service journalism, and she is the female lawyer of the year in elder law for 2017. She also has the highest rating possible - 10 - through Avvo, a legal services rating service. Lewis was awarded the Indiana State Bar Foundation's Law Related Education Award in October of 2005 and received the Indiana State Bar Association's GP and Solo Practice Hall of Fame Award for 2009. Lewis has also been named most valuable attorney of the year by the Indiana Chapter of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys (NAELA). She is also the 2024 winner of NAELA's prestigious Powley Elder Law Award. NAELA chooses one attorney from its United States members who demonstrates a commitment to promote a greater understanding of the rights and needs of older Americans and people with special needs.

Lewis was named as a Fellow of Indiana State Bar Foundation in 2010 and a Master Fellow in 2014. Established in 1979, the Fellows are an elite group of Indiana attorneys who demonstrate commitment to the ideals of the Foundation in advancing justice, promoting public understanding of the law, and enhancing the legal professions' performance of its ethical responsibilities. Only 1,000 Indiana attorneys are currently members of this select group. In 2012, she was also inducted as a Fellow of the Indianapolis Bar Foundation.

Lewis enjoys spending time traveling and hiking with her hubby of more than 40 years. While she loves her two children and their spouses, she absolutely adores her two precious grandchildren and has wonderful adventures with them and her German Shepherd, Lucy Lew.

attorneys.name: Felicia A. Locke
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Clients need an attorney who understands their needs and who can be an advocate for them, while providing competent legal services. That is where I come in. My name is Felicia Locke, an attorney in central Indiana focusing on the legal needs of everyday people. My practice focuses on personal injury, bankruptcy, family, criminal law and civil litigation. I offer full and limited scope representation.

Originally I had a career in real estate and finance, I later pursued a legal degree. I received my undergraduate degree from Indiana Wesleyan University and received my law degree from Indiana Robert H. McKinney School of Law.

Since becoming an attorney, I have developed a unique practice in which I assist clients who may not be able to afford traditional legal services or full representation. I believe that everyone needs equal access to the justice system and I recognize the genuine need to offer affordable legal services. I offer Limited Scope Representation, which allows clients to “unbundle” their services and pay for only what they need.

I have a heart for serving others and have been a volunteer advocate for abused and neglected elders and a mentor for under-privileged teens. I currently serve as the legal partner for a non-profit organization that provides resources to struggling women.

attorneys.name: George A. Lohmeier
attorneys.firm_name: Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Dissolutions of marriage when custody or parenting time is a primary issue Lawyers in Greenfield, IN
attorneys.bio:
George Lohmeier grew up in Clinton, Iowa and spent the first four years after high school graduation serving in the United States Navy aboard an aircraft carrier, the U.S.S. Franklin D. Roosevelt. Upon being honorably discharged, he studied at Florida State University and spent summers working as a brakeman on the Chicago Northwestern Railroad. Having earned a degree in political science, he moved to Indianapolis to attend Indiana University School of Law. Three years later, in 1978, George passed the Indiana Bar Exam and began serving as deputy prosecutor in Morgan County. He later established himself in Indianapolis and began to concentrate in the areas of divorce and child custody in addition to criminal defense. With a well-established private practice, George joined the firm of Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP in 1997.

Maintaining a focus primarily on family law, George has developed an extensive practice in the family law areas of divorce and child custody for parents, grandparents and non-parents. His interest in this area of law stems back to his own childhood and his upbringing by his single father in a blended family resulting from his parents' divorce. George's practice takes him throughout the State of Indiana, as well as out of state where he has been admitted to practice in those states pro hoc vice (case by case basis). His expertise in child custody litigation extends to resolving conflicting states' orders as well as locating children who have been wrongfully removed from the State of Indiana and whose whereabouts are not specifically disclosed.

George lives in Indianapolis with his wife, Cathy, and has three grown children. Flying has been a life-long passion since the age of 17. He enjoys flying his 1948 Cessna 170 as much as possible and attending the Oshkosh Air Show in the summer to camp with other dedicated pilots.

attorneys.name: Molly Lokitis
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce & Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Molly Lokitis is an attorney at Hollingsworth Law Group who brings a significant amount of litigation experience to the firm. Molly’s primary area of practice is family law, but she also has a vast amount of experience in criminal defense work, and has allowed our HLG Team to expand to serve clients with criminal law issues for misdemeanors (up to level 6) including but not limited to domestic violence issues as well as drug and alcohol issues such as driving under the influence, possession, public intox, etc.

Prior to joining HLG, Molly worked as a Public Defender in Marion County and practiced both family and criminal law in the private sector.

Being a child of divorce herself, Molly has always had passion for family law, and prides herself on aggressively fighting for her clients’ rights while providing compassionate legal counsel and warmth during life’s most difficult transitions. Molly has experience assisting clients with all types of divorce and family law issues including legal separation and divorce, custody, parenting time/visitation, child support, paternity, post-decree modifications and enforcement, contempt, relocation, protective orders, grandparent rights and military divorces.

Molly’s proactive, fast-moving approach to resolve family law cases fits perfectly with HLG’s motto of “Divorce Done Differently.” Molly believes open communication, trust, and sometimes a dash of brutal honesty leads to inevitable success. And, while her style of practice lends itself to the resolution of most cases by settlement, Molly is also ready and willing to put her trial advocacy skills to work in defending her clients’ rights in Court when settlement is not possible.

attorneys.name: Leslie Lorenzano
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Divorce is a very difficult and stressful time as both parties are going through a major life transition. That's why Leslie Lorenzano enjoys working with clients to help them through the process as painlessly as possible.

"I think when clients first come into the office, they sometimes feel like they have no control over the proceedings, especially if the other party files for divorce," Ms. Lorenzano said. "Anything I can do to help them understand the process and how to best approach the issues at hand is one of the most important, and often most rewarding, parts of my job."

Doing her job successfully requires strong lines of communication between an attorney and client, so you feel your attorney really listens to your concerns, and so your attorney understands what your goals are, she said.

"I feel that part of my job is to make sure the client understands that I’m someone they can call when an issue arises, or when they feel like they just need to talk about something they are finding frustrating," Ms. Lorenzano said. "I think it's helpful to show clients that I am here to listen and be invested in their case with them."

attorneys.name: Anne Medlin Lowe
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Anne is a 2008 graduate of DePauw University, where she was a Media Fellow, Honor Scholar, award-winning student journalist and on-air personality, and interned with media organizations such as Clear Channel Radio and MTV Networks. After graduating from DePauw, Anne worked for two years as an associate producer at an Indianapolis video production firm specializing in legal video. During law school, Anne volunteered as a Guardian ad Litem, was named to the Order of the Barristers, and argued in the final round of the Staton Moot Court Competition. She also participated in the Evans Constitutional Law National Moot Court Competition both as an advocate and as a coach. Anne was the Executive Note Development Editor for the Indiana International and Comparative Law Review and in 2013 earned the Norman Lefstein Award of Excellence for her pro bono service. Anne spent the first years of her legal career clerking for the Honorable Paul D. Mathias of the Indiana Court of Appeals. It was here she learned the art of meticulous, thorough research and crisp, compelling legal analysis. Anne has spent the years following her clerkship as a trial and appellate litigator, handling cases ranging from simple auto accident matters to small business litigation to complex high-stakes civil appeals before the Indiana Supreme Court. Every year since 2017, Anne has been recognized on the Super Lawyers "Rising Stars" list.

attorneys.name: Brian K. Lowe
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Greenwood, IN
attorneys.bio:
Since 2002, Brian has represented clients in Family Law and Personal Injury cases. While in law school, Brian worked for the Greenwood, Indiana law firm of Smart, Kessler, & Torres and remained at the different iterations of that firm for 19 years. Brian moved on from what eventually became Smart, Kessler & Lowe, LLC in June of 2019 to join Greenwood family law attorney, Jonathan Deenik.

Brian’s experience includes representing Indiana Personal Injury clients involved in semi-truck accidents, motorcycle accidents, truck accidents, pedestrian accidents, premises liability cases, and automobile accidents. Brian has helped clients navigate wrongful death and child injury cases. Serving as co-counsel, Brian has assisted in the representation of clients with civil rights, negligence, and medical malpractice claims.

Brian’s Family Law representation includes divorces, paternity actions, child custody, parenting time issues, child support, emancipation, post-secondary education (college) expenses, relocations, modifications, adoptions, guardianships, and pre-nuptial agreements. Brian practices Family Law in Johnson, Marion, and Morgan County Indiana. Brian also serves as a Registered Domestic Relations Mediator and is a Family Law Arbitrator.

In 2008, Brian became a duly appointed Administrative Law Judge (ALJ) with the Indiana State Department of Health and subsequently with the Indiana Department of Education in 2010 until shortly after the founding of Deenik Lowe. Brian’s experience in hearing cases as an ALJ provides him with a unique perspective in advocating for his own clients.

Zondervan Publishing released a book Brian co-authored with his wife, Cherie in 2018 entitled Your Money, Your Marriage. Through the promotion of the book, Brian appeared at book signings, speaking engagements, and on several podcasts. Brian gave interviews on national media including the Focus on the Family daily broadcast and Family Life Today. Articles about Brian’s personal finance habits have appeared in the Wall Street Journal, the Chicago Tribune, and several major newspapers and media outlets across the country.

attorneys.name: Valerie Loya
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Valerie Loya was born and raised right outside the nation’s capital in Northern Virginia. She attended Virginia Commonwealth University in Richmond, VA and joined the Virginia Army National Guard in 2011. Valerie continued her service after graduation while she attended the University of Iowa College of Law. During this time Valerie began working for the Johnson County Attorney’s Office which sparked her love for litigation.

Upon graduating and being admitted to the Indiana bar in 2016, Valerie began her career as a Prosecutor in Marion County. She litigated different types of cases ranging from low level misdemeanors to attempted murder. Primarily dealing with victims of domestic violence, Valerie understands the importance and impact of an empathetic ear. In December of 2019, Valerie proudly joined Hensley Legal Group as a Spanish-speaking personal injury attorney and is excited to serve the Spanish-speaking community in the State of Indiana.

Valerie is an active mentor with Starfish Initiative. She also serves on the board of La Plaza, Inc. advocating for the educational success of Latino students in central Indiana and connecting families with health and social services. Valerie and her husband Anthony live in downtown Indianapolis, where they love to explore the ever-evolving city.

attorneys.practice_type: Emerging Business Creation Lawyers in Fishers, IN
attorneys.bio:
Steven M. Lutz joined the firm as a partner in October 2009. Steve's general civil practice areas include: emerging business creation and general business representation, general commercial litigation, real estate litigation, appellate practice, estate planning and administration, and creditor's rights. Mr. Lutz is admitted to practice before the Supreme Court of Indiana, and the United States District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana.

Mr. Lutz was born in Jasper, Indiana, and raised in Hershey, Pennsylvania, graduating from Lower Dauphin High School in 1993. He obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Industrial Management/Industrial Engineering, with a minor in psychology, from Purdue University in 1998. While at Purdue, he served as President of Lambda Chi Alpha fraternity. He graduated from Indiana University School of Law at Indianapolis in 2002 earning his Juris Doctorate, cum laude. While in law school, he served as a Fellow on the Dean's Tutorial Society and was a co-founding member of the Society to Promote Student Legal Services.

Currently, Mr. Lutz serves as a Member of the Board of Directors for several charitable organizations including the Indianapolis Senior Citizens Center and the C. James and Mary Lou Wilson Charitable Trust Foundation. Mr. Lutz has been providing volunteer legal services to members of the Indianapolis Senior Citizens Center for many years regarding their estate planning needs and related matters. He is also a member of the Indianapolis Bar Association, and the Indiana State Bar Association where he is a Member of the Litigation Section and the Probate, Trust and Real Property Section.

Steve lives in Fishers with his wife, Stefani, an accountant at the national headquarters of Hatworld-Lids, in Indianapolis. Steve is an avid golfer and enjoys spending his non-working hours with his wife, their family and friends, and their cocker spaniel, Hershey.

attorneys.name: Adam S. Lutzke
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Adam Lutzke has vast experience in the area of family law and estate planning. Since he was admitted to practice law in 2010, he has focused his career primarily in the areas of divorce, legal separation, child custody, child support, guardianships, and wills. Adam received a Lead Counsel Rating in the areas of divorce and family law in 2015 by the Lead Counsel Review Board and was recently selected as one of the Top 40 Lawyers Under 40 for family lawyers in the state of Indiana for 2016 by the American Society of Legal Advocates.

Along with having handled hundreds of divorces and custody cases, Adam can also help you with certain estate planning matters, including wills, powers of attorney, living wills, health care representatives, trusts, including educational trusts for your children, and pre-nuptial agreements. He also has experience in collections and landlord/tenant issues.

Adam was born and raised on the northeast side of Indianapolis, Indiana, and attended Lawrence Central High School. He then studied criminal justice and business at Indiana University-Bloomington prior to obtaining his Juris Doctor from the Saint Louis University School of Law. After returning to Indiana in 2010, Adam met his beautiful wife and they now live on the northeast side of Indianapolis.

attorneys.name: Dallin Lykins
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Dallin is a Spanish-speaking immigration attorney with 15 years of experience handling a wide range of cases. A Super Lawyer and active AILA member, he frequently speaks on immigration issues and has appeared before multiple federal agencies. He lives in Indianapolis with his wife and six children.

Dallin has been practicing immigration law for 15 years. He handles all types of immigration matters for individuals, families, churches, and other clients. He has worked on family petitions, affirmative and defensive Asylum cases, applications for Cancellation of Removal, Special Immigrant Juvenile petitions, U Visa and VAWA petitions, DACA, Adjustment of Status, Work Permits, TPS, Military Parole-in-Place, Consular Applications, Waivers, and other immigration matters. He has appeared before the U.S. Department of Justice, the Board of Immigration Appeals, the U.S. Department of State, and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. He is fluent in Spanish.

Dallin has presented on immigration issues at state and national conferences, published articles on a variety of immigration topics, been interviewed on television and radio regarding immigration updates, and been a featured speaker on multiple occasions. He is the past chair of the Latino Affairs Committee of the Indiana Bar Association and currently serves as the Secretary to the Indiana Chapter of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA). He has been recognized as a Super Lawyer, and he has been a member of AILA for 15 years. He is also a member of the Indiana State and Indianapolis Bar Associations.

Dallin graduated cum laude from the Maurer School of Law in Bloomington in 2010 and received a Bachelor of Arts degree from Brigham Young University in Provo, UT in 2006. Before practicing law, Dallin worked as a Communications Specialist and a speechwriter in Washington, D.C. He also served as a full-time, volunteer, missionary for his church in Costa Rica from 2000-2002. Dallin grew up on a farm in south central Indiana, and he now lives in Indianapolis with his wife and their six children.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Recognized as a Super Lawyers

attorneys.name: Kimberly Lytle
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Kimberly Lytle brings a rare combination of lived experience, legal insight, and determination to her family‑law practice. Before becoming an attorney, she spent years working as a paralegal — gaining hands‑on knowledge of the legal system. During that time, she was also a single mother of two young children, rebuilding after her own divorce. Those experiences didn’t just shape her; they sharpened her resolve to advocate for others.

While raising her children and working full‑time, she put herself through law school — a path that demanded grit, discipline, and a deep commitment. That journey gives her a perspective few attorneys can offer: she understands the emotional, financial, and practical realities her clients face because she has lived them. Kim understands how legal decisions affect day‑to‑day life, children, finances, and peace of mind.

Today, she brings that grounded perspective to a modern, high‑caliber family‑law practice. Her clients value her for her ability to combine empathy with strategic, experienced advocacy. Whether guiding someone through divorce, custody issues, or another family transition, she approaches every case with the same philosophy that carried her through her own challenges — people first, solutions forward, and advocacy you can trust.

Kim was born and raised in Central Indiana, and that background influences her approach to client relationships. She believes in being accessible, straightforward, and genuinely invested in the people she represents. Clients are not just case numbers—they are individuals facing real challenges who deserve respect, honesty, and strong advocacy.

Kim received her Juris Doctor from the University of Dayton School of Law. She earned undergrad degrees in Political Science from Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis and Criminal Justice from Indiana University Kokomo.

Kim is known for being loyal, assertive, and personable. She takes the time to truly listen, understanding her clients beyond intake forms, and uses that insight to pursue meaningful results. Colleagues describe her as tenacious and approachable, and clients appreciate her ability to balance professionalism with warmth and humor.

Outside of work, Kim enjoys traveling, spending time in the mountains and national parks, and unwinding with cards and coffee on Sunday mornings—usually playing cribbage with her husband. She’s a dog‑lover, a believer in morning affirmations, and is powered by copious amounts of caffeine and liberal doses of sarcasm.

attorneys.name: Jamie A. Maddox
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jamie began working at Betz + Blevins as a law clerk in October of 2005 during her third year of law school. She sought to work at Betz + Blevins because she is passionate about advocating for individuals. She is now a partner at the firm.

Since joining Betz + Blevins, Jamie has represented numerous individuals in employment and civil rights matters before federal and state courts as well as administrative agencies. As the daughter of a special needs schoolteacher, Jamie has a personal and professional understanding of and extensive experience in representing teachers in negotiations and termination proceedings. These experiences have provided Jamie with the skills to represent clients at all stages of administrative and civil litigation, from pre-filing investigation through trial and appeal.

Jamie received a Bachelor of Arts in Social and Behavioral Science in 2003 from Indiana University - Kokomo, where she graduated with highest distinction.

While in law school, Jamie was a member of the Women's Caucus and served as Secretary for Legal Advocates for Disability Rights in Education (LADRE). Jamie graduated in 2006 from Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis.

Prior to joining Betz + Blevins, Jamie served as a law clerk for Joseph M. Dietz at Meils, Thompson, Dietz & Berish in Indianapolis, and Wood, Tuohy, Gleason, Mercer & Herrin in Indianapolis. Jamie also served as an intern for the Honorable Stephen M. Jessup of Howard County, Indiana as well as an intern in 2002 for United States Senator Evan Bayh.

Jamie is a member of the Indianapolis Bar Association, the Litigation Section of the Indianapolis Bar Association, and the National Employment Lawyers Association, both nationally and the Indiana chapter. She is admitted to practice in all courts of the State of Indiana, including the Indiana Supreme Court as well as the Northern and Southern U.S. District Courts. She is also admitted to practice in the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals.

attorneys.practice_type: Mediation Lawyers in Madison, IN
attorneys.bio:
Pat has a diverse range of experience in numerous areas of law. Currently, Pat focuses on Appellate law, Government law, and Mediation. Pat has represented clients in cases involving personal injury, family law, criminal defense, and complex litigation issues. Pat has provided assistance to clients at all levels of the litigation process from pretrial proceedings to Supreme Court appeals.

Pat is certified as a Civil Mediator and a Family Law Mediator and enjoys assisting parties reach mutually beneficial outcomes. Pat assists clients with Appeals to the Indiana Court of Appeals and Indiana Supreme Court in cases involving complex litigation issues, criminal issues, and family law issues. Pat has represented clients on appeal at the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals and in opposition to Certiorari at the Untied State’s Supreme Court. For several years, Pat has represented Jefferson County and Switzerland County as well as several other government entities. Pat has provided legal advice to local government clients at almost all levels and has represented local government clients in complex litigation issues.

attorneys.bio:
Elizabeth first began working at Betz + Blevins as a law clerk in 2004 during her second year of law school. She sought to work at Betz + Blevins because of the firm's prestigious reputation as passionate advocates for individuals.

Since joining Betz + Blevins, Elizabeth has represented numerous individuals in employment and civil rights matters before federal and state courts as well as administrative agencies. Over the past several years, Elizabeth has continued to broaden her experience in the legal field, writing briefs and memoranda for other attorneys around the State. She also established a literary publishing company and continues to run the business as a sole proprietor.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Andrew C. Mallor leads the firm's private client division, handling all legal needs of the firm's private clients, from complex matrimonial cases to wealth management and family wealth planning, and has been a leading family lawyer in Indiana for over 45 years. He is board certified in family law and is an acclaimed trial lawyer. By applying his many years of experience and his innate creativity to the issue at hand, Andy is often able to devise unique solutions to achieve his clients' objectives. His distinctive team approach in family law matters ensures both a quick response and a total focus on his clients' interests.
