attorneys.practice_type: Divorce, Custody and Support Matters Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Mann has been selected for inclusion in Super Lawyers SuperLawyers Edition for 2009 through 2025.

Mr. Mann is a Certified Family Law Specialist by the Family Law Certification Board. Many think this certification applies only to divorce, it also applies to custody, support, orders of protection (commonly called protective orders or peace bonds), visitation matters, adoptions, guardianships, juvenile matters such as paternity, criminal and Children in need of services.

Mr. Mann and his firm are proud to have been one of the firms who represented Same-Sex couples who were successful in overturning Indiana's ban on Same-Sex marriage. He continues to fight discrimination in the law.

If you are looking for an experienced Indianapolis Divorce Lawyer or Indiana Family Lawyer, you should consider our firm. Mr. Mann has been practicing Family Law for more than 40 years in the Indianapolis area and throughout the State of Indiana.

Mr. Mann regularly practices in the Boone, Hamilton, Hancock, Hendricks, Johnson, Marion, Morgan, and Shelby County courts.

Mr. Mann is a Registered Family Law and Civil Law Mediator. He also is Guardian ad Litem and Parenting Coordinator. Mr. Mann uses his experience in many areas of practice to aggressively represent his clients. Due to his experience in criminal, business and tax arenas Mr. Mann provides a more full service representation in Family Law matters.

While a large portion of Mr. Mann's practice is in the Family Law area he also represents several corporations on contract, personnel and other matters. He also has a varied General Practice in wills, estates, juvenile matters, collections, probate throughout the state of Indiana. Mr. Mann has tried murder cases as well as a death penalty case.

Family Law matters often involve a wide variety of legal issues. Mr. Mann believes in bringing in the experts necessary to handle your cases properly based upon the issues and the budget available.

If he or his associates do not handle a type of case in which you are involved, he will refer you to someone who does. He believes that you are better served being sent to a professional who handles your issue on a regular basis.

Mr. Mann has a Martindale-Hubbell A-V Rating, the highest possible rating in both legal ability and ethical standards. This rating is based upon confidential evaluations by attorneys and judges who are familiar with Mr. Mann.

Mr. Mann was admitted to the Bar of the Supreme Court of the United States of America on May 18, 2015.

Mr. Mann is an approved FINRA arbitrator.

attorneys.name: Cynthia A. Marcus
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Founder, The Marcus Law Firm, LLC in Fishers, Indiana

Cynthia Marcus concentrates her practice in the areas of family law and professional license defense. She is a trained mediator, using her skills to represent clients in divorce, child support and custody, and nursing license cases.

Cynthia “Cynde” Marcus was born in Corona, California. She grew up in Michigan, graduating from Rockford High School. Following graduation, she attended the University of Michigan. She served in the United States Air Force. After completing technical training as a Operating Room Technician, she was assigned to Homestead Air Force Base in Florida.

After completing her service in the Air Force, Cynde used her GI Bill to complete her Bachelor’s degree in nursing at Ball State University. As a Registered Nurse, she worked in the areas of critical care, surgery, and rehabilitation. She was commissioned as an officer in the United States Army Reserves where she worked on active duty establishing and directing the multistate HIV testing program for the Army Reserves.

While attending basic training for the United States Army Reserves, she met Ed Marcus. They later married. Ed is a dentist in Indianapolis. They have two children and enjoy scuba diving, traveling, and canoeing.

Her experience as a Registered Nurse is invaluable in defending nurses before the Indiana State Board of Nursing. As a Registered Nurse, the most important part of her job was advocating for her clients. As a lawyer, her ability to advocate for others has been taken one step further.

Cynde graduated from Indiana University School of Law. She worked for several years in an Indianapolis firm before leaving to start the Marcus Law Firm in 2002. She is a litigator who tries cases in both state and federal courts. She appeals cases in the areas of Family Law and business litigation. Her military experience assists her in the representation of both service members and current/former spouses of service members with regard to divorce, custody, and military retired pay.

With over 29 years experience in Family Law, Cynde has represented hundreds of clients embroiled in divorce litigation involving their children and financial futures. She is an aggressive, level headed lawyer who will be with you and stand for your rights every step of the way.

Cynde represents health care providers before the Indiana Health Professions Boards in actions against their licenses. Her unique perspective both as a nurse and as an attorney allows her insight into the many pressures faced by health care providers.

She has been active with both local and state youth hockey organizations. Cynde has volunteered as a guardian ad litem for youth in Hamilton County.

attorneys.name: Ashley D. Marks
attorneys.practice_type: Long Term Disability Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Ashley D. Marks is a Partner at the Hankey Marks & Crider, which she joined in 2011. She had previously worked at the firm for two as a Law Clerk while she finished law school. Her primary practice areas are Long Term Disability, Short Term Disability, Personal Injury, ERISA, life insurance litigation, and Social Security Disability.

She attended law school at the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law, graduating in 2011. Prior to this, she attended Indiana University, where she obtained two Bachelor degrees in English and Philosophy. While in law school, she was an intern for the Indiana University School of Medicine's legal department. She also served on the board for the International Moot Court Competition as a writer, and was awarded the best overall written brief during the school's 2010 annual competition.

During her legal career, Ashley has been recognized as an Advocate by the American Association for Justice. In 2014, she was named as one of the National Trial Lawyers Top 40 under 40. She has also been named as a Rising Star by Super Lawyers for numerous years, from 2015-2020. In addition, she remains active in several professional legal organizations.

Ashley considers herself blessed to be a part of the legal community as a whole. As an attorney, she prides herself on attention to detail, being compassionate to the needs of others, and being diligent in the representation of her clients. She is proud to help lead the legal team at the Hankey Marks & Crider, an office committed to serving the injured and disabled throughout Indiana and the Midwest.

Ashley truly enjoys serving within her community. Professionally, she regularly represents the Hankey Marks & Crider at various events which provide support for individuals living with disabilities. Personally, she frequently volunteers at her church, and her town's local foodbank. One of her favorite events to participate in at her church is Night to Shine, which provides an unforgettable prom experience for individuals with special needs.

In her free time, Ashley enjoys spending time with her son and family, cheering on her favorite sports teams (Braves, Pacers and Colts), and traveling. She also enjoys anything that keeps her active, including rock climbing and running. She regularly runs half marathons, including all her local favorites: the Indianapolis Half Marathon, the Monumental Marathon, and the 500 Mini Marathon.

attorneys.bio:
James D. Masur II ("JD") has provided legal services to individuals, small and medium size businesses owners, and multi-billion dollar corporations since 1984. He earned his JD from the University of Virginia after having been graduated Phi Beta Kappa from Miami University, where he was awarded the superior student award in his department and achieved fluency in French and German. JD is admitted to the bar of the United States Supreme Court, and to practice before various federal and state trial and appellate courts in Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Wisconsin, Illinois, and Alabama.

attorneys.name: Gerald W. Mayer
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Born, raised, and educated in Indiana, Jerry Mayer has been successfully prosecuting medical malpractice, serious personal injury, and wrongful death cases since 1992. Mr. Mayer graduated from Indiana University with a major in biology and a concentration in biochemistry and graduated from the Indiana University School of Law with a special interest in health care law. This background helps him to understand complex medical issues, which is crucial to prosecuting medical malpractice, personal injury, and wrongful death cases. Mr. Mayer is a member of the American Association of Justice and the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association.

When doctors, nurses, hospitals, and other healthcare providers make mistakes, patients in their care can be seriously injured or can die. Medical errors are often committed by medical professionals who are inadequately trained, who are impaired as a result of alcohol or drugs, or who are just plain careless or too busy to be thorough in their work.

Mr. Mayer was a practicing psychologist for 10 years before beginning his law career, which allows him to bring a unique perspective to his work as a trial lawyer. He understands the enormous stress that victims of malpractice and their families suffer due to careless mistakes of the very people who were trusted with their care. We believe you will be very comfortable working with Mr. Mayer and the entire Greene & Schultz team.

Greene & Schultz works on a contingency fee basis. We only get paid if we win your case. Call us to see if we can be of assistance with your case.

attorneys.name: Jordyn Katzman McAfee
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
It is not every day that you hear someone say that they love their job, but I truly do. From a young age, I knew I wanted to become a lawyer. As a child of two lawyers, I saw how knowledge of the law could be used to help people overcome some of the most trying times in their lives. After earning my law degree, I handled complex business litigation matters for one of the largest law firms in Indianapolis. The experience I gained there was invaluable and laid the foundation for my legal career. It was not until I had my first family law client, however, that I realized that this was the area of law in which I wanted to dedicate my practice.

For most people, going through a divorce or dealing with family related issues represent some of the darkest times in their lives. For certain, these circumstances are difficult by their very nature, but they don’t have to be paralyzing or life-defeating. I believe that if you gain an understanding of your rights and entitlements under the law, you can begin to take the “unknown” out of your situation, and ultimately begin to plan your course out of and beyond your current circumstance. Whether it is handling a divorce, or modifying child custody and support, my focus is on helping my clients understand their rights and on providing them with skilled and compassionate legal advice. I want my clients to know that they have someone on their side; someone that is going to listen to them, counsel them on their rights under the law, and have their best interests at heart.

The area of family law is diverse, but I focus my practice primarily in working with and mediating for (as a Registered Domestic Mediator) clients in divorce matters (pre & post), child related matters (custody, support, relocation), paternity matters, divorce decree enforcement, emancipation, and custody evaluations. I am familiar with dividing retirement assets owned by government and military employees, as well as marital estates that include closely held family businesses.

“Divorce is a hard time in anyone’s life. Not knowing what your future may hold in the next ten years, or even the next ten days can be terrifying. That’s where I come in. I listen to my client’s story, expectations, and concerns, and provide them sound legal advice to guide them through their family law matter.”

attorneys.name: Dan T. McAfee
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Inspired by many of Indiana's own local artisans and their dedication to their particular craft and the patrons they serve, my focus is on working with entrepreneurs and business owners in creating, maintaining, and expanding the businesses they have the passion and courage to build. As a "craft business" lawyer, my goal is always to provide my clients with skilled, experienced, and individually tailored legal work. Over the past decade, I have worked with many craft businesses in a wide range of industries, including cosmetics, design, eSports, tabletop gaming, medicine, music, photography, and other various professional services.

I understand that for most, the thought of going to see an attorney may be a bit like going to see the dentist – you don’t really want to go, but you know that if you don’t, you may be inviting more trouble and “pain” down the road. Discussing your business and its legal needs doesn’t have to be like this. Whether it is helping clients with the inital formation of their business, negotiating or drafting an important contract, or helping to resolve or litigate a business-related dispute, I advise and advocate for my clients in a way that is approachable and client-focused (or as I like to call it, "small-batch" legal services). In representing my clients in this way, I have found that I am able to add value to our relationship not just as "their lawyer," but as a trusted friend who understands law.

“For me, the practice of law is not just about knowing the answers to my client’s issues or being a skilled advocate, those elements are important for sure, but it’s also about building a relationship with my client that lasts beyond the resolution of the legal need that initially brings them to my office.”

I am happy to be able to bring a multidisciplinary perspective to my work in family law, informed by a strong background in mental health, public health, and child and family systems.

Prior to practicing law, I worked (and still work) as a child and family mental health therapist, where I support families navigating complex emotional, behavioral, substance use and systemic challenges. My professional experience also includes work with the Department of Child Services (DCS) and probation-related cases, giving me valuable insight into cases involving child welfare, court oversight, and family stability.

My unique background allows me to approach family law matters with both legal precision and a deep understanding of the human factors involved. I am committed to advocating for my clients with empathy, clarity, and a focus on practical, sustainable outcomes.

It is an honor, that I do not take lightly, to be trusted by families who seek my assistance, during what may be one of the most vulnerable and difficult times of their lives.

attorneys.name: Edward F. McCrea
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Ed has practiced law with this family firm since September 26, 1972. Ed’s 44 year career was patterned after and reflects his father’s general practice of law, with an emphasis upon being an effective courtroom advocate for his clients. Now a certified mediator, Ed has engaged in bench and jury trials in Monroe County and all counties contiguous to Monroe County for more than four decades.

Throughout his career, Ed has been involved with personal injury and wrongful death cases, as well as the areas of estate planning, administration of estates and trusts, real estate transactions and controversies including landlord/tenant issues, and business law. For 40 years Ed has represented teachers and their families through the Indiana State Teachers Association (ISTA), and Ed represents five rural not-for-profit water corporations in Monroe County. Ed has lived in Bloomington and Monroe County all of his life and helped start the Girls Club of Monroe County (now Girls, Inc.) in 1974 when the area was served only by a Boys Club. Ed is a lifetime member of the Monroe County Historical Society for which he helped secure tax exempt status as a not-for-profit entity and has served on the Board of Directors of the Monroe County Chapter of the American Red Cross.

Ed obtained his undergraduate degree, cum laude, from Harvard University in 1969 and his law degree from Indiana University School of Law in 1972. He is a member of the Indiana State Bar Association and Monroe County Bar Association.

attorneys.firm_name: Parr Richey Frandsen Patterson Kruse LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lebanon, IN
attorneys.bio:
Parr Injury attorney John McLaughlin has focused his practice on representing personal injury victims since his first year joining the firm. John primarily handles automobile and trucking accident cases involving serious injuries and wrongful death, and he also handles all other areas of the firm’s injury practice including medical malpractice. John serves as the Managing Partner for Parr Richey Frandsen Patterson Kruse LLP at each of its three office locations.

John has worked on behalf of his clients in reaching numerous settlements and jury trial verdicts since his first year of practice, including multiple recoveries exceeding $1,000,000.00 since 2018 with John serving as lead counsel on those cases. John also worked to obtain compensation on behalf of victims injured in the Indiana State Fair Sugarland stage collapse incident that occurred in 2011.

John was recognized and selected as an Indiana Super Lawyer in 2024 for his work representing personal injury victims. John was recognized in the Indiana Super Lawyers Magazine from 2013 through 2023 as a Rising Star. John was recognized by Best Lawyers in 2023 for his work representing personal injury victims. In 2014 through 2023, John was invited and selected to become a member of The National Trial Lawyers: Top 100 Trial Lawyers for the State of Indiana. In 2016 through 2023, John was invited and selected to become a member of The National Trial Lawyers: Top 40 Under 40.

John proudly serves on the Indianapolis Legal Aid Society Board of Directors and currently serves on its Executive Committee as Secretary. He also proudly serves on the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association Board of Directors.

John has repeatedly been invited to present and speak to other attorneys through for continuing learning education by various associations and organizations over the years related to his practice of representing injury victims. These speaking opportunities include seminars put on by: the National Business Institute; the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association; the Indiana State Bar Association; the Boone County Bar Association; and the Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum.

John graduated magna cum laude from Indiana University School of Law at Indianapolis before joining Parr Richey Frandsen Patterson Kruse LLP as an attorney.

John is admitted to practice law in the State of Indiana and the Federal District Court for both the Southern District of Indiana and the Northern District of Indiana.

John grew up on a grain and livestock family farm in LeRoy, Illinois. He resides with his family in Zionsville.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Brooke McMillin’s natural abilities to be focused and well-organized were born out in her initial career as a project manager for a major national corporation. While she enjoyed significant success in this career, the study of law had long been her true interest. Before becoming an attorney, Brooke spent seven years working as a paralegal in family law, gaining firsthand experience with the complexities and deeply personal nature of domestic relations cases.

Brooke ultimately pursued her long-standing interest in the law by earning her Juris Doctor from the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law. Her experience in family law both before and after admission to the bar allows her to approach cases with practical insight, careful organization, and attention to detail, helping clients navigate challenging legal matters with clarity and confidence. She works with clients on a variety of domestic relations matters, including divorce, custody, parenting time, and related family law issues.

In working with clients, Brooke focuses on helping them understand both what is happening in their case and why. She believes that explaining the legal process and the reasoning behind important decisions helps clients feel informed and involved rather than overwhelmed. Drawing on the organizational and communication skills developed during her career as a project manager, she works to keep cases on track while building trust and maintaining clear communication with her clients.

Outside of the office, Brooke enjoys exploring her many interests. She has a particular appreciation for history and architecture – especially historic buildings – which she happily admits to obsessing over in her spare time. She also enjoys a good glass of wine and spending time with her cats.

attorneys.name: James W. McNew 1949
attorneys.firm_name: Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Greenfield, IN
attorneys.bio:
1949 – 2018

James Walker McNew was born in Indianapolis, Indiana, on January 31, 1949. He graduated from the University of Kentucky with a double-major in Political Science and History. He then attended and graduated from the Indiana University School of Law in Indianapolis, Indiana. Jim was admitted to the Indiana State Bar in 1976.

From 1976 through 1979, Jim was a Deputy Prosecutor in the Major Felony Division of the Marion County, Indiana, Prosecutor’s Office. In 1981, Jim became the Trial Supervisor with the Lake County, Indiana, Prosecutor’s Office, where he worked until 1989.

In 1989, Jim moved to Greenfield, Indiana, and joined the firm of Brand & Allen as a criminal defense attorney. In 1999, the firm was renamed Allen Wellman McNew, and then in 2014 changed to Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP. Jim practiced law as a partner of the firm until his death. Jim passed away peacefully on December 7, 2018, following a battle with cancer.

Jim was a champion of criminal justice rights and a firm believer in the rule of law. As a young deputy prosecutor, Jim was the lead trial attorney in the successful prosecution of Paula Cooper, who at age 16 was convicted of the murder of an elderly woman in her home. The case received international attention when the Lake County Prosecutor decided to seek the death penalty, which was an option under Indiana law at the time. Jim also represented the State in the death penalty phase of the case, and Paula was sentenced to death.

Paula Cooper’s death sentence was reversed by the Indiana Supreme Court. The Court held that Indiana’s death penalty statute, without a minimum age, was unconstitutional. Cooper v. State, 540 N.E.2d 1216 (Ind. 1989). The case thus became the change-point in protecting minors from the death penalty in Indiana. Although Jim did not personally believe, at the time, that minors who committed murder should be subject to the death penalty, Jim accepted his role to represent the State of Indiana based upon the status of the law as it applied to that case.

The Paul Cooper case exemplified Jim’s respect for the law as it applied to his cases. After moving into private practice as a defense attorney, Jim worked diligently to see to it that his clients received a proper and effective defense – regardless of the extent to which their financial resources would provide for such representation. Jim also pursued changes in the law through the appellate process when the opportunity arose to do so. Jim appealed the case of Danielle Kelly v. State of Indiana, 997 N.E.2d 1045 (Ind. 2013) to the Indiana Supreme Court, where he presented oral argument on behalf of his client. As a result of that case, the Indiana Supreme Court provided clarification on the matter of a person’s Miranda warning rights. The decision strengthens protection of the constitutional rights of Indiana citizens in the context of an arrest.

Jim’s other appellate work resulted in the following decisions:

State v. Lime, 619 N.E.2d 601 (Ind.Ct.App. 1993)

Dickson v. State, 624 N.E.2d 472 (Ind.Ct.App. 1993)

Kinsey v. Kinsey, 640 N.E.2d 42 (Ind. 1994)

Wilson v. State, 847 N.E.2d 1064 (Ind.Ct. App. 2006)

McNelly v. State, 20 N.E.3d 224 (Ind.Ct.App. 2014)

Jim also gave back to and supported law enforcement in Hancock County. At the time of his death, Jim was a member of the Hancock County Sheriff’s Merit Board, serving on the Board since 2014. Jim also assisted the local judiciary, serving as judge pro tem in all of Hancock County’s courts on a regular basis.

Jim was recognized within our firm and in the Hancock County Bar as a mentor for young attorneys learning the practice of criminal defense. Several attorneys in our firm have benefited greatly from his teaching. He was a highly respected member of the Hancock County Bar Association. In June, 2018, the Hancock County Bar Association recognized Jim’s skills as a trial attorney by presenting him with the James L. Brand Trial Advocate Award.

Jim was a wonderful person and law partner. He had a keen intellect, and a commanding presence in the court room. He leaves our firm with a remarkable legacy.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
1949 – 2018

James Walker McNew was born in Indianapolis, Indiana, on January 31, 1949. He graduated from the University of Kentucky with a double-major in Political Science and History. He then attended and graduated from the Indiana University School of Law in Indianapolis, Indiana. Jim was admitted to the Indiana State Bar in 1976.

From 1976 through 1979, Jim was a Deputy Prosecutor in the Major Felony Division of the Marion County, Indiana, Prosecutor’s Office. In 1981, Jim became the Trial Supervisor with the Lake County, Indiana, Prosecutor’s Office, where he worked until 1989.

In 1989, Jim moved to Greenfield, Indiana, and joined the firm of Brand & Allen as a criminal defense attorney. In 1999, the firm was renamed Allen Wellman McNew, and then in 2014 changed to Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP. Jim practiced law as a partner of the firm until his death. Jim passed away peacefully on December 7, 2018, following a battle with cancer.

Jim was a champion of criminal justice rights and a firm believer in the rule of law. As a young deputy prosecutor, Jim was the lead trial attorney in the successful prosecution of Paula Cooper, who at age 16 was convicted of the murder of an elderly woman in her home. The case received international attention when the Lake County Prosecutor decided to seek the death penalty, which was an option under Indiana law at the time. Jim also represented the State in the death penalty phase of the case, and Paula was sentenced to death.

Paula Cooper’s death sentence was reversed by the Indiana Supreme Court. The Court held that Indiana’s death penalty statute, without a minimum age, was unconstitutional. Cooper v. State, 540 N.E.2d 1216 (Ind. 1989). The case thus became the change-point in protecting minors from the death penalty in Indiana. Although Jim did not personally believe, at the time, that minors who committed murder should be subject to the death penalty, Jim accepted his role to represent the State of Indiana based upon the status of the law as it applied to that case.

The Paul Cooper case exemplified Jim’s respect for the law as it applied to his cases. After moving into private practice as a defense attorney, Jim worked diligently to see to it that his clients received a proper and effective defense – regardless of the extent to which their financial resources would provide for such representation. Jim also pursued changes in the law through the appellate process when the opportunity arose to do so. Jim appealed the case of Danielle Kelly v. State of Indiana, 997 N.E.2d 1045 (Ind. 2013) to the Indiana Supreme Court, where he presented oral argument on behalf of his client. As a result of that case, the Indiana Supreme Court provided clarification on the matter of a person’s Miranda warning rights. The decision strengthens protection of the constitutional rights of Indiana citizens in the context of an arrest.

Jim’s other appellate work resulted in the following decisions:

State v. Lime, 619 N.E.2d 601 (Ind.Ct.App. 1993)

Dickson v. State, 624 N.E.2d 472 (Ind.Ct.App. 1993)

Kinsey v. Kinsey, 640 N.E.2d 42 (Ind. 1994)

Wilson v. State, 847 N.E.2d 1064 (Ind.Ct. App. 2006)

McNelly v. State, 20 N.E.3d 224 (Ind.Ct.App. 2014)

Jim also gave back to and supported law enforcement in Hancock County. At the time of his death, Jim was a member of the Hancock County Sheriff’s Merit Board, serving on the Board since 2014. Jim also assisted the local judiciary, serving as judge pro tem in all of Hancock County’s courts on a regular basis.

Jim was recognized within our firm and in the Hancock County Bar as a mentor for young attorneys learning the practice of criminal defense. Several attorneys in our firm have benefited greatly from his teaching. He was a highly respected member of the Hancock County Bar Association. In June, 2018, the Hancock County Bar Association recognized Jim’s skills as a trial attorney by presenting him with the James L. Brand Trial Advocate Award.

Jim was a wonderful person and law partner. He had a keen intellect, and a commanding presence in the court room. He leaves our firm with a remarkable legacy.

attorneys.name: William P. Means
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
William P. Means is a Founder of Hollingsworth Roberts Means, LLC. He is admitted to the Indiana State Bar, as well as the United States District Court for Indiana’s Northern and Southern Districts.

Bill focuses his practice on representing individuals who find themselves, whether voluntarily or not, in the midst of a family dispute, including the following areas:

Divorce

Custody

Parenting Time

Child Support

Paternity

Legal Separation

Grandparent Visitation

Third-Party Custody

Relocation

Guardianship

Prenuptial Agreements

Military Divorce

Protective Orders.

Bill’s approach to family law matters is to guide the firm’s clients through life-changing events with a combination of tact, sensitivity, and problem-solving. Not every case requires a hammer-like approach, and for those matters Bill will do everything he can to steer your case to an efficient and agreeable resolution.

Having said that, everyone has a line beyond which they will not compromise. That issue may revolve around a parenting time schedule, distribution of the marital estate, or another matter upon which a compromise is not reached. In those instances, Bill draws upon his extensive litigation and courtroom experience to zealously advocate for your best interests.

Bill’s favorite part of his work is going to court. From the perspective of the attorney, it is a unique intellectual and professional challenge. However, Bill recognizes that for the client, going to court can be an emotionally and financially draining endeavor. Making the decision to go to court can be difficult, and Bill will guide you in making the best decision for you and your family.

Following five years working in the mental health field, Bill attended law school at the Indiana University School of Law – Indianapolis, earning his Juris Doctorate, cum laude.

Prior to focusing his practice on family law, Bill also gained experience in the following areas of civil litigation:

Creditor’s rights

Contract disputes

Medical malpractice

Hobbies

Away from work, Bill enjoys spending time with family, friends, and his two mini-goldendoodles. Bill also enjoys supporting both IU and Purdue sports, in addition to the Pacers and Colts.

attorneys.name: Shannon L. Melton
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Discrimination, Wrongful Discharge, and Retaliation Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Shannon Melton is a partner and litigator with the law firm of Wilson Melton, LLC. Shannon focuses his practice on representing employees during some of the worst times of their lives, after they have suffered embarrassing and humiliating discrimination or retaliation at the hands of their employers. In order to help aggrieved Hoosier employees all across Indiana, Shannon practices in Indiana state courts as well as both the Northern and Southern Federal District Courts. Shannon has served as lead counsel in cases involving employment discrimination and/or retaliation under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Americans with Disabilities Act, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act, the Family Medical Leave Act, the Fair Labor Standards Act, and state wage and hour laws.

Shannon resides on a small farm in Johnson County, Indiana with his wife and two daughters. When he is not helping clients, Shannon enjoys spending time outdoors, taking care of his farm, working on vehicles, and corralling his girls.

Corey Meridew is a Partner at Camden & Meridew, P.C. Corey is a litigation attorney who prides himself on solving his client's problems as quickly and efficiently as possible. Mr. Meridew's practice centers around the representative of two primary client groups. The first group are business clients. attorneys.name: Anthony Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Anthony grew up in Greenwood, Indiana on the south side of Indianapolis. Ever since he was a young kid, Anthony made it his goal to be an attorney, telling everyone that is what he was going to be when he grew up. Anthony’s first step towards that goal would be attending Indiana University Bloomington from 2014 to 2018. While attending IU Bloomington, he was a part of the Civic Leaders Learning Center and would eventually intern at Indiana Legal Services as part of the intake department to help those in need receive free legal services. He graduated Indiana University in the Spring of 2018 with a Bachelor in Public Affairs in Law Public Policy and a double minor in Public Management and Public Policy Studies.

Immediately after graduating from Indiana University Bloomington, Anthony moved back to Greenwood where he would attend Indiana University Indianapolis Robert H McKinney School of Law. After his first year at the McKinney School of Law, Anthony became a Law Clerk in Hensley Legal Group’s Pre-Litigation Department in the summer of 2019. He continued his work as a Law Clerk part time throughout his entire legal education. While at the McKinney School of Law, Anthony participated in Moot Court and Trial Practice to receive some litigation experience. He received his J.D. from the McKinney School of Law in the spring of 2021 and would be sworn in as an Attorney in Indiana, along with Southern and Northern Federal Districts of Indiana, in October of 2021. Ever since interning at Indiana Legal Services and working at Hensley Legal Group, Anthony has enjoyed being able to help those in need and will carry that passion over as an attorney in Hensley Legal Group’s Premises Liability Department.

In his free time, Anthony enjoys going on hikes, traveling across the United States, going to concerts, and attending Indianapolis Colts football games. As a Hoosier he will always cheer on the IU Men’s Basketball team.

attorneys.name: Christina J. Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Crown Point, IN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Christina J. Miller joined the Miller Sachs & Hess, PC law firm in 2018. Attorney Miller has been a devoted member of the Indiana legal community since October of 1988. In her 35 years of practice, Attorney Miller has served in many capacities, including her judicial appointment as Magistrate of the Lake Circuit Court beginning in 1995. Initially she served on the Family Court bench, hearing various family law matters including dissolution of marriage, custody, child support, interstate child support, interstate paternity, and adoptions. After nearly ten (10) years of service on the Family Court bench, Attorney Miller then transferred to the civil bench where she presided over a general civil docket including jury trials, real estate tax cases, breach of contracts, foreclosures, mental health detentions and she also enjoyed serving as Judicial Settlement Officer for the Court, settling nearly all cases brought to her in that capacity. After 12 years of service, in the Spring of 2007, Attorney Miller left the bench to take a position as a partner with a local law firm and went on to conduct several hundred mediations with a highly successful settlement rate. Attorney Miller has also enjoyed serving her clients in private practice in the field of dissolution of marriage, custody, child support, adoption, corporate dissolution, personal injury and general civil litigation matters. On January 1, 2018, Attorney Miller joined Miller Sachs & Hess, PC, in 2022 Attorney Miller became the owner and managing partner of the firm, and remains committed to providing the best in legal services to her clients.

Attorney Miller has demonstrated her commitment to giving back to the legal community and her local community in many ways. She served on the Continuing Legal Education Commission for the State of Indiana for 10 years from 2010 through 2019. The Continuing Legal Education Commission is an Indiana Supreme Court agency which oversees the continuing legal education of attorneys, mediators and the judiciary for the State of Indiana. Attorney Miller has also served the legal community as an adjunct professor for approximately ten (10) years at the Valparaiso University School of Law. She has undertaken to teach numerous continuing legal education seminars and classes for attorneys, mediators and the judiciary. She has served as Vice Chair of the Family Law Section for the American Bar Association. While still a member of the Indiana judiciary, Attorney Miller served on the Board of Managers for the Indiana Judicial Conference and as District Director for the National Association of Women Judges.

Attorney Miller has also demonstrated a long-standing commitment to her family and community including currently serving on the Board of Directors for St. Jude House in Crown Point, Indiana; serving on the Advisory Council for her children's school (St. Mary's Catholic Community School, Crown Point). She has served on the Parish Council for her church (Holy Spirit Catholic Church, Winfield). She currently acts as the Chairman for the Grievance Committee for the Lakes of Four Seasons Property Owners Association, a volunteer position. She has been a Girl Scout leader, soccer coach and "team mom" for soccer teams, basketball teams, swim teams, and the like. Attorney Miller's philosophy of giving back to the community and teaching children by example has led to countless hours of volunteerism for sports teams and charities.

The Continuing Legal Education Commission is an Indiana Supreme Court agency which oversees the continuing legal education of attorneys, mediators and the judiciary for the State of Indiana. Attorney Miller has also served the legal community as an adjunct professor for approximately ten (10) years at the Valparaiso University School of Law. She has undertaken to teach numerous continuing legal education seminars and classes for attorneys, mediators and the judiciary. She has served as Vice Chair of the Family Law Section for the American Bar Association. While still a member of the Indiana judiciary, Attorney Miller served on the Board of Managers for the Indiana Judicial Conference and as District Director for the National Association of Women Judges.

Attorney Miller has also demonstrated a long-standing commitment to her family and community including currently serving on the Board of Directors for St. Jude House in Crown Point, Indiana; serving on the Advisory Council for her children's school (St. Mary's Catholic Community School, Crown Point). She has served on the Parish Council for her church (Holy Spirit Catholic Church, Winfield). She currently acts as the Chairman for the Grievance Committee for the Lakes of Four Seasons Property Owners Association, a volunteer position. She has been a Girl Scout leader, soccer coach and "team mom" for soccer teams, basketball teams, swim teams, and the like. Attorney Miller's philosophy of giving back to the community and teaching children by example has led to countless hours of volunteerism for sports teams and charities.

attorneys.name: N. Alan Miller III
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Law Lawyers in Lawrenceburg, IN
attorneys.bio:
N. Alan Miller III began his legal career as a law clerk at a Lawrenceburg law firm in 2003. After his admission to the Indiana bar, he began his legal practice in 2005 as an associate attorney with the same firm, where he was made a partner in 2007. In 2013, Alan left this firm to start Miller Law LLC. In September 2016, Alan's sister, Adrienne Flannery, joined the practice and Miller Law became Miller Flannery Law.

Over the course of his practice, he has developed a reputation as a compassionate and empathetic attorney who listens and advises his clients in a non-judgmental way. Alan has over 20 years’ experience in the field of bankruptcy law. He works with families and individuals in difficult situations navigate options.

Alan is a certified civil and family law mediator. He also represents both men and women in divorces with children and without children. His approach is to focus on resolutions for his clients through negotiation and collaboration.

A life-long resident of Dearborn County, the Millers can trace their family roots in Dearborn County to before the Civil War. Alan is active in the community and resides in Aurora with his wife, Kyle (Thayer), and their daughter, Ryan. He loves the Reds, IU sports, being outdoors and spending time with his family.

In her spare time, Silvia enjoys attending her children's year round softball and baseball games, getting to as many Cubs games as possible, and spending time with friends and family.

attorneys.name: Ryan G. Milligan
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury/Product Injury Lawyers in South Bend, IN
attorneys.bio:
Ryan G. Milligan, a former partner in one of America’s largest law firms, brings over a decade of complex litigation, dispute resolution, and trial experience to PM&S. After defending some of the nation's largest banks, corporations and insurance companies, he now applies his trial and litigation skills to advocate for victims of personal and financial injury.

Responsive and results-oriented, Ryan is a lawyer who helps clients understand and navigate through the following types of legal matters:

Personal injury, product injury and premises liability

Ryan represents the legal interests of people who have been injured in car accidents, truck accidents, motorcycle accidents and by defective or recalled products. He also represents plaintiffs in premises liability cases and wrongful death actions.

Financial Injury/Consumer Protection

Ryan represents victims who have had their credit ruined or peace of mind violated by harassing debt collectors, robo calls, predatory lending, vehicle repossessions, consumer fraud, data breaches and other consumer protection matters. He also represents plaintiffs in insurance coverage disputes, including the bad faith denial of insurance coverage, and indemnification matters.

Class Actions

After several years defending class actions, Ryan has significant experience with class action practice, including class certification and class settlements. Class actions can secure justice for a class or group of individuals that has been treated improperly, such as victims of mass torts, robo calls, or predatory lending or collection practices.

Fixed Fee Appeals

Ryan has experience handling dozens of appeals in state and federal court, both protecting positive trial court results and reversing negative outcomes. To provide certainty and avoid unexpected costs, Ryan handles appeals on a fixed fee basis.

Contingent Fee Business Litigation

Ryan also combines his considerable experience as a business lawyer and former business owner to represent selective clients as plaintiffs in contingent fee commercial lawsuits and business litigation.

attorneys.name: Daniel L. Moore
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Dan grew up in Lawrence and Franklin Townships in Indianapolis. The son of a police officer and bank teller, Dan's upbringing included being taught (often the hard way) the value of hard work, fundamental fairness and an appreciation for taking charge of your own future. After graduating high school, moving out of his parents' home for a year of learning a little something of the real world, Dan managed to get accepted to Ball State University. Excelling academically, even earning an undergraduate Fellowship, Dan began saving his earnings from employment in his dorm's dining service with hopes of earning more than just a Bachelor's Degree. Following his Ball State University graduation, Dan applied to law school at Valparaiso University, was accepted and ultimately graduated near the top of his class in 1990.

Dan opened his law firm in 1990 with the idea that everyone deserves a good lawyer and those whose freedom is at stake, deserve the best lawyer. Practicing criminal defense exclusively since the firm was founded, Dan has acted as lead defense counsel in over 4,000 criminal cases. His experience includes defending persons charged with serious crimes like murder and robbery and misdemeanor crimes like drunk driving and minor drug offenses. Dan has practiced all over Indiana in our State Trial Courts, the Indiana Appellate Courts and before the Indiana Supreme Court. Few lawyers have that breadth of experience and fewer still have that level of experience in such a narrow field.

Dan has served as Judge pro temp or special Judge in multiple counties and has presided as Judge over cases as serious as murder and as common as possession of marijuana and driving while suspended. Dan defends persons accused of crimes, anyone whose gun rights or driving privileges are in jeopardy, anyone whose record should be expunged and anyone being investigated by the police, state, local or federal. Dan has represented clients referred to him by Judges, prosecutors, police and the NRA. What better recommendation could he be given? His decades of experience and his unique perspective combine to make him your best choice in a defense lawyer. Don't stand alone. Call Dan and build your best defense now.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Josh Moudy earned his undergraduate degree from Wabash College and his law degree from Indiana University School of Law - Indianapolis. Before joining Richard Kammen, he served as both a private and court-appointed attorney for clients whose charges ranged from public intoxication to rape, robbery and murder.

Mr. Moudy has always had a desire to defend those involved with the criminal justice system, but perhaps more importantly, he understands the confusion and concern that comes from being the subject of a criminal investigation. He knows that in addition to a passionate defense, most clients need answers, patience and to be heard. He strives to provide that to every client.

Mr. Moudy has repeatedly been invited to speak on criminal defense issues and has instructed other attorneys on handling criminal cases. He has served on the Indianapolis Bar Association on numerous committees. He has been named a Bar Leader by the Indianapolis Bar Association. He has also been selected as a Super Lawyer and is a member of the National Assocation of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Elkhart, IN
attorneys.bio:
Douglas A. Mulvaney is a sole practitioner practicing at Mulvaney Law Office, LLC in Elkhart, Indiana. His trial practice concentrates in the areas of worker's compensation and personal injury. He exclusively represents injured parties. He received his college degree from Hope College in Holland, Michigan in 1980 and his law degree from Vermont Law School in South Royalton, Vermont in 1983. He has practiced in Elkhart, Indiana since 1983. He is a member of the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association, and the Elkhart City Bar Association.

When he is not in his law office Mr. Mulvaney enjoys skiing, snowboarding, sailing, golfing and bicycling. Along with his legal practice he is active in several not-for-profit organizations in the Elkhart Community including the Kiwanis Club of Elkhart and is a past President, Elkhart Legal Aid where he is president of the Board of Directors, the Elkhart Education Foundation where he serves as a Board member, the Clear Lake Township Land Conservancy where he serves as a Board member, and Friends of the Elkhart Public Library where he serves as President. He previously served on the City of Elkhart Historic and Cultural Preservation Commission both as a Commission Member and their President. He currently serves on the City of Elkhart Board of Zoning Appeals as their Chair. He also serves as a volunteer judge for the Elkhart County Teen Court.

Mr. Mulvaney lives in Elkhart with his wife Jennifer Nielsen, an infusion nurse and a houseful of pets. Their daughter Anne graduated from Trine University, and unlike her dad, is a math and science wiz, and graduated with a B.S. degree in forensic science. She currently lives in Milford, Massachusetts with her husband Steve.

attorneys.name: Erin M. Mundy
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
We are in a new era where real estate is readily viewable on the internet and my practice has developed to assist buyers and sellers who have decided to take on part or all of the buying or selling property themselves (both residential and commercial). Just because you may want to buy or sell your property yourself, doesn't mean you have to do it by yourself.

I provide professional legal services to my clients with their sale/purchase needs.

Typical services include:

• Sales Negotiations

• Drafting Purchase Documents

• Drafting Inspection Responses

• Reviewing Title Policies

• Resolving Title Issues

• Loan document review

• Representation at Closings

I provide my clients professional legal services based on an hourly rate rather than a commission set by the sale price of the property. And if problems arise and the real estate transaction does not close, I am able to assist my clients with informal negotiations and/or formal litigation to come to a resolution in such circumstances.

In addition to real estate, I have a passion for banking law, business transactional work, business litigation and estate law. Whether I am preparing loan documentation and conducting loan closings on behalf of a bank and/or working for individuals and business entities, forming a business, handling the business transactional work (drafting employee contracts, buy-sell agreements, leases/subleases, etc.), business litigation, or estate work, I am here to handle my client’s legal needs.

I earned my J.D. degree, graduating magna cum laude in 2001, from the Indiana University School of Law in Bloomington. I am admitted to the Indiana bar and the U.S. District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana. I am also a member of Phi Beta Kappa, the Order of the Coif, and the Indianapolis and Indiana Bar Associations. I have had the privilege of serving on the Jewish Community Center's board of directors, volunteering at my children's schools, and am actively involved with the ALS Association Indiana Chapter.

attorneys.practice_type: Automobile Dealership Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Patrick C. Munson is an attorney in Mallor Grodner Plummer Attorneys’ business and professional practice services division. His practice areas include business law, litigation, and automotive dealer representation. Patrick’s passion for the automotive industry began during his childhood in Morristown, Indiana, where his father ran dealerships as a finance officer.

Patrick earned his law degree from the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law, in Indianapolis. He joined Mallor Grodner Plummer Attorneys in February of 2021 as a law clerk. With a strong commitment to client-centered practice, Patrick looks forward to building strong relationships with clients, thoughtfully representing his clients’ interests and helping them successfully resolve conflicts and find solutions to meet their needs.

When not in the office, Patrick enjoys golf, softball, reading philosophy, and spending time with his family on the lake.

attorneys.name: Brandon C. Elkins
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Brandon C. Elkins-Barkley is a Certified Family Law Specialist, family law litigator, mediator, and parenting coordinator with practice and experience are uniquely tailored to complex asset division, including retirement benefits, and a child-focused approach to custody matters. Brandon provides comprehensive family legal services involving custody disputes, parenting issues, and property division, including high net-worth clients with business interests, complex employment benefits packages, and financial issues. Experienced in state and federal courts, Brandon holds a Masters of Law in Taxation from the University of Denver. While Brandon is a family law attorney with over a 15 years of experience, his practice has allowed him to represent clients in the Indiana Supreme Court, Indiana Court of Appeals, state trial courts, and in federal administrative appeals. Also, Brandon brings his unique experience of having worked in an international family law firm to his client matters involving disputes and issues reaching far beyond Indiana. Brandon regularly presents at continuing legal education seminars about retirement and employee benefits and how those assets are handled in divorce cases, as well as other topics.

A graduate of the Indiana University Maurer School of Law in Bloomington. As the child of parents who divorced in his infancy, Brandon has a direct and personal perspective on how the divorce process effects children , which guides him as a parenting coordinator. He clerked for the Honorable Judge Richard Caschette in Colorado’s 18th Judicial District before entering private practice. Brandon returned to Indiana in 2018, where he has been ever since.

Brandon believes keeping a focus on litigation preparation and creative strategy is essential in representing clients, he also is always looking for opportunities to resolve and minimize intrafamily conflict. He emphasizes the importance of a positive and constructive attorney-client relationship and believes the best result for his clients will only come from an open and trusting line of communication. Brandon listens, cares, and always gives thoughtful, honest, and practical legal advice.

Your family dynamic is changing, and Brandon is here to provide a complete legal framework for minimizing the impact of those changes.

attorneys.name: Mariellen "DeeDee" Katzman
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
I love what I do! Over the past 40 years I have been fortunate to be able to incorporate into my legal career the knowledge and skills I mastered when I attained my Bachelor of Science Degree from the "Indiana University of Medicine" (1973) and experience I gained as a hands-on provider of rehabilitation services to those suffering from acute disabilities (spinal cord injuries, auto accident and burn victims, stroke and other neurological disorders, amputations, surgical complications). I graduated with honors (Cum Laude) from Indiana University School of Law at Indianapolis in May, 1978 and I was able to jump into law almost immediately, having taken and passed the bar exam before I graduated from law school. Although I received top honors (American Jurisprudence Award) in criminal procedure, I have always focused my practice on dealing with people who are seeking legal advice due to their personal struggles - whether it be from the emotional stress and mental anguish connected with divorce and post divorce issues or the physical and emotional pain that results from traumatic injuries.

My husband and other senior partner Alvin Katzman and I are honored to work with six other outstanding lawyers in our firm. Our love of assisting people with their legal issues, is well-reflected by the fact that our daughters both chose to become lawyers. We are blessed to work side-by-side with them in and out of the courtroom.

We have also been privileged and personally gratified to participate alongside with the members of our firm in many philanthropic endeavors that are dear to our hearts. We have assisted in preparing and serving meals to families staying at the Ronald McDonald House, raised money for and walked in fundraisers for the Susan G. Komen Race for the Cure, the Walk to End Alzheimer's, and other worthy causes.

Awards and Honors

Honors

American Jurisprudence, Criminal Procedure

attorneys.name: Brandon C. Elkins
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Brandon C. Elkins-Barkley is a Certified Family Law Specialist, family law litigator, mediator, and parenting coordinator with practice and experience are uniquely tailored to complex asset division, including retirement benefits, and a child-focused approach to custody matters. Brandon provides comprehensive family legal services involving custody disputes, parenting issues, and property division, including high net-worth clients with business interests, complex employment benefits packages, and financial issues. Experienced in state and federal courts, Brandon holds a Masters of Law in Taxation from the University of Denver. While Brandon is a family law attorney with over a 15 years of experience, his practice has allowed him to represent clients in the Indiana Supreme Court, Indiana Court of Appeals, state trial courts, and in federal administrative appeals. Also, Brandon brings his unique experience of having worked in an international family law firm to his client matters involving disputes and issues reaching far beyond Indiana. Brandon regularly presents at continuing legal education seminars about retirement and employee benefits and how those assets are handled in divorce cases, as well as other topics.

A graduate of the Indiana University Maurer School of Law in Bloomington. As the child of parents who divorced in his infancy, Brandon has a direct and personal perspective on how the divorce process effects children , which guides him as a parenting coordinator. He clerked for the Honorable Judge Richard Caschette in Colorado’s 18th Judicial District before entering private practice. Brandon returned to Indiana in 2018, where he has been ever since.

Brandon believes keeping a focus on litigation preparation and creative strategy is essential in representing clients, he also is always looking for opportunities to resolve and minimize intrafamily conflict. He emphasizes the importance of a positive and constructive attorney-client relationship and believes the best result for his clients will only come from an open and trusting line of communication. Brandon listens, cares, and always gives thoughtful, honest, and practical legal advice.

Your family dynamic is changing, and Brandon is here to provide a complete legal framework for minimizing the impact of those changes.

attorneys.name: Mariellen "DeeDee" Katzman
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
I love what I do! Over the past 40 years I have been fortunate to be able to incorporate into my legal career the knowledge and skills I mastered when I attained my Bachelor of Science Degree from the "Indiana University of Medicine" (1973) and experience I gained as a hands-on provider of rehabilitation services to those suffering from acute disabilities (spinal cord injuries, auto accident and burn victims, stroke and other neurological disorders, amputations, surgical complications). I graduated with honors (Cum Laude) from Indiana University School of Law at Indianapolis in May, 1978 and I was able to jump into law almost immediately, having taken and passed the bar exam before I graduated from law school. Although I received top honors (American Jurisprudence Award) in criminal procedure, I have always focused my practice on dealing with people who are seeking legal advice due to their personal struggles - whether it be from the emotional stress and mental anguish connected with divorce and post divorce issues or the physical and emotional pain that results from traumatic injuries.

My husband and other senior partner Alvin Katzman and I are honored to work with six other outstanding lawyers in our firm. Our love of assisting people with their legal issues, is well-reflected by the fact that our daughters both chose to become lawyers. We are blessed to work side-by-side with them in and out of the courtroom.

We have also been privileged and personally gratified to participate alongside with the members of our firm in many philanthropic endeavors that are dear to our hearts. We have assisted in preparing and serving meals to families staying at the Ronald McDonald House, raised money for and walked in fundraisers for the Susan G. Komen Race for the Cure, the Walk to End Alzheimer's, and other worthy causes.

Awards and Honors

Honors

American Jurisprudence, Criminal Procedure

attorneys.bio:
Eric Neidlinger has 17 years of private and in-house practice experience in the areas of real estate transactions and land use, commercial and multifamily residential development, business organizations and commercial transactions, employment, insurance and liability.

Eric's practice at Cohen Garelick & Glazier is focused in the areas of real estate, business and commercial services. He represents owners, developers, builders, and contractors in all aspects of the acquisition, financing (debt and equity), development, ownership, leasing and sale of commercial and residential real estate projects. Eric also represents lenders in the negotiation and documentation of commercial loans, commercial property owners in landlord-tenant and fair housing matters, and businesses in transactional, employment and litigation matters.

Before returning to private practice in 2014, Eric was in-house counsel at Pedcor Companies, a collection of businesses that operate under an umbrella of common ownership and engage in a wide variety of business lines, including the development, ownership and management of multifamily housing communities and commercial properties. As Vice President and Associate General Counsel, he provided counsel to the Companies' owners and executive officers in matters relating to the Companies' business interests and activities in the areas of real estate development, transactions and land use, the fair housing and employment laws, insurance and liability.

attorneys.name: Casandra J. Nelson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
CASANDRA J. NELSON ("Casi") grew up in Noblesville, Indiana, and was admitted to the Indiana Bar in 2014. Ms. Nelson is also licensed to practice in the U.S. District Court for the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana. She graduated from Indiana University in 2010 with a B.A. in Journalism. She received her law degree, magna cum laude, from Florida Coastal School of Law in 2014. Ms. Nelson's academic achievements include graduating in the top 4% of her class, being a Dean's Scholar, and belonging to the country’s number one ranked Moot Court program, where she received semi-finalist and finalist titles at national competitions, as well as a best individual oral advocate award and a best written brief award. While in law school, Ms. Nelson interned for the Honorable James R. Klindt, United States Magistrate Judge, and for a law firm in Jacksonville, Florida. After passing the bar, Ms. Nelson started her legal career as an associate attorney for the law firm, Campbell Kyle Proffitt LLP. She then owned her own law practice for more than eight years before joining Altman, Poindexter & Wyatt LLC. Ms. Nelson is involved with the Indiana State Bar Association and serves as Office Administrator for the Hamilton County Bar Association. Ms. Nelson was recognized as a Super Lawyers Rising Star from 2019-2024.

Ms. Nelson currently practices in the areas of appellate law; estate planning and probate; civil litigation; and family law, including issues related to divorce, custody, parenting time, child support, paternity, prenuptial agreements, post-decree modifications, emancipation, relocations, CHINS, adoption, and protective orders. Ms. Nelson is also a qualified and registered Family Law Guardian Ad Litem (GAL) through the Indiana Courts and advocates for the best interests of children. She is also a staff attorney for the Hamilton County GAL/CASA Program.

Ms. Nelson lives in Carmel, Indiana with her husband, their three daughters, and their dog.

attorneys.name: Michael O. Nelson
attorneys.practice_type: Environmental & Insurance Lawyers in Zionsville, IN
attorneys.bio:
Michael O. Nelson is the President of Nelson Law Group LLC. Prior to founding the firm, Mr. Nelson was a shareholder and attorney concentrating on complex environmental and insurance coverage cases, including mass toxic tort suits and Superfund litigation with the national law firm of Hunsucker, Goodstein & Nelson. As a shareholder at Hunsucker, Goodstein & Nelson, he managed the mid-western office in Indianapolis, Indiana; taking the local presence from a mere two cases to over 60 total cases.

At Nelson Law Group LLC, Mr. Nelson represents clients in a wide range of industries, including construction, dry cleaning, property management, development, foundries, metal working and oil distribution.

Mr. Nelson works with clients, consultants and regulatory agencies to contain client liability and to obtain site closure in hazardous waste cases. He has obtained successful outcomes in multi-party coverage litigation to win substantial policy benefits for a number of clients. Mr. Nelson has represented clients throughout Indiana, including the communities of Anderson, Richmond, Muncie, Greensburg, Brazil, Ft. Wayne, Evansville, Logansport, Gary, Whiting, Demotte, Ossian, Lynn, Thorntown, and Rushville, as well as Indianapolis. Mr. Nelson has also worked on behalf of local governments to investigate and remediate contaminated properties within their borders.

Prior to joining Hunsucker Goodstein & Nelson PC in 1996, Mr. Nelson worked as a legal intern in the San Francisco District Attorney’s office handling research on civil and criminal environmental issues, and as a law clerk for the United States Environmental Protection Agency, Region IX in San Francisco, in the area of Clean Water Act enforcement. Mr. Nelson was also previously a California State Senate Field Representative in the office of State Senator Lucy Killea.

In his spare time, Mr. Nelson volunteers with the Neighborhood Christian Legal Clinic and other local organizations.

attorneys.bio:
Brandon was born in South Bend, Indiana in 1993. He attended Indiana University at Bloomington and graduated as a double major in political science and economics. While in law school, he was a member of the Moot Court Society as well as an Executive Article Editor on Law Review. Brandon was admitted to the Indiana State Bar and the U.S. District Court, Northern District of Indiana Bar in 2019.

Brandon is a member of the Elkhart County, St. Joseph County and Indiana State Bar Associations.

In addition, Brandon has extensive criminal law trial and plea bargaining experience that was gained from both of his respective tenures as a public defender for Elkhart Legal Aid in the Elkhart City Court and felony arraignment hearings in St. Joseph County.

Brandon serves on the Board of Directors at RETA, which is a family resource center in Elkhart committed to helping men and women find the support they need when facing a pregnancy and beyond.

attorneys.name: Kyle Noffsinger
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Kyle was born and raised in Evansville, Indiana. As the son of a trial lawyer, his interest in trial work began at an early age, when he would go to watch his father in trials. After graduating from Indiana University, he followed up by obtaining his law degree from Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis.

He has served our community as a deputy prosecutor in the Marion County Prosecutor’s Office where he obtained great experience, trying major felony cases, including murder, robbery, fraud, aggravated battery, and burglary. After that, he spent time at a personal injury law firm in Indianapolis, where he gained civil trial experience and learned the value of fighting insurance companies to maximize the value of his client’s cases. That brought him to Crossen Kooi Law.

Kyle was also recently named to The National Trial Lawyers’ Top 40 Under 40. He has handled cases state-wide, and has been admitted to practice law by the Indiana Supreme Court, and the United States District Courts for both the Southern and Northern Districts of Indiana.

Kyle has served as a Big Brother for the past seven years in Big Brothers Big Sisters of Central Indiana. He enjoys playing and watching sports, particularly Indiana University basketball. Kyle and his wife, Martha, live in Carmel with their two children.

attorneys.name: T. Blake Orner
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
As a partner at Grant & Grant, Attorneys, Blake's practice is focused on Litigation, Subrogation, Personal Injury, and Estate Planning and Probate. He represents many national and regional insurance carriers in complex subrogation litigation, including large structural fires for commercial and residential property, construction defects, and products liability. With a background in complex litigation, Blake also focuses on plaintiffs' personal injury, including auto accidents, premise liability, commercial trucking collisions, and product liability.

Licensed to practice in both Indiana and Illinois, Blake has represented clients in both state and federal court. Further, as part of his practice, Blake coordinates the litigation of cases with law firms for matters arising in other states throughout the country, as well as being retained by out-of-state law firms to serve as local counsel in Indiana and Illinois.

Blake is a member of the Indianapolis Bar Association and serves on the Executive Committee of the Litigation Section. He is also a member of the Indiana State Bar Association, Illinois State Bar Association, and National Association of Subrogation Professionals (NASP). Blake has taught and chaired seminars for the Indianapolis Bar Association and the Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum.

An active volunteer in his community, Blake served as President of his Homeowners Association for five years and is a volunteer coach for youth sports in his community. He is a current board member on the Plainfield Optimist Baseball Board and is an avid tennis player.

attorneys.name: Briceida Ortega
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Briceida Ortega was born and raised in a small town in southwest Kansas. She made Indiana home after graduating from Valparaiso University Law School in 2016.

Since a young age, Briceida knew she wanted to be an attorney that helped the disadvantaged. Whether it be due to financial difficulties, injuries, or a language barrier, she wanted to help those in need. Briceida found her love for litigation while in law school when she interned for the Indiana Federal Defenders, an organization that represents indigent defendants at a federal level, and then when she earned a spot on the law school’s Criminal Defense Clinic representing clients that could not afford an attorney.

After passing the Indiana Bar in 2016, Briceida continued her work seeking justice for those who couldn’t afford it as a public defender for Marion County. After several years as a public defender, Briceida turned her focus to another community in need of representation: the Hispanic community. She worked for an immigration firm in Indianapolis, representing clients before several U.S. Immigration Courts, including Chicago, Kansas City, Puerto Rico, and El Paso. Briceida focused on litigating cases in court, however, she also represented individuals in visa matters. Briceida joined Hensley Legal Group, PC in October of 2022 and is excited to continue helping those in need, regardless of income, who have suffered from a car accident, truck accident, slip and fall, or other personal injury.

Briceida serves as the Chair of the Hispanic Lawyers Division of the Indianapolis Bar Association and was appointed by the Mayor of Indianapolis to serve on the Indianapolis Charter School Board. Briceida lives in Indianapolis with her family and loves cheering on the Colts, Pacers, and eating at all the great restaurants.

attorneys.name: Kerry Ann Pangere
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce, Custody, Child Support, Parenting Time Lawyers in Crown Point, IN
attorneys.bio:
KERRY ANN PANGERE

Ms. Pangere was born and raised in Northwest Indiana and is a 1990 graduate of Purdue University where she received her B.A. in Communications with a concentration in English and Psychology. Prior to attending law school, she spent six years in sales and advertising. Ms. Pangere received her J.D. degree, cum laude with honors, from Valparaiso University School of Law in 1999. Ms. Pangere has over 24 years of litigation experience in Family Law and is licensed to practice in all Indiana state courts and the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana.

Ms. Pangere is a former Referee Judge having served as a judicial officer in the Lake Circuit Court from January 2020 through January 2022 where she presided over a vast array of civil matters including divorce, child support, custody, personal injury, commercial collections, and protective orders. Ms. Pangere served as an adjunct professor of law at Valparaiso University School of Law teaching from 2006 through 2017.

Ms. Pangere continues to concentrate her practice in Family Law (divorce, adoption, child support, paternity, emancipation, and custody) and Estate Planning. Ms. Pangere represents her clients with compassion while having the skill, experience, and knowledge of the law. Balancing the client’s needs and wants with the law is what makes Family and Estate Law so unique. Ms. Pangere attempts to tailor her representation to the unique set of facts of each and every client.

Ms. Pangere is a Certified Guardian Ad Litem representing the best interest of children who at times are caught in the midst of their parents’ disputes. Ms. Pangere is a member of the Indiana and Lake County Bar Associations as well as The Women’s Bar Association.

Honors

Outstanding Service to the Community and the Lake Circuit Court Domestic Relations Bureau, 2004

attorneys.name: Joseph Pearman
attorneys.practice_type: Tax Controversy Lawyers in Crown Point, IN
attorneys.bio:
Representing individuals and businesses, with tax delinquencies and related matters, before the Internal Revenue Service, the Indiana Department of Revenue, and the Illinois Department of Revenue the professionals, at Joseph Pearman, Attorney at Law, provide unmatched support, advocacy, and counsel for a variety of tax controversies.

An attorney since 1993, Mr. Pearman has focused exclusively on tax controversy law since 2002 and he holds a Master of Laws in Taxation from DePaul University College of Law. Mr. Pearman established his law firm in order to protect the rights and interests of those dealing with enforced collection activity such as liens, levies, and other related serious tax issues.

Joseph Pearman, Attorney At Law is an Indiana based tax controversy law firm with offices in Crown Point and Fishers. Mr. Pearman has represented taxpayers, with Federal and State tax problems, from down the street to as far away as Hong Kong and Australia.

Mr. Pearman will initially meet with you to help you understand the extent of your tax problem and offer sound legal advice as to what it will take to resolve it. As your attorney, Mr. Pearman will devise and implement the appropriate legal strategy to quickly and efficiently achieve the best outcome possible.

Regardless of how complex your tax problem, you can trust Joseph Pearman, Attorney At Law to remain by your side, throughout the entire process, to ensure the best outcome possible.

For more information, you can contact Joseph Pearman, Attorney at Law by calling the office or visiting the website to schedule an initial consultation.

Daniel joined Terry Legal Group, LLC after spending twenty-two years as a Judge in Hamilton County, Indiana. Daniel served as the first Magistrate from 1995-2005. In his spare time, he enjoys running, biking, traveling and spending time his wife and family.
