attorneys.name: Brian M. Simpson
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Fort Wayne, IN
attorneys.bio:
I was born in Wurzburg, Germany, where my father was stationed during the Vietnam War. My parents were both from the Fort Wayne area, so we returned here soon after I was born. I was a 1990 graduate of Snider High School.

While in college, I competed for the Indiana University Racquetball Team. In my final year of competition, the IU men's team finished #3 in the country and I was the individual national champion. You can see my picture in the Faces in the Crowd in the April 21, 1997, issue of Sports Illustrated. I still compete in one or two major tournaments per year, and my current world professional ranking is #32.

My primary areas of practice are business organizations, commercial transactions, real estate, and taxation. I came to practice in these particular areas because of my background in business education; I went to business school at Indiana University majoring in finance and later went on to pass the Certified Public Accountant (CPA) Exam. With my combined education in business, finance, and accounting, I am able to advise clients in multiple areas of a transaction and can often be an asset because of my ability to communicate with and understand the other professionals involved in a business matter.

My wife, Wendy, is a New Haven native, and we have two young girls - Abby born in 2004, and Anna born in 2006.

attorneys.name: George “Rich” Slater
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
G. Richard Slater is the managing partner of Slater Law Office LLC in Carmel, Indiana. Founded in 1991 by his father, George G. Slater, and joined in 2001 by his mother, Nancy Slater, after she transitioned from her career as a physician, the firm has grown into a multigenerational practice grounded in trust, guidance, and long‑term relationships.

Rich carries that tradition forward with the philosophy that elder law is not limited by age and is an ongoing relationship with clients, not a one-time transaction. He works closely with individuals and families to craft and update comprehensive life plans, including wills, trusts, special needs trusts, powers of attorney, guardianships, probate and trust administration, Medicaid planning strategies, and planning for individuals with mental or physical disabilities.

Rooted in Hamilton County, Rich grew up on his family’s farm before attending Culver Military Academy for high school. He began his undergraduate studies at Rose‑Hulman Institute of Technology in Terre Haute, Indiana, then redirected his path from engineering to business, earning both his bachelor’s and master’s degrees in Business Administration from Stetson University in DeLand, Florida. He subsequently moved to the Cayman Islands to manage a home improvement company and served as a volunteer officer with the Royal Cayman Islands Police Service. Returning to the United States in 2009, he joined Slater Law Office LLC as a law clerk by day while completing evening studies, earning his J.D. in 2015 from the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis.

An active volunteer in the legal community, Rich frequently speaks on estate planning and elder law topics and provides pro bono services to veterans through his work with the Indianapolis Bar Association. His professional memberships include the Estate Planning & Administration Section of the Indianapolis Bar Association; the Probate, Trust & Real Property Section and Elder Law Section of the Indiana State Bar Association; the American Bar Association; and the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys (NAELA).

Outside the office, Rich is a licensed private pilot, amateur (ham) radio operator, and beekeeper. He enjoys playing tennis, camping, assisting his neighbors with yard and home maintenance, and spending time with his fiancé, Valerie, and their dogs—Cora, a German Shepherd, and Asher, a Husky. He looks forward to serving the community for decades to come, carrying forward the legacy and client‑focused values on which his family’s practice has been built.

With the goal of becoming an attorney, she attended Purdue University and obtained a Bachelor of Arts degree in political science. As an attorney, Mallory takes great pride in helping Hoosiers get through some of the most challenging times they will have to face.

attorneys.name: Lyndon Small
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Lyndon Small is the Managing Partner at Doyle Family Law, LLC and a dedicated family law attorney serving clients throughout Indiana. Since beginning his legal career in 2017, Lyndon has built a reputation for thoughtful advocacy and compassionate client representation in complex family law matters.

Lyndon has extensive experience handling a wide range of family law cases, including divorce, custody disputes, guardianships, paternity actions, contempt, post-decree modifications, relocations, protective orders and related family law matters.

Over the course of his career, Lyndon has successfully managed hundreds of cases. His approach balances strong courtroom advocacy with a practical focus on achieving positive and efficient outcomes for families navigating difficult transitions. He has successfully litigated several highly contested cases that have withstood post-judgment challenges at both trial and appellate levels.

Lyndon understands that the legal process can be scary, confusing, and overwhelming for many people, which is why he strives to provide honest, straightforward, and loyal representation to all his clients while advocating diligently for their best interests.

Before becoming Managing Partner, Lyndon served as an associate attorney and later as Managing Attorney overseeing family law, business litigation, and real estate law departments. In those roles, he supervised associate attorneys, developed case-management systems, and handled a substantial independent caseload while mentoring younger lawyers and supporting firm operations.

When not practicing law, Lyndon enjoys spending time with his wife and son and attending ITOWN Church in Fishers, Indiana.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law (Property Division, Children’s Issues and Post-Decree Modification) Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Deborah Farmer Smith practices exclusively in the areas of family law and alternative dispute resolution. She received her B.S., cum laude, from Butler University in 1976 and her Juris Doctor, magna cum laude, in 1983 from the Indiana University School of Law in Indianapolis. Ms. Farmer Smith joined Cohen Garelick & Glazier in 2016 after practicing for 32 years with Campbell Kyle Proffitt LLP.

Ms. Farmer Smith is one of fewer than twenty Fellows of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers in Indiana. She has co-chaired the Family Law Certification Board, which certifies attorneys as family law specialists in Indiana, since 2002, and is a Certified Family Law Specialist. Deb is also a Registered Domestic Relations Mediator in Indiana, and has successfully mediated hundreds of family law matters. She has also served as a family law arbitrator.

Deb is a former Chair of the Family & Juvenile Law Section of the Indiana State Bar Association, and in 2010 received its Gale M. Phelps Award. She has been listed numerous times in recent years as a Super Lawyer in family law by Indianapolis Monthly magazine, including having been listed among the Top 25 Women Attorneys in Indiana. She has the A-V rating in Martindale-Hubbell, the highest rating available.

Ms. Farmer Smith served as the first Counsel to the President of the Indiana Bar Association, after two years on its Board of Managers. She has received three Presidential Citations from the ISBA. Deb is also a former President of the Indiana Bar Foundation. She has chaired and spoken at dozens of seminars for the Indiana Continuing Legal Education Forum. When not practicing law, Deb is the pianist for the First United Methodist Church in Noblesville, and has conducted many musical theater productions at local community theaters, for which she has received nine Encore Awards.

attorneys.name: Michael Ray Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Michael Ray Smith, who has been an Indiana attorney for more than 25 years, sometimes explains that he is in his third career. His first career was as a chemical engineer with Eli Lilly and Company after graduating from Vanderbilt University. From 1978 through 1993 (with two years out to get a master's degree in chemical engineering from Purdue University), he worked in manufacturing and process development areas and as a department head of biochemical engineering. He completed law school while he was working full time in those positions.

Mike's second career began when he finished law school in 1993 and joined Lilly's Law Division as in-house counsel, where his responsibilities included environmental law, securities, and commercial transactions. While working as an attorney with Lilly's commercial transactions group, he worked on a variety of strategic sourcing initiatives, joint ventures, and other transactions. He also developed a system for writing and maintaining contract templates for use by the company's procurement professionals in areas as diverse as laboratory research, construction, advertising, and market research.

Mike began his third career in 2008 as a business lawyer in private practice, when he left Lilly and opened a solo practice in Fishers, Indiana, known as Michael Smith Law Office, LLC, focusing on business and commercial transactions, limited liability companies (or LLCs), corporations and corporate law, nonprofit organizations, and estate planning. In 2009, the name of the firm changed to Smith Rayl Law Office, LLC when he was joined by Attorney Susan Rayl, who opened an office in Indianapolis practicing criminal defense. Mr. Smith brings this extensive business law experience to Hand Ponist, where he concentrates on providing personal service and practical advice to businesses, especially small businesses, their owners, and nonprofit organizations.

Michael also has a passion for teaching. While he was at Lilly, he developed and taught several training courses for Lilly personnel, including an extensive course in contract law for Lilly's procurement organization. After he left Lilly, he supervised law students in an externship program jointly conducted by the Community Development Law Center and the Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law, and for two years he served as an Adjunct Professor at the same school, teaching Contract Drafting to second year law students. He has taught continuing legal education courses for the Indiana State Bar Association and the National Business Institute, mostly in contract law and limited liability companies.

Awards and Honors

Honors

2004 Heartland Pro Bono Award, Heartland Pro Bono Council, Indiana

attorneys.name: Scott Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Dissolution/Divorce Lawyers in Noblesville, IN
attorneys.bio:
N. SCOTT SMITH obtained his undergraduate degree in Political Science with a minor in Foreign Language from Indiana University in 1999, with high distinction. Prior to beginning law school, Mr. Smith worked as a Governor's Fellow with the Office of the Governor of Indiana. During law school, Mr. Smith not only completed coursework graduating in the top 12% of his class, but also worked for the the Integrated Public Safety Commission on legislation for a statewide first responder communications system and as a research assistant to then Assistant Dean, Andrew Klein. Mr. Smith obtained a real estate sales agent license, which he held for several years.

Mr. Smith holds a juris doctorate from IU Robert H. McKinney School of Law, which he earned, cum laude, in 2004. He was admitted to the bar in Indiana in 2005. Mr. Smith received several scholarships and recognitions including, but not limited to: graduating with honors; recipient of the John J. Dillon Scholarship; and Finalist in Moot Court Championship arguments.

Prior to opening his own firm in 2016, Smith Legal LLC, Mr. Smith was a partner with the firm Campbell Kyle Proffitt LLP until 2016. While at Campbell Kyle Proffitt, Mr. Smith had a diverse litigation practice focusing primarily in divorce and family law matters, but also in adoption, real estate, business and personal injury.

Mr. Smith specializes in family law mediation and litigation, limited to only: dissolution (divorce), post-dissolution, paternity and adoption. He is a registered domestic relations and civil mediator with an average of 2-3 mediations per week serving as mediator by court appointment and attorney selection. Mr. Smith is also a collaboratively trained dissolution lawyer and parenting coordinator.

Super Lawyers recognized Mr. Smith in family law in 2020 - 2025 and as a Rising Star in General Litigation in 2014 and 2015. Additionally, he served or serves currently on a number of boards and commissions and for non-profit organizations, including: City of Noblesville Plan Commission (Vice President); Indiana State Bar Association (Past Delegate District #6, Board Member); Noblesville Midday Rotary Club (Past President, Member); Hamilton County Leadership Academy (Alumnus, Past Board Member, Committee Chair); Noblesville Main Street (Current Board Member); Miller Ambassador (2020); Meals on Wheels (Past President); Venture Christian Church (Deacon). Mr. Smith is also pro bono legal counsel to Cherish, a non-profit child advocacy organization.

attorneys.name: Natalie M. Snyder
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Natalie Snyder is a Certified Family Law Specialist certified by the Family Law Certification Board. She is also a trained collaborative lawyer, a trained parenting coordinator, a trained civil mediator, trained in child informed mediation and has been named as one of the Super Lawyers in Indianapolis Monthly magazine for family law from 2018 to 2025, and a Rising Star by Super Lawyers from 2012 to 2015. She has lectured and written on various family law issues and represented medical, legal, accounting, financial, closely held business owners, family farms, executives, teachers, fireman and police officers, and other professionals and spouses. In addition to complex legal divisions of assets and debts, Natalie has specialized in developing unique custody and parenting time plans to meet the needs of her individual clients. Natalie is a former board member of the Indianapolis Bar Association, and she is the past Chair of the Family Law Section of the Indianapolis Bar Association. Natalie is an Indianapolis Bar Foundation Distinguished Fellow and was a member of the Foundation's Grant Committee in 2012. Natalie is a Board Member and the Past President of the Central Indiana Association of Collaborative Professionals and a Past President and Board Member of the Indiana Association of Family and Conciliation Courts. Natalie is also a member of the Collaborative Solutions Collaborative Law Practice Group.

Natalie resides with her husband and daughter in Cicero, Indiana. Natalie has concentrated her practice in legal matters related to relationship transitions including matrimonial and family law, high conflict family resolutions, paternity, collaborative law, international family disputes, premarital and postnuptial agreements, child custody, relocation, parenting time, support, grandparent visitation, and interstate disputes and modifications.

Natalie has specialized in the peacemaking process of alternative dispute resolution through collaborative law, mediation, parenting coordination, and other closed processes for counseling and evaluations, including specializing in high conflict parents, personality disorders, and addictions in families. Natalie understands the lifelong consequences of conflict on children and helps to resolve matters through peacekeeping processes, when possible, and litigation when not possible.

attorneys.name: S. Reese Sobol II
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Reese Sobol brings empathy and a passion for helping people to his practice at Garau & Germano. Reese has long been interested in a career as a plaintiff's attorney and will work tirelessly to deliver each of his clients the best possible outcome.

With deep midwestern roots, Reese grew up in a small town in Illinois. He attended Illinois Wesleyan University for his undergraduate studies, where he played four years of football and graduated with a bachelor's degree in Financial Services, cum laude. Reese later obtained his legal education from Indiana University Maurer School of Law in Bloomington. He graduated magna cum laude in 2021 and was selected as a member of the Maurer Chapter of the Order of the Coif.

After graduating law school, Reese clerked for the Honorable James Patrick Hanlon on the United States District Court for the Southern District of Indiana. In this role, Reese worked on a wide variety of criminal and civil matters at every stage of litigation from the filing of a complaint through trial. This experience gave him a keen and unique insight on the litigation process from the perspective of the court and equipped him with the skills necessary to effectively represent clients in state and federal court. Reese is licensed to practice in Illinois and Indiana and is eager to take on clients wherever help is needed.

attorneys.name: Betsy Sommers
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Betsy is a partner in the litigation group at Coots, Henke & Wheeler, where she concentrates her practice on defending businesses and municipalities in employment-related claims, including EEOC investigations and cases involving wrongful termination, discrimination, harassment, wage disputes, and other employment law matters. In addition to employment law, Betsy has extensive experience defending premises liability cases, municipal cases, general tort claims, dram shop litigation, and real estate disputes. Betsy’s expertise spans all phases of the litigation process—from pre-suit negotiations and discovery to summary judgment proceedings and appeals—ensuring her clients receive comprehensive, strategic counsel.

Betsy also has significant family law litigation experience. She regularly represents individuals in divorce and post-dissolution proceedings, guardianships, and civil protective orders, as well as drafting and negotiating prenuptial and postnuptial agreements. As a trained Guardian Ad Litem, she advocates for the best interests of children in court proceedings.

attorneys.name: Codey L. Spear
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Moseley & Martinez, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Merrillville, IN
attorneys.bio:
Codey L. Spear graduated from the Valparaiso University School of Law in 2016 and has practiced in various areas of law including criminal, personal injury, bankruptcy, and family law. Since joining the Law Offices of Moseley & Martinez, LLC, Codey has taken pride in representing his clients' diverse needs with a focused, client-first approach, in both civil and criminal litigation.

Codey is an Indiana native having been born and raised in the small, central Indiana town of Crawfordsville. Upon graduating Crawfordsville High School, Codey attended Indiana State University, where he received a Bachelor's Degree in Music Business Administration. While at Indiana State, Codey was a member of the Indiana State University Sycamore Football team, playing center and guard on the offensive line. He also was a member of Indiana State Jazz Band, Wind Orchestra, and toured Bangkok, Thailand playing alto saxophone in the Nomine Saxophone Quartet.

When not advocating for his clients, Codey enjoys spending his free time in the gym and riding his motorcycle with his wife, Katrina. As an avid strength athlete, Codey is decorated competitor in both strongman and powerlifting, regularly participating in both Indiana and Illinois competitions, even earning a spot in the 2018 United States Strongman Nationals.

attorneys.name: Larry D. Stassin
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce and Family Law Lawyers in Dyer, IN
attorneys.bio:
Larry D. Stassin was born in Chicago, Illinois in 1965, and raised in Lake County, Indiana, until 12 years of age when his parents moved to the State of Illinois. After graduating from Homewood-Flossmoor High School, Larry attended Indiana University in Bloomington where he received a Bachelor of Arts Degree 1987. Larry then enrolled at the Indiana University School of Law in Indianapolis where he graduated from in 1990 and was admitted to the bar that same year. Larry is currently licensed to practice before the U.S. Supreme Court, the U.S. Federal Court for the Northern District of Indiana, as well as all Indiana state and local Courts. Larry is a member of the State of Indiana Legal Ethics Committee, as well as the Committee On the Unauthorized Practice of Law. In addition to the above, Larry makes it a practice to donate as much time as he has available to the Legal Services of NW Indiana/pro bono commission to aid people in the community who need legal help but cannot afford it.

Larry's practice consists of a concentration in divorce and family law; personal injury and workmen's compensation; criminal defense; guardianship and estate work; bankruptcy; and real estate. Larry has represented several criminal defendants in high profile criminal cases in Lake County. In addition, Larry has secured large personal injury settlements for clients against defendants such as the Town of Griffith, Highland, EJ&E Railroad and Subway. Throughout his career, Larry has developed a reputation as an aggressive yet practical lawyer getting the best results possible for his client without burying his client in mountains of legal debt.

Larry currently lives in the Town of Griffith with his wife and three boys. Much of Larry's free time is devoted to youth activities such as coaching and running the soccer program for the Griffith Soccer Club as it's current president, assisting with both middle school and high school wrestling teams, as well as helping run the youth wrestling club, giving lectures and presentations to local school science programs regarding the raising and breeding of reptiles. When Larry has free time, he spends that time playing golf with his sons and traveling with his wife.

attorneys.name: Melanie M. Sterba
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Schererville, IN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Melanie M. Sterba earned her Bachelor of Arts Degree from Michigan State University in 1975. She received her Juris Doctor Degree from Valparaiso University School of Law in May, 1983 and began practicing law June 3, 1983, having passed the Indiana Bar Exam in 1982.

Attorney Sterba opened her own practice in the Twin Towers in Merrillville, Indiana. She relocated to Schererville, Indiana in 1997. In 2007, Attorney Sterba partnered with Jill S. Swope to become the managing partner of Sterba & Swope, LLP.

Attorney Sterba has practiced exclusively in the area of family law for over 30 years.

attorneys.name: Amy L. Stewart
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
Known as a thoughtful, determined problem-solver, committed to finding positive, constructive approaches for resolving family legal issues, Amy Stewart practices exclusively in the firm's family and matrimonial law division. She assists clients with a full range of family law matters, including separation and divorce, paternity, asset valuation, division and distribution, child custody, child support, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, cohabitation, and domestic partnership.

Amy brings to her clients a passion for designing creative out-of-court solutions, honed during more than 30 years of professional experience. Well-versed in each of the alternative legal processes available to families, Amy helps clients select the process that fits them best. She is a leader in Collaborative Practice in Indiana, and also serves clients as a perceptive and resourceful mediator and coach. Amy's dignified, discrete approach resonates well with her clientele, which includes business owners and professionals in the financial, legal, and medical fields, celebrities, professional athletes, and community leaders.

With her energy for problem solving, negotiation, and out-of-court settlement, Amy skillfully guides clients in identifying and achieving their interests and in maintaining healthy family relationships, protecting children from the harm of family conflict, and preserving wealth and assets from costly, prolonged litigation. While clients may begin a legal process in considerable distress, Amy's calm and grace, combined with her wisdom and experience, allows clients to honor their values and look forward to the future.

Before joining Mallor Grodner Plummer Attorneys in 2014, Amy was for several years a partner at a large Indianapolis law firm. Prior to her legal career, Amy had the opportunity to hold high-level positions in government and business. She credits that experience with teaching her the value of building trust and respect, even between people with differing views; with broadening her perspective, beyond legally-based solutions; and with giving her an unshakable belief in people’s ability to be their best selves and live their best lives.

Racquetball is his favorite sport, even though he is too out of shape to play!

attorneys.name: John M. Stringfield
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation and Appeals Lawyers in Bloomington, IN
attorneys.bio:
John M. Stringfield, joined as an Senior Litigation Associate at Clendening Johnson & Bohrer, P.C. in June of 2020 and focuses his practice in civil litigation.

John attended undergrad at Ball State University and completed his undergraduate degree in December of 2014.

In 2017, John was a fellow with the Indiana Supreme Court Coalition for Court Access, which focused on evaluating access to courts in rural areas of Indiana for indigent and pro-se litigants. During his time as a fellow with the Coalition, he conducted field research, interviews, and presented his findings to members of the Indiana Supreme Court.

In 2018, John graduated from the IU Robert H. McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis, Indiana and was admitted to the Indiana bar in December of 2018.

John previously served as the Chairperson of the Young Lawyer Division for the Defense Trial Counsel of Indiana. In 2023, John was named the “Young Lawyer of the Year” by the Defense Trial Counsel of Indiana. He currently serves on the Board of Directors for the Defense Trial Counsel of Indiana.

Notable cases

Gilead Sciences, Inc. v. Allied Health, et al. Second chair in an action in Miami Federal Court seeking $43 million dollars in damages from forty-nine (49) healthcare businesses for alleged fraud and trademark violations in the distribution of Gilead’s anti-AIDS medications distributed in Southwest Florida. Clendening Johnson & Bohrer represented six of the defendants. The case involved complicated legal issues arising from intellectual property law and healthcare regulations and numerous complex discovery disputes and injunctions. Over 100 depositions were taken over a year and a half prior to settlement.

attorneys.name: Jill S. Swope
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Schererville, IN
attorneys.bio:
Jill earned her Bachelor of Science Degree from Valparaiso University in 1992. She then attended Valparaiso University School of Law where she was a member of the Moot Court Honor Society Executive Board, and participated as a team member in national moot court competitions across the county.

Jill began as a law clerk with her now-partner's law firm during her first year of law school in 1993. After graduating cum laude from Valparaiso University School of Law in 1995, she passed the Indiana and Illinois bar exams that same year.

Jill has practiced in the field of family law for most of her career. She successfully completed the rigorous application and testing process to become one of the first Certified Family Law Specialists, as certified by the Family Law Certification Board in the State of Indiana in 2002. She remains one of only a handful of certified specialists in Lake County and now serves as a member of the State Family Law Certification Board.

Jill is also a Registered Family Law Mediator and a trained Parenting Time Coordinator, providing services in high conflict matters. With extensive experience in dissolution of marriage, paternity, child custody, child support, adoption, name changes and appeals, Jill enjoys affecting the lives of her clients by making difficult times less stressful and easier to understand.

Most recently Jill completed extensive training to begin working as a Collaborative Law Professional. Collaborative law allows parties to work with a collaborative group of professionals from multiple disciplines who share their desire to resolve matters outside of the court system. It is less stressful, more holistic, and creative at its core. It is an exciting option that Jill hopes to employ as often as possible.

Jill has been a presenter of continuing legal education seminars in the area of family law and has authored successful appeals in both the Indiana Court of Appeals and the Indiana Supreme Court.

Jill is actively involved in the Indiana Chapter of the Association of Family and Conciliatory Courts (AFCC), currently serving on the Board of Directors, as Treasurer of the organization, and on the Programming Committee. This involvement has solidified her passion for multi-disciplinary work in which legal professionals, the judiciary and mental health professionals can work together to educate one another and assist high-conflict families.

Jill has volunteered as a speaker for Indiana State Bar Association programs which seek to educate children about the law and civics. She has presented on behalf of the "Why Lincoln Was a Lawyer?" community outreach program and the Indiana Kids' Election Speaker's Bureau, as well as serving as a judge for the We The People program.

Andrew R. Tanzillo was born in 1955 and was raised in Calumet City, Illinois. He attended T.F. North High School, where he participated in football, basketball, and track. He attended Valparaiso University and earned his Bachelors of Arts Degree with Distinction in 1977. He continued his education at Valparaiso University School of Law, and earned his Juris Doctorate Degree in 1980, and was admitted to practice law in the State of Indiana that same year.

In his many years of practice in Lake County, Indiana, Mr. Tanzillo has developed a substantial practice in family law matters including dissolution of marriage, custody, support, visitation and paternity matters. In addition, he has also concentrated his practice in criminal misdemeanor and traffic law including operating while intoxicated cases. Also in 1981, Mr. Tanzillo was appointed by the Court to serve as a Public Defender in the Lake Superior Court, County Division, Room Number One, to represent indigent defendants in criminal and traffic matters.

Mr. Tanzillo is a member of the Indiana State Bar Association and the Lake County Bar Association. He resides in Munster, Indiana with his wife and two children.

attorneys.name: John Taylor Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
When facing a family law matter, it is important to have an attorney who can guide you with both skill and understanding. John Taylor is a Senior Associate Attorney with Stange Law Firm, proudly serving clients from the firm’s Indianapolis, Indiana office. He is committed to providing thoughtful representation to individuals and families as they navigate difficult and emotional legal challenges.

John earned his Juris Doctor from Indiana University School of Law – Indianapolis, graduating magna cum laude in May 2008. During his time in law school, he distinguished himself academically and served as a Note Development Editor for the Indiana Health Law Review. Prior to law school, John completed his Bachelor of Science in Marketing at Indiana University in Bloomington, graduating in December 2003.

Before joining Stange Law Firm in Indianapolis, Indiana, John developed extensive experience in litigation and client advocacy across a variety of legal roles. Most recently, he served as an Associate Attorney with The Liberty Mutual Group in Indianapolis, Indiana, where, for a decade, he represented clients in all phases of litigation. His work included drafting pleadings and motions, preparing for depositions and trial, conducting discovery, assisting with negotiating settlements, and mentoring junior attorneys and staff. Prior to that, John worked as a Paralegal at Liberty Mutual and as a Staff Attorney at AHC, Inc. in Gainesville, Virginia, where he focused on analyzing health insurance contracts, handling appeals, and negotiating resolutions. These positions gave him a wide range of practical experience, from motion practice to client counseling, that he now applies to his work at Stange Law Firm.

John is licensed to practice law in Indiana and holds an associate membership with the Virginia State Bar. His background in litigation, combined with his dedication to client service, allows him to approach family law cases with clarity and compassion. He understands the challenges that clients face during divorce and custody disputes and is committed to advocating for outcomes that protect their rights and support their future.

attorneys.name: Rodney V. Taylor
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accidents - Plaintiff Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Rodney V. Taylor is an attorney with the Christopher & Taylor law firm in Indianapolis, Indiana. A top-rated trial attorney with more than 45 years of legal experience, Mr. Taylor focuses his practice primarily on plaintiff personal injury claims and helping his clients obtain the full amount of compensation they deserve for the injuries and losses they suffered as the result of someone else's negligence. In addition, he also handles business litigation involving a wide range of disputes, including issues involving energy and natural resources.

A native of Illinois, Mr. Taylor graduated from the University of Illinois in 1969 and served in the U.S. armed forces. Upon completing his service, he attended Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in Indianapolis, where he obtained his Juris Doctor in 1973.

The Indiana State Bar Association admitted him to practice that same year, and he is also admitted to practice in Kentucky, Illinois, Missouri, Ohio, New York and Washington, D.C., as well as before the U.S. District Courts for the Southern District of Indiana, the Northern and Southern Districts of Illinois, and the District of Columbia; the U.S. Courts of Appeals for the 6th, 7th and 9th Circuits; and the U.S. Supreme Court. He also handles cases throughout Canada and the Caribbean.

Along with maintaining a successful legal practice, Mr. Taylor supports his local community through his involvement with various philanthropic efforts. He is the founder of The Miracle Ride Foundation and the Indianapolis Air Show, and he serves as president for The Miracle Ride Foundation. Through his efforts, he has helped raise almost $6 million for the Riley Hospital for Children. He also serves on the board of The Athenaeum Foundation as well as general counsel for ABATE of Indiana, ABATE of Illinois and ABATE of Ohio.

In recognition for his selfless service, he was appointed Sagamore of the Wabash in 2007 by Governor Mitch Daniels, and he has earned numerous awards and honors for his impeccable professionalism, including a listing in the Martindale-Hubbell* Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers. He is also a licensed pilot and received the Indiana Aviator of the Year award in 2012.

attorneys.name: John S. Terry
attorneys.practice_type: Probate and Estate Administration Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
John was admitted to the Bar in 1998 and is a second generation lawyer. He is a lifelong resident of Carmel. He says that he went to all three Carmel schools – Carmel Elementary, Carmel Junior High and Carmel High School. His father worked for one of the biggest law firms in Indiana, but counselled John to strike a balance between work and life which helped drive his decision to open his own law firm. With Terry Legal Group LLC he is bringing his 20 years of legal experience to his home community to fulfill his father’s advice.

John regularly advises men and women, their companies and families, through the day to day and long term challenges they may encounter. John prepares simple “mom and pop” wills and trusts as well as more complicated estate documents for those that need to develop a plan to avoid or mitigate the federal estate tax. For business owners, he provides advice regarding business formation and entity selection, contract preparation and review, asset and stock sales and acquisitions, and business succession planning. The touchstone of his practice is the lasting relationships he makes with his clients.

Community service is also an important hallmark of John's non-professional life. He previously served on the Board of Directors for the Friends of Hamilton County Parks and the Actors Theatre of Indiana. He can be found also coaching his children's sports teams through the Carmel Dad's Club.

John is a past president of the Hamilton County Bar Association. He holds a preeminent AV rating from Martindale Hubbell, is rated as a 10 out of 10 attorney by Avvo, and has been previously recognized as a Rising Star by the Indianapolis Monthly Magazine. In 2015 he was a contributing author for a Thompson Reuters publication called Inside the Minds™ – Best Practices for Structuring Trusts and Estates.

John is a life member of the NRA and a fan of IU Basketball, the Pacers, the Colts and the Wabash College Little Giants. In his spare time he enjoys reading classic mysteries like Sherlock Holmes. He also writes poetry and literature and hopes one day to publish his own book of fiction.

attorneys.name: Kayleen M. Teufel
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Valparaiso, IN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Kayleen Teufel brings to Langer & Langer a commitment to use her legal skills and background to assist individuals and families going through a vulnerable situation. She reveals empathy, intelligence and sensitivity as she counsels clients on family law matters.

Kayleen earned her undergraduate degree in business management and leadership at Bradley University. Kayleen earned her J.D. from Valparaiso University School Of Law. During her law school career, she worked as a law clerk for a Superior Court Judge in a neighboring county. The position provided her with valuable exposure to the courtroom and chambers. During law school, she was active in the Student Bar Association and completed internships at the Illinois Liquor Control Commission, Hammond Legal Aid Clinic and Valparaiso University’s Criminal Law Clinic.

Since becoming a lawyer, Kayleen has focused the majority of her practice on assisting clients navigate custody disputes, divorce, child support issues, adoption and guardianship. Kayleen also has experience preparing prenuptial and post-nuptial agreements and litigating issues that arise involving such documents.

Kayleen has demonstrated her commitment to the local legal community by serving on the board of the Porter County Bar Association for the past several years, which culminated in serving as president of the Porter County Bar Association in 2022. Kayleen also co-chairs the Porter County Family Law Section and Porter County Local Rules Committee for family law.

Kayleen is admitted to practice in Indiana in the Northern and Southern Districts.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Merrillville, IN
attorneys.bio:
Will Theodoros is the newest attorney to join the team at Theodoros & Rooth, P.C., having joined in the fall of 2014 after graduating from the Robert H. McKinney School of Law: Indiana University in Indianapolis. Before law school, Will received a bachelor's degree in Business from Miami University in Oxford, OH. Will is admitted to practice law in both Indiana and Illinois.

Will is very proud to join Theodoros & Rooth, P.C., following his father, Perry, and his grandfather, William, in the practice of law. He looks forward to adding to the over 110 years combined legal experience at the firm.

Will focuses his practice in the field of personal injury. As an attorney, Will's goal is to help his clients that have been hurt due to another's negligence. Whether it is a car accident, truck accident, defective product, or medical malpractice, Will promises to fight for you and to hold the responsible parties accountable for their actions so you can get the compensation you deserve.

Outside of the office, Will enjoys traveling as much as possible. He spent a summer studying international business in Europe, traveling to many different countries including France, Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, and Greece. He also enjoys working out and is an avid golfer.

attorneys.name: Angelina Torres
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
A steadfast champion for justice, Angelina Torres developed her commitment to fighting for the rights of others over the course of a journey that took her from Metro Detroit to Washington, D.C.

While attending American University, where she was a member of the Alpha Chi Omega sorority and the college dance team and spent a semester abroad in Madrid, Angelina immersed herself in the intricacies of government. Her studies inspired her to work first on Capitol Hill and then with the United States Government Accountability Office (GAO), focusing her efforts on the Departments of Justice and Homeland Security.

Angelina’s desire to empower those in need ultimately drove her to delve into the complexities of the legal system at DePaul University College of Law in Chicago. After earning her Juris Doctorate, she embarked on a career getting innocent victims the compensation they deserve in car accidents, product liability, wrongful death, and government immunity cases. She joined Hensley Legal Group in 2024, where she continues her fierce advocacy for personal injury plaintiffs.

When she is not in the office, Angelina enjoys spending time with her family, playing with her Labrador Retriever Tilly, and trying new restaurants.

attorneys.bio:
Jacob Troxell joined Allen Wellman Harvey Keyes Cooley, LLP in 2023. Jacob graduated from IU Robert McKinney School of Law and was admitted to practice law in the state of Indiana in the same year.

Jacob is originally from central Indiana. Prior to his legal career, Jacob earned his Bachelor of Arts degree from Franklin College in 2017 and went on to obtain his Master of Arts degree from Ball State University in 2019. While at Franklin College, Jacob was a part of the Franklin College baseball team. During his time at Ball State University, Jacob was a Graduate Assistant in the Department of Political Science and briefly held a possession with the Anderson University baseball team.

Jacob's journey into the legal realm was marked by a series of impactful experiences. His professional background includes positions with the Bose Public Affairs Group, the Indiana Fiscal Office of the Senate Majority Caucus, and the Office of offices of Senator Todd Young and Congresswoman Susan Brooks (IN-5).

Jacob currently resides in Pendleton Indiana with his wife, Jessica, their son, Hudson, and their dog, Cali. In his free time, Jacob enjoys playing recreational sports, spending time with his family, and going to the movies. Jacob and his family attend the Sanctuary of New Castle Church in Henry County.

attorneys.name: Denise Laureen Turner
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
"The first time I saw my brother brought into juvenile court in handcuffs, I decided I would be the best lawyer I could be."

Denise has been helping those accused of crimes since graduating in 2010 from George Washington University Law School in Washington, D.C. She started her legal career at the Marion County Public Defender Agency, where she handled criminal cases ranging from misdemeanors, such as public intoxication and OVWIs, to major felonies, including robbery, burglary, rape, and murder.

Denise went into private practice in 2017, and expanded her practice to include areas outside of Marion County, and other areas of the law, including appeals, expungements, and sentence modifications. She is certified to handle death penalty cases and she was appointed to the federal CJA panel in 2020 where she represents indigent clients charged in federal court.

During her time at GW Law, she focused on criminal law and trial skills. Denise was the Vice-President of Internal Mock Trials on the Mock Trial Board and has continued to serve as a mock trial judge for high school and undergraduate mock trial competitions sponsored by the Indiana Bar Foundation. Denise also volunteers with the IndyBar helping law students prepare for the bar exam.

Having been on the other side, Denise knows how difficult an arrest can be on the person charged and their families. "I've been the one calling and paying for lawyers. I've posted bonds for my brother. I know what that's like; which is open, and honest communication with my clients and their families is very important to me."

She is licensed in Indiana and her home state of Florida. Just in case her brother ever needs her.

attorneys.name: Ronald J. Waicukauski
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Rights Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Ron Waicukauski is a trial lawyer whose practice focuses on plaintiffs’ complex litigation including matters involving business disputes, property rights, professional malpractice, and class actions. He has tried more than eighty jury cases to verdict as lead counsel in both state and federal courts. He has been plaintiffs’ lead trial counsel in cases that resulted in class action verdicts of $79 million and $130 million, a civil rights verdict of $31 million, and other multi-million-dollar verdicts in antitrust and legal malpractice cases.

Ron has been recognized in Best Lawyers in America (2006-2023), Indiana Super Lawyers (2004-2023) and with an AV Rating from Martindale-Hubbell. Ron has also received the Indiana Lawyer Leadership in Law Distinguished Barrister Award.

Ron received his bachelor’s degree with Distinction from Northwestern University, his J.D. degree from Harvard University where he was named Best Oralist in the Ames Moot Court Competition, and an LL.M. degree, with Highest Honors, from George Washington University. Ron has taught trial and appellate advocacy at the Indiana University Schools of Law in Bloomington and Indianapolis, and has served on the faculties of the National Institute of Trial Advocacy and the Defense Counsel Trial Academy.

Ron has also served as President of the Indianapolis American Inn of Court, as Chair of the Continuing Legal Education Board of the International Association of Defense Counsel, and as Co-chair of the Training the Advocate Committee, Litigation Section, American Bar Association. He formerly was a JAG and Captain in the U.S. Marine Corps and served as the elected Prosecuting Attorney in Monroe County, Indiana.

Ron co-authored The Twelve Secrets of Persuasive Argument (2009 ABA), The Winning Argument (2001 ABA), Classical Rhetoric and the Modern Trial Lawyer, Litigation (Winter 2010); and Ethos and the Art of Argument, Litigation (Fall 1999). Ron also wrote Learning the Craft, Litigation (Spring 1998) and was the editor and a contributing author of Law and Amateur Sports (Ind. Univ. Press 1982). Since 2004, Ron has been a regular speaker to the Indianapolis Law Club on recent developments in Indiana law.

Wine and Canvas v. Muylle (2015)—Represented defendant Muylle in suit for trademark infringement; jury trial resulted in verdict for Muylle on Wine & Canvas’ trademark claims and in favor of Muylle on counterclaim for abuse of process; as a result of verdict, Muylle now owns Wine & Canvas.
Ping v Ramey (2021)—Represented plaintiff in suit against ex-husband and his girlfriend on claim for false reporting to DCS; jury trial resulted in verdict totaling $201,500; affirmed on appeal.

Hayes Lemmerz Intern., Inc. v. Law Firm (2011)—Represented plaintiff in legal malpractice case, resulting in judgment for substantial damages following bench trial; matter settled on appeal for confidential amount.
Lite Machines v. Clary (2006)—Represented small business in legal malpractice case; jury trial resulted in $3.6 million verdict for plaintiff; affirmed on appeal.

attorneys.name: John D Walls
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of John D. Walls, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Walls is the principal shareholder of the law firm of J.D. Walls & Associates, P.C. His practice is focused on the representation of business and employers in all aspects of employment and business-related law and litigation. He also practices bankruptcy law in both Chapter 7 and 13 cases.

He has extensive experience counseling employers regarding compliance with all types of employment and business-related issues. Mr. Walls has over 10 years of experience in Corporate Management within the Human Resource/Employee Relations functions in businesses with annual revenues exceeding $500M and over 3000 employees throughout the United States. John’s prior experience also includes over a decade of experience in the private and corporate practice of law. Most recently, John served as General Counsel and Senior Director of Human Resources for SM&P Utility Resources, Inc. located in Carmel, Indiana. In his bankruptcy practice, Mr. Walls provides his clients with thoughtful and efficient representation through difficult financial times and enables them to make a clean start with their financial lives.

John believes in a hands-on, holistic approach to the practice of law. This means he spends much of his time teaching corporate management and ownership how to avoid litigation, as well as guiding them through the process should it become necessary. John has experience in all areas of business and employment law and in federal, state, local and administrative jurisdictions. He has authored articles on various subjects and has been a frequent trainer, facilitator and guest speaker throughout his career. John is also a fully qualified Civil Mediator in the state of Indiana.

Mr. Walls is a 1995 graduate of the Ohio Northern University of Law where he was a national semi-finalist in the National Administrative Law Moot Court Competition, recipient of the Ohio Northern Labor Law Scholarship and served as law clerk to Federal Magistrate Judge Thomas Carlson in the U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Michigan. He has served on the Board of Directors for the State of Indiana Association of Corporate Counsel and is a member of the Indiana State Bar Association Employment and Labor Law Division.

attorneys.name: Thomas J. Walz
attorneys.practice_type: Business and Corporate Law Lawyers in South Bend, IN
attorneys.bio:
Tommy was admitted to practice in the State of Indiana, including the United States District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of Indiana in 2007. Tommy received his B.B.A in Business Finance cum laude from the University of Notre Dame in South Bend, Indiana in 2004 and his J.D. from the University of Dayton School of Law in Dayton, Ohio in 2007.

Prior to joining Hahn|Walz, Tommy worked in the legal department of Lauth Group, Inc., an Indianapolis-based commercial real estate development firm specializing in the development, construction, management and ownership of retail, medical, professional and industrial office buildings throughout the continental United States.

After leaving Lauth Group, Inc., Tommy gained extensive litigation and trial experience as a deputy prosecutor with the Marion County Prosecutor's Office in Indianapolis, Indiana from 2008-2012. As a deputy prosecutor, Tommy was involved in the prosecution of hundreds of cases wherein he tried nearly 100 bench trials and over 20 jury trials ranging from misdemeanors and low-level felonies to major felonies and homicides.

Tommy is a member of the St. Joseph County, Indiana State, and American Bar Associations. Tommy practices in the areas of Estate Planning and Probate, Wills and Trusts, Collections and Bankruptcy, Business and Corporate Law, Personal Injury, Labor Law, General Civil Litigation, and Criminal Defense.

Passionate about the community involvement of and provision of opportunities for those with special needs, Tommy serves as a member of the Corporate Board of Directors at the Logan Center in South Bend.

attorneys.name: Matthew J. Warner
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Hammond, IN
attorneys.bio:
Matt Warner is an associate of Westland & Bennett P.C. Matt is a Region native who grew up in Highland and now lives there with his wife and 3 sons. At a young age, he set his sights on becoming an attorney. After high school, Matt began working for a law firm in Chicago as a legal assistant. He continued working for this firm while he attained his bachelor's degree from Purdue University and his law degree from Valparaiso University School of Law. After he passed the Illinois bar exam, he began working at the same firm as an associate.

For the next 6 years, Matt continued working in Chicago, gaining experience in multiple areas of law (from creditor's rights to real estate to insurance litigation and everything in between). While it gave him great experience; working in Illinois did not provide Matt with the chance to help individuals from the Region. Matt really wanted to start giving back to his community and creating stronger ties to the area he grew up in. In 2020, Matt joined Westland & Bennett P.C. Not only did this give Matt an opportunity to expand his practice and help people within his community, it also gave him the opportunity to give back in other ways. Matt and his wife are involved in many different organizations, and they are members of the Board of Highland Little League. When not fighting for a client, Matt can likely be found cheering on one of his sons.

attorneys.name: Delmar Dean Weldon III
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Lawrenceburg, IN
attorneys.bio:
Del Weldon is a partner at the firm and focuses his practice on trial work and litigation. He is experienced in many areas of Litigation, including criminal defense with an emphasis on OWI/DUI defense, personal injury, family law and CHINS defense. He is an experienced trial attorney, winning verdicts at jury trials and bench trials. He is also a skilled negotiator, securing plea agreements and forcing dismissals in criminal matters and obtaining settlements in civil matters.

As a criminal defense attorney, his experience working at the prosecutor's office, including trial work and a murder case, is a major strength and provides great value to his clients. With hundreds of cases completed, he is an experienced and knowledgeable advocate. He is a graduate of both the Misdemeanor and Felony Trial Practice Institute and the OWI Trial Practice Institute, and is a graduate of Gerry Spence's Trial Lawyers College.

In civil matters, he is an aggressive and experienced advocate and works to obtain the outcomes needed to put individuals and families back together. He has secured for his clients recoveries in many different types of cases, including six- and seven-figure recoveries.

In addition to his work as an attorney, Del also teaches trial advocacy at Chase College of Law and is a professor at Ivy Tech College. He teaches criminal justice and paralegal studies. He focuses on teaching advocacy in legal research and writing as well as the constitutional fundamentals of the justice system with his students. Del also hosts "Law Talk," an informational radio show on Eagle 99.3 FM.

Del graduated from Indiana University and the Kelley School of Business in 2002, and from Chase College of Law in 2008. He is a member of Phi Alpha Delta Law Fraternity International. Del is very active in the community and is a member of the Board of Directors for Melodic Connections. He is also a mentor in Big Brothers/Big Sisters, and works with the Key Club and Builders Club as part of his membership in Kiwanis International.

attorneys.name: Marshall P. Whalley
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Crown Point, IN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Whalley is an experienced Trial Lawyer, Author, Lecturer and former Judge Pro Tempore. The secret to success for Marshall P. Whalley has been his widely varied interests and seemingly boundless energy to pursue them. Having immersed himself in such fields as physics, psychology, engineering, consumer protection and medicine, Mr. Whalley has acquired a wealth of knowledge directly applicable to the investigation and litigation of complex personal injury cases. He has over 32 years experience successfully handling multi-million dollar litigation in several states.

Mr. Whalley’s father attended M.I.T., earning two engineering degrees and going on to design tanks for the government. His mother was a nurse educator with a Bachelor of Science, a Master’s degree and applied to Law School at 78! Growing up near the Motor City, Mr. Whalley spent long hours designing, building and racing cars and boats, and working on his grandfather’s farm in North Dakota.

Mr. Whalley attended the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor where he studied physics and psychology, earning his B.S. in 1980. His graduate work there in psycho-physics at the Kresge Medical Hearing Research Institute involved training rare monitor lizards to respond to acoustic stimuli. His other pursuits included designing and implementing pilot programs at the Milan Federal Correctional Institute allowing inmates to obtain GED certificates and at the Maxey Boys Correctional Institute for troubled youth.

During college, Mr. Whalley also worked in the Consumer Protection Division of the Washtenaw County Prosecutor’s office, where he mediated consumer complaints, securing the largest consumer settlement to date in the Division’s history. At the same time, he worked for a Tenant’s rights group helping educate renters regarding their rights vis a vis large corporate landlords. During the summer months, Mr. Whalley continued to attend class at the University of Michigan while working 40 to 50 hours per week on the assembly line in Detroit building cars for Chrysler and General Motors. On the line, he ran presses, welded wheels, performed manual assembly, body work, and painted cars.

Thereafter, Mr. Whalley received a scholarship to Valparaiso University School of Law. He continued to work on cars and drag raced to help pay college expenses. He then took a job clerking for a well-respected personal injury firm doing medical research, legal writing and investigation. He became a lawyer at the firm, then partner. As an Associate, he used his background in physics and medicine in his first year to facilitate settlements of the two largest brain-damaged baby cases in Florida’s history. Mr. Whalley’s background in physics allowed him to employ a waveform analysis of fetal monitor strips to prove when a critical tocolytic drug had been stopped.

Over the past 30 some years, Mr. Whalley’s myriad interests have helped him be an effective advocate for his clients. Designing, building, racing and repairing all types of vehicles, Mr. Whalley developed insight into crash dynamics that few lawyers have. His training in physics, medical research and litigation has provided a unique perspective on the causes of complicated crashes and their medical consequences. Marshall P. Whalley has used this unique background to prove-up millions of dollars in valid claims that might otherwise have been lost.

attorneys.name: Luisa M. White
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Lafayette, IN
attorneys.bio:
Luisa is an attorney practicing primarily in the areas of civil litigation, criminal defense, and family law. She is admitted to practice in the State of Indiana (2013); the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Indiana (2013); and the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana (2013).

Luisa was born in Morristown, New Jersey, and grew up in The Woodlands, Texas. She attended Purdue University as an undergraduate and continued her education at Valparaiso University where she obtained a Masters in Psychology and a Juris Doctor in 2012.

Luisa began her career volunteering for District 4 Pro Bono Corporation and Indiana Legal Services, Inc. in Lafayette, Indiana where she was awarded the "Pro Bono Attorney of the Year" in 2013. Luisa was then hired to manage and direct Wabash Valley Volunteer Attorneys, Inc., a Pro Bono corporation managed by the Indiana Bar Foundation, where Luisa single-handedly operated legal aid programs in 8 Indiana counties that provided legal services to the indigent population. In 2014, Luisa went on to private practice when she joined Raquet, Vandenbosch & Steele, in Kokomo, Indiana as an Associate where she represented many individuals in the areas of Criminal Law, Family Law, and Civil Litigation. In 2016 she was hired as Deputy Public Defender for Howard County where she provided legal assistance to individuals with limited resources and was invited to join Gambs Mucker & Bauman in Lafayette, Indiana where her work focused mostly on Civil Litigation, Family Law, and Criminal Law. Luisa is now an independent practitioner dedicated to providing personalized legal services while building strong, long-term attorney-client relationships.

Luisa is fluent in Spanish and works closely with Hispanic communities all over Indiana assisting them with various civil and criminal matters that affect their immigration status.

Luisa believes in a strong work ethic and puts her clients first, listens to them, and finds effective resolutions to their legal issues.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Pro Bono Attorney of the Year, 2013

attorneys.bio:
A 1975 honors graduate of the University of Evansville, Terry A. White joined The Law Team in 1982, four years after being admitted to practice in front of the Indiana Supreme Court. His admittance came the same year (1978) as his graduation from the Indiana University School of Law in Indianapolis, where he received his Doctor of Jurisprudence.

After graduation, Mr. White held several legal positions in Warrick and Vanderburgh counties, practicing prosecutorial, defense, and municipal law.

Those positions included:

Intern for Vanderburgh Circuit Court Judge William Miller

Deputy Prosecutor, Vanderburgh County Prosecutor's Office, 1979 - 1981

Chief Deputy for Misdemeanor Court, Vanderburgh County Prosecutor's Office, 1979 - 1980

Chief Deputy for Superior Court, Vanderburgh County Prosecutor's Office, 1980 - 1981

Public Defender, Vanderburgh Circuit Court, Jan. 1983 - March 1990

Board Attorney, Warrick County Area Planning Commission and Board of Zoning Appeals, 1993 - June 1996

County Attorney, Warrick County, 1996 - 2000

Public Defender, Vanderburgh Superior Court, Jan. 2006 – Apr. 2007

Mr. White was active in the legal community while attending Indiana University's Law School, where he served as President of the Indiana University Student Bar Association, Vice Justice of the Phi Alpha Delta Law Fraternity Law Review, and Associate Editor of the Indiana Law Review. Those honors were in addition to his undergraduate work at the University of Evansville, where he was President of Student Congress, Vice President of the Blue Key Academic Honorary Fraternity, and graduated cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science in 1975.

Mr. White is licensed to practice in the Supreme Court of the United States and United States Court of Appeals, as well as the U.S. District Court for the District of Southern Indiana.

attorneys.name: Joseph N. Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Class Action Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Joe is a trial lawyer, who focuses his practice on representing the rights of the physically and economically injured. He recently provided the closing arguments after a six-week jury trial against State Farm, resulting in a $14.5 million verdict for his client. Earlier this year, Joe was lead trial counsel in a breach of contract case that resulted in a $230,000.00 jury verdict. He also recently recovered $1.2 million for a client that was severely injured by a defective product. Joe handles all types of trial work, ranging anywhere from personal injury to complex business disputes to products liability.

Joe also devotes a portion of his practice to protecting consumers through statewide and nationwide class action litigation. He has experience in all stages of class action litigation, maintaining a strong focus on the class certification procedure. Joe has successfully handled all aspects of class certification, including the briefing, arguing, and obtaining of class certification in the trial court, and protecting a successful class certification decision in the Court of Appeals and state Supreme Court.

Joe received his J.D. from Vanderbilt University Law School, where he was awarded the Tennessee Bar Association’s Access to Justice Law Student of the Year in 2004. He was honored with selection to the Indiana Super Lawyers’ Rising Stars in both 2010, 2011 and 2013, a designation that recognizes the top up-and-coming attorneys in the state.

Joe is admitted to practice law in the State of Indiana, the U.S. District Courts for the Southern and Northern Districts of Indiana, and the Northern and Central Districts of Illinois, and the Fifth and Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals.

attorneys.name: Bradley L. Wilson
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Discrimination, Wrongful Discharge, and Retaliation Law Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Bradley Wilson is a partner and litigation attorney at Wilson Melton, LLC, in Indianapolis, Indiana. He has fought long and hard for nearly 25 years in and out of court for employees who have experienced unlawful wrongful discharge, discrimination, harassment, and retaliation in the workplace. Bradley founded his law firm, along with Shannon Melton, because of his passion for civil rights and justice on behalf of employees. He has represented nearly 1,000 employees in legal matters with their employers.

Bradley is a member of the bars of Indiana, Georgia, the United States District Court for the Northern District of Indiana, the United States District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals. Bradley has predominantly represented former and current employees in all aspects of employment law, including claims for wrongful discharge, unpaid wages, overtime violations, and employment discrimination and retaliation, before state and federal courts and administrative agencies, including the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. He has also served as lead counsel on behalf of employees in multiple class and collective actions alleging sex discrimination, unpaid wages, and unpaid overtime under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Fair Labor Standards Act, and the Indiana Wage Statute.

Bradley has a unique perspective in disputes between employees and employers. He practiced for a few years at an Indianapolis law firm where he represented companies in employment matters before federal and state courts and administrative agencies as well as advised management professionals in making personnel decisions and in ensuring that their policies were compliant with federal and state employment laws. In short, Bradley has been on both sides of the aisle and has a perspective on how employers generally think.

Bradley is a magna cum laude graduate of Ball State University and a summa cum laude graduate from Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law.

attorneys.name: Jerome L. Withered
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lafayette, IN
attorneys.bio:
Lawyers help people find solutions --- that's what we do. Whether you've been hurt in an accident, have a business problem, need your will written, or have any number of other issues needing legal attention, we are here to help guide you through the legal process. Call us and let us help you find the answers to your issues.

A native Hoosier and practicing lawyer in Lafayette since 1980, Jerry serves clients in personal injury cases and litigation of all types, represents small businesses, and works with individuals on estate planning. He has tried a wide variety of jury trials and bench trials in personal injury, wrongful death, medical malpractice, contract, real estate, business, estate, and other cases. In his appeal work, he has argued cases before the U.S. Court of Appeals (7th Circuit), the Indiana Supreme Court, and the Indiana Court of Appeals.

Jerry is Board-certified Civil Trial Advocate (National Board of Trial Advocacy), is rated AV by Martindale-Hubbell, selected for inclusion in Indiana Super Lawyers® (2005, 2007-Present), and by invitation is a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates and Litigation Counsel of America. He graduated from Purdue University (B.S. 1973), the University of Virginia (M.A. Economics 1976), and received his legal education at Indiana University McKinney School of Law (J.D. summa cum laude, 1980).

attorneys.name: Holly S. C. Wojcik
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Merrillville, IN
attorneys.bio:
Holly Wojcik is a partner at the Merrillville law firm of Theodoros & Rooth, P.C., where she focuses her practice in the areas of medical malpractice and other personal injury cases. Holly earned her B.A. degree in psychology, magna cum laude, from Michigan State University in 1998 and her J.D., cum laude, from Valparaiso School of Law in 2001. She clerked in London, England and at the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service in Chicago before entering her law practice.

She is a member of the Lake County Bar Association, the Indiana State Bar Association, the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association, ITLA Women's Law Caucus, and the American Association for Justice.

Holly was the first woman ever elected to the Indiana Judicial Qualifications/Nominating Commission and served as a commissioner from 2021-2023. She has recently been appointed to the Indiana Attorney Disciplinary Commission. She currently sits on the Board of Directors for the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association. Holly has handled hundreds of medical malpractice claims in Indiana and was on the legal team that prosecuted 288 claims against Dr. Mark Weinberger, "The Runaway Doctor" featured on America's Most Wanted and American Greed, which resulted in a $55 million dollar settlement for her clients after the indictment, extradition, and imprisonment of the Merrillville doctor.

Holly has been named as an Indiana Super Lawyer for 2019-2024. Her firm, Theodoros & Rooth, has been nominated for the Best of the Region for several years running. She has been pleased to speak at various ITLA, ICLEF, and Lake County Bar seminars, the Kentucky Justice Association Women Lawyers Caucus (2023), the Embrace Your Inner Badass conference in Palm Springs, California (2023), and volunteers at Chesterton and Merrillville High Schools educating high school students on what it is like to practice law. Holly has also written articles published in Res Gestae.

When she is not working, Holly enjoys fishing and spending most of her time doing anything outdoors including canoeing, kayaking, and hiking. Holly is a huge soccer fan, having played women’s soccer in college. She has a passion for traveling which has taken her all over the world including backpacking across Europe, camping in the Boundary Waters of Minnesota, on an all-women's rafting trip in the Grand Canyon, and most recently, a safari in South Africa. Holly is originally from St. Joseph, Michigan and currently lives in Valparaiso, Indiana.

Holly can be reached at holly@trinjurylaw.com or Theodoros & Rooth, P.C., 8750 Broadway, Suite A, Merrillville, Indiana 46410. Theodorosrooth.com Phone: (219) 769-6393.

attorneys.name: Christopher Wolcott
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law -- Employee Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
When you’re confronted with workplace challenges or facing discrimination, having a dedicated advocate in your corner can make all the difference. I’m attorney Chris Wolcott, and I am here to courageously stand up for your rights and fight for the justice you need.

Having founded The Wolcott Law Firm LLC in Indianapolis, Indiana, I leverage my extensive experience in human resources and over 25 years of legal practice to provide unwavering support for workers across the state. My focus is exclusively on employment law, ensuring that my clients receive specialized and effective representation tailored to their individual needs and circumstances.

I believe that every client deserves not just a lawyer, but a trusted partner. You can rely on me for honest, personalized, and professional guidance throughout your legal journey. I understand that navigating employment law issues can be daunting and that the stakes are high, as they impact your future and your family’s well-being. That's why I prioritize clear communication, setting realistic expectations, and crafting customized solutions that deliver results.

When you work with me, I take the time to understand your situation and goals fully. Together, we will navigate the complexities of employment law, empowering you to reclaim control over your future and achieve the justice you truly deserve. Your rights matter, and I am here to ensure those rights are protected every step of the way.

If you have employment law concerns, do not delay addressing them. Please get in touch with me as soon as possible to discuss your case and explore your legal options. To get in touch with me, please call my Indianapolis office at 317-854-3435 or complete my online contact form to send a message.

attorneys.bio:
John Woods received a bachelor’s of science in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Evansville in 2006 and his Juris Doctor from Franklin Pierce Law Center in 2009. John started his legal career at Krieg Devault, LLP where he practiced in the areas of patent prosecution, intellectual property licensing, and litigation.

While John has experience in various facets of intellectual property law including trademarks, trade secrets, and copyright, John has maintained a focus on patent prosecution. John has drafted and prosecuted patent applications in the subject areas of internal combustion engine technologies, hybrid technologies and electrical vehicles, after-treatment systems, air and refrigeration compressor system technologies, electronic controllers and systems, turbo-machinery, as well as various mechanical systems and devices generally. John has prepared numerous right-to-use, infringement, invalidity, and patentability opinions.

John Woods is licensed to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office. John is an Eagle Scout, and he volunteers for various organizations and remains active within the Indianapolis legal community.

attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Greenfield, IN
attorneys.bio:
Joseph Scott Wooldridge graduated with a bachelor’s degree in 1997 from Bluffton University, where he majored in biology and pre-medicine. In 2001, Scott graduated from Indiana University – Indianapolis with a Master in Health Administration (MHA).

Scott started business school and law school in 2002. While in law school, he worked as a research assistant for Professors Eleanor Kinney and David Orentlicher within the Hall Center for Law and Health. Additionally, Scott did an internship with St. Vincent Health System legal department and was a law clerk for Allen, Wellman and McNew. Scott received his JD from Indiana University – Indianapolis with a Health Law concentration; also he graduated at the same time with a Master in Business Administration (MBA), finance concentration, from the Indiana University – Kelley School of Business. He was admitted into the Indiana bar in 2008.

Mr. Wooldridge joined Wolf Law Firm in January 2010.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Carmel, IN
attorneys.bio:
SCOTT P. WYATT was admitted to the bar in Indiana in 1998. He obtained his undergraduate degree from Truman State University in 1993 with his major in English and Minors in Theater and Journalism. Prior to attending law school, Mr. Wyatt was a writer/producer/director for KTVO television in Kirksville, Missouri. He obtained his law degree from Indiana University – Indianapolis in 1998, during which time he also served as a certified intern with the Marion County Prosecutor’s Office. Upon graduation and passing the bar in 1998, Mr. Wyatt served as a Marion County Deputy Prosecutor from 1998-2001. During this time, Mr. Wyatt was responsible for handling all aspects of criminal cases including offenses ranging from simple misdemeanors to murder. Mr. Wyatt left the Marion County Prosecutor’s Office in 2001 and joined the law firm of Campbell Kyle Proffitt LLP, where he quickly became a partner. attorneys.name: Robert W. York
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Indianapolis, IN
attorneys.bio:
Robert W. York has been a practicing Indiana Attorney since 1973 having obtained his Doctor of Jurisprudence with honors from Indiana University School of Law. He is a former Deputy Prosecuting Attorney, a former Indiana Administrative Law Judge and, currently, a frequent Special Judge presiding over major felony criminal cases. He is the senior lawyer in a six member law firm in Indianapolis, Indiana and devotes his practice to participating in trials in courts throughout Indiana. He is admitted to the bar of the United States Supreme Court and all of the courts of Indiana. He has memberships in a number of trial lawyer associations and Bar Associations. He is a recognized author in a number of legal publications and was Editor of Verdict magazine for 12 years. He and his wife, Donna, have been married for 39 years and are the parents of two sons, ages 28 and 22. He has been certified by the United States Hockey Association as a Master Coach and has coached 40 youth hockey and baseball teams.
